**Cleanup**: `TopPickCard.tsx`, `PopularReviewCard.tsx` (replaced by `ReviewFeedCard.tsx`), `getRecommendations`/`RecommendationItem`, and `getTopPicks`/`TopPick` were all deleted as genuinely orphaned (confirmed via grep — none had any other caller after this change); `getSuggestions`/`SuggestedUserCard` and `discoverLists` were kept since `network.tsx`/the new Lists tab still use them respectively. `StackedAvatars.tsx` is a new shared component extracted from what was previously `TopPickCard`'s inline-only stacked-avatar implementation (plain `View`s with a negative-margin overlap, no SVG) — now reused by `AddedByCard.tsx` (the new Popular This Week/Popular with Friends card, composing the existing `ContentCard` with a footer row).

i18n: new keys `"Films"`, `"Popular with Friends"`, `"Reviews from Friends"`, `"Lists from Friends"`, `"added_count"`/`"added_count_plural"` (mirrors the existing `rating_count` pattern), plus two new empty-state strings — all translated across all 12 locales. Note `"Films"` is a deliberately different label from the bottom tab bar's existing `"Movies"` — the user's own explicit wording for this specific tab, flagged in case it wasn't intentional.

### Home redesign refinements + Lists tab: likes, views, Popular Lists
Follow-up polish pass on the Home redesign above, plus a genuinely new feature the user flagged explicitly. Small fixes first: header wordmark bigger (custom `headerTitle` render function in `home/_layout.tsx`, since a plain `title` string can't embed an image); the `films` tab's label changed from `t("Films")` to the already-existing `t("Movies")` (the `"Films"` key was removed as orphaned); `ReviewsSection.tsx`'s internal Movie/Series sub-tab now uses the exact same underline style as the outer Films/Series/Reviews/Lists bar, instead of its own boxed-border segmented control — the user wanted the two tab bars visually consistent.

**A real, confirmed bug fix, not just a preference**: Popular This Week/Popular with Friends cards were showing a bare "—" under the title — traced to `ContentCard.tsx`'s `meta` line always falling back to that placeholder when no `year` prop is supplied (which these items never have). Initially fixed by having `AddedByCard.tsx` stop composing `ContentCard` and show the content's TMDB `vote_average` as small stars instead — **superseded the same day** (see the addendum below): the user pointed out this created a real data inconsistency with Content Detail's Rating Distribution chart (which reflects only this app's own users' ratings, so a title with zero in-app ratings would show "No ratings yet." right next to a Home card confidently displaying a TMDB-sourced star rating for the same title) and asked for the rating to be dropped from these cards entirely rather than reconciled — `AddedByCard` now shows poster → title → who-added-it, no rating. The `vote_average` plumbing added to `getPopularAdds()`/`PopularThisWeekItem` for this was reverted as no longer used. The new `src/components/StarRatingDisplay.tsx` component built for this stays in use elsewhere (see below) — this is only about what `AddedByCard` shows.

Two other numeric `★ X/10` text badges were replaced with `StarRatingDisplay` (the read-only counterpart to the existing interactive `StarRatingInput.tsx`, reusing its exact half-star clip trick but non-interactive and small) and are unaffected by the above: `ReviewFeedCard`'s rating badge, and `FeedItemRow`'s "rated" activity sentence — the latter required restructuring the sentence itself, since RN's `<Text>` can only nest other `<Text>`, not a `<View>`-based star row; the sentence now ends after the content link, with the star row rendered as its own line below it (matching how the "reviewed" case already renders its excerpt below the sentence).

Activity section now shows 5 items initially with "Load more" up to a hard cap of 15 (`FEED_PAGE_SIZE=5`, `MAX_FEED_ITEMS=15` in `ContentTypeSection.tsx`) — purely a client-side display cap layered on the existing real pagination, no backend change needed. Also fixed real wording left over from the earlier Watched-List rename milestone: the "watchlisted" activity sentence said "...to their watchlist" — corrected to a new `"to their watched list"` key (old key removed, confirmed via grep it had exactly one call site).

**Lists tab: new card design + "Popular Lists" (new feature, explicitly requested).** `CustomList` gains `likes: [ObjectId]` (exact same shape as `Review.likes`) and `views: Number`. New `POST /api/lists/:id/like` mirrors `toggleReviewLike` exactly. `GET /api/lists/:id` now increments `views` (skipped for the owner browsing their own list) and returns `likeCount`/`hasLiked` alongside the existing `list`/`isOwner`. New `GET /api/lists/popular` (registered before `GET /:id`, same ordering requirement `/discover`/`/me` already follow) ranks by like count via aggregation, mirroring `getPopularReviews`'s exact shape — **a deliberate, documented judgment call**: ranks by likes only, not views, matching `getPopularReviews`'s own precedent; views are tracked and shown on the List Detail screen but don't feed the ranking. Both `/discover` and `/popular` now also hydrate a `previewItems` field (first 5 items' title+poster, bulk-fetched the same `movieMap`/`seriesMap` way `feedController.js`/`reviewController.js` already do) — previously `items` was raw `{itemId,itemType,addedAt}` with zero content lookup, which the new card design needs to show mini-posters.

`DiscoverListCard.tsx` redesigned in place (now backs both Lists-from-Friends and Popular Lists, per the user's "same design for both" ask): list name top-left, owner avatar+username top-right (reversed from the old top-left owner row), up to 5 poster-only preview thumbnails in a row below, description last. Rendered as a full-width vertical card now (previously a 170px horizontal-rail card) since the user explicitly described lists stacking one below another — matches `ReviewFeedCard`'s vertical-list pattern. `ListsFromFriendsSection.tsx` renamed to `ListsSection.tsx` and restructured like `ReviewsSection.tsx` (two vertical sections in one component: Lists from Friends + the new Popular Lists). `ListDetailScreen.tsx` gained a like button (same optimistic-toggle pattern as `ReviewFeedCard`'s) and a view-count line — opening this screen is what increments `views` server-side, no separate "mark as viewed" call needed.

**Same-day addendum: real logo, dropped Home-card rating, darker header.** `assets/icon.png` turned out to be the **unmodified Expo template icon** (a generic blue chevron placeholder graphic) — never actually replaced with Cinephix's own branding, confirmed by opening the file directly. The real brand mark lives at `frontend/src/assets/cinephix_logo.png` (a solid "C" glyph, transparent background — the matching `.svg` is a complex multi-shade auto-traced export unsuitable for a themeable inline `react-native-svg` component, so the flat PNG was copied to `mobile/assets/cinephix_logo.png` instead and referenced directly). Both places that used the wrong asset are fixed: the Home header wordmark and the About screen's header. `assets/icon.png` itself (the actual OS app icon / splash / adaptive-icon source per `app.json`) was deliberately left untouched — that's a separate, bigger-scope fix (affects native builds) outside what was asked here, flagged for whenever that's actually addressed. i18n: new keys `"to their watched list"`, `"Popular Lists"`, `"No popular lists yet."`, `"view_count"`/`"view_count_plural"` (mirrors the existing `rating_count` pluralization pattern) — all 12 locales. Removed (orphaned): `"Films"`, `"to their watchlist"`.

### List Detail screen redesign
`ListDetailScreen.tsx` (reached from Home's Lists tab and the standalone Lists tab) fully reorganized per a precise user spec. Header title bug: the screen was calling `navigation.setOptions({title: fetchedList.name})`, silently overriding the route's own already-correct static `title: t("List")` (declared in both `home/_layout.tsx` and `lists/_layout.tsx`) — removed both calls, so the static title now shows through as intended.

Info block reorganized top-to-bottom: owner byline (`UserAvatar` + tappable username — new, wasn't shown here before) → list name + public/private badge → description → one consolidated icon-led stats row (item count, like button, view count — previously split across two visually inconsistent lines) → edit button. New All/Movies/Series sub-tab (`t("All")` reused a key that already existed from an earlier milestone) sits below, reusing the exact underline style from `ReviewsSection.tsx`/`home/index.tsx`'s outer tab bar — purely a client-side filter over the already-hydrated `items` array, no new fetch.

Grid went from 2 columns to 6, with a new `src/components/MiniContentCard.tsx` (poster-only) replacing the full `ContentCard` — 2-column-sized posters read as oversized once compared against the app's other dense grids. `getListById`'s return type also got more accurate: `GET /lists/:id` actually populates `owner` (unlike `/me`, `POST /`, `PATCH /:id`, which don't) — new `CustomListDetail` type reflects that instead of overloading the shared `CustomList.owner: string` shape used everywhere else.

**Same-day follow-up: tighter grid spacing, rating dropped entirely.** The 6-column grid initially used `width:"15%"` cards with `columnWrapperStyle:{justifyContent:"space-between"}` — visually too loose, and a genuinely wrong approach for a grid whose last row usually isn't a full 6 items (space-between spreads a short last row across the *entire* width, producing huge gaps between just 2–3 cards). Replaced with explicit pixel math via `useWindowDimensions()` (`cardWidth = (screenWidth - padding*2 - gap*5) / 6`) and a fixed `GRID_GAP` applied as `marginRight` on every card except the 6th-in-row (computed from the `renderItem` `index`) — gap stays constant regardless of how a row happens to fill. Also added a small `marginBottom` on the All/Movies/Series tab bar itself, since the first card row was touching it directly with zero breathing room. Separately, the per-card average-rating line initially added (see the paragraph above, since superseded) was dropped entirely per explicit follow-up feedback — `MiniContentCard` is now purely visual (poster only), and the backend `GET /ratings/averages` endpoint + its mobile plumbing (`getAverageRatings`, the `RATINGS.GET_AVERAGES` route constant) were reverted as genuinely orphaned, consistent with this session's practice of not leaving unused code behind after a design walked back.

### Content Detail (movie/series) page redesign
`ContentDetailScreen.tsx` fully reorganized per a precise user spec, touching layout, a new stats endpoint, the review-writing UX, and a new social section.

**Header title removed**: unlike List Detail (which had a real bug — a dynamic title silently overriding an already-correct static one), here the route's static option was already a deliberately blank `title: ""`; the real title only ever came from this screen's own `navigation.setOptions({title})` call. Deleting that call (along with the now-unused `useNavigation` import) leaves the header blank, exactly as requested — nothing to "fix," just remove.

**Layout**: poster shrunk and moved into a `topRow` (`flexDirection:"row"`) alongside a `topRightCol` holding title+year (same line), a `numberOfLines`-truncated overview, and `RatingDistributionChart` — absorbing what used to be three separate full-width sections (title/meta, standalone Overview section, standalone Rating Distribution section) into one compact side-by-side block. The old TMDB `vote_average` meta line is gone entirely (consistent with the earlier `AddedByCard` decision — this app doesn't mix TMDB ratings with its own-platform rating displays).

**New info-stats row**: four counts (Watched / Reviews / Favorites / Lists — the last one explicitly the user's own `CustomList` feature, not either watchlist concept) on a `colors.base200` background, icon-above-label. Backed by a brand-new `GET /api/content/:type/:id/stats` (public, `backend/routes/contentStatsRoute.js`) that just runs four independent `countDocuments` queries against fields that already existed (`User.watchlist`, `User.favoriteMovies`/`favoriteSeries`, `CustomList.items`, `Review.contentId`) — no schema changes needed.

**Rating and review moved into the compact action-button grid.** The old standalone "Your rating" (`StarRatingInput` inline) and "Your review" (`ReviewComposer` inline, always-visible textbox) sections are gone — folded into two new buttons (Rate, Add/Edit Review) alongside the 4 existing action buttons (now 6 total, same `48%`-width wrap grid). Each opens the file's existing `modalOverlay`/`modalCard` pattern (already used for the Add-to-List picker) with the same unchanged inner component (`StarRatingInput` / `ReviewComposer`) — zero changes needed inside either of those components. The Review button's label toggles Add Review ↔ Edit Review based on `myReview` being null; the modal auto-closes on successful save or delete. **Per-review-card delete removed from the review list**: `ReviewCard.tsx` already gated its delete button on `isOwn && onDelete` — simply no longer passing `onDelete` from `ContentDetailScreen.tsx` silences that button with zero changes to `ReviewCard.tsx` itself, so editing/deleting your own review is now only possible via the Edit Review button/modal, not from within the Friends/Popular list.

**New "Watched by Friends" section**: profiles from your network who have this content on their *watched* list, each showing `StarRatingDisplay` (the gray multi-star component built earlier this session) instead of a number — explicitly requested ("sayıyla değil, yıldızlarla"). Backed by a new `GET /api/content/:type/:id/watched-by-friends` (auth required, `contentStatsRoute.js`): looks up the caller's `following`, filters to those with the content in `watchlist`, then joins in each one's own `Rating` for it (`null` if they watched but never rated) — same `following`-lookup pattern already established in `feedController.js`/`customListRoute.js`'s `/discover`.

**Friends/Popular review tabs restyled**: from the old filled-pill `reviewTabRow`/`reviewTabButton*` style to the established underline `tabBar`/`tabButton`/`tabButtonActive`/`tabText`/`tabTextActive` style (verbatim from `ListDetailScreen.tsx`) — the fourth reuse of this tab style this session.

Verified: `getContentStats`/`getWatchedByFriends` curled against real data (a content ID with a real review, one with a real list membership, one with 30 real watchers/6 favorites) all returned correct counts; `watched-by-friends` verified against 3 real followed users — 2 with real `Rating` docs (returned their actual values) and 1 without (returned `rating: null`), confirming the join is correct in both directions. 8 new i18n keys landed in all 12 locales. Metro bundle grepped for `getContentStats`, `getWatchedByFriends`, `WatchedByFriend`, and the new i18n strings — all present; the old `"TMDB ★"` string confirmed gone.

**Same-day refinement pass, no backend changes.** `RatingDistributionChart.tsx` rebuilt: bars shrunk (60→36px max height), the tiny per-bar numeric labels (0.5/1/1.5.../5) removed entirely and replaced with a scale metaphor — a small half-filled star (same half-clip technique used everywhere in this app) at the bars' bottom-left, and a full 5-star row (reusing `StarRatingDisplay`) at the bottom of the summary column on the right, both landing on the exact same baseline as the bars via the container's existing `alignItems:"flex-end"` — no manual offset math needed. New press-and-hold interaction per bar (`Pressable`'s `onPressIn`/`onPressOut`, fires immediately on touch-down): holding a bar swaps the average number for that bar's raw count, hides the total-count text, and morphs the summary's 5-star row into that bar's exact rating (`StarRatingDisplay` fed `pressedValue * 2`); releasing reverts everything. `StarRatingInput.tsx` gained an optional `size` prop (default 30, unchanged elsewhere since it has exactly one call site) and center-aligned its row — the Rate modal now passes `size={44}` for bigger, easier-to-tap stars.

Action button grid reordered and its "colored border" treatment narrowed to exactly two buttons (previously an inconsistent three-vs-rest split): Watched List (unchanged) and Rate (newly given the same `toggleButton` treatment, active-filled once `myRating > 0`) — Watchlist, previously also colored, moved to the Rate button's old slot and restyled to the plain `listButton` treatment with a `time`/`time-outline` icon (mirroring Favorites' `star`/`star-outline` pattern) instead of its old `+`/🕓 text-emoji prefixes. `ReviewCard.tsx`'s like button moved from a separate footer row up into the header row (right-aligned, level with the avatar) — its `isOwn`/`onDelete`/`currentUserId` machinery was fully dead code since the previous milestone moved delete into the Edit Review modal, so it was removed rather than left unreachable, consistent with this session's orphaned-code discipline. `ReviewComposer.tsx`'s outer card lost its own redundant `base200` background (it was nested inside the modal's already-`base200` card, contributing to the "looks bad" complaint); the `TextInput` itself gained a real input-field treatment (`base100` background, radius, padding) so it reads as a distinct field; Save/Delete shrank slightly. The Review modal's bottom "Close" text button was replaced with a small `Ionicons "close"` icon absolute-positioned top-right (`reviewModalCard: {position:"relative"}` applied only to this modal instance, not the shared `modalCard` style, so the List/Rate modals' existing bottom "Done" buttons are untouched). "Watched by Friends" now sits in a `base200` box matching the stats row's treatment; a "Reviews" heading (reusing the `"Reviews"` key from the stats row) was added above the Friends/Popular tabs, which had none before. `RatingDistributionChart` moved out of the poster's right column to its own full-width row below, so the overview text now ends level with the poster as asked. Verified via `tsc --noEmit` (clean) and a fresh Metro bundle grep for the new style symbols (`barActive`, `modalCloseIcon`, `friendsBox`, `scaleStarWrap`, `reviewModalCard`) — all present.

**Second same-day refinement pass.** Fixed a real layout bug: `RatingDistributionChart`'s summary "total rating count" text was conditionally *unmounted* while a bar was pressed (not just hidden), so the summary column's height changed between press states — since the row is `alignItems:"flex-end"`, everything bottom-anchored (bars, star row) visibly jumped up/down on every press/release. Fixed by always rendering the `Text`, only swapping its content (a single space when hidden) so the column's height never changes. Average now reads `"X.X/5"` instead of a bare number.

**Half-star rendering redone from the ground up, in two different ways for two different needs.** `StarRatingDisplay.tsx` (read-only, used in the chart's summary star row, Watched by Friends, and now `ReviewCard`) no longer clip-renders a half star at all — it shows `floor(value)` filled ★, then a small `"1/2"` text label for the remainder, then empty ★ for the rest. Root cause this sidesteps: a Unicode `★` glyph's *visible* shape isn't reliably centered within its own text layout box, so a 50%-width container clip doesn't reliably bisect the shape you actually see — this was the "yarım yıldızlar bozuk görünüyor" complaint. The chart's left-end scale marker (previously a lone half-clipped star) became the same `"1/2"` text treatment. `StarRatingInput.tsx` (the interactive Rate-modal picker) can't use text for its half-state — you're tapping to *choose* a half star — so it was rebuilt on `react-native-svg` (already a dependency, same import pattern as `MatchPercentageRing.tsx`/`CineGraphDonut.tsx`) instead: one shared 10-point star `Path` (chunkier than a font glyph — outer radius 11, inner radius 4.5 — delivering "daha şişman" as geometry, not a font-weight hack) rendered twice, the colored overlay clipped by an exact-geometry `<Rect>`/`<ClipPath>` (`width={12}` of a `viewBox="0 0 24 24"` for half, `24` for full). Since both copies share the literal same path data, the half-clip is now mathematically exact — the "renk yıldızın tam ortasından geçmiyor" alignment bug can't recur. Content Detail's Rate modal bumped `size` 44→52.

**Reviews now show the reviewer's own rating next to the like button.** `getContentReviews`/`getFriendsReviews` (`backend/controllers/reviewController.js`) didn't join a rating before — only `getPopularReviews`/`getReviewsFromFriends` did, via a per-document `$lookup` (needed there since `contentId` varies per row across a global feed). Since these two functions always operate on one fixed `contentId`, a per-document lookup isn't needed — new `attachRatings(reviews, contentId)` helper does one bulk `Rating.find({contentId, user:{$in:userIds}})` and maps the result back onto each review. **Real bug caught during verification, not shipped blind**: the first version crashed with a 500 (`Cannot read properties of null`) against real data — a pre-existing orphaned review (its `user` populated to `null` because that account was since deleted) isn't something `.map(r => r.user._id)` can handle unconditionally; fixed by filtering those out before building `userIds` and short-circuiting `rating: null` for them. Verified with a throwaway account that both reviewed and rated the same movie (curled `GET /reviews/content/:id` → `rating:7` on that entry, `rating:null` on the orphaned one) and a second throwaway account following the first (curled `GET /reviews/content/:id/friends` → same `rating:7` came through), then fully cleaned up (review, rating, both accounts deleted). `Review` type (`mobile/src/types/index.ts`) gained `rating: number | null`; `ReviewCard.tsx` shows it via the exact same `{review.rating != null && <StarRatingDisplay .../>}` convention `ReviewFeedCard.tsx` already established, placed just left of the like button.

**Also this pass**: thin `hairlineWidth` dividers added above "Watched by Friends" and above "Reviews" (there was no visual separation from the button grid / friends box before). Overview text becomes tap-to-expand (`numberOfLines={5}` ↔ `undefined`, toggled by wrapping it in a `Pressable`); `topRow` gained explicit `alignItems:"flex-start"` (was implicit `"stretch"`) so the aspect-ratio-locked poster never tries to stretch to match a taller expanded overview — it stays its natural size and the row just grows, leaving empty space below the poster when the text is long, exactly as asked. Verified via `tsc --noEmit` (clean), the backend curls above, and a Metro bundle grep (`overviewExpanded`, `STAR_PATH`, `clipPath`, `scaleFraction`, `divider` — all present).

**Dev-stack lesson from this pass, worth remembering**: `mobile/scripts/start-codespace.sh`'s cleanup step (`pkill -f "nodemon server.js"`) only matches processes whose command line literally contains that string — a backend started some other way (e.g. a bare `node server.js` left running from an earlier ad-hoc verification session) survives the script's cleanup, keeps holding port 5000, and silently serves *stale* code while nodemon crashes with `EADDRINUSE` and sits waiting. First symptom was the new `rating` field being completely absent from a response (not even `null`) despite the source code clearly having it — always check `ps aux | grep "node server.js"` for more than one match before trusting a "it's not working" result against a Codespace backend.

**Third same-day refinement pass.** Two corrections to things the second pass got visually wrong, plus a real interaction fix.

**Active/"done" coloring now applies to all 6 action buttons, not just 2** — clarifies the earlier ask: the always-colored *border* base style stays exclusive to Watched List and Rate, but every button now flips to the same filled/colored look once its own action is taken, matching how Watched List already worked. `toggleButtonActive` widened from `{backgroundColor: colors.primary}` to also set `borderColor: colors.primary`, so the same style correctly overlays either base (a `toggleButton`'s already-colored border, or a `listButton`'s neutral one) — applied to Add to List (→ "Manage List", new i18n key, active once `inAnyList`), Add to Favorites, Watchlist, and Add/Edit Review, each switching icon/text color to `colors.primaryContent` when active. `inAnyList` needed `myLists` fetched eagerly on page load (`getMyLists()` folded into the main `Promise.all`) rather than lazily on modal-open, so the button shows the right state before the modal's ever been opened. Rate button's label format also fixed: was showing the raw `myRating` as `"★ 8/10"` (10-point scale); now `` `${(myRating/2).toFixed(1)} ★` `` — e.g. `"3.5 ★"`, matching the app's 5-star convention and the chart's own `"X.X/5"` formatting.

**Two real color mistakes from the second pass, corrected**: `mobile/src/theme/palettes.ts` empirically checked (`base100:#171212 > base200:#100e0e > base300:#0b0a0a` in brightness for the default `forest` theme — **higher number is darker**, opposite of the naive assumption made last round). The Review modal's textbox had been set to `base100`, which is actually *lighter* than the `base200` modal card it sits in — the exact opposite of "koyu olsun açık olmasın" (should be dark, not light). Fixed to `base300`. `ReviewComposer.tsx`'s Delete button text also changed from `colors.error` (red) to `colors.placeholder` (gray), as asked.

**All 5-star displays now show only the earned stars — no trailing gray ones.** `StarRatingDisplay.tsx` dropped its empty-star tail entirely: a 2.5 rating now renders as `★★ 1/2` and stops, instead of padding out to 5 slots with gray stars. Since this is the one shared component behind the chart's summary row, Watched by Friends, and `ReviewCard`, fixing it here fixed all three at once.

**Overview's collapsed height now reaches the poster's actual bottom edge instead of a hardcoded guess.** `numberOfLines={5}` never reliably matched the poster's real rendered height across screen sizes. Replaced with a measured approach: `onLayout` on the poster and on `titleRow` capture their heights into state; collapsed `numberOfLines` is computed as `Math.floor((posterHeight - titleRowHeight) / OVERVIEW_LINE_HEIGHT)`, falling back to unclamped until the first layout pass resolves (self-corrects within a frame). Tap-to-expand/collapse and `ellipsizeMode="tail"` are unchanged.

**`StarRatingInput.tsx` rebuilt again — this time the interaction model, not just the visuals.** The half-tap-misses/sluggish complaint traced to the five independent `Star` components each split into two half-width `Pressable`s with `hitSlop={4}` — at the boundary between a star's two halves (exactly where half-star precision matters most), each side's hitSlop extended 4px into its neighbor's territory, creating an ambiguous dead zone. Worse, independent per-half `onPress` handlers structurally can't support dragging a finger from star 5 onto star 3's left half and seeing it live-update — RN's touch responder keeps routing move/release events to whichever view captured the initial touch-down; sliding onto a sibling never re-targets the gesture. Replaced with a single `PanResponder` (RN built-in, no new dependency) spanning the whole row; each `Star` is now purely visual (the SVG rendering from the previous round, unchanged). The row computes a star+half value directly from `evt.nativeEvent.locationX`, tracked in local `liveValue` state for continuous visual feedback while dragging — the parent's `onChange` (which triggers a network save via `handleRate`) fires exactly once, on `onPanResponderRelease`, not on every move, or a single drag would fire dozens of redundant saves. `row`'s style changed from `justifyContent:"center"` (centers content *inside* a row stretched to the modal's full width — wrong coordinate space for the `locationX` math) to `alignSelf:"center"` (row shrink-wraps to exactly the 5-star content width and centers *itself*), which was necessary for the touch-position math to correspond 1:1 with star indices.

Verified via `tsc --noEmit` (clean) and a Metro bundle grep (`inAnyList`, `PanResponder`, `liveValue`, `"Manage List"`, `posterHeight`, `titleRowHeight`, `onPanResponderRelease` — all present).

**Fourth same-day refinement pass — two of these are real bugs, not polish.**

**Bug: the rating chart's count could balloon ("4'ten 20'lere çıkıyor").** `handleRate`'s success path, and the two deferred-save paths (`toggleWatchlist`'s add-branch, `handleOpenFavorites`), all did `setRatings((prev) => [...prev, value])` — an **unconditional append** on every successful save. The backend upserts (one `Rating` doc per user, no duplicates), but nothing stopped a user from re-saving their own rating several times in one visit (trivial now with the drag-based picker) while the client-side array just kept growing, since there was no matching "remove my old value first" step — each re-save double-counted the same person. Fixed by replacing all three append sites with a single `refreshRatings()` helper that re-fetches `getAllRatingsForContent(id)` and replaces the array outright — this can't drift from the server's true state no matter how many times a rating gets resaved, and it also naturally satisfies "the chart shouldn't update until the rating is actually saved to the watched list," since a rating that never got persisted (the watchlist gate returned early) was never in that authoritative response to begin with.

**Bug: the star picker "acted wrong" after changing your mind mid-session.** `StarRatingInput.tsx`'s `PanResponder` is constructed exactly once via `useRef(...).current` (recreating it every render risks interrupting an in-flight gesture) — but its handlers were closing over `onChange`/`disabled`/`size` directly from whichever render first built it. `ContentDetailScreen.tsx` passes `handleRate` as `onChange` without `useCallback`, so a *fresh* closure (over the current `myRating`/`inWatchlist`/`ratingSaved`) gets created every render — but the frozen `PanResponder` kept calling the *first* render's copy, evaluated against increasingly stale state. Every interaction after the very first was silently wrong. Fixed with the standard pattern for this class of bug: mirror `onChange`/`disabled`/`size` into a `useRef` object reassigned unconditionally every render, and have the handlers (and `computeValue`) read `stateRef.current` instead of closing over the props — the `PanResponder` object itself stays stable, only the values it reads become live. The underlying per-touch math was already correct and needed no change (it's purely positional, no dependency on any prior value) — the bug was entirely in what got called with that correct value.

**Also this pass**: Favorites button's star is now a fixed `colors.warning` (this app's amber/gold design-system token, already defined per-theme) in both states, instead of following the shared active-color swap — stars read as gold everywhere, the near-universal convention. Rate button's text grew (`fontSize` 18) and the star sits level with the number now — both share an explicit matching `lineHeight` plus `textAlignVertical:"center"` (RN's dedicated prop for this, Android-only, no-op on iOS), since a `★` glyph's font metrics don't center the same way as digits on the same line otherwise. The exact same fix applied to `StarRatingDisplay.tsx`'s `"1/2"` fraction label, which had the identical "sits a bit high" problem next to its star. "Watched by Friends"/"Reviews" section headers bumped `fontSize` 16→18.

Verified via `tsc --noEmit` (clean) and a Metro bundle grep (`refreshRatings`, `stateRef`, `rateText`, `colors.warning`, `textAlignVertical` — all present).

### New unified Search tab — replaces Movies + Series
The separate Movies and Series bottom tabs are gone — `app/(app)/movies/` and `app/(app)/series/` were deleted entirely (genuinely unreachable once untabbed) and replaced by one **Search** tab (`app/(app)/search/`, icon `search`/`search-outline`) with 5 internal sub-modes: Films / Series / Reviews / Lists / Users. Layout: one `SearchBar` (reused as-is, already self-debouncing 400ms — live-as-you-type with no Enter needed) at the top feeding a single **lifted** `query` string state in `search/index.tsx`, then a 5-tab underline bar below it (`films`/`series`/`reviews`/`lists`/`users`) — this is a deliberate deviation from Home's tab-bar pattern, where each tab body owns its own fully independent state: here all 5 tabs react to the *same* shared query, so switching tabs mid-search doesn't clear what you typed. Otherwise it's the exact same lazy-mount-once-then-`display:none` mechanics as `home/index.tsx`, just extended from 4 tabs to 5.

Films/Series (`src/components/search/SearchContentGrid.tsx`, parameterized by `contentType` like `ContentTypeSection.tsx`'s precedent) port the exact browse/search call the old tabs used (`getMovies`/`getSeries`, already defaulting to a popularity-sorted listing with no query) onto the dense 6-per-row grid `ListDetailScreen.tsx` established (`MiniContentCard` + `GRID_COLUMNS=6`/`GRID_GAP=4`/`GRID_PADDING=16` pixel math) instead of the old 2-column `ContentCard` layout — deliberately **no** `ContentFilterPanel` carried over, not asked for (it stays in use elsewhere, e.g. `messages/recommend.tsx`, so wasn't touched). Reviews (`SearchReviewsSection.tsx`) and Lists (`SearchListsSection.tsx`) reuse `ReviewFeedCard`/`DiscoverListCard` verbatim — same cards Home's Popular Reviews/Popular Lists already use — now also live-searchable (see backend section below). Users (`SearchUsersSection.tsx`) is genuinely new: a plain vertical avatar+username `FlatList`, since nothing else in the app has this exact shape.

**Real generalization required before reuse**: `ReviewFeedCard.tsx` and `DiscoverListCard.tsx` both **hardcoded** `router.push('/home/content/...')` — unlike `ContentCard`/`MiniContentCard`, they were never parameterized by which tab rendered them, because until now they'd only ever been used from Home. Both gained a required `basePath: "/home" | "/search"` prop (Home's own call sites in `ReviewsSection.tsx`/`ListsSection.tsx` updated to pass `basePath="/home"` explicitly, preserving existing behavior); `MiniContentCard`'s and `ListDetailScreen`'s existing `basePath` unions gained `"/search"`. Skipping this would have silently jumped users into Home's Stack on every tap from Search, breaking the back-navigation-returns-to-the-right-tab guarantee this whole architecture exists for.

**Backend: three new/extended search capabilities, all following the same portable regex `$match` style** (confirmed via direct code read that this codebase's *only* portable search precedent — as opposed to Movies' Atlas-Search-index-dependent `$search`, which doesn't exist for these collections — was `searchUsers`'s existing `{username:{$regex,$options:"i"}}`):
- **`searchUsers`** (`userController.js`) used to hard-400 on an empty query. Now: empty/missing `query` returns a random default sample (`$match{_id:{$ne:self}}` + `$sample`, not paginated — a fresh sample each call is the point) instead of erroring, so the Users tab has something to show before typing anything. Non-empty query behavior unchanged.
- **`GET /lists/popular`** (`customListRoute.js`) gained an optional `?q=` — regex-matches `CustomList.name`, inserted before the existing likeCount sort so search results stay popularity-ranked, not relevance-ranked.
- **`getPopularReviews`** (`reviewController.js`) gained an optional `?q=` for content-title search. Since `Review.contentId` points at a separate movies/series collection that can't be `$lookup`'d within this aggregation (same reasoning `attachRatings`/`getReviewsFromFriends` already established in this file), it follows their exact two-step bulk-map-join style instead: regex-match Movie/Series titles first to resolve matching IDs, then `$match:{contentId:{$in:ids}}` as the aggregation's first stage. Empty match set short-circuits to an empty result immediately, matching this file's existing empty-result convention.
- New shared `escapeRegex()` helper added to both `customListRoute.js` and `reviewController.js` (user text going into a `$regex` needs escaping first — an unescaped string lets a caller inject regex metacharacters, at best a crash, at worst ReDoS-shaped). Not retrofitted onto `searchUsers`'s pre-existing unescaped regex — out of scope for this pass, but not repeated in the new code.

Verified against real data (throwaway test account, cleaned up after): `/lists/popular` returns its normal popularity-sorted default with no `q`, empty array for a non-matching `q`, correct case-insensitive matches for a real list name. `getPopularReviews` verified the same three ways, plus confirmed `q`+`type` compose correctly (a real movie-only match returns nothing when `type=series` is also passed). `searchUsers` with no query returns `200` (not the old `400`) with a random sample that's genuinely different across repeated calls, non-empty-query search unchanged. Metro bundle grepped for the new components/route and confirmed `MoviesScreen`/`SeriesScreen` are completely gone from the bundle.

**Also required**: two hardcoded post-login redirects to `/movies` (`(auth)/_layout.tsx`, `setup-profile.tsx`'s `goToApp`) now point at `/home` instead, since `/movies` no longer exists.

**Same-day follow-up: no header on the Search index screen at all** — no title text, no `NotificationBell`, the search box is the very first thing on the page (`search/_layout.tsx`'s `index` route gets `headerShown: false`, unlike every other tab's index route in this app). Since removing the native header also removes the top safe-area inset it was providing, `search/index.tsx` now applies `useSafeAreaInsets().top` as the container's `paddingTop` directly (same hook/pattern `OfflineBanner.tsx`/`Toast.tsx` already use) so the search box doesn't sit under the status bar/notch.

**Second same-day follow-up: unreadable placeholder, filters brought back, titles + bigger cards.** Real bug: `SearchBar.tsx`'s `TextInput` never set `placeholderTextColor`, so the "Search" placeholder rendered in the OS default gray — unreadable against this app's dark theme. Fixed with `placeholderTextColor={colors.placeholder}` (the app's own token, already used everywhere else for exactly this). Fixes all 3 `SearchBar` call sites at once (Search, `messages/recommend.tsx`, `messages/new.tsx`), not just Search.

`ContentFilterPanel` — dropped when the old Movies/Series tabs were deleted — is back for the Films/Series tabs, reachable via a new optional `onFilterPress` prop on `SearchBar.tsx` (an `Ionicons "options-outline"` button at the bar's right end, only rendered when the prop is passed — the other 2 call sites don't pass it, so they're visually unaffected beyond the same placeholder fix). `search/index.tsx` owns one `showFilters` boolean toggled by that button, passed to both `SearchContentGrid` instances; each instance still owns its *own* independent year/genre/hasPoster state internally (movie and series genre sets differ) and renders `ContentFilterPanel` as its `FlatList`'s `ListHeaderComponent` when shown — same structure the original `movies/index.tsx`/`series/index.tsx` used, just relocated.

`MiniContentCard.tsx` gained an optional `title` prop (rendered only when passed — List Detail's existing poster-only usage is untouched, since it never passes one) — Search's Films/Series grid now passes it, and grew from 6 columns to 5 (bigger cards, still tight-gapped) to give the title line room. Both changes are local to `SearchContentGrid.tsx`'s own `GRID_COLUMNS`/render call; nothing shared with List Detail's identical-looking-but-separate grid constants changed.

**Third same-day follow-up: filter panel redesign + bigger cards again.** `ContentFilterPanel.tsx` (shared with `messages/recommend.tsx`, so this redesign lands there too) was one long vertically-wrapping column — Years chips wrapped across several rows, then Genres did the same below it, pushing the whole panel very tall. Rebuilt as two fixed-height (`BOX_HEIGHT=180`) scrollable boxes side by side (Years left, Genres right, chips still wrap *inside* each box, just vertically scrollable now instead of growing the panel), with "Has Poster?" centered below both (`alignSelf:"center"` on the segmented row, dropped the old `flex:1`-per-segment full-width stretch). `SearchContentGrid.tsx`'s `GRID_COLUMNS` went 5→4 (bigger cards again) and its page-size fetch 25→24 for a clean last row at 4 columns.

**Fourth same-day follow-up: the filter boxes weren't actually scrolling.** Real bug, not just a redesign ask: nesting a same-axis (vertical) `ScrollView` inside `ContentFilterPanel` — itself rendered as `SearchContentGrid`'s outer `FlatList`'s `ListHeaderComponent`, i.e. a scrollable-within-scrollable — needs `nestedScrollEnabled` on Android or the outer list's pan responder claims the drag first, leaving the inner box looking frozen on whatever fit in its fixed height. Added `nestedScrollEnabled` to both boxes. Content also switched from a wrapped multi-per-row chip grid to one chip per row (`boxContent` dropped `flexDirection:"row"`/`flexWrap`, each chip `alignSelf:"flex-start"`) and `BOX_HEIGHT` shrunk from 180 to 110 (~3 rows tall) — matches the actual ask: a short peek-height box you drag inside to reveal more, not a grid. Also: `MiniContentCard.tsx`'s new `title` text gained `textAlign:"center"` — it was already below the poster but left-aligned by RN's Text default, not centered under it.

**Fifth same-day follow-up: chips → divided rows sized to their own content, Has Poster removed entirely.** `ContentFilterPanel.tsx`'s Years/Genres rewritten again — no more pill chips wrapped in a grid, now plain rows (one per line, `borderBottomWidth` divider between each) inside the same short fixed-height (`BOX_HEIGHT=110`, ~3 rows) drag-to-reveal box. Column widths are no longer `flex:1` (half the panel each) — Years is a fixed `YEAR_BOX_WIDTH=64` (just fits "YYYY"), Genres is computed from the actual longest genre name in whichever set is active (`genreOptions.reduce` for max `name.length`, times a rough px/char estimate, clamped `[70,200]`) — movie and series genre sets differ, so this box is genuinely a different width per tab. "Has Poster?" removed outright, not just visually hidden — its state/prop plumbing pulled from `ContentFilterPanel.tsx`, `SearchContentGrid.tsx`, and `messages/recommend.tsx` (the other shared call site) alike, plus the now-fully-unused `"Has Poster?"` i18n key removed from all 12 locales. Deliberately **kept**: `contentService.ts`'s `ContentFilters.hasPoster` type field and the backend's `?hasPoster=` query param support on `GET /movies`/`GET /series` — that's still a working, harmless, reusable capability at the data layer; only the UI control (and the state that only ever existed to feed it) was genuinely dead once removed, not the underlying feature.

**Sixth same-day follow-up: visual polish pass, dynamic kept as-is.** User liked the drag-to-reveal box interaction but not how it looked — an open-ended "make it look nice" ask, no specific direction given. Redesigned as small elevated "cards" (`shadowOpacity`/`elevation`, `borderRadius:14`, no border) instead of flat bordered boxes; `BOX_HEIGHT` bumped 110→132 — tall enough for 3 full rows *plus a visible sliver of a 4th*, a deliberate scroll affordance (you can see there's more without any hint icon/text) rather than an exact 3-row cutoff. Row text centered; selected state changed from a plain color swap to a small rounded primary-color pill around just the text (`badge`/`badgeText`), closer to this app's established "selected chip" look without literally being the wrapped chip-grid that was removed for looking too busy. Row dividers are now separate inset `View`s between items (`marginHorizontal:14`, not drawn after the last row) instead of a `borderBottomWidth` on every row — avoids a redundant line right at the box's bottom edge. "Years"/"Genres" labels restyled as small uppercase muted section headers (`textTransform:"uppercase"`, `letterSpacing`, `colors.placeholder`), centered above each box. `YEAR_BOX_WIDTH` widened 64→92 and the genre-box padding constant increased to comfortably fit the new pill badge's own padding around the widest genre name, not just the bare text.

**Seventh same-day follow-up: real bug — tapping a filter chip reloaded the whole page.** `SearchContentGrid.tsx`'s `if (loading) return <SkeletonGrid/>` fired on *every* `loading` transition, not just the first one — since toggling any year/genre changes `loadPage`'s identity, triggering the same `setLoading(true)` → refetch → `setLoading(false)` cycle as the initial mount, which unmounted the entire `FlatList` (filter panel included) into a full-page skeleton and back, on every single tap. Fixed by adding `hasLoadedOnce` (set once, after the first load ever completes): the full skeleton now only gates the true first load (`loading && !hasLoadedOnce`); every subsequent reload keeps the `FlatList` — filter panel, scroll position, and the previous cards — mounted and visible, with just a small `ActivityIndicator` in the header below the panel while the new page fetches. `items` was already only replaced once a fetch resolves (never pre-emptively cleared), so cards now swap in place instead of the whole screen flashing away and back.

**Eighth same-day follow-up: filter icon only on Films/Series.** `search/index.tsx` now only passes `SearchBar`'s `onFilterPress` when `mainTab` is `"films"` or `"series"` — `undefined` otherwise, which `SearchBar.tsx` already treats as "don't render the icon" (no change needed there). Reviews/Lists/Users have no filters, so the icon disappears on those tabs instead of sitting there doing nothing.

### Much later round: Search redesigned into an actual search (not browse), row-based results, post-style Lists/Reviews cards, and a real filter sheet on all four content tabs

Direct ask, after this same session's Sync tier-leveling work: Movies/Series/Lists/Reviews all showed a full popularity-sorted browse list *before* any input at all — genuinely a "browse" screen wearing a search bar, not a search. Also asked for: Movies/Series results as rows (poster+title+year) instead of a dense poster grid; Lists/Reviews cards redesigned to match the Media feed's own post design (`ShareCard.tsx`), with the author's profile and like/view counts folded into the box (a feed post keeps those in its own outer header/footer, which doesn't exist on a bare search result); tapping a review opening the same kind of in-place modal `ShareCard` already uses for a long review, instead of navigating away; and the old boxed-column `ContentFilterPanel` (Movies/Series only — Lists/Reviews had no filters at all) redesigned into something matching the app's current, more professional visual bar, with a recommendation asked for and given before implementing.

**Empty-until-you-search, all four content tabs.** Each of `SearchContentRows.tsx` (new, replaces the deleted `SearchContentGrid.tsx`), `SearchListsSection.tsx`, and `SearchReviewsSection.tsx` now gates its own fetch on `hasSearchCriteria` — a typed query OR an active filter (a filter alone, with no typed text, is treated as a legitimate way to browse, e.g. "just 2020s Comedy"). With neither, each tab shows a large icon + short info line (`t("Search any movie you want to find it.")` etc.) instead of fetching anything.

**Movies/Series: row layout replaces the 4-column grid.** New `SearchContentRow.tsx` — poster (52×78) + title + release year (sliced from `release_date`/`first_air_date`, already on hand, no backend change needed) in one row, hairline `ItemSeparatorComponent` between. `MiniContentCard.tsx` itself untouched — still used by `ListDetailScreen.tsx`'s own 6-column grid, which wasn't asked to change.

**Lists/Reviews: new post-style cards, not a reuse of `ShareCard.tsx`.** Following this codebase's own established precedent (`DiscoverListCard.tsx` already copies `ShareCard`'s film-strip geometry verbatim rather than sharing the component, since `ShareCard` consumes a `Share` object — a different shape from these search endpoints' `DiscoverListItem`/`PopularReview`) — new `SearchListCard.tsx` and `SearchReviewCard.tsx`, matching `ShareCard`'s own list/review box *order* (list: name → description → film strip → item count; review: poster left, title+rating+quoted-italic-excerpt right) with the author's `UserAvatar` + username added at the top of the box and like/view counts (icon + number, read-only — display, not an interactive like button, per what was actually asked) added at the bottom. Neither `DiscoverListCard.tsx` nor `ReviewFeedCard.tsx` (both also used elsewhere — Home's Popular Lists/Reviews, Content Detail's Lists tab) were touched. `SearchReviewCard.tsx` opens the same kind of in-place `Modal` `ShareCard.tsx` already uses (poster, reviewer row, scrollable full quote) on tapping a truncated (`numberOfLines={3}`) review — a third instance of this same pattern in the codebase (`ShareCard.tsx`, `ReviewSwipeCard.tsx`, now this), all independently implemented rather than sharing one component, consistent with the existing precedent rather than a new one being invented here.

**Real backend additions — Lists/Reviews had no filter criteria at all before this.** `getPopularLists` (`backend/routes/customListRoute.js`) gained a `sort` param (`liked` — the existing default popularity formula, unchanged — `items`, `newest`); `getPopularReviews` (`backend/controllers/reviewController.js`) gained `sort` (`liked` default, `newest`, `rating`) and `minRating`/`maxRating`. The reviews aggregation needed real restructuring, not just an added `$match`: its own rating value used to be joined *after* the `$sort`/`$limit` stage (fine when the only sort was by like count, which needs no join at all) — filtering or sorting by rating needs that value before the final sort, so the `ratings` lookup (and the `users` lookup it depends on) moved earlier, ahead of an optional rating-range `$match` and the now-parameterized `$sort`. Live-verified all three (`sort=rating` returns rating-10 reviews first, `minRating=8` correctly excludes lower ones, `type=series&sort=newest` still combines correctly with the pre-existing type filter) via the JWT-minting convention.

**New filter UI: a bottom sheet, not an inline panel.** New `FilterBottomSheet.tsx` — a shared shell (slide-up `Modal`, dimmed backdrop, grabber, title, Clear All / Done footer) — recommended over sticking with `ContentFilterPanel`'s always-visible boxed-column layout because a slide-up sheet is the standard modern pattern for this (Letterboxd/Spotify-style) and doesn't permanently push search results down the way an inline panel does; filters still apply live (unchanged interaction model, "Done" only closes the sheet) rather than introducing a separate staged-then-committed state, to keep the change scoped to the visual chrome as asked. Movies/Series' own content (`ContentFilterSheetContent.tsx`) replaces the old boxed year/genre scroll-lists with wrapping pill chips — genres as before, years as the most recent 12 individually plus whole-decade chips for anything older (tapping a decade toggles all its years at once; still sent to the server as the same flat year-string array, no backend change needed there). Lists/Reviews get their own new content (a shared `SortOptionsList.tsx` radio-row list, Reviews additionally getting a rating-range chip row) inside the same shell. `ContentFilterPanel.tsx` itself was left untouched — still used by `socials/messages/recommend.tsx`, out of this round's scope.

**Search bar itself**: gained a leading magnifying-glass icon (universal across all 3 existing call sites — Search, and the two `recommend.tsx`/`new.tsx` message-composer usages — a safe, positive change everywhere it appears) and the filter trigger button now fills with `colors.primary` (icon switching to `primaryContent`) whenever the active tab actually has a filter applied — each of the four sections reports its own `hasActiveFilters` up via a lightweight per-tab callback map in `search/index.tsx` (the filter *values* themselves stay owned by each section, not lifted — too different a shape per tab: years+genres vs. sort vs. rating range+sort — to be worth a shared state model).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `node --check` on both touched backend files; live JWT-minted requests confirming the new sort/rating-range params on both endpoints; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirming every new component compiled in and the deleted `SearchContentGrid.tsx` is fully gone from the bundle.

**Immediate follow-up, same round: the Users tab was missed the first pass.** `SearchUsersSection.tsx` had the same "browses before you search" issue (empty query defaulted to a random `$sample` of users) — now gated on `hasQuery` the same way, empty info state (`t("Search any username you want to find them.")`) until a name is actually typed. No filter added here — genuinely considered and decided against: unlike genre/year or rating/sort, a bare username+avatar+tier result has no rich-enough signal to filter by that would actually be useful, and "find this specific person by name" doesn't naturally want narrowing the way the other four tabs' browsing does. The backend's own `$sample` empty-query branch (`GET /users/search`) was left in place rather than removed — every current mobile call site already guards against calling it with an empty query (the other two callers, `messages/new.tsx` and `UserSharePickerModal.tsx`, already did before this round), but it's a reasonable server-side fallback to keep rather than a literal dead code path worth deleting.

### New unified Socials tab — replaces Messages + Community
Same merge pattern as Search (Movies+Series → one tab): the separate Messages and Community bottom tabs are gone — `app/(app)/messages/` and `app/(app)/community/` were deleted entirely and replaced by one **Socials** tab (`app/(app)/socials/`, icon `people`/`people-outline`, carries the combined DM+group `tabBarBadge` that used to live on Messages). `socials/index.tsx` renders a Messages/Communities underline tab bar (default Messages) using the same lazy-mount-once-then-`display:none` mechanics as Search/Home, with each sub-tab's body extracted into its own component: `src/components/socials/MessagesSection.tsx` (moved verbatim from the old `messages/index.tsx`) and `src/components/socials/CommunitiesSection.tsx` (moved from `community/index.tsx`, plus a new addition — see below).

~~**Dynamic header**: Messages' header (gift + new-message icons + `NotificationBell`) and Communities' header (bell only) genuinely differ, so `socials/index.tsx` used `useNavigation()` + `useEffect(() => navigation.setOptions({headerRight: ...}), [mainTab])` to swap the header reactively.~~ **Superseded the same day** — see the follow-up paragraph below: the gift/new-message icons moved out of the header entirely, so the header is static again (`socials/_layout.tsx`'s `index` screen just sets `headerRight: () => <NotificationBell />`, same convention every other tab uses).

**Routing collision avoided via static namespace prefixing**: once merged under one tab, `[conversationId].tsx` and `[slug].tsx` can't sit as flat dynamic siblings — Expo Router can't disambiguate two differently-named dynamic segments at the same level. Fixed the same way `home/lists/[id].tsx`/`search/lists/[id].tsx` already do it: nested under `socials/messages/[conversationId].tsx` and `socials/communities/[slug].tsx`. `socials/content/[type]/[id].tsx` is the usual thin re-export of `ContentDetailScreen`, shared by both sub-tabs.

**New addition: a "joined communities" view, zero backend work needed.** `getAllGroups()` already returns every group with a per-item `isMember` flag computed server-side (`groupController.js`), so `CommunitiesSection.tsx` fetches once (not per sub-view — All and Mine are two filtered views of the same array, keeping optimistic join/leave updates reflected in both for free) and adds a second, inner underline tab bar directly below the existing category chip row: **All** (default, unchanged existing browse-all behavior) | **Mine** (`groups.filter(g => g.isMember)`, composed with the existing category filter). "Mine" was a deliberate i18n choice, not the user's own rough suggestion ("member of community") — the obvious reuse candidate, the existing `"Joined"` key, was already used elsewhere in this exact file's member-list cells for "member joined [date]" text, and several locales' existing translations for it (Japanese "参加日", Korean "가입일") are literal join-*date* compounds that would've read as broken/incomplete reused standalone as a tab label — caught by checking existing translations before reusing a string-identical key, not just the English text.

**Cross-cutting call sites fixed** (outside the moved folders, found by grepping the whole app for `/messages/` and `/community/` string literals): `app/notifications.tsx`'s `message`-notification tap target, and `src/components/RecommendationMessageCard.tsx`'s tap-to-Content-Detail target (this one is genuinely live — rendered by `ChatRoom.tsx` for `recommendation`-type messages in both DM and group rooms — an initial research pass had assumed it was dead by only checking `recommend.tsx`'s send flow, which indeed never navigates there; the receive/view flow in `ChatRoom.tsx` does).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after all the file moves (each shifted one level deeper, so every relative import gained an extra `../`). Metro bundle grepped for the new route registrations (`app/(app)/socials/index.tsx`, `socials/messages/[conversationId].tsx`, `socials/messages/new.tsx`, `socials/messages/recommend.tsx`, `socials/communities/[slug].tsx`, `socials/content/[type]/[id].tsx`) and confirmed both `MessagesScreen`/`CommunityScreen` (old component names) and any lingering `/messages/content` or bare `/community/` string literals are completely gone from the bundle.

**First on-device test found two real, pre-existing bugs unrelated to this merge, both fixed in passing.** (1) `ChatContext.tsx`'s socket forced `transports: ["websocket"]` — through this Codespace's dev tunnel, a raw WebSocket-only connection failed outright (`connect_error: websocket error`), and the handler's `err.message` access on a malformed error object threw, crashing the whole app (uncaught, since `ChatProvider` wraps the entire tree with no boundary below it). Removed the forced transport (socket.io now negotiates polling→upgrade like everywhere else it's used) and made the handler read `err?.message`. (2) Home's Popular This Week/Popular with Friends cards could show the *same* adder avatar twice — `getPopularAdds()` (`feedController.js`) merges `adderIds` from two separate aggregations (`watchlist` and `toWatchList`), and a user can have the same title in both lists at once, so a naive concatenation could put their id in `topAdders` twice, tripping a React duplicate-key warning in `StackedAvatars`. Fixed by deduping `adderIds` (via a `Map` keyed by the stringified id) before slicing to the top 3. Neither bug came from the Socials merge itself — both were just never exercised together (a real device, over this specific tunnel, hitting a title in both lists) until this was the first on-device test of the session.

**Also found, separately from app code**: this Codespace's port 5000 (the backend, `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`/`EXPO_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL`) had silently reverted to `private` visibility — `mobile/scripts/start-codespace.sh`'s `gh codespace ports visibility 5000:public || true` call was failing without surfacing an error (the `|| true` swallows it). A private port serves an auth redirect/401 instead of JSON to an unauthenticated device, which crashed `ContentTypeSection.tsx`'s render (`feedItems.length` on a response that was never actually the expected `{items,...}` shape). Not a code bug — re-running `gh codespace ports visibility 5000:public` fixed it — but worth checking first if `.length of undefined` errors reappear after a fresh `start-codespace.sh` run right after this session.

**Same-day follow-up: header icons moved into the tab, recommend picker gained a Community tab, recommend screen redesigned.** Three follow-up requests, all in `socials/`/`messages/recommend.tsx`/`UserSharePickerModal.tsx`:
1. **Gift/new-message icons out of the header, into `MessagesSection.tsx`** — a small `actionRow` (two right-aligned `Ionicons` buttons, bordered bottom like a mini toolbar) now sits above the inbox `FlatList` (and above the loading skeleton too, so it's always visible). Since the header no longer needs to vary by sub-tab, `socials/index.tsx`'s entire dynamic-header `useEffect`/`MessagesHeaderRight` was removed — `socials/_layout.tsx`'s `index` screen just sets a static `headerRight: () => <NotificationBell />` now, the same convention every other tab's `_layout.tsx` already uses (see the struck-through paragraph above).
2. **`UserSharePickerModal.tsx` gained an optional `allowGroups` prop** (only `messages/recommend.tsx` passes it — `ProfileAnalysisModal.tsx` doesn't, since `analysis_share` messages aren't supported for group rooms on the backend, only `recommendation` is). When set, the modal shows a Users/Community underline tab bar above the search box. Users tab is the original following∪followers-default + live-all-user-search behavior, now with a "Network" section label above the default (non-searching) list. Community tab lists only **joined** groups (`getAllGroups().filter(g => g.isMember)`, fetched once when the modal opens) — its search box (placeholder "Search community...") filters that already-joined list client-side by name, deliberately **not** a live server search against all communities, since the whole point is "you can only message communities you're already in." `onConfirm` signature widened from `(userIds) => void` to `(userIds, groupIds) => void`; `ProfileAnalysisModal.tsx` needed no code change since a function with fewer declared params is structurally assignable where more are expected (its `groupIds` argument is simply never passed since `allowGroups` is unset there, so `selectedGroups` stays empty).
3. **Recommendation sends now reach groups too**: new `sendGroupRichMessage()` (`groupService.ts`) — confirmed via direct backend read that `sendGroupMessage` (`groupController.js`) already handles `type:"recommendation"` with `contentType`/`contentId`/`contentData` identically to the DM controller (only `analysis_share` is DM-only), so this needed zero backend changes, just the missing mobile-side call. `recommend.tsx`'s `handleConfirmRecipients` now takes `(userIds, groupIds)` and fires both kinds of sends in one `Promise.all`.
4. **Recommend screen redesign, cosmetic-only, no logic change**: the Movies/Series boxed radio buttons became the same underline tab bar used everywhere else (Search, Socials' own Messages/Communities bar); the separate "⚙️ Filters" button row was removed in favor of `SearchBar`'s existing `onFilterPress` icon slot (the same mechanism Search's Films/Series tabs already use) — one less bespoke control, one more reuse of an established pattern.

2 new i18n keys (`"Search community..."`, `"Network"`) across all 12 locales; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `sendGroupRichMessage`, `allowGroups`, `"Search community"` (all present) and the old `MessagesHeaderRight` symbol (confirmed gone).

**Second same-day follow-up: real backend bug (group sends invisible in the inbox), recommendation card redesign, and two layout fixes.**
1. **Real bug: sending a recommendation to a group never updated that group's inbox row** — DMs worked (moved to the top, showed the new preview), groups silently didn't. Root cause, found by comparing `conversationController.js`'s REST `sendMessage` against `groupController.js`'s REST `sendGroupMessage`: the DM REST handler always denormalized `lastMessage`/`lastMessageAt`/`unreadCounts` onto the `Conversation` document after creating the `Message`, but the group REST handler never did the equivalent onto `Group` — that logic only existed in the **socket** `send-message` handler's group branch (`sockets/chatSocket.js`), which the REST route (used for one-off sends like this and for a disconnected socket) never went through. Fixed by porting that exact same denormalize-and-notify block (`Group.findByIdAndUpdate` with `lastMessage`/`lastMessageAt`/`lastMessageSenderId`/per-member `unreadCounts` increment, plus `conversation-updated` socket emits to every member) into `sendGroupMessage`, mirroring `chatSocket.js` line-for-line rather than reinventing it.
2. **`RecommendationMessageCard.tsx` redesigned** — previously a small horizontal row (44×64 thumbnail + title + year) with the message's own sentence (`"{{user}} recommends {{title}} to you"`, generated in `recommend.tsx`) never actually rendered anywhere, so the card alone didn't read as a recommendation at all. Now a single vertical card: a real poster (`w342` TMDB size, not `w154`, fills the card's `180`-wide top edge at a `2/3` aspect ratio) with the message text below it in a padded footer — colored to match the surrounding chat bubble's own/other convention (`colors.primary`/`primaryContent` vs `colors.base200`/`baseContent`, same bottom-corner-radius convention every other bubble type uses), via a new required `isOwn` prop passed from `ChatRoom.tsx`. Tap-to-Content-Detail behavior unchanged (was already wired correctly).
3. **`MessagesSection.tsx`'s icon row** gained a left-aligned `"Network"` label (`justifyContent` changed `flex-end`→`space-between`) so the row reads as a labeled section header instead of two icons floating in empty space.
4. **`CommunitiesSection.tsx`'s two stacked control bars merged into one row**: the All/Mine switch was previously a full-width underline tab bar identical in weight/style to the outer Messages/Communities bar directly above it — two heavy stacked bars read as cluttered, and with no top padding on the grid below, the first `GroupCard` row visually crowded right up against the category chips. Redesigned as a single row: All/Mine is now a compact rounded segmented control (`colors.base200` pill, active segment filled `colors.primary`) fixed to the left, a thin vertical divider, then the category chips continuing to scroll in the remaining space — one line of controls instead of two, plus `paddingTop:12` added to the grid for breathing room.

No new i18n keys needed (reused `"Network"`, `"All"`, `"Mine"`, category names — all already added in earlier passes). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; backend nodemon restarted cleanly; Metro bundle grepped for `CARD_WIDTH` (new card), `segmentButtonActive` (new segmented control), `actionRowTitle` (new label) — all present.

### CineGraph redesign: decluttered genre list + tap-through genre detail screen

User-approved via an interactive HTML mockup (published as an artifact, phone-frame prototype using the app's real `forest` theme tokens and `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s actual 8-color slice palette) before any code was written — the mockup let the user click through the real proposed interaction (sorted/capped legend → tap a genre → detail screen) rather than evaluate static screenshots or prose.

**Problem**: the genre legend below the donut was unsorted (`Object.entries()` insertion order) and uncapped — a heavy watcher with 10-15+ genres got that many full-width rows with zero hierarchy. Tapping a genre (slice or legend row) only toggled a local "selected" highlight, no navigation existed.

**Real finding that shaped the implementation, not assumed**: `User.movieCineGraph`/`seriesCineGraph` (`backend/models/User.js`) already store a per-genre `avgRating`, which looked like a free, cheap source for a new "average rating per genre" feature — but a dedicated research pass found this Map has **confirmed, real correctness bugs**. Three independent code paths rebuild it inconsistently: TV Time import and Letterboxd import (`userController.js`'s `rebuildUserCineGraph`) both wipe the Map and rebuild from `Rating` documents alone, dropping the `ratedCount` field entirely and repurposing `count` to mean "rated items" instead of "watchlist items" — permanently corrupting the schema's `{count, ratedCount, avgRating}` contract for any user who's ever imported; the activity-log revert flow (`logController.js`'s `recalculateUserCineGraph`) has the identical bug pattern independently. This Map is **not dead data** — it's a live input to the CineMatch scoring algorithm (`matchController.js`'s `computeMatchBreakdown`) and `getRecommendations`, so the drift is already silently skewing match percentages for import users today. **Fixing that bug is out of scope for this task** (flagged to the user as a separate, real, pre-existing issue worth a future pass) — the new CineGraph features instead recompute `avgRating` fresh at read time by joining `Rating` against `Movie`/`Series.genre_ids` (the same join shape `getUserCineGraph` already does for counts), never reading the buggy Map.

**Backend, additive only**: confirmed `frontend/src/pages/ProfilePage.jsx`/`PublicProfilePage.jsx`/`MatchPage.jsx` (web) all call this same `GET /users/cinegraph-data/:id` endpoint, so `getUserCineGraph` (`userController.js`) gained two new *sibling* fields — `movieGenreRatings`/`seriesGenreRatings: Record<string, number|null>` — rather than restructuring the existing `movieStats`/`seriesStats`, so web is unaffected. Computed via one extra batch `Rating.find()` (note: `Rating.contentId` is a plain String, not an ObjectId ref — coerced before matching) joined against the same per-genre tallying loop the endpoint already runs, raw 1-10 scale (matches `Rating.value`'s own scale; the `/2` to a 0.5-5 star display happens client-side, same as `StarRatingDisplay.tsx` already does for every other rating shown in this app). New `GET /users/:id/genre-detail?type=movie|series&genre=<name>` endpoint (query params, not path segments — so series genre names containing `&`, e.g. "Action & Adventure", don't need special path-segment handling) returns every watched item in that genre with the user's own rating per item (sorted rating-descending, unrated last) plus the genre's average — reuses `isAuthorizedToView` for the same private-account masking `getUserCineGraph` already has.

Verified against real data: a throwaway test account seeded with a watchlist spanning 11 genres and a mix of rated/unrated items, hand-verified two genres' averages by arithmetic against the raw ratings (e.g. Comedy: `(7+9+10)/3 = 8.7`, matched exactly), confirmed `null` avgRating for fully-unrated genres, confirmed the `&`-containing series genre query round-trips correctly through `encodeURIComponent`, confirmed 400s on invalid `type`/unknown `genre`. Cleaned up after.

~~**`CineGraphDonut.tsx` rebuilt**: entries sorted by count descending, legend capped to top 5 with a "Show N more genres" expand toggle, each row a rating chip + chevron, tapping a slice or row navigating directly via a new `onGenrePress(genre)` callback.~~ **Superseded same day by a second design pass — see below.** The list-based legend (even sorted and capped) was replaced entirely by a leader-line layout after the user saw the v1 mockup and asked for something more dynamic.

**Same-day v2 redesign: leader-line labels + tap-to-open callout, no list at all.** Second mockup round on the same published artifact (redeployed to the same URL, not a new one) — a phone-frame prototype demonstrating the exact interaction (elbowed connector lines radiating off the ring, tap opens an animated callout, neighbors slide apart) before any React Native code was written; approved with one refinement request (the tapped connector/dot turns white while its callout is open, reverting to gray on close).

`CineGraphDonut.tsx` rebuilt a second time, fully replacing the legend concept:
- **Every genre gets a permanent leader line off the ring** — no cap, no "show more" (the whole point of this pass was to replace capping with a layout that scales to many genres without hiding any). Each connector is a 3-segment orthogonal path (`M ring-point → L elbow-out → L elbow-vertical → L label-column`, mirrored left/right depending on which half of the circle the slice's midpoint angle falls in) ending in a small dot, with the genre name past it — connector, dot, and label all render in a neutral gray (`colors.placeholder`) so only the ring itself carries per-genre color meaning.
- **Guaranteed-unique colors regardless of genre count**: the old fixed 8-color array (which repeated past 8 genres) was replaced by `genreColor(index, total)` — an evenly-spaced HSL hue sweep (`hue = 360/total * index`) that never repeats a hue for any `total`, not just up to 8.
- **Label rows are pre-spread evenly** along the left/right edge in angular order (so connector lines never cross), computed once per render pass. Tapping a slice or its label doesn't navigate anymore — it opens a small callout **anchored at that label's position**, showing count·percentage and average rating, with a `Detail` button inside as the only thing that actually navigates (`onDetailPress(genre)`, replacing the old direct-navigate `onGenrePress`). Opening a callout pushes the rows immediately above/below it apart (`ROW_GAP_OPEN`) to make room, and they settle back when it closes.
- **Animation, built without a new dependency**: this codebase's existing precedent for custom animation is the plain React Native core `Animated` API (`SwipeCardStack.tsx`'s `PanResponder`-driven cards) — no `react-native-reanimated` anywhere in the project — so the leader-line/label motion follows that same convention rather than adding a new native module. Since the moving part is an SVG `Path`'s endpoint coordinates (not a transform/opacity Animated natively interpolates), the layout uses one shared `Animated.Value` progress driven by `Animated.timing`, with a listener that forces a re-render each frame; the current interpolated Y per genre is computed inline from stored from/to values — the same "gesture/time-driven value feeds a fresh SVG render" idiom `StarRatingInput.tsx`'s `PanResponder` already established in this codebase, just time-driven here instead of touch-driven. The callout's own mount/dismiss animation (opacity + scale) **is** a plain native-driver `Animated.spring`, since those two props are natively interpolatable.
- Donut itself grew (`outerRadius` scales off `useWindowDimensions()` instead of a fixed 160px) and sits alone per content type instead of two stacked side by side.

**`ProfileCinegraphsTab.tsx` gained a Movies/Series underline sub-tab bar** (same style used throughout the app), default Movies — replacing the previous "both donuts stacked vertically" layout, since only one donut renders at a time now this also gives each graph the full width for its leader lines.

1 new i18n key (`"Detail"`) across all 12 locales for the callout's button (`"Watched"`/`"Average Rating"` still reused from the v1 pass; `"Show {{count}} more genres"`/`"Show less"`/`"Unrated"` are now unused dead keys left in place, matching this codebase's general tolerance for a handful of orphaned i18n strings over the cost of a 12-locale removal pass for a same-day superseded feature). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `genreColor`, `onDetailPress`, `ROW_GAP_OPEN` — all present.

**Same-day v3: on-device testing of v2 found one real rendering bug and several sizing/polish requests.** All in `CineGraphDonut.tsx`.
- **Real bug: genre labels rendered in the platform-default text color (effectively black), not gray.** `styles.label` (which carried `color: colors.placeholder`) was applied to the label's outer `Pressable` — a `View`, which doesn't propagate a `color` style down into its child `Text` the way nesting inside another `Text` would. The inner `<Text>` itself never received a color style in its non-open state, so it fell through to RN's own default. Fixed by applying color directly to the `Text`, and unified it with the connector line/dot color via one shared `const color = isOpen ? colors.baseContent : colors.placeholder` per item — label, line, and dot now always match exactly, both when idle (gray) and when a genre's callout is open (**new**: turns white — the one addition to the previously-approved v2 mockup, requested this round).
- **Real bug: connector lines could visually cross back over the ring.** The first segment's turn point was previously offset from each slice's *own* point (`p0.x ± ELBOW_OUT`) — clears that specific point's radius, but for any slice not exactly at the 3/6/9/12 o'clock position, the *next* (spread-axis) segment at that x/y could still cross back through the ring's wider footprint. Fixed by pinning the first turn to a fixed clearing line per side (`centerX ± (outerRadius + RING_GAP)` for left/right, `centerY ∓ (outerRadius + RING_GAP)` for top/bottom) instead of an offset from the individual point — geometrically guarantees the line never re-enters the ring, confirmed by the same distance-from-center inequality that makes the fix work for every angle, not just the ones near the axis.
- **Graph enlarged and centered**: `outerRadius` was a small fixed fraction of the box width; recomputed from the box's actual geometry (`centerX - SIDE_MARGIN - RING_GAP - 10`), which — combined with the new top/bottom routing below freeing up the side columns — lets the ring grow considerably larger while everything else still fits.
- **"Watched Movie/Series Genres" heading removed** — redundant now that the new Movies/Series sub-tab bar (v2) already states which graph is showing; `CineGraphDonut` no longer takes a `title` prop at all.
- **New: long genre names route to a top or bottom row instead of a side column.** Purely side-based routing (left/right only) meant a graph any bigger would either need very wide side margins (eating into the ring) or clip long names like "Science Fiction"/"Action & Adventure". Names over 8 characters now route to a top or bottom connector instead — vertical-first-turn, horizontal spread, vertical-final-turn (the same 3-segment orthogonal idea as the side connectors, just transposed to the other axis), spread evenly along the box's width rather than its height. Short names (most common single-word genres) still use the side columns. The row/column "push apart around the open callout" logic (`assignPositions`) was generalized to work identically on either axis, so this didn't need a second implementation.

No new i18n keys this pass. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `RING_GAP`, `NAME_LEN_THRESHOLD`, `anchorFor` — all present.

**Same-day v4: the leader-line connectors were abandoned entirely** ("çizgi işi olmuyor" — the line thing isn't working) **for a plain list-beside-graph layout with expanding accordion rows.** `CineGraphDonut.tsx` rewritten a third time, this one structurally much simpler and with no SVG-path geometry to get wrong: a two-column row — genre names stacked vertically on the left (each with a small color-matched dot), the donut on the right, no connector lines/labels-on-the-graph at all anymore.
