Tapping a genre row **or** its donut slice selects it: the dot disappears, and the row itself grows into a bordered card (`borderColor` = that genre's own slice color) containing count·percentage, average rating, and the `Detail` button that navigates — this is the same callout content from v2/v3 the user explicitly liked, just **inlined into the list row instead of floating** so the colored border naturally wraps the genre name and its stats together as one visual unit (no separate "connect the two" logic needed — they're literally one `Pressable` container, the stats block just conditionally renders inside it when selected). The row's height growing to reveal that content **is** the "bigger than its siblings" effect asked for, and animates via `LayoutAnimation.configureNext()` (React Native's core layout-transition API — new to this codebase, no existing precedent, but zero extra dependency; Android needs `UIManager.setLayoutAnimationEnabledExperimental(true)`, called once at module load, guarded since newer/Fabric-based RN doesn't always expose or need it). The selected donut slice also gets a subtle pop (slightly thicker stroke, siblings dimmed to 40% opacity) — carried over from the very first (pre-leader-line) version of this component, never actually rejected, just superseded along the way.

This design sidesteps every geometry problem the two leader-line attempts had (label color, ring overlap, sizing/centering, long-name clipping) by construction — there's no path math left to get wrong, positioning is plain flexbox. No new i18n keys. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `genreRowSelected`, `LayoutAnimation.configureNext` — both present.

**Same-day v4 sizing follow-up.** v4's initial layout gave the genre list `flex:1` (fill remaining space) and the donut a small fixed 150px column — backwards from what was wanted: the list should take only the width its content needs, and the donut should fill everything after it, as large as that leaves room for. Fixed by flipping the flex roles — `listCol` is now a fixed `152`px column (sized to comfortably fit both a collapsed row and an expanded card's stat lines without the column itself changing width when a genre is selected, which would otherwise jostle the donut's size on every tap), `donutCol` is `flex:1` and **measures its own actual rendered width via `onLayout`** rather than guessing — the donut's diameter is derived directly from that measurement (`donutColWidth - 8`, clamped `[170, 280]`), so it's provably "as big as the remaining space allows," not a hardcoded guess. This is also what makes the donut genuinely start right where the genre names end and reach the page's right edge, per the ask.

**The "move the graph out of the way when a callout expands" ask turned out to already be provided by ordinary flex layout, no custom collision code needed**: the outer row uses `alignItems:"center"`, so the donut is always vertically centered against the list's *current total height* — when a row expands (adding height above or below the donut's natural center), that center recalculates and the donut visibly shifts, and since this recalculation happens inside the same `LayoutAnimation.configureNext()` transaction as the row's own expand/collapse, the donut's shift animates too, not just the row. This is a general property of `alignItems:"center"` + `LayoutAnimation`, not a specific "does this box overlap that box" check — simpler and it degrades gracefully (any content-height change repositions the donut sensibly, not just the one case that was asked about).

Also removed a one-line Android `UIManager.setLayoutAnimationEnabledExperimental(true)` guard added defensively in the first version of this pass — a real device log showed it's a no-op on this project's Fabric/New Architecture setup (just prints a warning), so it was pure noise with no effect.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `donutColWidth`, `DONUT_MAX_SIZE` — both present.

**Same-day v5: the list-beside-graph layout was also abandoned** ("vazgeçtim bu tarzı da beğenmedim") **for a fifth `CineGraphDonut.tsx` rewrite — back to leader lines, but deliberately much simpler than the v2/v3 attempt.** Single big centered graph again (no side list), and every connector is now one plain straight radial segment — `M ring-edge → L (same angle, further out)` — instead of the earlier 3-segment orthogonal elbow. Since a straight line follows the slice's own angle outward by construction, it can never cross back over the ring the way the elbowed version's spread-segment could (that whole class of bug, and its fix, is moot here — there's no segment that travels perpendicular to the radius anymore).

Crowding (many chips at the same distance from the ring would overlap) is solved by **varying the line length instead of spreading positions along a column/row**: connectors are tiered into 3 lengths (`BASE_LINE + tier * TIER_STEP`), assigned by *angular* sort order (not count order) so any two angularly-adjacent genres land on different tiers — a deliberately simpler alternative to v2/v3's full position-assignment-with-push-apart-on-open logic, since there's no longer a fixed column to spread within (chips can sit at any angle around the full circle now, not just 2 or 4 fixed sides).

Each line ends in a **color-bordered chip** (border = that genre's own slice color) holding the genre name — replacing the old plain-gray-text label. Chips flow away from center (right-anchored if in the left half, left-anchored if in the right half; similarly for top/bottom) so they don't need their text width measured in advance to position correctly. Tapping a chip, its slice, or the connector line itself (the visible line is only 1.4px wide — a second **invisible** `Line` with identical coordinates but `strokeWidth={20}` and `stroke="transparent"` sits on top purely as a comfortable tap target, a real react-native-svg technique for making thin decorative strokes tappable) turns that line **white** (was gray) and reopens the same callout box from v2/v3 (count·%, average rating, `Detail` button) — content and behavior unchanged, only the connector geometry and the label-vs-chip visual changed.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `TIER_STEP`, `chipAnchor` — both present. (Also hit and fixed unrelated to this component: the Codespace's Metro/backend dev servers had both silently died between turns — restarted via `start-codespace.sh`, unrelated to any code change, a known possibility worth checking first if bundle verification suddenly can't connect.)

**Same-day v5 follow-up: two real bugs in the just-shipped straight-line design, both in `CineGraphDonut.tsx`.**
1. **Chips could overlap when genres were angularly crowded.** The v5 tiering assigned line length by `listIndex % 3` (angular sort order, but *position-in-list* parity) — a cluster of 4+ tiny slices bunched close together could still put two truly-adjacent genres on the same tier (e.g. items 0 and 3 both land on tier 0 despite being neighbors, since the cluster size wasn't a multiple of 3). Replaced with a **greedy nearest-available-tier assignment**: walk genres in angular order, and give each one the first tier (0 up to a capped `MAX_TIER=3`) where it isn't within `MIN_ANGULAR_GAP` (~26°) of anything already placed on that tier. Sparse genres all stay on tier 0 as before; a genuinely dense cluster now automatically claims as many of the available tiers as it needs instead of blindly cycling through a fixed count — this is what actually fixes the reported overlap, not just alternating lengths differently.
2. **Connector lines didn't reach the chip's actual center** — they were terminating at an approximate anchor point (`p1`, an edge with an eyeballed `-10`/`+10` offset), not the chip's true visual middle, and chip width/height genuinely vary with genre name length so a fixed offset was never going to line up exactly. Fixed properly: each chip's real rendered size is now measured via `onLayout` (`chipSizes` state, keyed by genre), and chips are positioned by anchoring their **near corner** (not an edge-plus-offset) exactly at the tier-based anchor point `p1` — once a corner is pinned precisely and the real width/height is known, the chip's center is exact arithmetic (`p1 ± size/2`, sign depending on which quadrant), not a guess. The connector line is then drawn all the way to that exact center — since the chip itself renders after the `Svg` in the tree (so it paints on top), its opaque background naturally covers the portion of the line underneath it, and the visible line reads as plugging directly into the middle of the button. A small `CHIP_FALLBACK_SIZE` estimate is used only for the very first frame before a chip's first `onLayout` fires, to avoid a visible jump.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `angularDistance`, `handleChipLayout`, `MIN_ANGULAR_GAP` — all present.

**Same-day v5 correction: fixing "line reaches the chip's center" (above) broke "line stays parallel to the slice's own angle."** The center-of-chip fix moved the line's endpoint by an axis-aligned `±width/2`/`±height/2` offset from the tier anchor point — a rectangular nudge, not one along the slice's own radial direction, so the line was no longer straight/parallel to its slice as originally specified. Corrected by flipping which side adapts: **the line's endpoint (`p1`) is never touched again** — it stays exactly on the slice's own angle, always. The **chip** moves to meet it instead: horizontally centered on `p1.x`, with whichever edge faces the ring (top edge if the point is in the lower half, bottom edge if in the upper half) pinned exactly to `p1.y` — so the midpoint of that edge, not some corner, is what lands on the line's tip. This still needs the chip's real measured size (`chipSizes`/`onLayout`, unchanged from the fix above) to compute precisely. A hard clamp keeps the (rare) outermost-tier, near-horizontal/vertical chip from spilling past the box edge — the clamp only ever nudges the chip, never the line, so the radial-parallel guarantee holds even in that edge case.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `chipLeft`, `chipTop` — both present.

**Same-day v5, one more round: chips could still overlap, root cause was a silent fallback in the tier assignment, not the geometry.** The greedy tier algorithm from the fix above was capped at `MAX_TIER=3` — when a cluster was dense enough that all 4 tiers were already occupied within `MIN_ANGULAR_GAP`, the assignment fell back to unconditionally reusing `MAX_TIER` anyway, silently recreating the exact collision the algorithm exists to prevent for any cluster past that size. Removed the cap entirely — the `while` loop now keeps incrementing the tier until it finds one that's actually clear, so a sufficiently dense cluster gets as many tiers as it genuinely needs.

Uncapped tiers need somewhere to render without clipping, which is what "put the graph in the center with room at the top" was asking for: **the box is no longer a tight square sized to just fit the ring plus a fixed margin.** `boxWidth` stays screen-width-bound as before, but `boxHeight = boxWidth + EXTRA_VERTICAL` (120px of deliberate extra headroom split above and below the ring) — the ring itself is unchanged in size, but a dense cluster whose genres happen to point up/down now has real room to extend into before running out of box. (`centerX`/`centerY` split apart accordingly — the ring is no longer assumed to sit in a perfectly square box, `boxWidth`/`boxHeight` are now tracked and used independently everywhere a bound was previously computed off a single shared `boxSize`.)

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `EXTRA_VERTICAL`, `boxHeight` — both present.

**Same-day v5, final overlap pass: replaced the fixed-degree collision threshold with a size-aware one, plus a slightly bigger ring.** Even uncapped, `MIN_ANGULAR_GAP` (~26°, a single constant for every genre regardless of name length) was never going to be correct for both a 3-letter genre and a 15-letter one, and didn't scale with a tier's actual radius the way real physical clearance does. Replaced with a proper per-pair check: required angular gap is now derived from each chip's *real measured width* (`chipSizes`, already collected via `onLayout` for the line-alignment fix) via the small-angle approximation (`arc length ≈ radius × angle`) at the *specific* radius that tier sits at — `(widthA/2 + widthB/2 + CHIP_GAP) / radius`. Bigger tiers (more radius) now correctly need less angular separation for the same physical clearance, and two long-named genres correctly get held further apart than two short ones would need to be.

This makes the tier assignment (`items` useMemo) depend on `chipSizes` now, not just `stats`/`genreRatings` — tiers are computed once with the fallback estimate on first mount, then **recompute automatically once real sizes land** (a few genres may visibly settle into their final tier a moment after first paint, not a bug). The already-existing "skip the state update if the value didn't actually change" guard in `handleChipLayout` is what keeps this from looping — a chip's width only ever depends on its text content, never its position, so once measured it never triggers another layout pass for the same genre.

Also bumped the ring itself bigger per the direct request — `MARGIN` (space reserved outside the ring) `92→78`, `TIER_STEP` `24→26` to keep proportional separation between tiers at the new radius.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `CHIP_GAP`, `requiredGap` — both present.

**Same-day v5, final overlap round: two more asks — shorter chips innermost/longer chips outermost, and chips must never touch the ring — turned out to share one root cause and one fix.** The flat `BASE_LINE` constant (14px for every chip, regardless of width) was the reason chips could touch the ring: a chip's near edge is a flat horizontal segment centered on its anchor point, but the ring is a circle, so a *wide* chip's corners can dip back toward (or past) the ring's boundary even when the anchor point itself clears it cleanly — worst-case right at a near-horizontal angle, verified algebraically (worked the worst-case-angle distance-from-center formula out by hand: at angle→0°, a chip's near corner ends up at distance `outerRadius + RING_CLEARANCE` from center regardless of its own width, once the line length itself is width-aware — the two effects exactly cancel).

Replaced `BASE_LINE` with `baseLineFor(chipWidth) = RING_CLEARANCE + chipWidth / 2` — every chip's own line length is now derived from its own measured width, guaranteeing `RING_CLEARANCE` (16px) of true clearance at its worst-case corner, at any angle, for any width. **This directly solves the ordering ask too, for free**: a wider chip now always starts from a longer base line than a narrower one, even with zero angular collision — and the greedy tier-assignment loop was also switched to process genres **narrowest-chip-first** (previously angular order) so that within any cluster that does collide, the narrowest one claims the earliest (innermost) available tier and progressively wider ones get pushed further out as they collide with what's already placed — exactly "shortest button innermost, longest outermost," without a second mechanism, since both asks reduce to the same "radius should scale with width" idea.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `baseLineFor`, `RING_CLEARANCE` — both present.

**Same-day v5, 5th overlap pass: replaced tier-index placement with exact rectangle-overlap placement — real data (4 genuinely clustered genres on the user's own account) still showed residual overlap and a new "line end floats away from its chip" glitch.** Root cause of both: `tier` was being treated as if it meant one shared radius, but each item's actual radius was `outerRadius + minRadiusFor(itsOwnWidth) + tier*TIER_STEP` — since `minRadiusFor` varies per chip width, two different-width chips nominally on "the same tier" sat at genuinely *different* radii, and the angular-gap collision formula assumed both items were at the *querying* item's radius. That mismatch let some genuinely-overlapping pairs pass the check. Separately, the position-clamping safety net (keeps an outermost chip from spilling past the box edge) moved the chip but never moved the line, which kept pointing at the pre-clamp position — a visible gap between the line's tip and the chip whenever clamping actually triggered.

Both fixed by dropping the tier abstraction entirely. Placement (still narrowest-chip-first) now searches a **continuous radius** per chip: start at its own true minimum (`outerRadius + minRadiusFor(width)`), and if its computed bounding box actually intersects any already-placed chip's real bounding box (`chipBoxAt()`/`boxesOverlap()`, exact rectangle math, no angular approximation), step the radius out by `RADIUS_STEP=6px` and recheck — repeat until clear. This is provably correct (it tests real geometry, not a proxy for it) and finer-grained than the old `TIER_STEP=26` jump, which is what "increase positioning precision" asked for directly. The line-detachment bug is fixed by having `chipAnchor()` compute the clamped chip's actual attach point (its own edge midpoint, post-clamp) and using *that* — not the pre-clamp point — as the line's endpoint whenever clamping actually occurs, so the line can never visually separate from its chip even in that fallback case.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `chipBoxAt`, `boxesOverlap`, `RADIUS_STEP` — all present.

**Same-day v5, 6th and final round on this component: the previous pass's own clamp-safety fix had silently reintroduced the very first rule this whole redesign started with — every line must stay parallel to its own slice.** The line-detachment fix from the prior round redirected a clamped chip's line to the chip's *clamped* edge midpoint instead of the true radial point — visually reconnecting the line to its chip, but bending it off the slice's angle to do so, exactly the thing v5's original spec explicitly ruled out. Corrected by making the priority ordering explicit and permanent: the line **always** ends at the true, unmodified radial point; only the *chip* is ever clamped. A rare small visual gap between a clamped chip and its line is judged acceptable — a bent line is not, under any circumstance.

To make that rare case rarer still, `MARGIN` (space reserved outside the ring for chips to occupy) went `78→115`, shrinking the ring somewhat in exchange for meaningfully more radial room for a colliding cluster's `RADIUS_STEP` search to push chips outward into before ever needing the clamp at all — directly per the user's own suggested trade-off ("shrinking the graph gives the lines more room to extend, so shrink it").

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle rebuilt successfully, no runtime errors.

**Same-day v6: the entire leader-line/callout direction (v2 through the 6 overlap-fix rounds above) was abandoned after still not converging, in favor of a structurally different interaction — rotate the ring to the button, not the button to the ring.** `CineGraphDonut.tsx` rewritten a sixth time: connector lines and per-genre collision math are gone. Genre chips now sit at **fixed scattered positions** around the ring, chosen once (seeded-random angle + radius jitter for an organic look, still run through the exact same rectangle-overlap placement search used in the last leader-line pass — just applied to randomized starting points instead of slice-derived ones, so "scattered" and "never overlapping" aren't in tension). Since chip position no longer needs to track a slice's own angle at all, the entire class of bug this component kept hitting (angular-gap approximations, tier/radius mismatches, clamp-vs-line-parallel conflicts) has no surface left to occur on.

**New interaction**: tapping a chip (or its ring slice) **rotates the whole donut** — via a `<G rotation={degrees} origin="cx,cy">` wrapping the slice `Circle`s — until that genre's slice angle lines up with the chip's fixed position, then a single connecting line is drawn from the now-aligned slice to the chip; tapping the same chip again rotates back to neutral (0°). Rotation is JS-thread-driven (a listener on an `Animated.Value` forcing a re-render each frame, the same idiom used throughout this component's history) rather than a native-driver transform, since the connecting line needs the live in-between angle every frame too, not just the ring itself. The target rotation is chosen via the shortest angular path (normalized delta, never spins the long way around on a second tap). Only the *selected* genre ever gets a line — every other chip just sits still.

**The info callout (count/%/average rating/Detail button) is deliberately disabled for this pass** per explicit instruction ("do this first") — `onDetailPress` stays in the prop signature (so `ProfileCinegraphsTab.tsx` didn't need touching) but is currently unused; re-adding some form of it, now anchored to a chip that doesn't move, is expected as a same-day follow-up.

No new i18n keys, no backend changes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `selectGenre`, `rotationAnim`, `seeded` — all present.

**Same-day v6 hotfix: on-device testing surfaced two real bugs in the just-shipped rotation design, both fixed without another rewrite.** All in `CineGraphDonut.tsx`.

1. **Chips escaping the container.** The placement search's `while(true)` loop grew a chip's radius with no upper bound whenever it kept colliding with neighbors — on a genre-heavy graph this pushed some chips' radius far enough that they rendered outside the `boxSize`×`boxSize` box entirely (RN doesn't clip overflow), visibly overlapping the Movies/Series sub-tab bar above or spilling past the screen edge. Fixed with a new `maxRadiusForAngle()` — an analytic (not searched) hard cap, computed per chip from where its box would first cross the container edge (`EDGE_PAD = 6`) along that specific angle — the placement loop now grows radius only up to this cap, accepting a rare residual overlap in dense cases rather than ever letting a chip leave the page. Also toned down `RADIUS_JITTER` (26→14) and `ANGLE_JITTER` (0.3→0.16 rad) — the capped placement made the scatter look tidier on its own, and the previous jitter magnitudes were partly what made it read as "too random."
2. **Connector line landing in the wrong place.** The line-endpoint calculation had its own, separately-reimplemented copy of the chip-box math, and that copy carried a bug: for chips placed *above* center it added a stray `+ height`, aiming the line past the chip entirely instead of at its near edge. Root cause was duplication — the exact same geometry (box position, near-edge point) was independently recomputed in three places (placement search, chip rendering, line endpoint), and only one of those three had the bug. Fixed by computing each chip's box **once**, in the placement `useMemo`, and storing the literal result (`left/top/px/py`) on the `ChipItem` — rendering and the line endpoint now both just read those stored fields instead of re-deriving them, so this class of bug can't reappear. With this fixed, the rotation's existing alignment math (already correct) now visibly delivers what was asked: the line exits the ring exactly along the slice's own axis and lands exactly on the chip, never elsewhere.

Also added a `minHeight` (≈50% of window height, floor'd at `boxSize + 40`) to the section wrapping the graph, with `justifyContent/alignItems: "center"` — keeps the donut vertically centered in the space below the Movies/Series sub-tabs rather than hugging the top, and gives the scatter more room to stay clear of the tab bar in the first place.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `maxRadiusForAngle`, `areaMinHeight` — both present. No i18n or backend changes.

**Same-day v6 second hotfix: chip placement switched from random scatter to a deterministic tiered ring, per explicit request for something more overlap-proof and more aesthetically circular.** `CineGraphDonut.tsx`. The `seeded()` pseudo-random function and its angle/radius jitter are gone entirely — angle is now strictly evenly spaced around the full 360° (`i/n * 2π`, no jitter), so chips form a clean ring fully surrounding the donut rather than clustering unevenly. Radius alternates between two tiers by position — even index sits at the inner radius, odd index sits `TIER_STEP` (40px) further out — the "girintili çıkıntılı" (indented/protruding) zigzag the user asked for. This isn't just cosmetic: alternating tiers is *why* overlaps got rarer, since two angularly-adjacent chips are never on the same tier, doubling the effective angular gap between same-tier neighbors for free, before the exact-rectangle collision search (unchanged from the previous hotfix — still pushes a chip further out along its own angle, still hard-capped by `maxRadiusForAngle` so nothing leaves the container) even has to do any work. Processing order changed from width-sorted to strict angular order — sorting by width would have reshuffled which chip lands on which tier independent of its position on the ring, breaking the zigzag's visual regularity; tier is now purely a function of position, not chip size. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for `TIER_STEP` (present) and `ANGLE_JITTER`/`RADIUS_JITTER` (both gone, confirming the old jitter code was fully replaced, not just shadowed).

**Same-day v6 third hotfix: zero-overlap made a hard guarantee, and the reveal sequence reordered** — user reported a small remaining residual overlap (previously an accepted trade-off) was no longer acceptable, and that the connecting line/highlight was appearing instantly on tap instead of only after the rotation settles. Both in `CineGraphDonut.tsx`.

**Overlap**: new `placeChip()` helper is now the single placement authority. It still grows a chip's radius along its own angle first (as before, capped by `maxRadiusForAngle` so it can't leave the page) — but if that alone can't clear a collision, it now falls back to small alternating angular nudges (±2° steps, up to ±24° from the base angle) until a collision-free spot is found, before giving up. This is a genuinely last-resort path — the tiered ring (previous hotfix) already prevents most collisions by construction — but it turns "usually no overlap" into "never," which is what was asked. The chip's *actual* placed angle (possibly nudged) is what's stored and used for the rotation-alignment math too, so a nudged chip still gets a correctly-aligned line.

**Reveal sequencing**: `selectGenre()` now resets a new `revealAnim` (`Animated.Value`, 0→1, separate from `rotationAnim`) to 0 immediately on every tap, and only starts fading it to 1 (`Animated.timing`, 220ms) inside the rotation animation's completion callback — and only if that rotation actually finished (not interrupted by a second tap mid-flight) and a genre is still selected. The connecting `Line` (now `AnimatedLine = Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Line)`, module-scope so it isn't recreated every render) and the highlighted chip overlay (now wrapped in `Animated.View`) both bind their opacity to `revealAnim` — so neither is visible at all during the rotation, and both fade in together only once the slice has actually arrived at the chip. Both also switched color from `colors.baseContent` to `colors.placeholder` (an existing muted-gray theme token) per "gri renkte olsun."

**Real ring-touching bug also fixed while in this code**: `placeChip` used to silently clamp `radius = Math.min(minRadius, cap)` — if a chip's page-edge cap for a given angle happened to be *smaller* than its required ring-clearance floor, this quietly placed it closer to the ring than `RING_CLEARANCE` allows, which is what the user saw as a chip touching the graph. **Same-day v6 sixth pass: the placement technique itself replaced, at the user's explicit request, with concentric invisible rings.** Not a bug fix this time — the search-and-nudge/tiered-zigzag placement (all previous hotfixes) is gone entirely, replaced with a deterministic scheme the user specified directly: invisible circles around the donut, bigger than it, with genres poured onto them shortest-name-first. **The algorithm**: candidates are sorted ascending by (measured or estimated) chip width — shortest genre names first, since a narrow button is exactly what lets a ring hold the most of them. Starting from ring 1 (radius = donut edge + `RING_CLEARANCE` + `CHIP_RING_PAD`), a new `ringCapacity()` finds the *maximum* number of items, taken as a prefix of the remaining sorted list, that fit evenly spaced around that ring's circumference without any two adjacent boxes touching — computed from the chord length between evenly-spaced points (`2·R·sin(π/N)`) against the widest item in that group of N (a safe, uniform stand-in for "the actual adjacent pair," since every gap is identical by construction). That many genres are placed on ring 1; whatever's left pours onto ring 2 (`ringBase + RING_GAP`), then ring 3, and so on — the `while` loop just keeps adding rings until everyone has a spot (the user said "you can go up to 3 if you need to"; this generalizes to "as many as needed" so it doesn't hard-fail on an unusually genre-heavy account). Successive rings alternate their starting angle by half a slot, purely so a ring's buttons don't sit radially in line with the ring inside it.

**Containment is still a hard guarantee, layered the same way as before**: `maxRadiusForAngle` (recomputed for the centered-box convention — the vertical term now uses `height/2` instead of the old one-sided `height`) caps any individual chip's radius below its nominal ring radius if that specific angle+width combination would otherwise leave the page; a `floor = outerRadius + RING_CLEARANCE + max(width,height)/2` guarantees it's never clamped closer to the donut ring than that either. `pushClear` (a rename of the old `placeChip`, now only used for shoving other chips out of an opened callout's way) also switched to the centered-box formulas.

**Real bug, reported live on the user's own account (Horror/Family genres flickering back and forth continuously)**: `chips`' candidate list is sorted by measured chip width, and RN's layout engine (yoga) can report *sub-pixel-different* widths for the exact same text across consecutive renders (rounding jitter, not a real size change). When two genres' widths are extremely close, that jitter could flip their sort order between renders — which changes both of their positions — which re-triggers `onLayout` on both (repositioning fires a new layout event even though the text/size didn't conceptually change) — feeding straight back into the same jitter, an unbounded oscillation. Fixed two ways: (1) `handleChipLayout` now rounds width/height to whole pixels before storing, collapsing the sub-pixel noise so the *same* text consistently produces the *same* stored value across renders; (2) the candidate sort gained a stable tiebreak (`a.width - b.width || a.genre.localeCompare(b.genre)`) so genuinely-equal widths still resolve to a fixed, deterministic order rather than whatever order `Object.entries` happened to yield that render. Neither fix alone was guaranteed sufficient — (1) removes the noise that was flipping the comparison, (2) removes any remaining nondeterminism if two rounded widths land exactly equal — together they close the loop.

(1) Since `spaceBelow > spaceAbove` (the shift-down asymmetry), the donut naturally sits in the upper portion of its own (now taller) box — expected and fine, the box's own height already accounts for it. (2) A new `PAGE_DOWN_SHIFT` (26px) `marginTop` on the box itself nudges the whole graphic down within the section's centered flex area, independent of the box's internal geometry — a simple, direct lever for "move the whole thing down the page" that doesn't get tangled up with the containment math above it.

**Same-day v6 twenty-third pass: real bug — row spacing evenly placed chip *centers*, not chip *edges*, so two wide neighbors could still touch.** User: some of the 4 bottom-row movie chips looked adjacent/touching. Root cause: `rowMargin`/`rowSpanWidth` (previous pass) spaced every chip's *center* an equal fraction apart, using the row's single widest member only to size the outer edge margins — but center-to-center spacing being uniform doesn't mean edge-to-edge *gap* is uniform when widths differ. Two long chips (e.g. "Science Fiction" next to "War") landing at neighboring evenly-spaced center slots could have a smaller real gap between their edges than two short chips at the same center spacing — occasionally small enough to touch.

Fixed by switching from center-based to **edge-gap-based** spacing: compute the row's actual leftover width (`boxWidth - 2·EDGE_PAD - Σ chip widths`), divide it into `n-1` equal gaps, and lay chips out left-to-right using each chip's real width plus that one shared gap — `left += chip.width + gap` per chip. This guarantees the *visual* gap between every adjacent pair is identical (not just their centers), and — since it's derived from the row's real total width rather than an approximation — provably never goes negative for a row this small (at most 4 chips). The old `Math.min/Math.max` edge clamp became unnecessary (the new math is inherently bounded) and was dropped.

Research found this app has **no light theme at all** — all 9 shipped themes (`forest`/`dark`/`dim`/`black`/`luxury`/`dracula`/`sunset`/`synthwave`/`coffee`) are dark-family, so a light/dark boolean branch would always resolve the same way and wasn't useful; instead, the meaningful, continuously-varying signal across themes is each one's `base100` background's own relative luminance (from true black at `black`/`luxury` up to a noticeably lighter dark at `dim`/`dracula`).

`CineGraphDonut.tsx`: new `hexLuminance(hex)` (standard relative-luminance approximation, 0–1) and `genreColor(index, total, bgLuminance)` — the pastel's lightness now nudges up (76%→~86% at the lightest dark theme) as the active theme's `base100` gets lighter, keeping contrast comfortable on themes like `dim`/`dracula` without needing to change anything on the near-black ones, where the baseline pastel already reads fine. `bgLuminance` is computed once via `useMemo(() => hexLuminance(colors.base100), [colors.base100])` and threaded into `slices`' `genreColor()` call.

**Real bug caught and fixed in the same pass**: the initial version produced `hsl(hue, 55%, NaN%)` — an invalid color RN's style layer rejected outright, logged as a real on-device warning across a full 16-genre set. Root cause: `hexLuminance` had no guard against a `base100` value that fails to parse as 6 hex digits (e.g. an empty/transient string before the theme context finishes loading), and a `NaN` luminance silently propagated all the way into the final HSL string. Fixed by having `hexLuminance` fall back to `0` (the same baseline as a true-black background — a safe, sensible default) whenever the computed value isn't finite, so a parse failure can never again reach a rendered color string.

### Lists page redesign: card style, edit-mode reorder/delete, tab-bar cleanup

User: the Lists page (its own bottom tab, and duplicated inline inside Profile's Lists sub-tab via `MyListsView.tsx`) had a plain-text row card design and a big full-width "New List" button, both disliked. Wanted: cards matching Home/Search's poster-preview list-card design (`DiscoverListCard.tsx`); the big button replaced by a short description text (same pattern as the CineGraph intro blurb above); two small icon-only buttons below that text — round "+" Add, pencil Edit; tapping Edit reveals a per-card trash icon (delete) and enables long-press-and-drag reordering. Separately: remove the Watched List, Watchlist, and Lists bottom tabs — confirmed reachable another way already (Profile's Overview sub-tab has "See All" links to `/watchlist`/`/to-watch`, and Profile's own Lists sub-tab renders `MyListsView` inline), so only the tab-bar buttons needed hiding, not the routes.

**Drag-to-reorder had zero precedent anywhere in this app.** Asked the user to choose between a proven library (`react-native-draggable-flatlist` + `react-native-reanimated`) or hand-rolling with `PanResponder`/`Animated` — given this session's own repeated jitter bugs from hand-rolled positioning logic (the CineGraph donut saga above), recommended and the user chose the library. `npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-draggable-flatlist` resolved Reanimated to v4.5.1 and draggable-flatlist to v4.0.3 — this monorepo (npm workspaces, hoisted root `node_modules`) already had reanimated v4.5.3 sitting in the tree transitively (via expo-router/gesture-handler/screens) but unused at the JS level by any app code until now; §6's claim that reanimated was deliberately not added is now stale, corrected there.

**New required infra, none of which existed before:** `mobile/babel.config.js` (didn't exist at all — Expo fell back to `babel-preset-expo`'s defaults) now explicitly sets `plugins: ["react-native-reanimated/plugin"]`. `mobile/app/_layout.tsx` (the true root, not `(app)/_layout.tsx`) gained `import "react-native-gesture-handler";` as its first import and now wraps the whole provider tree in `<GestureHandlerRootView style={{flex:1}}>` — required by `DraggableFlatList`, and nothing in this app had used a JS-level gesture-handler component before, so this wiring was genuinely new, not a gap-fill.

**Backend** (`backend/models/CustomList.js`, `backend/routes/customListRoute.js`): added `order: {type: Number, default: 0}` + an `{owner:1, order:1}` index — no prior concept of user-defined list ordering existed (`GET /me` previously just sorted `createdAt: -1`). `GET /me` now sorts `{order: -1, createdAt: -1}` and lazily backfills any list still at the schema default (`bulkWrite`, descending values assigned in current `createdAt`-desc order) the first time a user's lists are fetched post-deploy — no separate migration script, and verified via curl to preserve each user's pre-existing visible order with zero jump on first load. `POST /` now assigns new lists `currentMax + 1` (appears at top, matching the old newest-first default). New `PATCH /lists/me/reorder` (body `{orderedIds: string[]}`) validates every id belongs to the caller (400, no partial writes, on any mismatch) then bulk-writes descending order values. **`GET /me` also now routes through the existing `hydratePreviewItems()` helper** (previously only used by `/discover`/`/popular`) — this was a genuine latent bug fix: `/me` never set `likeCount` before (mobile's `CustomList` type claimed it as required, but it was actually always `undefined` at runtime), fixed for free by the same change that added poster-preview hydration.

All backend changes verified end-to-end with a throwaway test account before touching mobile: create → order assignment; `GET /me` → correct sort + hydrated `previewItems`/`likeCount`; reorder swap → persists; reorder with a foreign/bogus id → 400, no partial write; simulated pre-migration doc (`order` unset via direct DB edit) → backfill preserved the exact prior `createdAt`-desc order. Test account and its lists deleted after.

**Mobile types/API** (`types/index.ts`, `constants/apiRoutes.ts`, `api/listService.ts`): `CustomList` gained `previewItems?: ListPreviewItem[]` (optional — only `/me` populates it; create/update/detail responses don't) and `order: number`. New `reorderLists(orderedIds)` calling the new endpoint.

**New `src/components/MyListCard.tsx`** — a sibling to `DiscoverListCard.tsx`, not a reuse of it: `DiscoverListCard`'s contract requires a populated `owner` object (irrelevant/noisy for the user's own lists) and stays scoped to "read-only preview of someone else's list" (Home + Search). `MyListCard` copies its visual styling verbatim (poster row, description, count) but drops the owner row, keeps the existing Public/Private badge, and adds an edit-mode-only trash button + `onLongPress` wired to `DraggableFlatList`'s `drag()`. Poster thumbnails are not individually pressable here (unlike `DiscoverListCard`) — avoids accidental navigation mid-drag or mid-delete-mode.

**`MyListsView.tsx` redesign**: the two `newButton` render sites replaced with a CineGraph-intro-style block (two centered muted lines) plus a centered `actionRow` of two round icon buttons — Add (filled `colors.primary` circle, opens the existing unchanged create-list modal) and Edit (toggles new `editMode` state, fill color flips to `colors.primary` while active). `FlatList` swapped for `DraggableFlatList` unconditionally; dragging is gated per-item by only wiring `onLongPress={editMode ? drag : undefined}` in `renderItem` (the library's supported way to make dragging opt-in, avoids swapping list components or losing scroll position on mode toggle). `onDragEnd` does an optimistic reorder (capture→set→await→catch-rollback, the same pattern already established by `ListDetailScreen.tsx`'s like-toggle) calling `reorderLists`. `handleDelete` (pre-existing) is unchanged, just relocated from an always-visible per-row icon into `MyListCard`'s edit-mode-only trash button.

**Bottom tab bar** (`app/(app)/_layout.tsx`): added `href: null` to the `watchlist`, `to-watch`, and `lists` `Tabs.Screen` entries — verified directly against the installed `expo-router` source (`TabsClient.js`) that this hides a tab's bar button (`tabBarItemStyle: {display:'none'}`, `tabBarButton` returns null) while leaving the screen/nested stack fully mounted and routable. Confirmed nothing else needed to change: `router.push("/watchlist")`/`router.push("/to-watch")` (`ProfileOverviewTab.tsx`'s "See All" links) and `router.push("/lists/${id}")` (from `MyListsView`/`MyListCard`) all keep working exactly as before.

3 new i18n keys (two intro lines, one reorder-failure error message) across all 12 locales, anchored on the existing `"New List"` key via the established batch-insert script. Reused existing `"Edit"` key as-is (already present in all 12 locales) rather than adding a duplicate.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout. Metro restarted (new babel config required a fresh process, not just Fast Refresh) — bundle fetched and grepped for `MyListCard`/`DraggableFlatList`/`reorderLists`/`GestureHandlerRootView`, all present; dev log showed a clean `iOS Bundled` line (2200 modules) with no SyntaxError/module-resolution errors from the new babel plugin or dependencies.

**Flagged, not silently assumed away**: `react-native-draggable-flatlist`'s published peer range (`react-native-reanimated: >=2.8.0`) is loose enough to accept the resolved v4, and the bundle compiles clean, but actual on-device drag behavior (not just "does it bundle") still needs the user's own manual test — this is the one part of this milestone not verifiable from the dev environment alone.

### Profile page redesign: Instagram-style header, 4 category tabs, personal Activity feature

User: the Profile screen's main "Profile" sub-tab (avatar/username/bio/stats block + the always-stacked Favorites/Watched List/Watchlist/Activity rails below it, all in `ProfileOverviewTab.tsx`) should become Instagram-style — avatar left, username+follower/following stats right (stats block's bottom landing slightly above the avatar's own bottom), bio below, then 4 icon-only category tabs (Favorites, WatchedList, Watchlist, Activity) that switch content below instead of always showing every section stacked. Favorites keeps its current design; WatchedList/Watchlist become a capped 12-item Search-style 4-column grid with a "Go to page" button to the full screen; Activity is a brand-new personal feed (explicitly distinct from Home's existing network-activity feed, which stays untouched) showing the user's own week/month actions across ratings, reviews, review-likes, watchlist/watched-list adds, list creation, and group joins, with a This Week/This Month filter and its own dedicated full-screen view. The other 3 Profile sub-tabs (Cinegraphs, Lists, Analyses) and the outer tab row were explicitly out of scope — only the "Profile" sub-tab's own content changed.

**Real backend gap found and resolved during planning, not glossed over**: "which reviews have I liked" can't be date-filtered with the existing schema — `Review.likes` is just `[ObjectId]`, no per-like timestamp. Asked the user directly rather than guessing; they chose to add it properly. `Review.js` gained an additive `likeEvents: [{user, likedAt}]` array alongside the untouched `likes` array — `toggleReviewLike` (`reviewController.js`) now pushes/pulls both arrays in lockstep on like/unlike, so every existing consumer of `likes`/`likeCount`/`hasLiked` (verified via a spot-check of `getContentReviews` before/after) keeps working completely unchanged; only the new personal-activity endpoint ever reads `likeEvents`.

**New backend endpoint**: `GET /api/users/me/activity?range=week|month&page=&limit=`, new `backend/controllers/activityController.js` (kept separate from the already-large `userController.js`), modeled directly on `feedController.js`'s `getFeed` (same fan-out-then-merge-then-sort-then-paginate shape, one endpoint serving both the embedded preview and the full screen via `limit` rather than two endpoints). Rolling 7/30-day cutoff, matching `feedController.js`'s own convention (not calendar week/month). Queries 6 sources in parallel and merges into one `createdAt`-sorted stream with a `type` discriminator (`rated`/`reviewed`/`review_liked`/`watchlist_added`/`towatch_added`/`list_created`/`group_joined`): `Rating`/`Review` by `createdAt`, `Review.likeEvents` via `$elemMatch`, `User.watchlist`/`toWatchList` subdocs filtered in JS (same technique `getFeed` already uses for its own watchlist events — no Mongo date-range query is possible on array subdocs without `$elemMatch`+`$unwind`), `CustomList` by `createdAt`/`owner`, and `Group` via `$elemMatch` on `members: {user, joinedAt}` with a `members.$` positional projection. **Real bug caught during my own review of the plan agent's first draft**: the group query was originally written as two separate top-level conditions (`"members.user": userId` AND `"members.joinedAt": {$gte: cutoff}`) instead of one `$elemMatch` — those two conditions independently match ANY element of the array, not necessarily the SAME subdocument, so a group where the caller is a long-time member but some other member joined recently would have false-positived. Fixed to a single `$elemMatch: {user, joinedAt: {$gte: cutoff}}` before this ever ran against real data. Kept the existing "Watched List" reads `watchlist`/"Watchlist" reads `toWatchList` naming mismatch as-is (matches everywhere else in this codebase) rather than inventing a new convention.

Naming terminology note carried into the response: `watchlist_added` = UI's "WatchedList" tab, `towatch_added` = UI's "Watchlist" tab — same established (if confusing) mapping used throughout the app.

**Mobile**: new `PersonalActivityType`/`PersonalActivityItem`/`PersonalActivityResult` types (`types/index.ts`, siblings of the existing `FeedActivityType`/`FeedActivityItem` — deliberately NOT extending/reusing those, since `FeedActivityItem` always carries an actor `user` field for someone else's activity, which doesn't fit a feed that's always "you"), new `activityService.ts` (`getMyActivity`), new `MY_ACTIVITY` route block in `apiRoutes.ts`.

**New components**: `ProfileHeaderInstagram.tsx` (avatar-left/username+stats-right — the "stats bottom slightly above avatar bottom" requirement is satisfied declaratively, not with absolute-position math: the 84px avatar is deliberately a bit taller than the right column's natural stacked height (username line + stats row), so the stats block's bottom lands a few px above the avatar's bottom by construction, staying correct across font-scaling; tier badge + "Joined {date}" — not specified by the user, kept rather than dropped — moved to a small row below the bio since they didn't fit the header's now-tight height budget); `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx` (owns the 4-way `category` state and the icon row — Ionicons `heart`/`checkmark-done`/`bookmark`/`pulse`, outline-when-unselected/filled-when-selected, `colors.placeholder`→`colors.baseContent` for the gray→white translation, the same convention the outer tab row one level up already uses, since a literal `#fff` would break under any future light theme); `ProfileMiniGrid.tsx` (shared between WatchedList/Watchlist — slices to 12 **before** hydrating, since neither `getWatchlist()`/`getToWatchList()` support server-side limiting and hydration is N individual `getMovieById`/`getSeriesById` calls; a plain row-chunked `View` grid rather than `FlatList`, since a fixed 12-item preview inside the parent `ScrollView` doesn't need virtualization and would risk the usual nested-VirtualizedList warning; reuses `MiniContentCard` with Search's exact 4-column math, NOT `SearchContentGrid.tsx` itself, which carries pagination/filter machinery this static preview doesn't want); `PersonalActivityRow.tsx` (adapted from `FeedItemRow.tsx`'s visual language — poster + `StarRatingDisplay` for rated, italic excerpt for reviewed — but icon-led instead of avatar-led, since there's no "other user" in a personal feed); `ProfileActivityPreview.tsx` (This Week/This Month pill filter, top-8 preview, "Go to page" button); new screen `app/(app)/profile/activity.tsx` (independent filter state, `FlatList` + `onEndReached` pagination against the same endpoint, same pattern `SearchContentGrid.tsx` already uses) registered in `profile/_layout.tsx` (this Stack explicitly declares every screen — a confirmed sharp edge from earlier work in this codebase; a dropped-in file with no matching `<Stack.Screen>` entry doesn't get the shared header) — deliberately named `activity.tsx`, distinct from the pre-existing unrelated `activity-log.tsx` (the undo feature, untouched).

`MiniContentCard.basePath`'s closed union gained `"/profile"` (mirrors what `ContentCard.basePath` already included) — the target route `profile/content/[type]/[id]` already existed, so this was a type-only change.

**Cleanup**: `ProfileOverviewTab.tsx` deleted entirely (not edited in place) — of its ~230 lines, only the two Favorites rails survived, moved verbatim into `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx`'s Favorites body; the Watched List rail, Watchlist rail, and the entire network-activity section (`feedItems`/`getFeed()`/`FeedItemRow` — the explicit removal target) were all superseded by the new category-tab bodies. Confirmed via grep before deleting that nothing else imported it — `PublicProfileOverviewTab.tsx` (Public Profile's own, separate, untouched component) only shares a similar name, not a shared file. Home's own `getFeed()` usage (`ContentTypeSection.tsx`) is completely unaffected — confirmed it imports nothing from this file/component tree.

11 new i18n keys across all 12 locales (`"Go to page"`, `"This Week"`, `"This Month"`, `"No activity yet."`, and 7 per-type activity sentence templates), anchored on the existing `"Activity"` key via the established batch-insert script. Reused already-existing keys as-is where possible (`"Favorites"`, `"Watchlist"`, `"Watched List"`, `"Followers"`, `"Following"`, `"Joined"`, `"No bio yet."`, `"Your watched list is empty."`, `"Your watchlist is empty."`).

**Backend verification** (throwaway two-account setup — a second account was needed so the primary test account could like a review it didn't author): seeded one action per source (rate, review, like the other account's review, watched-list add, to-watch add, list creation, group join), confirmed `GET /me/activity?range=week` returned all 7 event types correctly sorted; confirmed `range=month` still included everything; backdated one seeded rating's `createdAt` 10 days via direct DB edit and confirmed it dropped out of `week` but stayed in `month`; unliked the review and confirmed the `review_liked` event disappeared; spot-checked `getContentReviews`'s `hasLiked`/`likeCount` were unaffected by the schema addition. Both test accounts and their seeded data fully cleaned up after.

**Also found and fixed mid-session, unrelated to the feature itself**: the backend's port-5000 listener was a stale, orphaned `node server.js` process (`PPID 1`) left over from an earlier `start-codespace.sh` run whose `pkill -f "nodemon server.js"` step killed the nodemon parent but not its already-detached child — the fresh nodemon instance from a later script run was alive but had never successfully bound the port (EADDRINUSE, silently idle, zero live worker child). This meant a chunk of earlier-session backend traffic was being served by pre-this-session code the whole time nodemon *looked* running. Killed the orphan directly and re-ran the startup script cleanly before doing any backend verification for this feature — worth checking `ss -ltnp`/process parentage directly (not just "is something responding on :5000") if a `start-codespace.sh` run ever seems to silently not pick up new code again.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro bundle grepped for all new component/service names plus confirmed `ProfileOverviewTab` (the deleted file) is genuinely gone — the only remaining bundle matches are `PublicProfileOverviewTab`, a distinct, untouched file that merely shares a substring in its name.

### Profile page follow-up: swap Cinegraphs/Analyses with WatchedList/Watchlist

User: swap where CineGraph and Watched List live, and separately swap where Analyses and Watchlist live. Concretely — Profile's outer 4-tab bar was `Profile | Cinegraphs | Lists | Analyses`; the "Profile" sub-tab's own 4 category icons (from the Instagram redesign above) were `Favorites | WatchedList | Watchlist | Activity`. After this pass: outer bar is `Profile | Watched List | Lists | Watchlist` (tapping either of the swapped-in tabs shows the actual full watched-list/watchlist **page**, not a preview), and the category icons are `Favorites | CineGraph | Analyses | Activity` (CineGraph gets a pie-chart icon — "yuvarlak parçalı chart" — Analyses gets a document/paper icon).

**Key implication that shaped the implementation**: the user's own wording — "bu bara basıldığında artık watchedlist sayfası gelecek" (pressing this tab now shows the watched list *page*) — meant the full `/watchlist` and `/to-watch` screens needed to render inline under these repositioned outer tabs, not a cut-down preview. This retired the whole 12-item `ProfileMiniGrid.tsx` preview-grid-plus-"Go to page"-button design built in the previous Profile redesign pass — that component is now dead (deleted; confirmed via grep it had no other consumers before removing it). Worth remembering: a UI element built for one arrangement of tabs can become fully obsolete, not just reposition, when the tab structure itself changes — don't assume "swap" means "just move existing pieces without checking whether one of them was built for a context that no longer exists."

**Extraction, mirroring the established `MyListsView` pattern**: `app/(app)/watchlist/index.tsx` and `app/(app)/to-watch/index.tsx` were previously self-contained screens (fetch + hydrate + `FlatList` + `RefreshControl`, ~115 lines each, near-identical). Extracted into reusable `src/components/WatchedListView.tsx` / `ToWatchListView.tsx` (`ListHeaderComponent` prop for the shared tab row, exactly like `MyListsView`'s existing precedent), leaving the two route files as thin 3-line wrappers. Also gave both a `basePath?: "/watchlist"|"/profile"` (resp. `"/to-watch"|"/profile"`) prop, defaulting to their own standalone route — **a real navigation-correctness fix caught before it shipped**, not an afterthought: `ContentCard`'s content-detail push needs to land in whichever tab's nested Stack the view is actually mounted under (this app's own established per-tab-Stack design, stated explicitly in `(app)/_layout.tsx`'s header comment) — a card pushed from inside Profile's embedded watched-list needs to push into `profile/content/[type]/[id]`, not `watchlist/content/[type]/[id]`, or back-navigation would silently jump the user to a different bottom tab. `profile/index.tsx` passes `basePath="/profile"` when embedding either view.

**`ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx`**: `Category` type changed from `"favorites"|"watched"|"watchlist"|"activity"` to `"favorites"|"cinegraph"|"analyses"|"activity"` (same 4 slots, only the 2nd/3rd swapped in kind). New props `cineGraph: CineGraphData | null` (threaded down from `profile/index.tsx`, unchanged fetch — just a different consumer). `ProfileCinegraphsTab`/`ProfileAnalysesTab` (plus its `ProfileAnalysisModal` + `analysisData`/`analysisModalVisible` state, previously owned by `profile/index.tsx` for the old top-level "analyses" tab) both moved to live entirely inside this component now, since they're only ever rendered from here. Icons: `pie-chart`/`pie-chart-outline` (CineGraph — literally a circular segmented chart, matching the user's own description) and `document-text`/`document-text-outline` (Analyses — a paper/report glyph, per the user's "kağıt" suggestion).

**`profile/index.tsx`**: `TABS`/`ProfileTab` relabeled (`"cinegraphs"`→`"watched"`, `"analyses"`→`"towatch"`, reusing the already-existing `"Watched List"`/`"Watchlist"` i18n keys as tab labels — no new keys needed). The single-tab early-return pattern already used for `"lists"` (`return <MyListsView ListHeaderComponent={tabRow} />`, bypassing the normal `ScrollView`+header wrapper) was extended to the two newly-swapped-in tabs (`return <WatchedListView .../>` / `<ToWatchListView .../>`), rather than shoehorning them into the existing `{activeTab === "lists" ? X : <ScrollView>...}` ternary — three sequential early returns read more clearly than nesting a 4-way ternary once a third "fully-embedded full-page tab" case joined "lists".

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for `WatchedListView`/`ToWatchListView`/`pie-chart`/`document-text`, all present; confirmed `ProfileMiniGrid` has zero remaining occurrences anywhere in the bundle. ### Watched List / Watchlist redesign: 4-column grid, Movies/Series sub-tabs, edit mode, sort/filter

User: `WatchedListView.tsx`/`ToWatchListView.tsx` (the shared view components behind `/watchlist`, `/to-watch`, and their embedded-in-Profile usage from the previous pass) should match Search's Movies grid — 4 columns instead of 2 — with a Movies/Series sub-tab bar right below the top (Movies default), an Edit button revealing a per-card "x" remove button, and a Filter button with sort/filter options (Alphabetical, Release Date, plus — Watched List only, since personal ratings only make sense there — Rated/Not Rated/Highest/Lowest Rating) that apply immediately on tap.

**No backend work needed**: `GET /api/users/ratings/:id` (`getUserRatings`) already existed and already returns every one of a user's `{contentId, contentType, value}` ratings in one call — it just had no mobile wrapper (`grep -rln "getUserRatings" mobile/src` returned nothing before this pass). Added a thin `getUserRatings(userId)` in `ratingService.ts` + `RATINGS.GET_USER_RATINGS` route constant — that's the entire "backend" side of this feature.

**No existing precedent for either new interaction, confirmed before building**: `ListDetailScreen.tsx`'s own "x" remove button (on `MiniContentCard`, reused verbatim here) is shown permanently for list owners — there's no toggleable edit-mode gating it anywhere in the app already, so the Edit-button-that-reveals-x-buttons interaction here is new UI, not copied from elsewhere (though it reuses `MiniContentCard`'s existing `onRemove` prop/badge styling as-is — no new remove-button visual needed). Likewise no sort-menu precedent exists — `ContentFilterPanel.tsx` (Search's genre/year filters) is multi-select checkboxes, a different shape from a single-select sort list — so the new filter panel borrows only its visual language (elevated `colors.base200` card, hairline row dividers, `colors.primary` for the selected state) from `ContentFilterPanel`, not its interaction model.

**New shared component `WatchlistGrid.tsx`**, since the amount of new logic (sort comparators, filter predicates, edit mode, sub-tabs, panel UI) would otherwise be duplicated near-identically across both pages a second time (mirroring why `WatchedListView`/`ToWatchListView` themselves were extracted last pass). Owns: `typeTab` state (Movies/Series, filters the grid to that content type), the Edit/Filter action row, an inline collapsible filter panel (toggle-visibility like Search's own filter panel, not a modal), and the 4-column grid itself — exact column math copied from `SearchContentGrid.tsx` (`GRID_COLUMNS=4, GRID_GAP=4, GRID_PADDING=16`). Sort/filter (`FilterKey`: `none`/`alpha_asc`/`alpha_desc`/`release_newest`/`release_oldest`/`rating_highest`/`rating_lowest`/`rated_only`/`not_rated_only`) computed via one `useMemo`, applied on top of the type-tab filter — `rated_only`/`not_rated_only` are true subset filters, the rest are comparators, missing/unrated values always sort last regardless of direction. `showRatingFilters: boolean` prop controls whether the 4 rating-based options even appear in the menu — Watchlist/to-watch never shows them.

**`WatchedListView.tsx`/`ToWatchListView.tsx` became thin data-layer wrappers** around `WatchlistGrid`: fetch + hydrate (unchanged from last pass) + (Watched List only) a parallel `getUserRatings(user._id)` call, wrapped in its own `.catch(() => [])` so a ratings-fetch failure never blocks the rest of the page, merged into each hydrated item as `rating: ratingMap.get(itemId) ?? null`. Remove handler calls the existing `removeFromWatchlist`/`removeFromToWatchList` then filters local state — no confirmation dialog, matching `ListDetailScreen.tsx`'s own established immediate-remove precedent for item-level (not list-level) removal.

`MiniContentCard.basePath`'s closed union gained `"/watchlist"`/`"/to-watch"` (both target `content/[type]/[id]` routes already existed, confirmed by the pre-4-column-grid `ContentCard` usage that already pushed there — type-only change).

10 new i18n keys (`"Filter"`, `"Default"`, 2 alphabetical variants, 2 release-date variants, 2 rating variants, `"Rated"`, `"Not Rated"`) across all 12 locales, anchored on the existing `"Edit"` key. `"Movies"`, `"Series"`, `"Edit"` already existed, reused as-is.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for `WatchlistGrid`, `getUserRatings`, and the new i18n strings, all present; no dev-log errors.
