**`user/[id]/index.tsx` restructure**: removed the outer `Profile | Cinegraphs` 2-tab bar and `activeTab` state entirely (nothing left to be a second outer tab now that Cinegraphs lives in the category row) — this screen is now a single scrollable view, not a tabbed one. Removed the old inline centered header block and its styles. All the Cinematch/Analyze state and handlers (`filters`, `matchResult`, `handleCinematch`, `handleAnalyze`, etc.) are completely unchanged — only *where* their JSX renders moved (into `ProfileHeaderInstagram`'s new `actionsSlot`), not the logic. The masked/private-account branch (`!profile.isAuthorized`) was left structurally as-is — a distinct minimal edge case with no bio/stats/categories to show either way, not something the user asked to redesign.

**5-across Favorites sizing, applied identically to both profile screens**: `ContentRail.tsx`'s `renderItem` prop widened from `(item: T) => ReactNode` to `(item: T, index: number) => ReactNode` (backward-compatible — the other 2 existing call sites, Home's `ContentTypeSection.tsx` and `network.tsx`, both declare single-arg callbacks and kept compiling unchanged, confirmed via `tsc` and a direct grep of both). Both Favorites call sites now compute card width via `useWindowDimensions` for exactly 5 columns with an 8px gap (replacing the old fixed `RAIL_CARD_WIDTH=110`), and zero out `marginRight` on the *true* last index of that specific array (`index === movies.length - 1`, not a hardcoded `index === 4`) so accounts with fewer than 5 favorites don't get a dangling trailing gap. Rail height became a proportional `Math.round(cardWidth * 1.5) + 60` instead of the old fixed 250 — a necessary side-effect fix, not an extra feature: the old fixed height would leave a large empty gap under the much-smaller new cards (~62-70px on typical phone widths vs. the old 110px).

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for `PublicProfileCategoryTabs`, `actionsSlot`, `goToNetwork`, all present; confirmed `PublicProfileOverviewTab` has zero remaining occurrences (no naming-collision risk this time, unlike the earlier `ProfileOverviewTab`/`PublicProfileOverviewTab` deletion which had to be checked against a substring match). No dev-log errors.

### Media: social sharing feed, Home→Media restructure, Profile drawer

The largest single feature built this session — a genuinely new "public post" concept the app never had before, built in 5 staged, independently-verified passes. User's own framing: the app needed to feel more like real social media, so Home became **Media**, split into **Paylaşımlar** (new — a deliberate-share feed with Facebook-style reactions, no comments) and **Keşfet** (the old Home, moved verbatim). Sharing a Profile Analysis, Review, or Recommendation is always via a pre-built card, never a freeform post composer, triggered from three existing content-creation points. Profile lost its outer tab bar again (single screen), gained a 3rd "Shares" stat and a "Your Sharings" category icon, and everything displaced (Activity, Watched List, Lists, Watchlist, Notifications, Settings) moved into the app's first-ever slide-out drawer.

**Stage 1 — backend (`Share` model, `shareController.js`, `shareRoute.js`).** New `Share` doc snapshots an analysis/review/recommendation at share-time (mirrors the pre-existing `Message.analysisData`/`contentData` snapshot convention used by DM sharing — never a live reference, so editing/deleting the original afterward doesn't affect an already-posted share). One reaction per user (6 Facebook-style emoji: like/love/haha/wow/sad/angry), re-tapping the same emoji removes it, switching emoji keeps the count at 1 — same one-entry-per-user shape as `Review.likeEvents` from an earlier pass, plus a cached `reactionCount` (mirrors `Group.memberCount`'s existing cached-counter pattern) so the Popular sort never has to count `reactions.length` per row. One `GET /shares/feed?sort=recent|popular|network&type=` endpoint serves both the Paylaşımlar screen and any future "load more," matching the established `getMyActivity`/`getFeed` one-parameterized-endpoint convention rather than three separate routes. Verified end-to-end with a throwaway account before any mobile work: all 3 share types, all 3 sort modes, the type filter, reaction add/switch/remove (count logic confirmed exact), ownership checks (can't share someone else's data, can't delete someone else's share), all clean.

**Real design correction found mid-implementation, not part of the original plan**: the plan's `createShare` for `type:"analysis"` was originally designed around an `analysisId` the backend would look up and snapshot server-side (verified ownership). Building the mobile wiring exposed that this was unreachable in practice — `getProfileAnalysis`'s response is the raw generated content only, no persisted `_id` is ever returned to the client, so the mobile `ProfileAnalysis` object genuinely has no id to send. Fixed by relaxing that one path to accept client-supplied `analysisData` directly — which, on inspection, is exactly how the already-shipped DM `analysis_share` message flow already works (`sendRichMessage`'s `analysisData` was never server-verified either) — so this wasn't a security regression, it was matching a trust model the codebase had already accepted for the identical data shape. Re-verified via curl before moving on. **Worth remembering**: a plan's data-flow assumptions (a client will "have an id available") should get a cheap concrete check (what does the actual existing endpoint actually return?) before the dependent backend code is written, not after — this one was caught during backend curl-testing itself, before it ever reached mobile, but only because verification happened before wiring, not after.

**Stage 2 — mobile plumbing.** `Share`/`ReactionEmoji`/`ShareFeedResult` types, `shareService.ts` (5 thin wrappers, same shape every other service file uses).

**Stage 3 — Home→Media restructure.** `(app)/_layout.tsx`'s `"home"` tab relabeled Media (`newspaper`/`newspaper-outline` icon). The entire former Home body (Movies/Series/Reviews/Lists 4-tab structure — unchanged internally, including Popular This Week/With Friends and the network Activity feed, both still living inside `ContentTypeSection.tsx` exactly as before) extracted verbatim into new `KesfetSection.tsx` — a pure move, zero behavior change, same extraction shape already used twice before in this app's history (Search's Movies+Series merge, Socials' Messages+Communities merge). New `home/index.tsx` becomes a 2-tab outer shell (Paylaşımlar default | Keşfet), same lazy-mount-then-`display:none` pattern this codebase already uses at 3+ other tab-shell sites. New `SharesFeedSection.tsx` + `ShareCard.tsx` — two independently-combinable single-select pill rows (Recent/Popular/Network scope, All/Analysis/Review/Recommendation type), reusing the exact tap-to-apply-immediately pill pattern from `WatchlistGrid.tsx`'s sort panel and `ProfileActivityPreview.tsx`'s Week/Month pills (that second component has since been deleted — see Stage 5). `ShareCard`'s hard requirements per the user: avatar+username top-left on every card (uses the shared `UserAvatar.tsx`, already tappable-to-profile — no new avatar code needed), review/recommendation additionally always show poster+title, analysis never shows a poster, no comment UI anywhere.

**Stage 4 — the three share-trigger points, which turned out to need two genuinely different UI shapes, not one.** Clarified directly with the user mid-planning: for Analysis and Recommendation, "existing sharing method" means the real DM/community picker (`UserSharePickerModal`) that already existed — Media is a true additional *destination*. For Review, there was no existing share mechanism at all — "existing way" just meant the review's normal default visibility (saved, browsable via Content Detail/Search/Activity) — so Media there is a true additional *toggle on Save*, not a second destination in a picker. Building one shared component for both would have forced an artificial destination-picker framing onto Review where none existed.
- New `ShareOptionsMenu.tsx` (2-row popover: "Send to a Person or Community" / "Share to Media") shared by `ProfileAnalysisModal.tsx` (replaces its old single Share-button-opens-picker flow — the DM path is byte-for-byte unchanged, only the button now opens this menu first) and Content Detail's new gift-box button.
- `ReviewComposer.tsx` gained a chevron next to Save revealing "Save Only" / "Save and Share to Media" — no picker at all, since reviews were never DM-shareable and aren't becoming so; a failed share-to-Media after a successful save surfaces its own toast rather than being folded into the save's own error path (the review itself did save correctly either way).
- **New Content Detail recommend entry point — confirmed via research this genuinely didn't exist anywhere before** (`ContentDetailScreen.tsx`'s action row had watchlist/rate/list/favorite/review buttons, no recommend button at all; the only existing recommend flow was a generic search-then-pick composer under Socials). New circular gift-box button (`Ionicons "gift-outline"`, size 22 — already this app's established icon for "recommend," reused from `MessagesSection.tsx`'s action row, not invented fresh) positioned so its own vertical center sits exactly on the poster's bottom edge, half overlapping — required introducing a new `position:"relative"` wrapper around just the poster `Image` (it previously had none, being a bare flex child of `topRow`), careful to keep `onLayout` on the Image itself rather than the new wrapper so the existing overview-line-clamping math (which depends on measured poster height) stayed correct. Tapping it opens the same `ShareOptionsMenu`; "send to a person" skips `recommend.tsx`'s search step entirely (the content is already known) and reuses the exact same `sendRichMessage(type:"recommendation")` fan-out that screen already uses.

**Stage 5 — Profile restructure: outer tabs removed (again), 3rd stat, Your Sharings, first-ever drawer.** `profile/index.tsx`'s outer `Profile|Watched List|Lists|Watchlist` tab bar (itself only added earlier this same session) removed entirely — single screen again, with Watched List/Lists/Watchlist relocated a second time, now into the drawer rather than outer tabs. `ProfileHeaderInstagram.tsx` gained an optional `shareCount` stat, non-interactive by design (no dedicated "all your shares" screen exists beyond the Your Sharings category tab one scroll away, so making it a dead tap target would be worse than a plain `View`). `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx`'s 4 icons became `Your Sharings (grid) | Your Favorites (heart) | Your CineGraph (pie-chart) | Your Analyses (document-text)` — Activity dropped from this row (now drawer-only), Sharings added as the new first/default tab (Instagram's own convention: the grid of your own posts is what a profile opens to). New `ProfileSharingsTab.tsx` — a simple capped (`getUserShares('me', 1, 30)`) list of `ShareCard`s, no infinite scroll, matching how the other 3 category bodies already render in-place inside the parent `ScrollView` without their own pagination.

**First-ever drawer in this app — `react-native-drawer-layout`, not a full Drawer-navigator.** The displaced items (Activity, Watched List, Lists, Watchlist, Notifications, Settings) live in completely different top-level tab Stacks, not as children of `profile/` — so this needed to be a slide-out **menu** that navigates elsewhere, not "a drawer of registered routes" in the Expo Router Drawer-layout sense. `react-native-drawer-layout` (the standalone gesture-driven primitive `@react-navigation/drawer` itself is built on) fits that directly without restructuring the route tree. `GestureHandlerRootView` root wiring already existed from the Lists-page redesign earlier this session — the drawer needed zero new root-level plumbing, just the one package install. Drawer state (`open`/`onOpen`/`onClose`) lives in `profile/index.tsx`; the hamburger button that opens it is supplied dynamically via `navigation.setOptions()` from inside `index.tsx` itself (the same dynamic-header-option pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase, e.g. `GenreDetailScreen.tsx`'s dynamic title) rather than statically in `profile/_layout.tsx`, since the button needs to reach state that only exists in the screen component.

**Cleanup, confirmed via grep before each deletion**: `ProfileActivityPreview.tsx` deleted (its only consumer was the now-removed Activity category-tab case; the full `/profile/activity` screen has its own independent implementation and never used this component). `SettingsButton.tsx` deleted (was only ever rendered in Profile's old static header; Settings is reachable via the drawer now, and grepping confirmed zero other importers — `NotificationBell.tsx` stayed, still used by 6+ other tab layouts).

Roughly 25 new i18n keys across all 12 locales this feature, added in batches per stage rather than all at once at the end (Media/Paylaşımlar/Keşfet tab names; Recent/Review/Analysis/Recommendation labels, reusing already-existing `Popular`/`Network`/`All`; the `ShareOptionsMenu`/`ReviewComposer` action labels; the `Shares` stat label) — deliberately staged so no literal-English fallback text was ever live for more than one implementation stage.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean after every stage (not just once at the end, given the size — this surfaced the `posterUrl: string|null` type mismatch in the recommend handler immediately rather than at the very end). Metro bundle grepped after every stage for that stage's new symbols; final full-app bundle fetch confirmed `ProfileActivityPreview`/`SettingsButton` (both deleted) have zero real occurrences (one harmless comment-string match, not an import). Backend fully re-verified end-to-end one final time after all 5 stages landed (all 3 share types, feed, `getUserShares`/share-count), and all test data — including one leftover analysis-share from the mid-implementation `analysisData` fix's own verification pass — cleaned up before finishing.

### Media polish pass: Instagram-post ShareCard, animated reactions, online-friends bar, filter redesign

Direct feedback round on the just-shipped Media feature (not a new planning cycle — same pattern as the CineGraph iterative-feedback rounds earlier this session): the share cards looked flat and low-signal, the always-visible 6-emoji reaction row looked "too plain," the 2-row/7-pill filter bar felt cluttered, and the user wanted an Instagram-Stories-style "who's online" bar at the top of Paylaşımlar.

**`ShareCard.tsx` rebuilt Instagram-post shaped.** Header (avatar + username + a colored, icon-led type badge — `sparkles`/accent for Analysis, `pencil`/info for Review, `gift`/warning for Recommendation — replacing the old plain gray subtitle text that wasn't grabbing attention) → full-width poster for Review/Recommendation (was a small 56×82 thumbnail beside the text; now the actual post image, matching the hard "poster must be prominent" ask) → a caption block below the poster (content title, star rating for reviews, then an Instagram-style caption line — bold username prefix + the review text, or the note/a "recommends this" fallback for recommendations) → the reaction bar.

**Reactions redone as a Facebook/Messenger-style animated picker, not a flat always-visible row.** Tapping the compact reaction button toggles a default "like" with a spring bounce (`Animated.spring`, scale 0.6→1); long-pressing pops a 6-emoji bubble above the button with a staggered spring entrance (`Animated.stagger`, each emoji scaling+translating in ~28ms apart) — picking one closes the bubble and bounces the main button to its new state. **Real layout bug caught and fixed before it shipped**: the card's `overflow:"hidden"` (originally there to clip the poster's corners) would have clipped this new absolute-positioned reaction bubble, since it pops slightly outside the card's own bounds above the button. Fixed by removing `overflow:"hidden"` from the card entirely — it was never structurally needed in the first place, since the poster sits between the header and caption blocks rather than touching the card's own rounded top/bottom edges, so nothing needed clipping to look right.

**New Online Friends bar (`OnlineFriendsBar.tsx`) — genuinely new backend capability, not just a UI addition.** Confirmed via grep before starting that no online/presence concept existed anywhere in this codebase. Added `backend/services/presenceService.js` — an in-memory, refcounted `Map<userId, connectionCount>` (refcounted so a user connected from multiple devices/tabs only flips offline once *every* socket disconnects), hooked into `chatSocket.js`'s existing per-connection `socket.user` (already authenticated there via JWT) with two new lines: `markOnline` on connect, `markOffline` on the socket's own `disconnect` event. New `GET /api/users/online` returns the caller's `following` list filtered to currently-connected ids. Explicitly a simple REST poll (fetched on mount), not a live socket-pushed feed — Media's feed isn't a real-time chat surface, and adding a new push-event type for this would have been more surface area than the feature needed. **Verified with a real Socket.io client connection**, not just curl: scripted a throwaway account connecting via `socket.io-client` with a real JWT, confirmed a following account's `/users/online` call showed them while connected and correctly showed empty immediately after disconnect — the refcount logic actually exercised, not just read.

**Filter bar redesigned from 2 rows / 7 bordered pills down to one row.** Recent/Popular/Network became a single sliding segmented control (one continuous rounded container, an `Animated.View` indicator spring-animates its `translateX` to the active segment's measured position, computed from the container's own `onLayout` width) — replacing 3 individually-bordered pills. The Analysis/Review/Recommendation type filter moved from a permanently-visible 4-pill row into a small icon-only button (`options-outline`, gets a red dot badge when a non-"all" filter is active) that opens a lightweight checklist popover — visible only when actually being used, rather than permanently taking up a row.

**A real, unrelated bug incidentally caught and fixed while verifying this round's Metro bundle**: `ProfileDrawerContent.tsx` (from the previous Media pass) was importing the deprecated core-React-Native `SafeAreaView` instead of `react-native-safe-area-context`'s (which this app already uses everywhere else, via the root `SafeAreaProvider`) — a live dev-log warning caught mid-verification, not something the user reported. Fixed to match the rest of the app's established convention.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout. Metro bundle grepped for every new symbol after each edit; backend presence tracking verified with an actual live socket connection (not just static curl) before any mobile wiring. All test accounts/data cleaned up.

### Media header slim-down + capsule-shaped Paylaşımlar/Keşfet switcher

More direct feedback on Media: the header (full "Cinephix" wordmark, centered) felt too heavy, and the Paylaşımlar/Keşfet switcher (an underline tab bar) should become a small, content-hugging pill instead of a full-width bar.

**Header** (`home/_layout.tsx`): dropped the "inephix" text entirely, kept just the logo glyph, moved it to `headerLeft` (was a centered `headerTitle`). `headerTitleAlign`/the wordmark `Text`/`View` wrapper all removed as now-dead code.

**New `MediaTabSwitcher`** (inlined in `home/index.tsx`, replacing the old underline-tab-bar `TABS.map` row): a small pill — the *inactive* side shows only its icon (`grid-outline` for Paylaşımlar, `compass-outline` for Keşfet), the *active* side shows the page name as text instead of its icon, with a solid `colors.primary` "window" background. **Implementation choice worth remembering**: this was first drafted as manual `Animated.Value` tracking of each slot's `onLayout` position/width (mirroring the Recent/Popular/Network segmented control from the previous Media round) — but realized before writing any of that code that it's the wrong tool here, because *both* slots' sizes change on every tap (icon↔text swap on both sides simultaneously), which the fixed-3-segment control never had to deal with. Switched to `LayoutAnimation.configureNext()` right before the state flip instead: since the "window" here is just the active slot's own background color (no separate overlay element), one `LayoutAnimation` call makes React Native animate icon/text swap, slot resize, and the whole capsule's width change all together automatically — no manual measurement, no correction-lag on the first frame the manual approach would have had. Far less code than the alternative, and the exact "sliding window across a dynamically-resizing capsule" look the user asked for falls out of it for free.

**Online Friends bar — confirmed working, not a bug, via a real live test, not just re-reading the code.** The user reported not seeing it; the code was already correctly wired in (verified by grep), and the actual cause is by design — `OnlineFriendsBar.tsx` renders nothing at all when zero followed accounts currently hold a live socket connection, which is a very likely real state for a solo tester. Rather than just asserting this, registered a fresh throwaway account, held a real `socket.io-client` connection open in the background, and had a second throwaway account follow+query `/users/online` — confirmed the backend still correctly reports it online right now, mid-session, with no backend restart in between. **User chose to keep the fully-hidden empty state as-is** (matches Instagram's own convention) rather than adding a visible "no one online" placeholder — decision explicitly asked and answered, not assumed.

### Same-day correction: switcher moved into the header, real sliding window, muted-gray palette

Immediate follow-up feedback on the capsule switcher above, before moving to any other task: (1) it should live *inside* the header itself (centered between the logo and notification bell), not as its own row below the header; (2) the "window" needs to visibly slide across, not flip on instantly; (3) both the capsule and the window should be muted gray, not the primary-tinted look from the first pass.

**Real bug in the first pass, worth naming precisely**: `LayoutAnimation.configureNext()` animates *layout* properties (position, size, opacity) — it does not smoothly interpolate `backgroundColor`. Since the "window" in the first version was implemented as the active slot's own background color turning on/off (no separate element), the color itself just snapped instantly even though the surrounding icon↔text resize animated fine — which is exactly the "bir anda seçiliyor" (selects all at once) the user was describing. Confirmed independently while checking this round's dev log: `setLayoutAnimationEnabledExperimental is currently a no-op in the New Architecture` — this app runs on the New Architecture (Fabric), where that legacy Android LayoutAnimation-enable flag is already a no-op, another reason to prefer `Animated` directly over `LayoutAnimation` here rather than debug around it.

**Fix: a real separate `Animated.View` window**, not a background-color toggle — `translateX` and `width` both driven by `Animated.timing`, targeting the currently-active slot's own measured `onLayout` position/size. This guarantees visible continuous motion regardless of what's changing underneath (icon↔text swap, resize, whatever), since `Animated` is explicitly interpolating position/size values frame-by-frame rather than hoping a property crossfades. First-ever measurement on mount snaps immediately (no undesirable grow-from-0 animation); every subsequent tab switch animates over 260ms.

**Header placement**: the switcher moved from `home/index.tsx`'s screen body into `home/_layout.tsx`'s `headerTitle` slot — set dynamically via `navigation.setOptions()` from inside `index.tsx` itself (identical pattern to Profile's drawer hamburger button from the earlier Media round), since the switcher needs the screen's own `outerTab` state, which a static `_layout.tsx` option can't reach. `headerTitleAlign: "center"` added back to center it between the already-set `headerLeft` (logo) and `headerRight` (notification bell).

**Colors**: both the capsule background and the window derive from `colors.placeholder` (this palette's own muted-gray-ish token, present in every theme) via a small `hexToRgba()` helper — capsule at low opacity (0.16), window more opaque (0.5) — rather than the previous pass's `colors.primary`-tinted look, and rather than a hardcoded universal gray that would ignore per-theme tone.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for the new symbols; confirmed the `setLayoutAnimationEnabledExperimental` warning is gone from the code (a stale log line from the just-replaced version, not a live issue) and no other new warnings appeared.

### ShareCard: square posters, promotional recommendation captions, StackedAvatars-style reaction stack

Third feedback round on Media's cards in the same day: posters were too large (should be square, Instagram-post shaped), the content title line was redundant, recommendation shares needed punchier "ad-style" copy instead of a flat title/fallback, and the 6-emoji reaction row should become an overlapping-circle stack (explicitly: "the same look Popular This Week uses for its stacked adder avatars") that expands into a picker on tap rather than sitting flat and always-spread.

**Square poster, no new dependency.** Movie/series posters are natively 2:3 (portrait), not square — letterboxing them into a 1:1 frame without cropping needed a backdrop behind the full, uncropped poster. Used React Native's own built-in `Image` `blurRadius` prop (no `expo-blur`, which isn't installed) — two stacked `Image`s in a square frame: one `resizeMode="cover"` + `blurRadius={22}` filling the whole square as a blurred backdrop (plus a dark tint layer for contrast), the other `resizeMode="contain"` on top showing the complete, un-cropped poster centered — the same trick Spotify/Apple Music use for non-square album art in square tiles.

**Caption rewrite**: the separate bold content-title line was dropped entirely (redundant with the poster itself now being the visual focus). Review captions are unchanged (the actual review text is real, specific content — the "ad-style" note didn't apply there). Recommendation captions became two new full-sentence templates (movie/series separately, not a single template interpolating a bare noun, since case-inflected languages like Turkish/Russian/Arabic can't cleanly drop a generic noun into an arbitrary sentence slot) — falls back to this promotional copy only when the sharer left no custom `note`. **Incidental cleanup**: this replaced the only call site of the earlier `"{{user}} recommends this"` key, so that key was removed from all 12 locales rather than left as dead i18n content — caught the removal-during-insertion collision on the first attempt (the batch-insert script's own `current_locale` reset from a same-pass insertion was clearing the state the removal check also depended on when the two touched the same locale block), fixed by doing the removal as a fully separate, unconditional pass.

**Reaction picker reworked around `StackedAvatars.tsx`'s exact visual grammar** (overlapping circles, `marginLeft`-based stacking, background-colored border for the "cutout" look) — applied to emoji instead of avatars. A "trigger" circle sits in front (empty `thumbs-up-outline` when you haven't reacted yet, otherwise whichever emoji you picked), with the 7 reaction options (❤️🔥👍😊👎😠😴 — the set itself changed too, replacing the earlier Facebook-6) fanned in tight slivers directly behind it via one shared `Animated.Value` driving both each option's `left` position and the whole container's `width` (collapsed→expanded) together, so nothing needs separate correction-lag handling. Tapping the trigger spreads the fan into a full row; tapping one of the revealed options bounces the trigger (spring scale 1.5→1) and collapses the fan back with the newly-picked emoji now shown up front.

**Backend enum change, needed since the reaction set itself changed**: `Share.reactions.emoji`'s enum and `reactToShare`'s validation list both updated from the old 6 values to the new 7 (`heart/fire/thumbs_up/happy/thumbs_down/angry/sleepy`). Verified via curl that the new set is accepted and the *old* values now correctly 400 as invalid — this is a genuinely breaking change for any already-stored reaction using the old enum, but there was no real production data yet (this whole feature shipped earlier the same session), so no migration was needed; flagging the shape of this risk for the future regardless, since a reaction-set change after real usage exists would need an actual data migration, not just a silent enum swap.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean (one real fix along the way: `StyleSheet.absoluteFillObject` isn't in this RN version's type defs — used `StyleSheet.absoluteFill` as a style-array value instead, which is the more idiomatic form anyway). Metro bundle grepped for every new symbol; the two warnings visible in the dev log during this round's own check (`SafeAreaView deprecated`, `setLayoutAnimationEnabledExperimental no-op`) were confirmed stale — both come from code already fixed/removed in the two immediately-preceding rounds, re-verified via direct grep of the current source finding zero remaining references to either.

### Same-day follow-up: poster crop-and-cover instead of letterbox, tap-to-reveal Details button

Fourth feedback round on the same `ShareCard.tsx` poster block: the blurred-backdrop + `resizeMode="contain"` letterbox trick from the round immediately above was rejected — the ask was simpler, don't try to fit the whole poster in the square at all, let it crop naturally to whatever fills the frame. Cropping is explicitly fine ("kırpılmış görünmesi sorun değil hatta amaç o").

**Poster rendering simplified to one `Image`, `resizeMode="cover"`**, filling the square frame — no blurred backdrop, no dark contrast tint, no second contain-mode layer. The whole three-layer trick from the previous round is gone.

**New interaction model, replacing tap-poster-to-navigate directly**: the poster sits under a semi-transparent black tint (`rgba(0,0,0,0.55)`) by default. Tapping the poster fades that tint out (`Animated.Value` driving `opacity`, native-driven, 200ms) and reveals a centered pill-shaped "Detail" button (reused the existing `"Detail"` i18n key already translated in all 12 locales — grepped first, confirmed present, avoided adding a duplicate key). Tapping the poster again while revealed fades the tint back in. Only tapping the Detail button itself calls `goToContent()` — tapping the poster background no longer navigates directly, it only toggles the reveal.

**Nested-Pressable pattern**: the Detail button is a `Pressable` inside a `pointerEvents="box-none"` wrapper, itself inside the poster's own `Pressable`. RN's touch responder system gives the innermost handler the touch (unlike DOM bubbling), so tapping the button doesn't also fire the outer poster's `toggleReveal` — confirmed via bundle grep + dev-log check that no double-fire warnings appeared, no `stopPropagation` workaround needed.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for `toggleReveal`, `detailsButtonWrap`, `detailsButton`, `posterTint` — all present; the old `blurRadius={22}` two-Image trick's call site is gone from `ShareCard.tsx` (remaining `blurRadius` hits in the bundle come from unrelated screens elsewhere in the app). Dev log clean, no new warnings.

### Same-day, fifth round: shorter poster frame, caption moved above the poster, no reaction-picker peek, reactor avatars + count

Fifth feedback round on `ShareCard.tsx` the same day. Four independent changes:

**Poster frame no longer square.** `posterFrame`'s `aspectRatio` went from `1` to `1.2` — a modestly shorter rectangle (not a big change, "biraz küçültelim dikeyde"). The card itself isn't constrained to be square, only the poster frame was; this only touches that one style value, the crop-and-cover rendering from the round above is otherwise unchanged.

**Caption moved above the poster, and made bold.** The `captionBlock` JSX now renders before `posterFrame` instead of after (header → caption → poster → footer). `caption`'s style gained `fontFamily: fonts.bold` (previously only the leading username fragment was bold via `captionUsername`; now the whole caption line is).

**Reaction-picker collapsed state no longer peeks a sliver of the next emoji behind the trigger.** The previous round's StackedAvatars-style fan had each option's collapsed `left` offset by `COLLAPSED_STEP` per index, so the first option (heart) visibly peeked out from behind the thumbs-up trigger at rest — user found this specific peek unwanted (trigger alone should be the entire collapsed view; the fanned circles should only become visible once actually expanded). Fixed by collapsing every option's `left` to `0` (exactly behind the trigger, fully hidden — trigger's `zIndex:100` keeps it on top) and shrinking `collapsedWidth` down to just `CIRCLE`; `COLLAPSED_STEP` is gone, unused. The spread-open animation on tap is unchanged.

**New: reactor avatars + total count, bottom-right of the footer row.** Requested explicitly in the same visual language as Popular This Week's "who added this" stack (`AddedByCard.tsx` → `StackedAvatars.tsx`). This needed real backend work, since `getShareFeed`/`getUserShares` previously stripped the whole `reactions` array from the response (`reactions: undefined`) and returned only `reactionCount`/`myReaction` — no reactor identity ever reached the client. Both endpoints in `shareController.js` now add `.populate("reactions.user", "username profile_pic_url")` (Mongoose supports populating a ref field nested inside an array-of-subdocuments path directly) alongside the existing `.populate("user", ...)` for the share's own author, and return a new `topReactors: FeedUserRef[]` (first 3 reactions' populated user, dedup not needed since reactions are already one-per-user) next to `reactionCount`. `Share` type in `mobile/src/types/index.ts` gained `topReactors: FeedUserRef[]`. `ShareCard.tsx`'s footer became `justifyContent:"space-between"`: `ReactionPicker` stays left, a new right-side `reactorsRow` renders `<StackedAvatars users={share.topReactors} size={18} />` plus the same `reactionCount` text that used to sit immediately after the picker (moved, not duplicated).

**Backend verified via live curl before any mobile wiring**: two throwaway accounts (register → force `isEmailVerified` → login), A created a real recommendation share against a real `Movie` doc, B reacted with `fire`, then fetched the feed as A and confirmed `topReactors` contained B's populated `{_id, username, profile_pic_url}` correctly. Test share and both accounts deleted afterward.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for `reactorsRow` and `topReactors`, both present. Dev log clean, no new warnings.

### Same-day, sixth round: the 7-emoji reaction system is gone — Instagram-style like + a new view-tracking feature

Sixth feedback round the same day, the largest of the day: the whole reaction feature (7 emoji, `StackedAvatars`-style fan picker) built earlier this same day was retired outright in favor of a single Instagram-style like, and a genuinely new feature — per-post view tracking with its own viewer-avatar stack — was added in its place on the footer's right side. Caption usernames also became tappable profile links.

**`reactions`/`reactionCount` removed from `Share.js` entirely** (not deprecated, deleted — the feature had shipped only hours earlier in the same session with no real user data to migrate). Replaced with two independent, much simpler fields: `likes: [ObjectId]` (mirrors `Review.likes`'s existing plain-ref-array shape) + cached `likeCount`, and `views: [ObjectId]` + cached `viewCount`. `views` is a plain ref array rather than reactions' old `{user, emoji}` subdocument shape specifically so it populates directly (`.populate("views", "username profile_pic_url")`) without the nested-array-path populate reactions needed.

**Two new endpoints replace `POST /:id/react`**: `POST /:id/like` (`toggleShareLike`) — simple toggle on/off, mirrors `reactToShare`'s existing add/remove-by-index shape but without the emoji-switch branch (there's only one "type" of like now). `POST /:id/view` (`registerShareView`) — deliberately idempotent per user: only pushes to `views` and increments `viewCount` the *first* time a given user is seen; a repeat call (e.g. the same `ShareCard` re-mounting while scrolling a `FlatList`) is a safe no-op, not a double count. `getShareFeed`/`getUserShares` now return `liked: boolean`, `likeCount`, `viewCount`, and `topViewers: FeedUserRef[]` (first 3 populated viewers) instead of `myReaction`/`reactionCount`/`topReactors`.

**`ShareCard.tsx` footer rebuilt**: left side is a plain `Ionicons` heart (`heart-outline` at rest, filled `heart` in `colors.error` once liked) with a small spring bounce on tap (same bounce mechanic the old reaction trigger used) plus the like count next to it — no picker, no fan, no expand/collapse state at all; the entire `ReactionPicker` function and its `REACTIONS`/`REACTION_GLYPH`/`CIRCLE`/`EXPANDED_SLOT` constants are gone. Right side keeps the exact layout shape from the round directly above (`StackedAvatars` + a count) but re-pointed at `topViewers`/`viewCount` instead of reactors, with a new `eye-outline` icon added between the avatars and the number (the round above had no icon there at all — this was a real addition, not a rename) since the user asked specifically for "sembolünü göz yap" once the right side stopped being reaction-scoped.

**New: view registration fires from `ShareCard` itself**, not from the parent feed/tab component — a `useEffect` on mount calls `registerShareView(share._id)` (fire-and-forget, errors swallowed) once per mount. This was a deliberate choice over threading a callback prop through both `SharesFeedSection.tsx` and `ProfileSharingsTab.tsx` (the card's two current consumers): since the idempotent-per-user contract lives entirely server-side, `ShareCard` calling its own view-registration endpoint needs no coordination with whichever screen happens to be rendering it, and both consumers automatically get view tracking for free without their own wiring.

**New: caption usernames became colored, tappable profile links** (`router.push(\`/user/${share.user._id}\`)`, the same route `UserAvatar.tsx`'s own avatar tap already uses elsewhere in the app — confirmed via grep before assuming the route shape, not guessed). Since a recommendation's caption is one fully-interpolated translated sentence (`t(key, {user: username})`), not separate JSX nodes, making just the username tappable+colored needed a small new helper, `renderCaptionWithUserLink()` — finds the literal username substring inside the final caption string and splits around it into `[plain][Text onPress, colored][plain]`, reused by both the review caption (`${username} ${reviewText}`, always finds it at index 0) and the recommendation caption (finds it wherever the sentence template placed it). Falls back to the plain, unlinked caption when the username genuinely isn't present in the text — the one real edge case being a recommendation share with a custom `note`, where the caption is the raw note text and never mentions the sharer by name at all (pre-existing behavior, unrelated to this round).

**Backend verified via live curl before any mobile wiring, more thoroughly than usual given the size of the change**: two fresh throwaway accounts, A created a real recommendation share, then confirmed the new document shape (`likes:[], likeCount:0, views:[], viewCount:0`, no `reactions` field at all). B liked it (`likeCount→1, liked:true`), unliked it (`→0, false`), liked it again (`→1, true`) — confirmed the toggle cycles correctly both ways. B called `/view` twice in a row — confirmed `viewCount` stayed at `1` on the second call (the idempotency contract actually holds, not just assumed). Fetched the feed as A and confirmed the full response shape: `liked:false` (correctly scoped to A, who never liked it), `likeCount:1`, `viewCount:1`, `topViewers` containing B's populated `{_id, username, profile_pic_url}`. Both accounts and the test share deleted afterward. One incidental note: editing the controller and route file in two separate steps briefly left nodemon crashed on a stale import (`reactToShare` no longer exported) between edits — self-healed the moment the route file's own edit landed a few seconds later; not a real bug, just an artifact of editing dependent files sequentially rather than atomically, caught immediately via the dev log rather than assumed fine.

**Worth remembering**: when a request removes a whole feature and replaces it with a simpler one in the same pass (not just changing behavior), check every file that imported the removed feature's exports (grepped `ReactionEmoji`/`reactToShare`/`myReaction`/`reactionCount`/`topReactors` across the whole `mobile/` tree here, not just the file being actively edited) — a feature built and shipped earlier the same day can still have picked up more call sites than expected by the time it's torn out.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for `onToggleLike`, `registerShareView`, `toggleShareLike`, `renderCaptionWithUserLink`, `eye-outline`, `heart-outline` — all present; `ReactionPicker` confirmed gone (zero hits). Dev log clean, no new warnings.

### Same-day, seventh round: Review posts redesigned — no poster, a two-line "shared a review on {title}" + quoted review text, both username and title as colored links

Seventh feedback round the same day, scoped specifically to Review-type `ShareCard`s (Recommendation and Analysis cards untouched this round). Three changes:

**No poster for Review shares anymore.** The `posterFrame` block's render condition narrowed from `share.type === "review" || share.type === "recommendation"` to `share.type === "recommendation"` only — Review cards no longer show any poster/image at all, just text.

**New two-line caption specifically for Review**, replacing the old single-line `"{username} {reviewText}"`: line 1 is bold, a new i18n-templated sentence — `"{{user}} shared a review on {{title}}."` (new key, added across all 12 locales via the established anchor-insert script, anchored on the existing `"Have you watched this series yet?..."` key) — with **both** the username and the content title rendered as separate colored, tappable spans (username → that user's profile, title → the content's detail page, reusing `goToContent()`). Line 2 is the actual review text itself, wrapped in literal straight quotes (`"..."`) and rendered in a new non-bold italic style.

**Real italic needed a real italic font, not just `fontStyle:"italic"`.** This app only had `DMSans_400Regular`/`_500Medium`/`_700Bold` loaded (`app/_layout.tsx`'s `useFonts()`); setting `fontStyle:"italic"` on a custom font family with no bound italic face is a known RN/iOS gap — it silently renders upright on iOS instead of synthesizing a slant, since the custom font has no italic glyph outlines for iOS to fall back to. Loaded the actual `DMSans_400Regular_Italic` face instead (already present in the installed `@expo-google-fonts/dm-sans` package, just not yet imported) and added it to `useFonts()` + a new `fonts.italic` token in `mobile/src/theme/typography.ts`, then used `fontFamily: fonts.italic` directly on the quote style rather than a `fontStyle` prop — guarantees the review quote actually renders slanted on every platform instead of depending on synthetic-italic support that this app's custom fonts don't reliably get.

**`renderCaptionWithUserLink()` generalized into `renderCaptionWithLinks()`**, since Review's caption line now needs two independently-tappable substrings (username *and* title) in the same sentence, not just one. New shape: takes an array of `{text, style, onPress}` link descriptors, filters to the ones actually present in the caption string, sorts longest-first (so a link text that happens to be a substring of another doesn't get matched partially), builds one combined regex, and splits the caption into an interleaved array of plain strings and tappable `<Text>` spans. Recommendation's caption (still just a username link) and Review's caption (username + title) both go through this same one function now.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle grepped for `renderCaptionWithLinks`, `reviewQuote`, `DMSans_400Regular_Italic`, and the new caption's literal text `"shared a review on"` — all present; the old `renderCaptionWithUserLink` confirmed gone. Dev log clean, no new warnings — this round touched font loading specifically, so the dev log was checked with extra care for any font-related warning, found none.

### `ShareCard.tsx` recommendation poster: full-bleed, edge to edge

The poster in Recommendation-type cards had visible side gaps — every current container renders `ShareCard` inside a 16px-padded parent (`SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s FlatList `list` style; the Profile Sharings modal's `modalOverlay`), and `posterFrame`'s `width: "100%"` was only ever 100% of that already-inset space. Fixed with the standard full-bleed technique: `marginHorizontal: -16` on `posterFrame`, canceling out the parent's padding so the poster spans the actual device width while the header/caption/footer around it stay inset as before. Since the two current containers didn't share the same padding value (`modalOverlay` was `padding: 20`, not 16), `ProfileSharingsTab.tsx`'s `modalOverlay` was split into `paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 20` — horizontal now matches the feed's convention so the negative margin lines up correctly there too, vertical breathing room around the modal card left untouched.

### Same-day correction: the full-bleed fix above only shifted the poster left, didn't actually grow it

Real bug, not a design disagreement — the user reported the poster now sat shifted toward the left with a visible gap still on the right. Root cause: `posterFrame` had *both* `width: "100%"` (a fixed width equal to the already-16px-inset parent) *and* `marginHorizontal: -16`. In RN's Yoga layout, a negative `marginLeft` on a fixed-width box shifts the whole box left (both edges move together, since width is pinned) — it does not grow the box. Only when width is left unset (falling back to the parent's default `alignItems: "stretch"` sizing) does a negative margin correctly *expand* the computed width symmetrically outward on both sides, which is what full-bleed actually requires. Fixed by removing the explicit `width: "100%"` from `posterFrame` entirely — `marginHorizontal: -16` alone, combined with `card`'s default column-flex stretch, now grows the box by 16px on each side instead of just relocating a fixed-size one.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Fresh Metro bundle built successfully. One unrelated dev-log ERROR appeared during this round's verification (`Can't perform a React state update on a component that hasn't mounted yet`) — investigated and ruled out as connected to this change: it carries no stack trace or component name, showed up while the app was actively running on a connected Android device (bundle-fetch-via-curl alone never executes component code, so it wasn't triggered by the verification fetch itself), and this edit only removed a `width` style property with zero state/lifecycle involvement — nothing in `ShareCard.tsx` calls `setState` synchronously during render. Flagged to the user rather than silently dropped; not chased further as part of this fix since there's no evidence tying it to this change.

**Same-day correction**: the first pass made *every* recommendation row full-bleed (`marginHorizontal: -16` on `recTopRow`/`recTeaser`/`recBottomRow`/`recPromo`, matching the poster). User: too far — only the poster should touch the true screen edge, everything else should keep some breathing room. **i18n**: the original single combined sentence (`"Have you watched this {movie|series} yet? {{user}} recommends it..."`) had to become 4 keys instead of 2, since it now renders in two separate places. Teaser halves stayed literal-English-text keys (`"Have you watched this movie yet?"` / `"...series yet?"` — genuinely different text, no collision). The promo half needed abstract keys instead (`recommend_promo_movie` / `recommend_promo_series`) rather than literal English text, because — unlike the teaser — the English promo text is *identical* for movie and series ("{{user}} recommends it — don't miss it..."), so it can't serve as two distinct object keys; splitting by literal text only works when the languages' text actually differs. Real finding while producing the translations: French, Italian, and German need genuinely different promo text between movie/series (gendered object pronouns — `le`/`la` in French, `lo`/`la` in Italian, `ihn`/`sie` in German — since "film" and "series" have different grammatical gender in those languages), while Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Turkish have identical promo text regardless of type (either no grammatical gender, or both nouns happen to share the same gender in that language). Kept two full separate keys for every locale anyway, even where currently identical, matching this session's established convention for exactly this class of problem (mirrors the earlier `movie_acc`/`series_acc` precedent) rather than trying to share one key across languages that don't actually need the split.

**Second same-day correction**: the bare avatar (no username, no type badge) above the poster read as too empty. Reverted the recommendation card's top area back to the exact same shared `headerRow`/`headerTextCol`/`username`/`typeChip` structure Review/Analysis already use — avatar, username, colored type badge stacked under it, `FollowButton` on the right — instead of the custom avatar-only `recTopRow`. The badge is no longer down in the footer at all (moved back to the header where it always lived); the footer now renders just the shared `likeViewRow` with no badge alongside it, matching Review/Analysis's own footer shape exactly. `recTeaser`/`recPromo` gained `paddingHorizontal: 12` (they'd had none since the full-bleed rows were undone) so they align with the now-reused header/footer's own 12px inset instead of sitting flush at the card's bare edge, 12px further left than everything above/below them. `recTopRow`/`recBottomRow` (both now unused) removed from the stylesheet.

### Real infra bug found after the GitHub push/merge: backend Codespaces port wasn't actually public, crashing the app on a phone

After pushing/merging the day's work and restarting via `start-codespace.sh`, the app failed to open on a physical device: a red screen (`OnlineFriendsBar.tsx:80`, `undefined is not a function` — `friends.map` on a non-array) plus a console error (`Chat socket connect_error: server error`). Not caused by the merge itself — root cause was `curl`-confirmed: the backend's Codespaces port-forward (`5000`) wasn't actually public even though the script had already run its `gh codespace ports visibility 5000:public` step — that command silently no-ops on failure (`|| true`), and this run it evidently didn't take effect. External requests (from a real phone in Expo Go, same as `curl` from outside the Codespace) hit GitHub's tunnel auth challenge (`401`, `www-authenticate: tunnel`) instead of the real API — explaining both symptoms: `getOnlineFriends()`'s REST call resolved (200-looking through Expo Go's fetch, but with a non-JSON/non-array body) instead of rejecting, and the socket.io handshake never reached the real server at all. Fixed by re-running the visibility command directly, confirmed via curl (`/api/health` → `200`, socket.io's polling handshake → `200`).

Two real fixes shipped, not just a one-off manual unblock: **(1)** `OnlineFriendsBar.tsx` now guards against exactly this failure mode — `setFriends(Array.isArray(res) ? res : [])` instead of trusting the resolved value is always an array, since a misconfigured tunnel can make a REST call resolve successfully with a garbage body rather than cleanly rejecting. **(2)** `start-codespace.sh`'s port-visibility step no longer silently trusts the `gh` command — it now polls the actual public health endpoint (up to 8 retries, re-issuing the visibility command each time) and prints a loud `WARNING` with the exact fix command if the port still isn't reachable after that, instead of printing a confident "Backend public URL: ..." line regardless of whether it's actually true.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `bash -n` syntax-checked the script edit. Fresh Metro bundle built successfully. Backend and socket.io both confirmed externally reachable via curl through the actual public URL post-fix.

### CineMatch redesigned from scratch: swipe gesture removed, filters are now the page itself, a CineGraph-caliber hero match ring + runner-up list

The largest redesign since Media. CineMatch used to be a Tinder-style `PanResponder` swipe stack (`SwipeCardStack.tsx`/`SwipeCard.tsx`) with a flat single-color percentage ring, filters hidden behind a top-right icon that opened a bottom sheet (`MatchFiltersModal.tsx`), and a "N of M swipes left today" daily cap. User's ask: drop the swipe gesture entirely, make the filter controls the page's *primary* always-visible content (not something opened via a button), and reach the same visual bar as `CineGraphDonut.tsx` (Profile's genre donut, this app's own acknowledged design high point) — because the page's actual purpose is simple: surface who you match best with, within your chosen filters, and that deserves a real result screen, not a picker queue.

**Real backend finding, not assumed — investigated by reading `matchController.js` directly before planning anything**: `computeMatchBreakdown` (deterministic, pure in-memory cosine-similarity/overlap math, no LLM, no network call) is the single scoring function already shared by the swipe queue, the one-on-one match endpoint, and the LLM-narrative `/analyze` endpoint. `getSwipeQueue` already called it per-candidate for up to 1000 users and already sorted by `matchPercentage` descending — it just destructured out only `matchPercentage` and threw away the full `breakdown: {collaborative, contentBased, social, diversity, bonus}` object every time. Surfacing it for every candidate (hero *and* runner-ups) cost nothing extra — no new bulk code path needed, just stopped discarding data already being computed. The LLM `/analyze` endpoint stayed completely untouched, out of scope — reserved for on-demand narrative commentary on one selected user, unrelated to this list.

**Two decisions confirmed with the user directly before building**: (1) the daily swipe-limit concept is gone entirely — unlimited browsing, only the filter *controls* stay Pro/Premium-gated (unchanged tier boundary). (2) despite dropping the swipe gesture, a small "not interested" affordance stays on the hero and every runner-up, reusing the existing reject+cooldown backend mechanism as-is.

**Backend** (`backend/controllers/matchController.js`, `backend/config/tiers.js`): `getSwipeQueue` now includes `breakdown` per candidate, dropped `swipesPerDay`/`swipesUsedToday` from its response. `swipeMatch` (accept/reject) dropped its daily-limit check block and `swipesRemainingToday` from its response — the `MatchDecision` recording and accept→follow/follow-request logic are untouched, still the same action the new hero/runner-up buttons call. The now-fully-unused `getSwipesUsedToday` helper and `swipesPerDay` tier field (confirmed via grep — no other consumer anywhere in backend or frontend) were removed outright, not just orphaned. Verified live via curl with two throwaway accounts: confirmed `breakdown` now returns per candidate, confirmed 11 consecutive `POST /match/swipe` calls all succeed (previously capped at 5 for free tier), confirmed the response shapes no longer carry the removed fields.

**New mobile components** (`mobile/src/components/match/`): **`MatchBreakdownRing.tsx`** — the hero visualization, built with the same techniques as `CineGraphDonut.tsx` (true animated SVG ring segments via `strokeDasharray`/`strokeDashoffset`, theme-token coloring, tap-to-reveal detail) but deliberately simpler structurally — CineGraphDonut solves a *variable*-genre-count layout problem (hence its chip-orbiting zone tables); this data is always exactly 5 fixed categories, so each gets a fixed equal-angle slot, no orbiting layout needed. Each segment's own arc fills to that category's 0-100 score independently (5 small progress arcs sharing one ring, not one pie divided by share-of-total like CineGraphDonut's genre slices) — grown in via the same dashOffset-animates-from-target-to-0 technique CineGraphDonut itself uses (animating `strokeDasharray` directly doesn't work with RN `Animated`, confirmed while building this). Selection happens via a legend row of 5 small chips below the ring rather than tapping the thin arcs directly — a far more reliable touch target than a few-degree-wide stroke, while keeping the same "tap to reveal a category's score + plain-language description" interaction CineGraphDonut made this app's default expectation. The matched user's `UserAvatar` sits centered inside the ring. **`MatchFilterStrip.tsx`** — replaces `MatchFiltersModal.tsx`'s sheet-behind-a-button pattern with an always-visible inline card at the top of the page (content-type segmented control, genre-matching mode + chip picker, the two signal switches), reusing `MatchFiltersModal`'s exact field logic but with no Apply button — every change calls `onChange` immediately, debounced 400ms before refetching (each change re-scores up to 1000 candidates server-side). Free tier sees the same layout dimmed and inert with a lock notice, rather than interactive-looking controls that the server would silently override anyway. **`MatchRunnerUpRow.tsx`** — compact list row reusing the existing simple `MatchPercentageRing` at small size (a 5-segment ring is illegible that small — the hero is the one place the fuller breakdown belongs).

**`match/index.tsx` rewritten**: slim header (archive/Rejected icon only — the filters icon is gone, the strip below is always visible now) → `MatchFilterStrip` → hero section (`MatchBreakdownRing`, username, bio, Follow + "Not interested" buttons) → "Next Best Matches" list (`candidates.slice(1, 5)`). Follow deliberately still calls `swipeMatch(..., "accept", ...)` directly rather than the generic `FollowButton`/`useFollowState` — this is the exact pattern the *original* implementation already had (`followGraph.applyFollow(...)` synced in after a successful swipe-accept, since `/match/swipe` bypasses the normal `/users/follow` path the shared `FollowGraphContext` cache otherwise learns about) — carried over unchanged, not reinvented. "Not interested" optimistically removes the candidate from local state immediately (the next-ranked candidate takes the hero spot) while the reject+cooldown decision records server-side. Pull-to-refresh added (`RefreshControl`), matching this app's other refreshable lists.

**Real mid-build catch, not assumed from the plan**: the plan initially said `MatchFiltersModal.tsx` would have zero remaining callers once the rewrite landed — grepping before deleting found this was wrong, `app/user/[id]/index.tsx` (Public Profile's separate one-on-one "Cinematch" compatibility widget, `getMatchWithUser`/`analyzeMatchWithUser` — a genuinely different feature, unrelated to the swipe/discovery page) still imports and uses it directly. Kept `MatchFiltersModal.tsx` completely untouched; only `SwipeCardStack.tsx` and `SwipeCard.tsx` (re-confirmed via grep to have zero remaining callers after the rewrite) were actually deleted.

**i18n**: 21 new keys across all 12 locales (established anchor-insert script pattern) for the new copy (section headers, empty/error states, filter strip labels, the 5 breakdown category names + one-line plain-language descriptions, the lock notice). Along the way, discovered several of `MatchFiltersModal.tsx`'s own existing keys (`"CONTENT TYPE"`, `"GENRE MATCHING"`, `"SIGNALS TO USE"`) had *never* actually been translated — a pre-existing gap in that file, unrelated to this round — added real translations for them now since `MatchFilterStrip.tsx` reuses the same literal key strings (didn't touch `MatchFiltersModal.tsx` itself, out of scope, but its shared keys are now translated as a side effect). Fixed one concatenation smell caught while writing this: the match-percentage badge was originally `{{percent}}% {t("Match")}` (two separately-translated pieces glued together with a hardcoded English word order) — changed to one full interpolated key, `t("{{percent}}% Match", {percent})`, avoiding the same "don't concatenate translated fragments" mistake this session already learned from earlier (the `movie_acc`/`recommend_promo_*` precedents).

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean on the first pass. Metro bundle grepped for `MatchBreakdownRing`, `MatchFilterStrip`, `MatchRunnerUpRow`, `Your Top Match`, and the percent/Match interpolation key — all present; confirmed `SwipeCardStack` fully gone. Dev log clean, no new warnings.

### CineMatch's filter section rebuilt as a genuine copy of CineGraphDonut — multi-select genre ring, Apply-All toggles, explicit "Find Your Match"

Immediate follow-up to the CineMatch redesign above: the user liked the overall rebuild but wanted the filter section specifically replaced with an actual copy of `CineGraphDonut.tsx` (Profile's genre donut) — matching happens *through* CineGraph data anyway, so picking filter genres by tapping the same visual already familiar from Profile is more coherent than a generic chip list, and reaches the same visual bar. Explicitly a copy, not a shared/parameterized component (`"cinegraph tasarımımı kopyalayalım"`, `"yapısını koruyarak kopyala"`) — and the right call technically too: `CineGraphDonut.tsx` is intricate and already-hard-won (positioning math, jitter fixes, rotation animation) that Profile depends on working exactly as-is; copying avoids any risk to it, while this context's interaction model diverges enough (multi-select, no rotation, empty center) that most of the *interaction* code wouldn't have been shareable regardless.

**New `mobile/src/components/match/CineMatchGenreRing.tsx`** — copies `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s zone tables, chip-positioning math (`chips`/`slices` `useMemo`, `maxRadiusForAngle`, `genreColor`/`hexLuminance`), and rendering verbatim, with three real, explicitly-requested behavior changes: **(1)** multi-select — `selectedGenres: string[]` + `onToggleGenre` props (controlled, not owned internally), any number of genres active at once, vs. Profile's one-at-a-time "view detail" selection. **(2)** no ring rotation at all — Profile's donut rotates the whole ring so a selected slice's angle aligns with its chip's angle before exploding it outward; here a selected slice just explodes *in place*, along its own resting angle (same `EXPLODE_OFFSET * cos/sin(angle)` math, minus the alignment step), independently per genre since several can be selected simultaneously — one `Animated.Value` per genre (`Record<string, Animated.Value>`, lazily created, synced to the `selectedGenres` prop via `useEffect` so an external change like "Apply All Genres" animates through the exact same path a direct tap does), not the single shared value the original uses. **(3)** empty center — no total-count summary, no genre-detail crossfade, no Detail button; this ring only picks filter genres, it shows no stats about them. Also doesn't early-return on "no data yet" the way `CineGraphDonut.tsx` does — a genre with zero watched items must still be selectable as a match filter, so the fixed-zone chip layout always renders (dimmed for absent genres) even with nothing to draw on the ring itself. `MATCH_GENRE_KEYS` (the two zone tables' own key sets) is exported so the filter panel's "Apply All Genres" can compute against the exact same genre set the ring renders chips for.

**`MatchFilterStrip.tsx` rewritten again** (same filename, third design this component has had today): `CineGraphSubTabSwitcher.tsx` (Profile's own Movies/Series capsule switcher, imported and reused directly, not reimplemented — same design the user pointed to) → a new info-note line explaining the page + the tap-to-filter mechanic → `CineMatchGenreRing` showing the viewer's own CineGraph for the active type → **Apply All Genres** / **Apply All Filters** toggle rows → the two signal `Switch` rows (kept from the previous round) → **Find Your Match**. The two Apply-All buttons' checked state is *derived*, not stored (`allGenresSelected = genres.length === totalGenreCount`, `allFiltersSelected = useCount && useAvgRating`) — manually deselecting even one genre after "select all" immediately reverts the button to unchecked with no separate sync logic, exactly the scenario the user described. This round also ends the previous one's live-apply/debounced-auto-refetch model entirely: nothing is selected by default anymore, and no search runs until "Find Your Match" is tapped — disabled/dimmed whenever nothing is selected (`!genres.length && !useCount && !useAvgRating`) for Pro/Premium/dev, but **always enabled for Free tier**, since the server silently forces its own default filters there regardless of what's shown, so the empty-selection guard would be meaningless for that tier.

**`match/index.tsx`**: fetches the viewer's own `CineGraphData` once on mount via the existing `getCineGraph(user._id)` (`mobile/src/api/userService.ts:47` — same call `profile/index.tsx` already makes for the exact same purpose) — this is what the new ring visualizes, unrelated to any search. Dropped the debounce/auto-load-on-mount entirely; a new `hasSearched` flag distinguishes "nothing searched yet" (a new, distinct copy line) from loading/error/empty-results, since a search genuinely never fires until the button is pressed now.

**Verified live via curl** (no backend changes this round, but `getSwipeQueue` and `getCineGraph` are now called from the same screen for the first time — worth actually confirming both work together rather than assuming): registered a throwaway account, confirmed `GET /users/cinegraph-data/:id` returns the expected `{movieStats, seriesStats, movieGenreRatings, seriesGenreRatings, isAuthorized}` shape and `GET /match/swipe/queue` still returns `breakdown` per candidate as before.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean on the first pass. Metro bundle grepped for `CineMatchGenreRing`, `MATCH_GENRE_KEYS`, `Apply All Genres`, `Find Your Match` — all present. Dev log clean (aside from the already-known, environment-level React Native DevTools library warning).

Checked state: circle fills `colors.placeholder` (gray, not the previous `colors.primary`), checkmark icon `colors.baseContent` for visible contrast against the gray fill — matches the exact "round, turns gray when pressed, checkmark should be a more visible light gray" ask.

**Two defensive fixes applied while verifying, not directly requested but caught mid-check**: a runtime `TypeError: Cannot read property 'slice' of undefined` appeared in the dev log right after this round's bundle fetch — no stack trace available, but `UserAvatar.tsx`'s fallback-initials code (`username.slice(0,2)`) is a very plausible match given this round added two brand-new call sites feeding it a `username` value (the ring's new avatar). ### Same-day: a real loading animation on Match press — chips collapse into the avatar, the ring spins, results auto-scroll into view

The user wanted pressing "Match" to feel like something is actually happening, instead of a generic full-screen spinner replacing the whole filter panel: genre chips move in a straight line toward the ring's center (the avatar) and fade out as they arrive, layered *behind* the ring/avatar rather than on top; at the same pace, the ring itself starts spinning clockwise; only once this settles do results load in and the page auto-scrolls down to them. Slow, deliberate motion was explicitly requested, not a snappy transition.

**`CineMatchGenreRing.tsx`** gained a `loading` prop and two `Animated.Value`s: `collapseAnim` (0→1, one-shot, `COLLAPSE_MS = 1300`) drives each chip's own `translateX`/`translateY` (interpolated per-chip from `[0,1]` to `[0, centerX - chipCenterX]`/`[0, centerY - chipCenterY]` — a straight line to the ring's true center) and `opacity` (fades out only in the animation's back half, `[0, 0.6, 1] → [restOpacity, restOpacity, 0]`, so chips visibly travel before vanishing rather than fading immediately); `rotateAnim` (0→1, looped via `Animated.loop` at the same `1300ms`-per-revolution pace, linear easing) drives a `rotate` transform on an `Animated.View` wrapping the whole `<Svg>` ring — since `centerX`/`centerY` already equal the box's exact visual center (`boxWidth/2`/`boxHeight/2`, confirmed from the existing layout math), wrapping just the Svg rotates the ring cleanly around the avatar with no extra transform-origin work needed. The loop keeps spinning for as long as `loading` stays true, independent of the one-shot collapse — a slow network just means a longer spin, never a stuck or cut-short animation. Layering fixed via explicit `zIndex` (`chip: 0`, ring wrapper: 1, avatar: 2) so collapsing chips visually pass *under* the ring and avatar, matching "katman olarak butonlar profil ve graphın arkasında olacak." Both slice taps and chip taps are disabled while `loading` (`pointerEvents="none"` on chips, guarded `onPress` on ring slices) so a mid-animation tap can't fire. When `loading` flips back to false, both animated values snap back to 0 instantly (not animated back) — acceptable since by then the user's attention has already moved to the auto-scrolled results below.

**`MatchFilterStrip.tsx`** threads a new `loading?: boolean` prop straight into `CineMatchGenreRing`, disables the Match button's `Pressable` while loading (without applying the "missing criteria" dim style, since being mid-search isn't the same disabled *reason*), and hides the disabled-reason note during loading too.

**`match/index.tsx`** now owns the orchestration: a new `matchAnimating` state (not the same thing as a raw network-loading flag) goes true the instant Match is pressed (`handleMatchSubmit`) and only flips back false after *both* `getSwipeQueue` resolves *and* `MATCH_LOADING_MS` (1300ms, matching the ring's own collapse duration) has elapsed since the press — computed as `Math.max(0, MATCH_LOADING_MS - elapsed)` so a fast response still waits out the full animation, and a slow one never gets cut short. The old full-screen `ActivityIndicator` branch is gone entirely — the ring animation *is* the loading indicator now, so while `matchAnimating` the content area below the filter panel renders nothing. Once it clears, a `useEffect` scrolls the `ScrollView` (`ref={scrollRef}`) down to `resultsY.current` — the results block's own measured Y-offset from an `onLayout` on its wrapping `View`, not a fixed guess, since the filter panel's own height varies. This made the old `loading`/`setLoading` state (which used to drive that spinner) fully dead, along with the `opts?.silent` parameter on `loadQueue` that only ever existed to suppress it during pull-to-refresh — both removed; pull-to-refresh now just calls `loadQueue(filters)` directly and still doesn't trigger the ring animation (it was never routed through `handleMatchSubmit`), preserving the original "silent background refresh" behavior with less code.

Dev log clean, no new errors after any of this round's fetches.

### Same-day bug-fix + polish on the loading animation: a real regression fixed, eased ring spin, a delayed reset, and a gap-fill disc

Direct itemized feedback on the round above, one real regression plus three polish requests:

- **Real regression, not a preference: genre chips/slices stopped being tappable at rest.** Root cause: the previous round wrapped the ring's `<Svg>` in an `Animated.View` (`ringWrap`, `zIndex: 1`) to drive its rotation — but that wrapper spans the *entire* box (same `boxWidth`×`boxHeight` as the whole ring+chips area), and with an explicit `zIndex` above the chips' own (`0`), it silently became an opaque hit-target across that whole rectangle, swallowing taps meant for chips positioned underneath it — even in areas where the SVG renders nothing visible. Fixed with `pointerEvents="box-none"` on that wrapper: the wrapper itself no longer claims touches, only its actual interactive children (the ring's `Circle` slices, which still have their own `onPress`) do, letting everything else fall through to the chips below exactly as before this whole animation feature was added.
- **Ring spin now eases in and out instead of snapping to/from a constant rate.** Replaced the single `Animated.loop` with a manual recursive spin (`spinLap`, re-triggered from its own `.start()` callback via a `spinningRef` flag) so the in-flight animation can be redirected rather than just stopped: on start, one `ROTATE_RAMP_MS` (500ms) lap with `Easing.in(Easing.quad)` (starts slow, accelerates) before the steady `ROTATE_MS`-per-lap linear loop kicks in; on `loading` flipping false, the lap in flight is redirected into a `ROTATE_RAMP_MS` `Easing.out(Easing.quad)` (starts fast, decelerates) run to `toValue: 1`, so it always lands cleanly on a 0°/360° seam instead of jerking to a stop mid-rotation.
- **Reset-to-rest delayed 1 second, matching "1 saniye beklesin."** The ring used to snap chips back to visible/at-rest the instant `loading` went false — visible mid-auto-scroll, which is exactly what the user didn't want ("bu keskin eski haline dönüşünü otomatik kayma esnasında görmemesi"). Now a `setTimeout(RESET_DELAY_MS = 1000)` holds the collapsed/hidden state before calling `collapseAnim.setValue(0)`/`rotateAnim.setValue(0)`, comfortably outlasting the page's own auto-scroll. A new `suppressInteraction` state (not just the raw `loading` prop) now gates chip `pointerEvents`/ring `onPress` and stays true through this whole delay window too — closes a real edge case where an invisible, still-collapsed chip would otherwise start accepting taps again the instant `loading` went false, before it was visually back home.
- **New `centerFill` disc fills the visible gap between the ring's inner edge and the (smaller) avatar.** Previously a collapsing chip would flash through visible background in that gap on its way to the center. A plain circular `View` (`radius = outerRadius - STROKE + 2`, `colors.base200`, 2px deliberately overlapping the ring's own inner edge to avoid an antialiasing seam) now sits there. Full stacking order, back to front: `chip (0) < ringWrap (1) < centerFill (2) < centerWrap/avatar (3)` — a collapsing chip passes under the ring's stroke, then disappears behind the fill well before it would ever reach the avatar.
