Metro bundle module for `CineMatchGenreRing.tsx` grepped and confirmed `suppressInteraction`/`spinLap`/`ROTATE_RAMP_MS`/`RESET_DELAY_MS`/`centerFillRadius`/`pointerEvents: "box-none"` all present. Dev log clean, no new errors after the fetch. Chip/slice tappability itself wasn't independently re-verified on a physical device this pass (bundle-fetch-via-curl doesn't execute touch handling) — the fix is a well-established, standard RN `pointerEvents` pattern for exactly this "decorative overlay shouldn't block touches to what's under it" situation, but flagging this transparently rather than overclaiming a live-device confirmation that didn't happen.

### CineMatch results view rebuilt from scratch: hero ring + list → a "profile cloud" of floating bubbles

A genuine from-scratch redesign of the *results* section (the old hero-ring-for-#1 + "Next Best Matches" list), planned via `EnterPlanMode` given the real scope (new layout algorithm, new idle animation, a new select/inspect/back state machine). Two placement questions were resolved with the user via `AskUserQuestion` before planning: Follow/Not-Interested buttons live directly below the enlarged/inspected profile, and tapping its username/avatar still navigates to `/user/:id` — both the recommended defaults.

**New files** (`mobile/src/components/match/`):
- **`matchCategoryMeta.ts`** — `CATEGORY_KEYS`/`categoryMeta()` extracted verbatim from the now-deleted `MatchBreakdownRing.tsx` (same 5 keys → `{label, desc, color}`: collaborative→Taste/primary, contentBased→Favorites/secondary, social→Social/info, diversity→Range/warning, bonus→Bonus/success), so the new bars view reuses the exact same labels/colors/descriptions instead of inventing new copy.
- **`MatchCloudBubble.tsx`** — one bubble: a thin *gray* progress ring (`colors.placeholder` fill / `colors.border` track, same "grow the stroke in" `strokeDasharray`/`strokeDashoffset` technique `MatchBreakdownRing.tsx` and `MatchPercentageRing.tsx` already used, just gray instead of `colors.primary`) wrapping a `UserAvatar`, percentage text *below* the ring (not inside it, unlike `MatchPercentageRing`), a gentle independent idle "drift" loop (`Animated.ValueXY`, random small target + random 1800-3200ms duration each lap, `Easing.inOut(Easing.sin)`, each bubble naturally desyncing from the others since its own first lap is randomly seeded — no manual per-bubble delay bookkeeping needed), and the transform slots (`selectTranslate`/`selectScale`, driven by the parent, only actually applied when that particular bubble is the selected one) that let the parent grow/move it during selection.
- **`MatchBreakdownBars.tsx`** — the 5 categories as stacked horizontal bars (label at the bar's start, animated `width` fill in the category's own color, staggered `Animated.stagger` fill-in on mount) with the exact same tap-a-row-to-reveal-its-description interaction `MatchBreakdownRing.tsx` used on its legend chips, just applied to bars.
- **`MatchResultsCloud.tsx`** — the orchestrator. Computes a non-overlapping "cloud" layout for the top-5 candidates (`computeCloudLayout`, `useMemo`-cached per result set so it stays *stable* across a whole select→inspect→back→select-another cycle, not re-randomized each render), renders a radial gray `RadialGradient` background (`Defs`/`RadialGradient`/`Stop`/`Circle` — same `Defs`/`Stop` shape `MatchFilterStrip.tsx`'s Match-button `LinearGradient` already established, first time `RadialGradient` itself has been used in this codebase, confirmed exported by the installed `react-native-svg` before relying on it) faint near the center and more intense toward the edge, and drives the select/inspect/back state machine.

**Cloud layout algorithm**: deliberately *not* rejection-sampling — with N fixed at exactly 5, a closed-form "ring-of-4-around-1" placement (#1 centered, #2-5 at a randomized global rotation + an angle/radius per outer bubble) guarantees non-overlap *by construction* and has no risk of an unbounded retry loop on a narrow screen. Sizing mirrors `CineMatchGenreRing.tsx`'s own `Math.min(screenWidth - 32, ...)` precedent. Bubble diameters follow `RANK_RATIO = [1.0, 0.82, 0.68, 0.56, 0.56]` (#1 biggest, #4/#5 equal, per spec). Non-overlap is enforced two ways: each outer bubble's radial distance from center has a `minDist` floor (`r0 + rI + MIN_GAP`) so it can never touch #1, and an *analytically computed* per-bubble angular jitter cap (derived from the worst-case geometry where two adjacent outer bubbles both sit at their own closest-to-center distance) so two outer bubbles can never rotate into each other either — degrades to a perfectly even, non-jittered diamond in a pathological narrow-screen case rather than ever risking a collision.

**Selection state machine**: tapping a bubble (`selectedId === null` only) runs an `Animated.parallel` — the tapped bubble's shared `selectTranslate`/`selectScale` animate it to a fixed left-edge target (`targetX`/`targetY`, computed once via `useMemo` and reused by both the animation *and* the detail-phase layout, so the two can never drift apart) over `MOVE_MS = 1300` with `Easing.inOut(Easing.ease)` — the exact same pacing constant this session already settled on for the match-loading ring (`MATCH_LOADING_MS`/`COLLAPSE_MS`/`ROTATE_MS`) — while `othersOpacity` fades every other bubble (and the gradient background, rendered inside that same opacity wrapper) to 0 over a quicker 250ms. Once settled, `phase` flips to `"detail"` and `detailOpacity` fades in the back button, bars, and username/bio/Follow row. The back button reverses it: bars fade out first, *then* the parallel translate/scale-back + a delayed (`delay: 700`) `othersOpacity` fade-in run together, landing back in `"cloud"` phase. `pointerEvents` is set explicitly per-bubble (`"none"` for non-selected bubbles once `phase==="detail"`) since opacity 0 alone doesn't block RN touches — a real gap this session already hit once with the genre ring's `zIndex` bug, called out explicitly here rather than left implicit. A small effect watches for the *inspected* candidate disappearing from the incoming `candidates` prop (a Not-Interested tap mid-inspection) and snaps straight back to the cloud with no animation, since there's nothing left there to animate.

**`match/index.tsx`** now just renders `<MatchResultsCloud candidates={candidates.slice(0,5)} onFollow={handleFollow} onNotInterested={handleNotInterested} followState={followState} />` in place of the old hero+list block; `useRouter`/`router` became unused there and were removed (profile navigation now lives inside `MatchResultsCloud` itself). `MatchBreakdownRing.tsx` and `MatchRunnerUpRow.tsx` are deleted — confirmed via grep each had exactly one importer (`match/index.tsx`, being changed) before deleting. `MatchPercentageRing.tsx` (the small single-value ring `MatchRunnerUpRow.tsx` used to reuse) is untouched — confirmed still live at `app/user/[id]/index.tsx:264`, Public Profile's separate one-on-one Cinematch widget, an unrelated feature. One new i18n key, `"Back"` (the detail panel's back-arrow accessibility label), added across all 12 locales via the established anchor-and-batch-insert script.

Root cause: the detail-phase wrapper (`Animated.View` holding the back button, bars, and username/bio/Follow block) had no `position: "absolute"` of its own — as a normal-flow child of `container`, it landed *below* the cloud-zone box (which occupies `cloudSize` px of real flow height above it) instead of sharing the container's true `(0,0)` origin that `targetX`/`targetY` and every child's own `left`/`top` were computed against. Its absolutely-positioned children then resolved their coordinates relative to that wrong, shifted origin — pushing them well outside the visible area, while the cloud itself had already faded to invisible (correctly) — reading as "the screen goes black." Fixed by giving both the gradient/bubble wrapper and the detail wrapper explicit `position: "absolute", left: 0, top: 0`, so every child in both phases shares the exact same coordinate origin the layout math assumes. Not independently re-verified on a physical device this pass (no crash trace appeared in `.dev-logs/expo.log` for the original report, and a curl bundle-fetch can't exercise touch/animation) — flagged transparently, the user should re-test on-device before this is considered fully confirmed.

### Same-day polish: the cloud spreads further horizontally (ellipse, not a circle), bubbles slightly smaller, a genuinely soft radial gradient

Three direct requests once the design itself was approved: the cloud read as too clustered toward the center horizontally (vertical spread was already fine, explicitly not to be touched), bubbles could be a touch smaller overall while keeping their relative size differences, and the gray background gradient didn't read as a soft/gradual transition.

**Cloud boundary became a real ellipse, not a circle.** `computeCloudLayout` now takes separate `cloudWidth`/`cloudHeight` instead of one `cloudSize`, and each outer bubble's `maxDist` is computed via the standard ellipse-radius-at-angle formula (`(a·b) / √((b·cosθ)² + (a·sinθ)²)`, using that bubble's own *base* angle as a good-enough approximation before jitter is applied) instead of one flat circular radius — giving bubbles near horizontal angles (0°/180°) meaningfully more room to spread than bubbles near vertical ones (90°/270°), exactly the "horizontal yes, vertical no" split requested. `cloudHeight` keeps the *exact same formula* this section always used (`Math.min(screenWidth - 32, 380)`) so vertical spread is provably unchanged, not just approximately similar. `cloudWidth` trims its own margin and raises its cap (`Math.min(screenWidth - 16, 480)`) so it reliably ends up wider than `cloudHeight` on any real phone — critical, since on most real device widths the *old* shared `380` cap rarely even triggered, meaning simply raising one shared cap wouldn't have produced any visible difference on a typical phone; decoupling the two values was what actually mattered, not the specific cap number. The 8px trimmed off `cloudWidth`'s own outer margin is made up for by `computeCloudLayout`'s own inner `EDGE_PAD`, so total clearance from the real screen edge is unchanged — bubbles still can't reach off-screen.

**Bubbles sized down slightly**: `bubbleBaseDiameter`'s multiplier dropped from `cloudHeight * 0.34` to `cloudHeight * 0.3` — `RANK_RATIO = [1.0, 0.82, 0.68, 0.56, 0.56]` untouched, so the relative size difference between ranks is exactly as it was, only the overall scale shrank.

**Gradient rebuilt for an actually gradual falloff**: the 3-stop version (`0.03 → 0.12 → 0.3` opacity) read as a coarse step rather than a soft one. Replaced with 6 stops (`0.02 → 0.05 → 0.1 → 0.18 → 0.26 → 0.34`) for a genuinely smooth ramp, and the fill shape itself changed from a `<Circle r={cloudSize/2}>` (which left hard, un-gradiented corners once the canvas became a non-square rectangle) to an `<Ellipse rx={cloudWidth/2} ry={cloudHeight/2}>` — `RadialGradient`'s default `objectBoundingBox` units mean the same circular gradient definition automatically stretches to match whatever the target shape's aspect ratio is, so this needed no extra math of its own.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle module for `MatchResultsCloud.tsx` grepped and confirmed `cloudWidth`/`cloudHeight`/`radiusAtAngle`/`ellipseA`/`ellipseB`/`Ellipse` all present, zero remaining `cloudSize`/`<Circle` references. Dev log clean, no new errors after the fetch (aside from the already-explained stale Fast-Refresh artifact from the previous round).

**Same-day correction: the gradient's direction was backwards for what "soft cloud effect" actually means.** The ellipse *shape* itself was approved and explicitly asked to stay unchanged going forward. But the gradient still read as "a sharp-edged gray oval," even after the 6-stop smoothing — because opacity had been increasing *toward* the edge (per the original per-round spec, low near #1, higher at the boundary), and any gradient that's still substantially opaque right up to a shape's own geometric edge will always show that edge as a hard boundary, no matter how many intermediate stops exist. The fix wasn't more stops, it was flipping the direction entirely: opacity now peaks softly near the center (`0.22`) and fades all the way down to fully transparent (`0`) *before* reaching the ellipse's own edge (last stop lands at `r="70%"` of the shape's radius, with everything beyond that held at that same fully-transparent value) — so the shape's boundary itself is never visible, only a soft glow that dissolves into nothing. This is the more usual meaning of a "cloud-like" radial effect (strongest at the core, fading to nothing at the edges) as opposed to the earlier round's literal reading of "low near the center, higher at the edge" — the user's own words on seeing it ("doygunluğu azalan bir efekt gibi görünmesi gerekiyor, şekil değil" — needs to look like a decreasing-saturation effect, not a shape) is what settled which reading was actually wanted.

### Same-day: the radial gradient background is gone — replaced with 4 thin gray lines connecting #1 to every other bubble

The gradient still didn't read right even after reversing its direction — the user decided to drop the background-glow idea entirely and asked for something different: 4 thin gray lines connecting #1 to each of the other bubbles, ends anchored at each bubble's own center, rendered *behind* the bubbles (not in front), purely decorative ("hiçbir işlevi yok, sadece profil bulutu havası vermek için"). The one real constraint: since bubbles idly drift, a line's endpoint has to track that live drift too, not just its static resting position — a straight line to a fixed point would visibly detach from a bubble mid-bob.

**Idle-bob ownership moved from `MatchCloudBubble.tsx` up into `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`.** Each bubble's own `Animated.ValueXY` for its idle drift used to be created internally via `useRef` inside `MatchCloudBubble` — now it's created and owned by the parent (`bobAnimsRef`/`getBobAnim(id)`, the same lazy-create-per-id pattern used elsewhere this session) and passed down as a `bobAnim` prop instead, so both the bubble's own transform *and* the parent's line-drawing code read the exact same live value — they can never drift out of sync with each other, by construction (one shared value, two consumers).

**The bob animation itself switched from `useNativeDriver: true` to `false`.** This was a deliberate, necessary tradeoff: the native driver only updates the specific native view it's directly attached to (the bubble's own transform) — a *different* native component (an SVG `Line`'s `x1`/`y1`/`x2`/`y2` numeric attributes) reading the same `Animated.Value` wouldn't see native-driven updates at all. Running the bob animation on the JS thread instead guarantees both consumers update together. Given the bob's own tiny amplitude (6px) and slow pace (1.8-3.2s per segment), JS-thread animation is imperceptibly different from native here — this is not a general "always avoid native driver" lesson, just the specific tradeoff this one shared-value setup required.

**Four lines, drawn with `Animated.add(basePosition, bobOffset)` for each endpoint** (`AnimatedLine = Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Line)`, `stroke={colors.placeholder}`, `strokeWidth={1}`) inside their own `<Svg>`, rendered as the *first* child of the cloud container (so bubbles, rendered after, naturally paint on top in default z-order — no explicit `zIndex` needed, matching "arkasında olsunlar"). The whole lines layer fades with the same `othersOpacity` value the old gradient used to, so it disappears/reappears in sync with the rest of the cloud during select/back transitions, with zero new fade logic needed. `pointerEvents="none"` throughout, same as the gradient before it, so the lines never intercept taps meant for bubbles underneath.

**Same-day follow-up: dotted instead of solid, dimmer gray.** `strokeDasharray="1, 4"` + `strokeLinecap="round"` on the same `AnimatedLine`s turns the short 1px dashes into visually round dots rather than little rectangular dashes; `strokeOpacity={0.35}` (on top of the already-muted `colors.placeholder` token) mutes the color further per direct request, rather than switching to a different color token.

**Same-day bug fix: the choppiness report was a real regression from the previous round's own `useNativeDriver: false` switch.** Forcing the idle-bob animation onto the JS thread (done specifically so the connecting lines could read the same value, since the native driver only updates the one native view an animation is directly attached to) made the bubbles' own visible movement noticeably janky — JS-thread `Animated.timing` loops are subject to JS-thread congestion in a way native-driven ones aren't, and with 5 bubbles bobbing continuously this was apparently perceptible in practice, not just a theoretical risk. Fixed by decoupling the two consumers properly instead of sharing one JS-driven value: `bobAnim` (drives the bubble's own transform) went back to `useNativeDriver: true`, smooth again; a second, separate `lineBobAnim` per candidate (`MatchResultsCloud`'s new `lineBobAnimsRef`/`getLineBobAnim`) is kept in sync via `bobAnim.addListener((value) => lineBobAnim.setValue(value))` inside `MatchCloudBubble` — RN's Animated listeners fire regardless of whether the underlying animation is native- or JS-driven, so this gets the connecting lines' endpoints a steady stream of near-real-time position updates without ever putting the bubble's own motion back on the JS thread. The lines render off `lineBobAnim` now, not `bobAnim` directly.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle module for `MatchCloudBubble.tsx` grepped and confirmed both `Animated.timing` call sites back to `useNativeDriver: true`, zero remaining `useNativeDriver: false`, and the new `addListener`/`removeListener`/`lineBobAnim` wiring present. Dev log clean, no new errors after the fetch. (Note: `Animated.add(...)`'s result needed no cast to pass as an `AnimatedLine` prop — `Animated.createAnimatedComponent`'s generated types already accept it directly, same as `AnimatedCircle`'s `strokeDashoffset` elsewhere in this codebase.)

### Same-day: results reveal is now a horizontal page-slide (Instagram-post-swipe style), not an auto-scroll-down

The user didn't like results appearing below the filter panel via auto-scroll — wanted an Instagram-post-carousel feel instead: once the loading ring finishes, the CineGraph/filter section slides *away sideways* and the results screen slides in to replace it, with a back arrow (bottom-left of the results screen) to slide back. This is a real structural change to `match/index.tsx`, not a tweak to `MatchResultsCloud` itself.

**Two fixed-width "pages" side by side in one row**, clipped by an `overflow:"hidden"` wrapper (`pagesClip`) and slid via a single `pageTranslateX` transform (`Animated.timing`, `PAGE_SLIDE_MS = 320` — deliberately snappier than the loading ring's own 1300ms pacing, matching an actual swipe-page feel rather than this feature's usual slow/deliberate moves): page 0 is the filter/CineGraph panel (`MatchFilterStrip` + the `!hasSearched` hint + the Rejected button, all unchanged from before, just relocated into their own page), page 1 is the results outcome (error+Retry, empty-state text, or `MatchResultsCloud` — whichever applies). Both pages stay mounted continuously (only shifted off-screen via transform, never unmounted), so `MatchFilterStrip`'s own internal state and the genre ring's animations are never lost switching between them.

**The reveal trigger moved from an auto-scroll `useEffect` to `goToPage(1)` inside `handleMatchSubmit`'s existing completion callback** — same `matchAnimating`/`MATCH_LOADING_MS` timing logic as before (still waits for both the network response and the minimum loading-ring duration), just a different action once ready. The old `scrollRef`/`resultsY`-based auto-scroll is gone entirely — no longer needed now that "reveal" means "slide to a different page" instead of "scroll further down the same page."

**Retry slides back to page 0 first.** If the user presses Retry from the results page (an error state), `handleMatchSubmit` calls `goToPage(0)` before starting the loading animation — otherwise the ring would be spinning behind results the user is still looking at, invisible. This keeps the interaction model consistent: every search attempt, first or retry, shows the loading ring, then slides to reveal the outcome, no special-cased path for retries.

**New `pageBackButton`** (bottom-left, circular, `colors.base200` background, `Ionicons name="arrow-back"`) on the results page calls `goToPage(0)` — a distinct button from `MatchResultsCloud`'s own internal back arrow (top-left, used for its unrelated cloud↔inspect-profile toggle within the results page itself); the two don't share any state or purpose.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle module for `match/index.tsx` grepped and confirmed `goToPage`/`pageTranslateX`/`pageIndex`/`PAGE_SLIDE_MS`/`pagesRow`/`pageBackButton` all present, zero remaining `scrollRef`/`resultsY`. Dev log clean, no new errors after the fetch.

### Same-day: select/inspect interaction removed from the cloud, a real page-swipe bug fixed, and the reported app-wide sluggishness traced and fixed

Three things in one round: the tap-to-select/grow/detail interaction on cloud bubbles is gone entirely (the user is redesigning this from scratch, wanted it fully out for now — "buraya farklı bir şey düşüneceğim"), a real bug where the filter page's own buttons stopped working (or worked very late) after sliding back from results, and a genuine performance regression traced to the connecting-lines sync mechanism from two rounds ago.

**`MatchResultsCloud.tsx` drastically simplified.** All of `selectedId`/`phase`/`selected`/`handleSelect`/`handleBack`/`selectTranslate`/`othersOpacity`/`detailOpacity`/`transitioningRef`, the whole detail-view JSX block (back button, avatar/bars columns, Follow/Not-Interested), and the `onFollow`/`onNotInterested`/`followState` props are gone — tapping a bubble does nothing now, exactly as asked. Two new files became genuinely dead once their only call site (the detail view) was removed and were deleted after confirming via grep neither had any other importer: `MatchBreakdownBars.tsx` and `matchCategoryMeta.ts`. `match/index.tsx` lost `handleFollow`/`handleNotInterested`/`followState`/`useFollowGraph`/the `swipeMatch` import along with them, since nothing called them anymore either — same "delete confirmed-dead code rather than keep it just in case" discipline this whole session has followed. `MatchCloudBubble.tsx` correspondingly lost `isSelected`/`selectTranslate`/`onPress`/`pointerEvents`/`opacity`/`bobbing` — it's now a plain, always-bobbing, non-interactive `pointerEvents="none"` visual. Bubbles/lines/idle-drift are all otherwise completely unchanged.

**New header/footer captions**: `"Your Top 5 Matches"` (bold, uppercase, small, above the cloud) and `"Tap a profile to see details"` (smaller, below it) — pure static text for now, not wired to any actual interaction yet, since the interaction itself is being redesigned separately. Two new i18n keys added across all 12 locales via the established anchor-and-batch-insert script.

**Real bug fixed: filter-page buttons stopped responding (or responded very late) after sliding back from results.** Root cause: both pages in the horizontal page-slide stay mounted continuously (by design, so `MatchFilterStrip`'s state survives switching), positioned via one shared `pageTranslateX` transform rather than being conditionally rendered. `overflow:"hidden"` on the clipping wrapper only reliably constrains *rendering* — on Android in particular, a sibling that's *visually* off-screen via transform can still intercept or delay touch dispatch depending on the platform's own hit-testing behavior, since RN's clipping doesn't universally guarantee touch-region clipping the same way across iOS/Android. This is the same category of gotcha already hit once earlier this session (the genre ring's `zIndex`-without-`pointerEvents="box-none"` bug) — assuming visual position alone controls touch routing. Fixed explicitly rather than relying on clipping: each page `View` now sets `pointerEvents={pageIndex === 0 ? "auto" : "none"}` (and the mirror condition for page 1), so only the currently-active page can ever receive touches, regardless of platform-specific hit-testing quirks.

**Performance regression traced and fixed: the reported app-wide sluggishness was the connecting-lines' per-frame JS sync, not the dotted rendering itself.** The lines' visual style (dashes/dots) costs nothing extra to render — a static SVG stroke pattern. The real cost was the *mechanism* keeping their endpoints in sync with 5 continuously-bobbing bubbles: `bobAnim.addListener(...)` was firing on every native-to-JS value sync (near frame rate) for all 5 bubbles simultaneously, each call writing to a separate JS-driven `Animated.Value` and triggering an SVG attribute update — real, continuous, unthrottled bridge/JS-thread traffic for as long as the match screen stayed mounted, not just during a brief transition. Fixed with a simple time-based throttle inside the listener (`LINE_SYNC_THROTTLE_MS = 120` — only propagate a value to the line-tracking `Animated.Value` if at least 120ms passed since the last one), cutting update frequency roughly 8-10x. Given the bob motion's own tiny amplitude (6px) and slow pace (1.8-3.2s per segment), this throttled sync is visually indistinguishable from an unthrottled one while being dramatically cheaper — the right fix for a purely decorative feature causing a real, disproportionate performance cost, rather than removing the feature outright.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle confirmed the two deleted files (`MatchBreakdownBars.tsx`/`matchCategoryMeta.ts`) are fully gone from the bundle; `match/index.tsx`'s module confirmed the new `pointerEvents` wiring and zero remaining `handleFollow`/`handleNotInterested`/`followState`; `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s module confirmed the new caption strings present and zero remaining `handleSelect`/`handleBack`/`selectTranslate`/`detailOpacity`/`MatchBreakdownBars`/`MatchAvatarRing` (the last one's detail-view usage — `MatchCloudBubble`'s own small-bubble usage of it is unaffected and still present); `MatchCloudBubble.tsx`'s module confirmed the new `LINE_SYNC_THROTTLE_MS`/`lastSync` throttle present and zero remaining `isSelected`/`selectTranslate`/`onPress`. Dev log clean, no new errors after the fetch.

### Same-day, immediate follow-up: `CineMatchGenreRing.tsx`'s genre chips weren't registering taps, and its ring slices needed to stop being interactive entirely

Two related asks on the filter panel's genre ring (not the results cloud — "CineGraph" in this session's shorthand means this component, the ring on the filter/CineGraph page): the chip buttons around the ring weren't detecting presses at all, and separately, the ring's own slices should stop being a selection target altogether — only the chips should ever toggle a genre.

**Root cause, and the fix for both asks turned out to be the same change.** The ring's slice `Circle` elements still had their own `onPress={() => onToggleGenre(s.genre)}` handler from before this whole loading-animation/collapse feature existed. `react-native-svg`'s touch handling for an interactive shape inside an `<Svg>` doesn't always hit-test the exact rendered stroke path — for a *stroked* (not filled) shape in particular, it can fall back to claiming touches across a broader region of the SVG's own bounding box, which is exactly the same bounding box the chip buttons' `Animated.View`s are absolutely positioned within. This is the likely reason chip taps weren't landing: the still-interactive slice `Circle`s were capturing them first. Removing the `onPress` from the slice `Circle`s (satisfying "dilimler basılınca işlevsiz olsun" on its own) very plausibly fixes the chip-detection bug as a side effect, since the `<Svg>` now has zero interactive descendants for react-native-svg to claim a touch on behalf of.

**`ringWrap`'s `pointerEvents` tightened from `"box-none"` to `"none"`.** `"box-none"` means "I don't claim touches, but my touchable descendants still can" — since there are no touchable descendants left inside the Svg at all now, `"none"` (nothing in this subtree, view or children, ever claims a touch) is the more accurate and more robust setting for the new reality, closing off any residual chance of a library-specific quirk still claiming a touch via the "box-none lets children through" pathway.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Metro bundle module for `CineMatchGenreRing.tsx` grepped and confirmed the only remaining `onToggleGenre` call site is the chip's own `Pressable` (the slice `Circle`'s call site is gone), and `pointerEvents: "none"` present on the ring wrapper. Not independently re-verified on a physical device this pass (no way to exercise real touch input via a curl bundle fetch) — this is a well-reasoned, plausible fix grounded in a known category of SVG touch-hit-testing behavior, not a blind guess, but flagging transparently that live confirmation is still the user's to do.

Explored three semantics with the user (any watched, similar ratings, both rated highly) — landed on **both rated ≥7/10**, since it reads as "you both loved this" and makes a stronger conversation-starter than a bare watch-overlap or an agreement-on-mediocre-films signal would. This needed real backend research first: `matchInsights.sharedGenres` only ever carried `{genre, meCount, targetCount}`, no content IDs.

**Backend, `matchController.js`**: new `getSharedGenreContent` (`POST /api/match/:targetUserId/shared-genre-content`, body `{type, genres}`) — computes the expensive part exactly once per call regardless of how many genres are requested (two `Rating` queries for both users' `value >= 7` ratings of the given content type, intersected by `contentId`, then one batched `Movie`/`Series` fetch for the shared set), then filters that same shared set per genre using `genre_ids` (numeric TMDB IDs) against `MOVIE_GENRE_MAP`/`SERIES_GENRE_MAP` (`backend/utils/genreConstants.js`) — the exact reverse name→ID resolution `getUserGenreDetail` (`userController.js:997-1075`) already established, reused rather than reinvented. Deliberately **not** based on that function's own approach of sourcing IDs from `watchlist` — this feature needs Rating-sourced "actually rated highly" content, a different data source on purpose, not an inconsistency. `mongoose` and the two genre-map imports are new, deliberate re-additions to this file (`mongoose` had been removed earlier this session as dead weight; this is a real new need, not scope creep back in).

**Mobile**: new `mobile/src/components/match/PosterRow.tsx` — the poster-thumbnail row extracted out of `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx` (now a thin fetch-then-delegate wrapper around it) so `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s genre-expansion UI can render the identical visual for already-fetched data with no second fetch. `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s "genres" card: chips are now `Pressable` (`expandedGenre` state, tap again to collapse — same interaction already established for the radar chart's category descriptions), and a single new `useEffect` calls `getSharedGenreContent` once on mount with *every* one of the candidate's `sharedGenres` at once (not per-tap) — the query is genre-independent up until the final filter, so batching avoids a network round trip and loading flicker on every tap. An empty result renders an explicit "you haven't both rated a {{genre}} title highly yet" line rather than nothing, so it reads as informative, not broken.

### Same-day follow-up: Shared Favorites now respects the active genre filter too (backend-only)

User caught a real inconsistency after the round above: with a genre filter active (e.g. "Comedy" only), the Taste score and Shared Genres list already correctly narrowed to that genre, but Shared Favorites kept showing overlap across the user's *entire* favorites list regardless. Confirmed in code before touching anything: `computeMatchBreakdown`'s `g1`/`g2` (Taste score + `sharedGenres`) already had `if (genres.length && !genres.includes(genre)) continue`, but `favorites1`/`favorites2` (content-based score + `favoritesOverlap`) never filtered by genre at all — always the full `favoriteMovies`/`favoriteSeries` arrays. Agreed direction: when a genre filter is active, the whole analysis should be scoped to it, favorites included; the existing broad behavior stays correct when no filter is set.

**Real architectural constraint driving the fix's shape**: `computeMatchBreakdown` is deliberately DB-call-free (its own doc comment: safe to call in `getSwipeQueue`'s up-to-1000-candidate loop specifically *because* it does no DB work). Favorites are bare ObjectId arrays with no genre info attached, so scoping them by genre needs a `Movie`/`Series` lookup — done as one **batched prefetch in each of the 3 callers**, mirroring the exact pattern the `recentRatings` prefetch already established: fetch once before scoring, pass the resolved data in as a new optional param (`favoriteGenreIds`, a `Map<contentId, genre_ids[]>`) alongside the existing `recentRatings`. `buildFavoriteGenreIdsMap(type, genres, favoriteIdLists)` returns `null` immediately (skips the query entirely) when no genre filter is active — zero added cost for the common case. A new `resolveGenreIds(genreMap, genreNames)` helper (reverse name→TMDB-ID lookup) is shared between this and `getSharedGenreContent`, which previously did the same resolution inline per-genre — refactored to call the shared helper instead, no behavior change.

**No mobile changes needed** — `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` already renders whatever `favoritesOverlap`/`sharedGenres` the backend returns; once the backend scopes favorites correctly, the UI reflects it automatically.

**On the reported "Crime/Mystery still shows with Comedy-only filter" symptom**: re-checked the *existing* `g1`/`g2` genre-filter logic — it's already correct (if `genres` truly is `["Comedy"]`, `sharedGenres` can't contain anything else). Nothing found pointing to a bug there, so no change made blind. If this is still observed after this round, the next thing to check is whether the mobile filter selection is actually reaching the request as `["Comedy"]` — a separate, not-yet-confirmed possibility.

### Found it: the "Crime/Mystery still shows despite Comedy-only filter" symptom was real — Express 5's default query parser silently dropped every array query param the mobile app ever sent

The user re-confirmed the symptom persisted, on a Pro/Premium/Dev-tier account (ruling out the tier-gating explanation from the round above). Live-reproduced against the real running backend before touching anything: registered two throwaway accounts, gave them overlapping CineGraph data across 5 genres, hit `GET /match/swipe/queue` with `genres` set to *every* movie genre except Comedy (mirroring "select all, then deselect Comedy" exactly) — `sharedGenres` still came back with Comedy in it. Added a temporary debug log at the top of `getSwipeQueue` and re-hit it: `req.query.genres` was `undefined`, even though the request URL clearly had `genres[]=Action&genres[]=Adventure&...` in it.

**Root cause, confirmed with a standalone `querystring`/`qs` comparison, not guessed**: axios always serializes an array-valued param with `[]` bracket notation — confirmed empirically, even a single-element array becomes `?genres[]=Comedy`, never bare `?genres=Comedy`. **Express 5 changed its default query parser** from `'extended'` (the `qs` package, which understands `key[]=` bracket syntax) to `'simple'` (Node's built-in `querystring` module, which does **not** — it treats `"genres[]"` as a literal, opaque key name). So `req.query.genres` was `undefined` on every single request the mobile app ever sent with an array genre filter, regardless of how many genres were selected or which ones — the swipe queue's own `Array.isArray(req.query.genres) ? ... : (req.query.genres ? [...] : [])` fallback silently resolved to `[]` (no filter) every time. This has nothing to do with anything built earlier this session — it's a latent bug from whenever this project's Express dependency crossed the 4→5 major version boundary, that only manifests for GET endpoints reading an *array*-shaped query param (confirmed via grep: `getSwipeQueue` was the only such call site in the whole mobile app — every other GET call either sends scalars or already comma-joins array filters into one string, e.g. `contentService.ts`'s `getMovies`/`getSeries`).

**Fix**: one line in `backend/server.js`, right after `const app = express();`: `app.set('query parser', 'extended');` — restores the pre-Express-5 default (`qs`, already present in `node_modules`, no new dependency needed), fixing this and any future array-query-param endpoint globally rather than patching just this one call site or changing axios's serialization mobile-side.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean (no mobile changes — this was a pure backend fix). **Live re-verified after the fix**: same repro (all genres except Comedy) now correctly excludes Comedy from `sharedGenres`; a second real-axios-shaped request (`?genres[]=Comedy` only) correctly returned `sharedGenres: [{genre:"Comedy",...}]` and `favoritesOverlap.intersectionCount: 1` together — confirming both this fix and the favorites-genre-scoping fix from the round above now work correctly end-to-end through the actual query-string shape the mobile app really sends, not just through a POST body (which was never affected by this bug and is why the earlier `getMatchWithUser`-based verification didn't catch it).

### Same-day follow-up: radar detail block — slower fade, true centering, font-size hierarchy fixed

Direct feedback on the polish round above, all in `MatchRadarChart.tsx`/`MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`:

- **Fade too fast.** `DETAIL_REVEAL_MS` 280 → 480 — same animation (opacity + translateY, `Easing.out(Easing.cubic)`), just slower.
- **Chart sat closer to the top than centered between the card title and the description.** `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s per-card inner `ScrollView` gained a conditional `contentContainerStyle` (`{flexGrow:1, justifyContent:"center"}`), applied only when `card.key === "breakdown"` — the other cards (lists/posters/narrative) stay top-aligned, which is what already read correctly for them; only the radar card's content (box + detail block, whichever is present) now centers vertically within the fixed `CARD_HEIGHT`.
- **Description text leaning right instead of centered.** Root cause: `detail`'s `alignSelf:"stretch"` was inheriting its width from an ambiguous chain of flex parents (the outer horizontal-paging `ScrollView` → the per-card vertical `ScrollView` → `MatchRadarChart`'s own `wrap`), and a shrunk-to-content width meant `textAlign:"center"` had no extra space to actually center within. Fixed by tying `detail`'s width to `SIZE` (240, the SVG box's own fixed width) instead of `alignSelf:"stretch"` — the box is already reliably centered by `wrap`'s `alignItems:"center"`, so giving `detail` that exact same known width and letting the same centering mechanism handle it keeps the two aligned regardless of how wide the surrounding scroll chain ends up being, without needing to reason about that chain's ambiguous default `alignItems` at all.
- **Font-size hierarchy was backwards.** The category detail title (e.g. "Activity") was `13`, actually *bigger* than the card's own "Match Breakdown" title (`12`) — the reverse of what should read as more important. Fixed by establishing a real hierarchy: `MatchAnalysisPanel`'s shared `sectionTitle` (every card's own title) → `15` (now the biggest text in any card, by design — a card's own name should always read as the most prominent thing in it); `detailTitle` (the category name) stays `13`, clearly one step down; `detailDesc` `13.5 → 12.5`; `detailScore` `12 → 11.5` — a clean `15 > 13 > 12.5 > 11.5` progression.

### Same-day, same-thread follow-up: card lengthened, chart no longer shifts when a category's description opens, Variety's description was getting visually cut off

Two related asks: don't touch the analysis title or the chart itself (both "already fine"); tapping a category's description shouldn't move the chart — that's specifically *why* the card needed to grow taller, not a separate ask. Plus a real bug: Variety's description was getting cut off, not fully visible.

**Root cause of both the chart-shift and the cut-off text, actually the same thing**: the detail block was only *mounted* (and therefore only occupying layout space) while a category was active — appearing/disappearing changed the `wrap` column's total content height each time, which is exactly what made the chart's own vertical position shift under the "center the breakdown card's content" fix from two rounds ago (more total height when active = the whole block, chart included, re-centers differently). And since the block only got exactly as much layout space as its own content needed, edge cases could end up visually constrained too.

**Fix, `MatchRadarChart.tsx`**: `detailReserve` — a new, **always-mounted**, fixed-height (`DETAIL_HEIGHT = 175`) `View` that sits below the chart box whether or not a category is active. The animated `detail` box (title/desc/score) now renders *inside* this fixed-size reserve, sized to `height:"100%"` with its own `justifyContent:"center"`, so it fills and centers within that constant space rather than being sized by its own content — meaning the reserve's height (and therefore everything above it, including the chart) never changes regardless of which category's description is showing or none at all. 175px was sized generously against the longest real description across all 12 locales (Variety's, ~4-5 wrapped lines at this width) plus the title/score/padding around it — comfortably fits with room to spare, not just exactly-fits.

**`MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`**: `CARD_HEIGHT` `380 → 500` to fit the now-always-reserved chart + detail area without needing to scroll — this is the "lengthen the card" the user asked for, and *is* the mechanism behind the no-shift fix, not a separate cosmetic change. Applies to all 5 cards uniformly (shared constant) — the non-chart cards just get a bit more breathing room at this height, harmless for a "one topic per card" uniform-size design.

Neither the chart's own `Svg`/`Polygon`/`Line`/`Circle`/label rendering nor `MatchAnalysisPanel`'s `sectionTitle` style were touched, per the explicit "these are fine, don't change them" instruction.

### Same-day follow-up: a real nested-ScrollView bug fixed, chips replaced with a genre carousel, and a deliberate two-tier reveal animation for poster ratings

Direct, detailed feedback after trying the round above live, closing out this thread. One item was a real, reported bug; the rest is interaction/animation refinement.

**Real bug: the poster row couldn't be scrolled — the outer card-paging carousel stole the gesture instead.** Confirmed as a genuine same-axis nested-`ScrollView` conflict (flagged as a *risk*, not yet a *problem*, when `PosterRow.tsx` was first built — it stopped being theoretical once a genre had enough shared titles to actually need scrolling, e.g. 10 for Comedy). Plain RN `ScrollView`s don't arbitrate two nested horizontal scrollers well; `react-native-gesture-handler` does, and it's already a dependency with `GestureHandlerRootView` already mounted at the app root (`app/_layout.tsx`, added earlier for the Lists drag-to-reorder feature) — so the fix was switching `PosterRow.tsx`'s `ScrollView` import from `"react-native"` to `"react-native-gesture-handler"`, a drop-in API swap, no new setup required.

**Genre chips replaced with a single carousel picker.** The user's own reasoning: a long-time user's match could have 10+ shared genres, and a wrapped chip row gets crowded fast — a one-genre-at-a-time picker with arrows doesn't. New `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` state: `genreIndex` (replaces the old `expandedGenre` string state entirely) with wrap-around `goToGenre(dir, total)`, and a small local slide animation (`genreSlideAnim` + a `genreSlideDir` ref for direction) — the pill's `Animated.Text` resets and re-enters from the direction of travel (16px, fading in) each time the index changes, giving the "current genre slides out, next one slides in" feel requested. The pill itself: border-only color per genre (`genreColor`, "içini boyama" — never a filled background), with the same live shared-count suffix as before ("Comedy · 10").

**Rating display fixed to the app's real 5-star scale.** `Rating.value` is 1-10 backend-side, but every other rating display in this app shows 5 stars with half-star steps (README §8) — the poster-rating reveal was showing the raw 1-10 number. New `formatFiveScale(value)` (`value/2`, one decimal only when it's not a whole number) fixes this — pure display formatting, no backend/type change needed.

**A real two-tier reveal, not one animation for everything.** Direct requirement: tapping any poster should animate in the "You"/`{username}` name labels and their ratings together the first time, but if the user then taps a *different* poster while that's still visible, only the rating numbers should re-animate — the name labels should stay put, not replay. Solved by calling `useRevealAnimation` **twice** with different keys: the name labels use `selectedPosterId ? "shown" : null` (a *stable* string that doesn't change across different poster selections, so the hook's underlying effect — which only reacts to its key actually changing — never re-fires for a poster-to-poster switch, only for the true "nothing selected" ↔ "something selected" transition); the rating numbers use `selectedPosterId` directly (replays on every distinct id, as before). ### Real bug found: analysis panel cards overflowed their actual container's right edge — `MatchAnalysisPanel` was sizing itself against the full screen width instead of the narrower container it actually renders inside

User report: the card's right side didn't fit, asked to shift it left. Root cause, confirmed by reading the actual render tree rather than guessing: `MatchAnalysisPanel` is rendered as the last child inside `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s own root `wrap`, which is capped at `cloudWidth = Math.min(screenWidth - 16, 480)` (`MatchResultsCloud.tsx:125,164`) — narrower than the full device width on every phone, and capped well below it on tablets. But `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` computed its own `cardWidth` from `useWindowDimensions()`'s *full* `screenWidth`, unaware it was actually confined to the narrower `cloudWidth` — a real, unaccounted-for mismatch (16px+ on phones, much more on wide screens) that pushed every card's right edge past the actual visible container, not a rendering fluke.

**Fix**: `MatchAnalysisPanel` gained a new required `containerWidth: number` prop — `MatchResultsCloud.tsx` now passes its own `cloudWidth` straight through (`<MatchAnalysisPanel ... containerWidth={cloudWidth} />`) instead of the child re-deriving a width independently that could disagree with its actual parent. `cardWidth` computation changed from `screenWidth - HORIZONTAL_PADDING*2` to `containerWidth - HORIZONTAL_PADDING*2`; `useWindowDimensions()` is still called for `screenHeight` (that one was never wrong — height isn't affected by `cloudWidth`'s cap). **Worth remembering**: when a component's rendered width might not match its own `useWindowDimensions()` reading (i.e., it's nested inside another component that caps/pads its own container narrower than the full screen), don't let the child re-derive width independently — thread the real constraint down as a prop from whichever ancestor actually owns it, the same fix shape as this one.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `containerWidth` threaded through correctly, and the source has zero remaining `screenWidth` references in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` (confirmed via direct grep, not just tsc). **Flagging transparently**: the dev log's connected-device session logged one `ReferenceError: Property 'screenWidth' doesn't exist` right after this change deployed — this is very likely a stale Fast Refresh artifact (React Native's hot-reload doesn't always cleanly reconcile a prop-signature change like this one against an already-mounted component tree), not a defect in the shipped code — the actual full rebuild that produced this exact code (2236 modules) completed with zero errors, and the source itself has no remaining reference to the removed variable. If this error is still visible live, a manual app reload (not a code fix) should clear it.

### Favorites card: center-focus "coverflow" poster carousel for 3+ items

Direct follow-up to the single-row redesign above: user wanted the poster row itself upgraded from a plain scroll to a center-focused carousel — the centered poster fully visible and larger, each neighbor only half-visible at the row's edges and smaller, growing/shrinking continuously as you drag (not just snapping to size on release). Scoped via AskUserQuestion to this card only (Shared Genres' own poster row is untouched) and confirmed the centered poster is auto-focused — its detail loads below as you scroll, no tap needed — replacing this card's tap-to-select interaction, which now only survives as the fallback for under 3 items (a coverflow has no real "neighbors" to peek with just 1–2 posters).

**New `PosterCoverflow.tsx`**: not built into the shared `PosterRow.tsx` (confirmed out of scope) — a small, self-contained component. Sizing is measured off its own available width via `onLayout` (never hardcoded against device width): `SIDE_W = viewportWidth * 0.38` (each item's at-rest width, also the scroll slot pitch), `CENTER_W = viewportWidth * 0.62` — by construction `CENTER_W + SIDE_W === viewportWidth`, i.e. centered poster fully visible plus exactly one side poster's width split as a half-peek on each edge, matching the literal spec. `ScrollView` imported from `react-native-gesture-handler` (not `react-native`) — same same-axis-nesting fix `PosterRow.tsx` already needed, since this also nests inside `MatchAnalysisPanel`'s card-paging ScrollView. `snapToInterval={SIDE_W}` + `decelerationRate="fast"`; scroll position drives each item's `transform:[{scale}]` via `Animated.event`/`interpolate` (transform-only, `useNativeDriver:true`, no layout width/height animated) so growth is continuous during drag, not stepped. Focus tracking mirrors `MatchRadarChart.tsx`'s existing JS-thread-mirror technique (`fillAnim.addListener`) — a `scrollX.addListener` computes the nearest index and calls `onFocusChange` only when it actually changes, firing continuously during drag rather than waiting for the scroll to settle. Added a `centerIndex` state purely to fix z-order: RN's default array-stacking paints the *next* item on top when scrolling forward but gets it backwards scrolling toward a lower index (the shrinking item would otherwise paint over the one growing into focus) — the currently-centered item gets `zIndex:10` regardless of scroll direction.

**`MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`**: branches on `orderedItems.length >= 3` — `PosterCoverflow` (scroll-driven focus) above that, the existing tap-based `PosterRow` below it. Renamed `selectedId` → `focusedId` (now driven by either mechanism depending on branch) — `detailFor` logic (exact/mine/theirs + client-side genre-name derivation) untouched. The old "Tap a poster..." hint only renders in the fallback branch — the coverflow branch always has a real focus (index 0 the instant it mounts, matching scroll position 0 at rest), so there's nothing for a hint to crossfade against there.

**Layout math verified analytically** (no device screen access this round): content width = `(viewportWidth - SIDE_W) + items.length * SIDE_W`, giving max scroll offset = `(items.length - 1) * SIDE_W` — exactly matches `focusedIndex = round(scrollX / SIDE_W)`'s upper bound, confirming the last item is reachable dead-center with no leftover dead space at the end of the scroll, by construction rather than by observation.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `PosterCoverflow`/`onFocusChange`/`SIDE_RATIO`/`CENTER_RATIO` present, no new build errors (dev log's stale `Animated`/`screenWidth` Fast Refresh artifacts and chat-socket connection errors are unrelated, unchanged from prior rounds).

**Real bug, caught live on-device the moment the user scrolled**: `TypeError: Object is not a function`, thrown 7–9 times in a row (once per scroll event) from `react-native/Libraries/Components/ScrollView/ScrollView.js:1147`'s `_handleScroll`, which unconditionally does `this.props.onScroll(e)`. Root cause, confirmed by reading the actual RN source: `Animated.event(argMapping, {useNativeDriver: true})` does **not** return a callable function — with a native driver it returns the raw `AnimatedEvent` instance itself (`AnimatedEvent.js`'s `__isNative` branch), which is only meant to be `__attach()`-ed to a view by `Animated.createAnimatedComponent`'s own internal machinery, never called directly as JS. `PosterCoverflow.tsx` had passed that object straight into `onScroll` on gesture-handler's **plain** `ScrollView` export (not Animated-wrapped), so RN's base `_handleScroll` tried to invoke it as a function and threw. **Fix**: `const AnimatedGHScrollView = Animated.createAnimatedComponent(GHScrollView)` — the same wrapping RN's own `Animated.ScrollView` applies to its plain `ScrollView`, now applied to gesture-handler's version instead, and rendering `<AnimatedGHScrollView onScroll={Animated.event(...)} .../>` in place of the raw `ScrollView`. **Worth remembering**: any third-party scrollable (gesture-handler's `ScrollView`, or any other non-Animated-wrapped component) needs `Animated.createAnimatedComponent(...)` before it's safe to hand it a native-driven `Animated.event` as `onScroll` — passing the event straight to a plain component compiles and type-checks fine (the crash is 100% a runtime-only failure, `tsc`/bundle-fetch verification does not catch it), and only fails the instant a real scroll event actually fires.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean after the fix, fresh bundle confirmed `AnimatedGHScrollView`/`createAnimatedComponent` present. No further "Object is not a function" lines appeared in the dev log after this fix's rebuild — but this session had no live interactive device control to trigger an actual scroll and visually confirm, so treat this as a well-grounded fix (traced to the exact failing line and RN's own documented `AnimatedEvent.__isNative` behavior) rather than an observed-fixed confirmation; a real on-device scroll test is still the next step.

Previously `CENTER_W + SIDE_W === viewportWidth` by construction meant at-rest neighbors touched the centered poster's edge with zero gap — introduced a fixed `GAP = 16` (mirrors `PosterRow.tsx`'s own row `gap: 10` in spirit, just a bit larger) added onto the scroll slot pitch (`pitch = sideW + GAP`, replacing bare `sideW` as the unit for `snapToInterval`, item width, content padding, and the scale-interpolation breakpoints — the poster's own box size `sideW`/`centerW` stayed the sizing math, `pitch` became the *spacing* math). At rest, two neighboring posters' edges now sit exactly `GAP` px apart; the centered poster still visually grows past its own slot into that gap when focused (intentional coverflow overlap, not a bug) — the max-scroll-offset-lands-on-last-item proof from the original round re-verified with `pitch` substituted for `sideW` throughout, still holds exactly.

**Same-day correction**: user reported posters still visually touched — the previous round's `GAP` only guaranteed spacing between *at-rest* neighbors; the centered poster still grows well past its own slot (the coverflow effect itself), and `CENTER_RATIO=0.46` let that growth overlap into the neighbors' rendered space (non-overlap requires `centerW <= sideW + 2*GAP`, which `0.46` violated on wider cards). Fixed by shrinking `CENTER_RATIO` to `0.35` and `GAP` to `14` — chosen so the inequality holds even at `MatchAnalysisPanel`'s widest realistic card width (~432px, tablets), verified analytically across the viewport range rather than assumed, so posters stay visibly separated at every point in the scroll, not just at rest.

### New Media share type: "list" — sharing a Custom List to the feed

User asked what other post categories the Media feed could support (exploratory question, answered short: Custom Lists was the strongest candidate — real data already exists, `MyListCard.tsx` already has a proven poster-preview UI, no new content modeling needed). Confirmed, discussed the post design (agreed: reuse the just-built `shareBox`/`analysisBox` "inner box" language, but a vertical stack with a horizontal poster strip instead of one poster+text row), then planned via `EnterPlanMode` given the real end-to-end scope (backend model/controller, a genuinely new share-trigger point, mobile type/API layer, a new `ShareCard` branch).

**Scope decisions, made explicit up front rather than discovered mid-build:**
- **Owner-only, public-only** — matches the existing precedent that every share type shares the sharer's *own* content, never a repost of someone else's; enforced both in the UI (share button only rendered when `isOwner && list.isPublic` on `ListDetailScreen.tsx`) and server-side (`CustomList.findOne({_id, owner: userId, isPublic: true})` in `createShare`) — confirmed via a real negative test (see Verification below).
- **No DM/community sharing for lists in this pass** — `ShareOptionsMenu.tsx`'s own header comment already explains why it exists: for entry points that already have a real DM/community picker (Analysis, Recommendation). Lists have no such precedent (same reasoning `ReviewComposer.tsx` used to skip that component too), so list-sharing is one direct "Share to Media" tap, not a 2-option bottom sheet. Building a DM message type for lists would be a materially bigger, separate feature not requested.

**Backend**: `Share.js` model gained `"list"` to the `type` enum plus `listId`/`listData: {name, description, itemCount, previewItems}` (a plain subdocument mirroring `contentData`'s existing style, not `Mixed`). `customListRoute.js`'s previously-module-private `hydratePreviewItems` (already used by `/discover`, `/popular`, `/me`) was exported and reused as-is in `shareController.js`'s new `createShare` branch rather than writing new hydration logic — zero duplication. `getShareFeed`'s `type` query-param allow-list and the `createShare` fallback error message both updated to include `"list"`.

**Mobile — share trigger**: `ListDetailScreen.tsx` gained a `sharingToMedia` state and `handleShareToMedia` (mirrors `ProfileAnalysisModal.tsx`'s `handleShareToMedia` exactly — `createShare({type:"list", listId})` → toast on success/failure), surfaced as a small icon-only button (`newspaper-outline`, matching `ShareOptionsMenu`'s own icon for the same action elsewhere) next to the existing owner-only `Edit` button, both now inside a new `ownerActionsRow`. **Real gap found and fixed along the way**: `ListDetailScreen`'s own `basePath` prop only accepted `"/lists" | "/home" | "/search"` — no `"/profile"` variant existed yet because Profile had never linked into a list detail screen before. Added a new `app/(app)/profile/lists/[id].tsx` thin re-export (mirrors `home/lists/[id].tsx` exactly) and registered `lists/[id]` in `profile/_layout.tsx` (`title: t("List")`, same key `home/_layout.tsx` already uses) — otherwise a "list" `ShareCard` tapped from the Profile tab's Sharings view would have had nowhere to navigate to.

**Mobile — `ShareCard.tsx`**: `typeMeta` gained a `"list"` case (`albums-outline` icon, `colors.accent` — the one palette token the other 3 types don't already use, reusing the already-existing `"List"` locale key rather than adding a duplicate). New `listBox` style (same `colors.base200`/`INNER_BOX_RADIUS`/margins as `shareBox`, but `flexDirection:"column"` instead of a row, since a list's preview is inherently several posters not one) renders: list name → description or a new fallback locale key `"{{user}} shared a list."` (12 locales, added via the exact same script-based bottom-to-top insertion this session has used for every prior locale batch) → a horizontal poster strip reusing `MyListCard.tsx`'s own `56×82` thumbnail size verbatim (not `shareBox`'s `64×96` — visual consistency with the Lists tab itself) → an `item_count` caption (reused existing key). Premium's gold border+glow (`premiumBorder`/`premiumInnerBox`) applies to `listBox` exactly like the other 2 boxed types. Tap target: new `goToList()` helper parallel to `goToContent()`.

**Verification**: `node --check` on all touched backend files, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on mobile. Full real end-to-end pass via the JWT-minting convention, not assumed from reading the code: created a real public list for test account Zachary (premium tier) via the actual `POST /api/lists` + `POST /api/lists/:id/items` endpoints, shared it via the real `POST /api/shares` (`type:"list"`) — confirmed the response's `listData.previewItems` came back with genuinely hydrated titles/posters (Minions & Monsters, Supergirl) — then fetched `GET /api/shares/feed?type=list` as a different account and confirmed it renders correctly there too, `accountTier:"premium"` included. **Negative-path tested too**: created a second, private list and confirmed `POST /api/shares` correctly rejects it (`"List not found"`, the intentional response for both "doesn't exist" and "exists but not owned/not public" — doesn't leak which).
