### Real bug: list-post cards showed no film/series posters — a seeding bug, not a pre-existing app bug
`ShareCard.tsx`'s list-type box only renders a poster `Image` when `item.poster_path` is truthy (`share.listData.previewItems[].poster_path`); it silently renders empty boxes otherwise. The real API path (`hydratePreviewItems` in `customListRoute.js`) always populates this correctly from the Movie/Series collection — but `seedMediaActivity.js`'s own hand-rolled preview-item construction (written before this was caught) set `poster_path: undefined` for every seeded list-share, since the script's `CONTENT_POOL` never fetched that field in the first place. Fixed two ways: (1) `CONTENT_POOL`'s `Movie.findOne`/`Series.findOne` calls now `.select(...poster_path)` and carry it through to `previewItems`, so future re-runs of the seed script don't reintroduce this; (2) a one-off backfill (`_tmp_fixListPreviews.js`, deleted after use) re-hydrated all 12 existing list-type shares' `previewItems` by calling the real `hydratePreviewItems` function against each share's actual `CustomList` — reusing production logic instead of re-deriving it a second time. Verified live: previously-empty list cards now return real `poster_path` values from the feed API.

### Real regression: Discover's Trending/Friends' Choice/Podium rails stopped responding to swipes after the Discover↔Shares pager landed
The earlier pager entry above claimed the new horizontal `pagingEnabled` outer `ScrollView` was "safe against the same-axis nested-scroll anti-pattern" because its direct children (`KesfetSection`'s `ScrollView`, `SharesFeedSection`'s `FlatList`) scroll vertically — true for that one parent/child pair, but wrong transitively: `KesfetSection`'s vertical scroll itself contains several **horizontal** scrollers (`ContentRail`'s `FlatList` for Trending Movies/Series/Friends' Choice/Reviews, `LeaderboardPodium`'s own paging `ScrollView`), and those share the outer pager's axis. Plain React Native `ScrollView`/`FlatList` have no built-in negotiation for this — the outermost horizontal scroller simply wins every horizontal drag, so the inner rails and podium stopped scrolling entirely once the outer pager existed. Fixed by switching every scroller in that ancestor chain — the outer pager (`home/index.tsx`), the intermediate vertical `ScrollView` (`KesfetSection.tsx`), and the two horizontal descendants (`ContentRail.tsx`'s `FlatList`, `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`'s `ScrollView`) — from `react-native`'s components to `react-native-gesture-handler`'s equivalents (already a project dependency, `GestureHandlerRootView` already wraps the app root in `app/_layout.tsx`). Gesture-handler's native pan-gesture resolution lets an inner scroller that can still move win the gesture, only bubbling to the outer pager once it hits its own scroll boundary — the standard fix for this exact nesting shape, not a workaround. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; confirmed via a fresh Metro bundle fetch that it compiles with no unresolved-import errors.

### `ListRailCard` third round: a real cascade-geometry bug fixed, corner badge restored, like/view moved into the overlay, owner row moved to a real footer
User flagged "major design problems" plus two things dropped that shouldn't have been. Root cause of the "big design problems": `OFFSET_STEP` (16→8 in the prior round, to satisfy "make them tighter") had been reduced to *exactly equal* `POSTER_RADIUS` (8) — the sliver each back card reveals is its own bottom edge, which is rounded on both corners, so an offset ≤ the radius reveals *only* corner curve with no straight edge at all, reading as a broken/discontinuous stack rather than a clean cascade. Fixed by setting `OFFSET_STEP:14` — comfortably clears the radius, still tighter than the original 16. Also dropped the per-item Android `elevation` that had shadowed each layer (zIndex alone is sufficient for sibling stacking order; the elevation was adding a muddy Material shadow under every poster that didn't help and wasn't asked for).

Two things were wrongly removed in the redesign two rounds back and are now back / repositioned per direct correction:
- **The top-left corner badge (stack icon + total item count) is back**, always visible on the front card regardless of reveal state — this was never supposed to be removed, dropped by mistake when the card was rebuilt around the overlay/reveal interaction.

### `PosterCascade` eighth round: fit-to-width for ShareCard (no fixed cap), permanent dim on back layers, per-consumer border, and the reveal-catcher bug actually fixed this time
Four corrections in one round, all on the same shared cascade system:

- **ShareCard's list-post cascade no longer caps at a fixed count** — the user's own ask: "satıra ne kadar sığıyorsa o kadar diz" (stack however many actually fit the row), not a fixed 5. `PosterCascade` gained a `fitToWidth` prop (horizontal only): its outer container renders at `width:"100%"` to receive whatever space `ShareCard`'s `listBox` flow gives it, measures the real value via `onLayout`, and computes `Math.floor((measuredWidth - posterWidth) / CASCADE_OFFSET_STEP) + 1` items to show (rendering just the front item until that first measurement lands, so there's never a one-frame overflow past the row's real bounds). This only helps if there's enough real data to fill with, though — `hydratePreviewItems` (customListRoute.js) was hardcoded to a 5-item slice everywhere; it now takes an optional `limit` param (default still 5, so `/discover`/`/popular`/`/:id` are unchanged) and `createShare`'s list-type branch passes `20` so new list-shares snapshot enough posters to actually fill a wide row. Existing list-shares were re-hydrated with the new limit via a one-off `_tmp_widenListPreviews.js` (deleted after running) so this is visible immediately, not just on future shares.
- **Back layers in Discover's cascade now carry a permanent dark tint that never lifts** — `PosterCascade` gained `dimBackLayers` (only `ListRailCard` passes it): every non-front layer gets the same `rgba(0,0,0,0.55)` tint the front card's own covered-state overlay uses, rendered by `PosterCascade` itself (unlike the front overlay, which is still `ListRailCard`'s own interactive element) and never removed — purely reinforcing the "these are stacked behind the front card" read, not implying they're individually interactive.
- **Border made per-consumer**: `PosterCascade` gained `borderWidth`/`borderColor` props (default `1.5`/`colors.primary`, i.e. unchanged for `ListRailCard`, which passes neither). `ShareCard` now passes `borderWidth={0}` — the border-color-to-primary change from two rounds ago was only ever meant for Discover's list rail ("rengi değiştir derken sadece discoverdaki list kısmından bahsediyordum"), and `ShareCard`'s cascade reverts to its pre-extraction plain-thumbnail look.
- **Real fix, this time robust, for tap-anywhere-to-close.** The previous round's `revealCatcher` (an absolutely-positioned sibling with a higher `zIndex`) was still reported broken — relying on `zIndex` alone to make an absolute sibling win a touch over a normal-flow one isn't a guaranteed cross-platform behavior in RN the way it is in web CSS. Fixed properly: `fan` and `footer` now get `pointerEvents:"none"` while `revealed`, which structurally excludes their entire subtree from hit-testing (not just paint order) — so `revealCatcher`, still sized to span the whole card, is the *only* thing that can receive a touch in that state, no ambiguity left. The "Detail" pill inside it remains its own nested `Pressable`, so its own tap still fires navigation rather than also re-covering.

### `PosterCascade`: back layers now fade instead of a flat dark mask
Design question asked and approved before building: a graduated opacity fade per layer reads as real depth, versus the flat single-tone dark mask every back layer previously got uniformly. `dimBackLayers` now applies `BACK_LAYER_OPACITY = [1, 0.85, 0.7, 0.55, 0.4]` (front layer always full opacity) instead of rendering a separate `rgba(0,0,0,0.55)` overlay View — the whole layer (poster + its border) fades together rather than a dark tint sitting on top of it, which also reads more naturally against both light and dark themes than a fixed-alpha black mask would. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

And the default border color, which a recent round had matched to `colors.primary` (the "Detail" pill's own color), is reverted to `colors.border` per direct reversal — the user explicitly changed their mind, wanting the frame color distinct from the pill again, back to the app's real semantic border token from an earlier round rather than the pill-matching one. `ShareCard`'s own `borderWidth={0}` override is unaffected either way. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

### `ListRailCard` tap-anywhere-to-close: rebuilt on nested-Pressable capture instead of sibling z-ordering, actual root cause found this time
The border treatment is now shared with `ShareCard`'s list-post box too (removed its `borderWidth={0}` override, per direct ask — same `colors.border` frame both places now).

The tap-to-close bug had survived two prior fix attempts (a same-level absolute sibling `revealCatcher` with a higher `zIndex`; then the same sibling with `pointerEvents:"none"` forced on `fan`/`footer`) — both still only worked when the tap landed within the front poster's own bounds. The real issue: neither approach is RN's actual well-tested mechanism for "one interactive region should swallow every tap except a couple of specific inner targets." Rebuilt around the pattern this app already relies on elsewhere (nested Pressables) instead: `card` itself is now the outer `Pressable` (`onPress` only acts while `revealed`), and `overlay` (tap-to-reveal), `detailsButton` (tap-to-navigate), and the footer's `UserAvatar` (tap-to-profile) are each a genuine *nested* Pressable inside it. A nested Pressable always claims its own tap and never lets it bubble to the parent — well-established, reliable RN behavior — so any tap that isn't on one of those three specific targets naturally reaches `card`'s own `onPress` and closes it, with zero dependency on sibling paint order, zIndex, or pointerEvents propagation. `revealCatcher` is gone entirely; the former `detailsWrap` is now just a plain positioning `View` (no Pressable, no pointerEvents prop needed) sized to the front poster so the pill still looks centered on it.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

### `ListRailCard`'s Detail pill rebuilt on a real `Modal` — page-wide dismiss, and the actual root cause of the earlier attempts
Two things: the user widened the ask to "anywhere on the *page*", not just the card, and separately reported the pill had stopped appearing at all (a real regression — the previous round's `detailsWrap` lost the `zIndex` its predecessor `revealCatcher` had, so the pill was rendering *behind* `PosterCascade`'s own z-indexed poster layers, completely hidden).

Rather than patch that one zIndex and try a fourth sibling-based dismiss technique, switched to a genuinely different mechanism: the revealed-state pill now renders inside a real `<Modal transparent>`, not inline on the card. Likely root cause of all three prior sibling/zIndex/pointerEvents/nested-Pressable attempts failing specifically outside the poster's own bounds: `ContentRail`'s horizontal `FlatList` (this card's ancestor) is a `react-native-gesture-handler` component — required for the outer Discover/Shares pager to coexist with Discover's own horizontal rails (see `home/index.tsx`'s own comment) — and gesture-handler runs its own pan/tap arbitration on that subtree, which plausibly doesn't honor plain-RN zIndex/pointerEvents/nested-Pressable assumptions the same way a normal view tree does. `Modal` sidesteps this entirely: it renders in its own native top-level layer, completely outside the card's (and the FlatList's) view hierarchy, so its full-screen backdrop `Pressable` reliably catches a tap anywhere on the page — not just the card — with no gesture-handler ancestor to compete with. The pill still looks anchored to the card: `cardRef.current.measureInWindow(...)` captures the card's real on-screen position at the moment of reveal, and the pill is positioned at those exact screen coordinates inside the Modal, reusing the same `CARD_WIDTH × POSTER_HEIGHT` centering box the old inline overlay used.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation. Not device-verified from this session (no screenshot tooling here) — this is a different-enough mechanism from the three failed attempts that it's worth a dedicated visual check before considering this fully closed.

### `ListRailCard`: one Modal shared across the whole rail, so switching between cards' Detail pills takes a single tap
The Modal fix from the round above worked, but exposed the next real issue: each `ListRailCard` had its own independent `Modal`, so tapping card A's poster then immediately card B's poster took *two* taps — the first tap only closed A's Modal (a `Modal`, by design, blocks all touches beneath it while visible, so that first tap on "B" never actually reached B's card at all, it hit A's backdrop), and only the second tap could reach B's now-unblocked poster.

Fixed by lifting the Modal to exactly one shared instance, owned by a new `ListRevealProvider` wrapping the whole Popular Lists rail (`KesfetSection.tsx`) instead of living inside each card. Since the single Modal still blocks direct touches to any card underneath it, the backdrop itself now has to figure out what the tap actually meant: every mounted `ListRailCard` registers its own ref in the provider on mount (unregisters on unmount — virtualized rail, cards come and go as it scrolls), and a backdrop tap re-measures every registered card live via `measureInWindow` (a genuinely current query against the native view tree at that instant — not a cached position, so it can't go stale even if the rail was scrolled since the card last measured) to check whether the tap point landed inside a *different* card's front-poster box. If it did, that card's pill opens immediately in the same tap; if it didn't land on any card, the modal just closes. `ListRailCard` itself now only tracks whether *it* is the currently-revealed one (`ctx.revealed?.listId === list._id`, derived from context, no more local `revealed` state) and asks the provider to `reveal()`/read from it.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean (one real type fix along the way: `useRef<View>(null)`'s ref type is `RefObject<View | null>` in this project's React types, not the bare `RefObject<View>` the registry was first typed with). Fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

### `ListRailCard`: Modal removed — it was blocking the whole page, not just the card
Direct correction: the Modal-based Detail pill (two rounds above) made the page feel "locked" — a `Modal` blocks every touch underneath it while visible by design, so the user couldn't scroll the rail or use anything else on the page while a pill was open. Traded "dismissible from literally anywhere" back down to "the page always stays fully usable": the pill is inline again (no Modal, no `measureInWindow`, no tap-coordinate registry — all of that existed solely to make a Modal's backdrop smart enough to hit-test other cards). `ListRevealProvider` now just holds `{ listId, onPress } | null` shared state; each card's own covered-state Pressable is directly, independently tappable at all times since nothing captures/blocks touches globally, so tapping a *different* card's poster switches straight to it in one tap — for the same reason nothing needs to be blocked to make that work. Dismissal is scoped back to tapping the poster area again (confirmed reliable at that scope in every round so far) — tapping anywhere else on the page just does whatever it would normally do (scroll, open another section, etc.), which is exactly the point.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

Detailed direct spec from the user, replacing the previous round's full-page swiper with something more minimal. Tapping the poster again, or the title, or the review text, or anywhere else on the card while the overlay is hidden, brings it back — as a single, deliberate "one action per tap" rule rather than one element trying to catch outside taps: three separate `Pressable`s (poster, title/rating, review text) each run their tap through the same `withOverlayGuard` — if the overlay's hidden, the tap just restores it and stops there; only once it's showing does that element's real action (navigate to content, or expand/collapse the review) fire. This sidesteps the whole class of "reliably catch a tap outside a specific region" problems `ListRailCard.tsx` hit repeatedly (zIndex, pointerEvents, nested-Pressable-in-Pressable, eventually a Modal that then had to be reverted) — every region here is independently, always reachable, so there's nothing to "catch," just a shared guard each one checks first.

### Real bug: the full-review popup didn't actually scroll past its own height cap
`modalCard`'s `maxHeight:"80%"` capped the box, but RN's default `overflow` is `"visible"` and the `ScrollView` inside had no `flex`/height of its own — so it just sized to its full text content instead of being bounded by that cap, meaning anything past 80% of the screen simply never scrolled into view. Fixed with the two pieces RN actually needs for this pattern: `overflow:"hidden"` on `modalCard` (so content can't render past the rounded-corner box) and `flex:1` on the `ScrollView` itself (so it's bounded by the now-fixed-height parent and can establish a real scrollable viewport). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

Separately: user flagged that the like/rating split ended up swapped from what makes sense (rating landed with the poster overlay/title, like count with the reviewer) — asked for a recommendation rather than a silent fix. Recommended: overlay gets title + like count (mirrors `ListRailCard`'s own "name + stats together" grouping exactly), the reviewer row gets avatar + username + rating (a rating is the reviewer's own personal verdict, belongs with their identity, not with the content summary). Not yet applied — waiting on confirmation before touching it.

### Like/rating split applied (approved), and a real flex bug that made the popup's text vanish entirely
Applied the recommended split: the poster overlay now shows content title + like count (mirrors `ListRailCard`'s own "name + stats together" grouping); the reviewer row shows avatar + username on their own line, with the star rating on the line *below* that (not next to the name, per direct correction), then the review text below the rating. Same rearrangement mirrored in the full-text popup's header for consistency.

**Real bug**: the previous round's scroll fix (`flex:1` on the popup's `ScrollView`) made the review text disappear entirely rather than scroll. Root cause: `modalCard` has no explicit height, only a `maxHeight` cap — its actual resolved height is content-driven, so a `flex:1` child has no definite "available space" to fill against and Yoga collapses it to zero. Fixed with `flexShrink:1` instead of `flex:1`: the ScrollView now takes its natural full-text size when that fits under the cap (short reviews render at their real size, no wasted empty space), and only shrinks down to the remaining space — becoming genuinely scrollable — once it doesn't.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

Fixed: the revealed state now uses a separate `detailsCatcher` style with no background at all, matching `ListRailCard`'s own correct version of this exact pattern (which never had this bug — the two components' styles had just drifted apart when `ReviewSwipeCard` was built).
- **Reveal state unified app-wide.** Extracted a new shared `src/context/PosterRevealContext.tsx` (`PosterRevealProvider` + `usePosterReveal(id)`) out of what used to be `ListRailCard`'s own local `ListRevealProvider`, and wrapped *both* the Popular Lists rail and the Reviews swiper in one shared instance (`KesfetSection.tsx`). Per direct request: at most one poster's Detail pill — a list card's or a review's, either section — is ever open anywhere on Discover, and tapping a different card's poster (same section or the other one) switches straight to it in one tap, exactly like switching between two list cards already worked. `ListRailCard.tsx` itself lost nothing (its `RevealState`'s `onPress` field was actually already dead code — a leftover from the Modal-based version several rounds back — the shared hook needed only a bare id).
- **Reviewer row / rating / review text now participate in the same reveal system**, not a separate local `overlayVisible` guard: tapping the reviewer row or the rating always calls the shared `close()` (closes whichever card, if any, is currently revealed — a no-op if none is); tapping the review text calls `reveal()` *and* opens the full-text popup in the same motion, per direct ask — no more "first tap just closes the overlay, second tap actually opens the popup."
- **Real bug: the full-text popup's scroll fix from two rounds ago still didn't reliably show overflow text.** Switched `modalCard`'s `maxHeight` from a `"80%"` percentage string to a concrete pixel value computed via `useWindowDimensions` (`screenHeight * 0.8`) — percentages resolved inside a `Modal`'s own layout root are less consistently reliable than a concrete number, and this is the same "pixel constants over percentages" convention `LeaderboardPodium`/`MatchSummarySwiper` already use elsewhere in this app.

### Real bug found: the popup's scroll was blocked by its own close-on-tap Pressable, not by sizing
Two rounds of sizing fixes (flex, then a concrete pixel `maxHeight`) didn't fix it because the actual cause was different: `modalCard` — including the `ScrollView` inside it — was a *descendant* of the backdrop `Pressable` that closes the popup on tap. A `Pressable` ancestor claiming the touch before its `ScrollView` descendant gets a chance to recognize a drag as a scroll gesture is a real, known class of conflict, and is the far more likely explanation for "sizing looks right but it still won't scroll" than anything about `flex`/`maxHeight` math.

Restructured so the `ScrollView` has zero `Pressable` ancestors: `modalRoot` (the dark backdrop) is a plain `View`, not a `Pressable`; a separate, absolutely-positioned `modalCloseZone` `Pressable` sits *behind* the card as a sibling and handles "tap outside the card closes it"; `modalCard` itself is `pointerEvents="box-none"` (transparent to touch itself, but lets its children handle their own), with just the header/reviewer/rating block wrapped in its own small close-on-tap `Pressable` — the `ScrollView` sits alongside that as a plain, unwrapped sibling with nothing above it in the touch hierarchy to compete with a scroll gesture. Tapping the card's own blank padding still closes it (falls through the `box-none` card to `modalCloseZone` underneath); tapping directly on the review text no longer closes the popup, which is also the correct behavior for something you're actively trying to scroll and read.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed compilation.

### Two real regressions fixed: Media pager felt slow/laggy on manual swipe, PeoplePodium stopped scrolling entirely
Both bugs traced back to the same-axis nested-horizontal-scroll issue this session already hit (and fixed) on the Discover side, just showing up again in two places that fix never reached:

- **`PeoplePodium.tsx` couldn't be swiped at all.** It's nested inside `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s (vertical, orthogonal, fine) `FlatList`, which itself sits inside `home/index.tsx`'s outer horizontal pager — but unlike `LeaderboardPodium.tsx` (Discover's equivalent, converted earlier this session), `PeoplePodium`'s own horizontal `ScrollView` was still importing from plain `react-native`, not `react-native-gesture-handler`. A same-axis plain `ScrollView` nested under a gesture-handler-based outer pager just loses every drag to the outer one. Fixed by switching its `ScrollView` import to `react-native-gesture-handler`, matching `LeaderboardPodium.tsx` exactly.
- **Manual swipe between Paylaşımlar↔Keşfet felt slow, and the header pill lagged behind the visible page.** `home/index.tsx` only synced `outerTab` (and lazy-mounted the destination tab via `visitedTabs`) on `onMomentumScrollEnd` — i.e. only once the whole drag+momentum had *fully finished*. The tap path (`switchTab`) doesn't have this problem since it mounts/fetches immediately on press, well before its own scroll animation completes — so a first swipe into Keşfet didn't even start its 5 parallel fetches until after the user had already arrived, and the pill visibly lagged the finger. Replaced `onMomentumScrollEnd` with continuous `onScroll` that flips `outerTab`/`markVisited` as soon as the halfway point to the next page is crossed — with only 2 tabs this can flip at most once per swipe (not the "state churn mid-drag" the settle-only design was originally guarding against), but now fires mid-gesture instead of after it, so Keşfet starts loading while still mid-swipe and the pill tracks the crossover instead of the settle.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed both files compiled with the changes present (grepped the dev bundle for each file's own new comment text).

### Follow-up: pill still visibly trailed the finger (crossover-flip wasn't enough), plus a real finding on "slow initial load"
The crossover-based `onScroll` fix above still only flips `outerTab` once — the header pill's own position was still driven by `CapsuleTabSwitcher`'s discrete 260ms tween on `activeKey` change, so it visibly caught up *after* the flip rather than tracking the finger. Fixed properly this time: `CapsuleTabSwitcher.tsx` gained an optional `dragOffsetX`/`pagerWidth` pair (an `Animated.Value` in pixels + the pager's own width) — when both are provided and both slots are measured, the window's `translateX`/`width` interpolate directly off that live value instead of the tween, so it moves in the same frame as the drag. Kept fully optional and additive: Profile's CineGraph toggle and Socials' Messages/Community toggle (the switcher's other two consumers, no external pager to track) pass neither and keep the original tap-tween exactly as before. `home/index.tsx` now feeds this via `Animated.event` on the outer `ScrollView`'s `onScroll` (`useNativeDriver: false`, since `width` isn't a native-driver-eligible property, same constraint the tween already had) — the event's `listener` option still runs the exact same crossover logic as the previous round for `outerTab`/`visitedTabs`, so that part is unchanged, just now paired with a truly continuous visual on top of it.

Separately investigated "yavaş yükleniyor" (initial load feels slow) with real measurements rather than guessing, since the code already fires each tab's fetches in parallel (`Promise.all` in `KesfetSection`, independent sibling effects for `PeoplePodium`/`ActivitySection`/`LeaderboardPodium`) — so the slowness wasn't an obvious client-side serialization bug. Timed every endpoint both tabs hit on first mount (11 total) via the JWT-minting convention, first sequentially (0.85s–2.19s each) then as a real concurrent burst matching actual app behavior. **Real finding**: this environment's MongoDB connection processes concurrent operations at a fairly fixed ~277ms each, in something close to a single queue — confirmed all the way down to bypassing Express/Mongoose entirely and firing 11 bare `admin().ping()` calls directly against the driver (`maxPoolSize` confirmed at the default 100, so not a pool-size issue): completion times still staircase up in ~277ms steps regardless of concurrency. This is an environment/cluster-level constraint (very plausibly Atlas free-tier throughput, or the Codespace's own network path), not an application bug — no amount of client-side parallelization avoids it, since operations queue at the DB layer either way.

Given that constraint, the one lever that *does* help is cutting the total number of round trips fired per tab-open, since each one — parallel or not — buys a queue slot. The biggest, safe, genuinely global win: `backend/middleware/authMiddleware.js`'s `User.findById(decoded.id)` runs on *every single* authenticated request, and a tab mounting fires ~9-11 of those for the same caller within the same instant — each independently re-fetching the identical document. Added in-flight request coalescing (a `Map<userId, Promise>` cleared the instant each lookup settles) so concurrent requests for the same user share one DB round trip instead of paying for one each — not a TTL cache, so no staleness risk, and safe to share the resulting document across requests since no controller mutates `req.user` in place (`grep` confirmed — writes always go through a separately `.save()`d document). Verified via the same live burst test: this alone collapsed what would otherwise be ~9-11 redundant auth round trips in the queue down to effectively one.

### `getNetworkActivity` (Discover's Activity section) rewritten as 4 self-contained aggregations — real, verified 3-4x speedup on that endpoint
Was the single slowest individual endpoint measured (~2.2-3.9s), with a genuine two-phase data dependency: fetch ratings/reviews/lists/following-users first, *then* fetch whichever movies/series they referenced, since the second phase's ids aren't known until the first completes — a real sequential round-trip pair, not something `Promise.all` could paper over. Rewrote it as 4 independent aggregation pipelines (ratings/reviews/lists/watchlist-events), each resolving its own actor and content via `$lookup` server-side, all 4 still running in parallel via `Promise.all` — collapsing the old "phase 1 (4 queries) → phase 2 (2 queries)" shape into one round trip per event type.

First attempt used correlated (`let`/pipeline) `$lookup`s to pick movies-vs-series by `contentType` as part of the join condition itself — verified against real data (373/360 real events across the 2 seeded test accounts) that this actually made things *worse*: it timed out server-side (`MongoServerError: MaxTimeMSExpired`) at the volumes this endpoint handles, since a correlated `$lookup` forces Mongo into a per-document nested-loop join instead of a real hash join. Caught before ever touching the real endpoint, since this was built and tested standalone first. Fixed by joining both `movies` and `series` unconditionally via plain equality `$lookup` (cheap, hash-joinable) and picking the right one afterward with a trivial in-memory `$cond` — the standard fix for a "join then branch on a sibling field" shape. Also had to add an explicit `$convert`-to-`objectId` step before `Rating`/`Review.contentId`'s own `$lookup`: that field is schema-typed `String`, while `movies`/`series` `_id` is a real `ObjectId` (Mongoose defaults `_id` to `ObjectId` even under `strict:false`) — the *old* JS-loop code only worked because Mongoose's query-casting silently converted `.toString()`'d values back to `ObjectId` before hitting the wire, which a raw `$lookup` doesn't do (`$convert` with `onError:null` rather than bare `$toObjectId`, so a malformed id just finds no content instead of throwing and failing the whole pipeline). `User.watchlist.itemId` didn't need this — already schema-typed `ObjectId`.

Verified rigorously before shipping, not just by inspection: wrote a standalone script embedding the *old* implementation verbatim alongside the new one, ran both against the 2 real seeded accounts (Zachary.Macejkovic73330, Peter.Altenwerth29467) for page 1 and page 3, and deep-compared every field after normalizing key order — byte-identical output on both users, both pages (373 and 360 real events respectively). Also separately eliminated `getNetworkActivity`'s own redundant `User.findById(userId).select("following")` — `req.user.following` is already populated by the now-coalesced auth middleware, so this reuses it instead of paying for a second identical lookup. Measured standalone: **3879ms → 877ms** and **2316ms → 823ms** for the two test accounts, byte-identical results. In a live full-burst test (all 11 tab-open endpoints fired concurrently through the real running server) this endpoint moved from being the clear worst straggler (~3.0s, finishing dead last) to finishing solidly mid-pack (~2.2s) — the specific "Activity section visibly still spinning after everything else" symptom is fixed. The burst's *total* wall-clock time didn't move much on this round (other endpoints — `popular-with-friends` was the new worst at ~3.9s — still queue behind the same environment-level DB-round-trip serialization described above), which is expected given that constraint: cutting one endpoint's own round-trip count helps that endpoint, not the shared queue everyone sits in.

### Follow-up: same method applied to `getPopularAdds` (backs both `popular-with-friends` and `popular-this-week`) — the burst's new worst straggler
User asked to apply the same treatment to whichever endpoint was now the worst offender — that was `popular-with-friends` (~3.9s in the previous burst). It's backed by a shared helper, `getPopularAdds` in `feedController.js` (also used by `popular-this-week`), with the identical two-phase shape: aggregate watchlist/toWatchList adds into a ranked, deduped list (phase 1, 2 parallel queries) → hydrate whichever movies/series/adders/ratings that ranked list references (phase 2, 4 parallel queries that can't start until phase 1's ids are known). Folded phase 2's `movies` and `series` lookups (previously two separate `.find()`s) into one aggregation, seeded from the already-computed ranked list via Mongo's `$documents` stage, joining both collections by id via plain equality `$lookup` and picking whichever matched with a `$cond` — same pattern as `getNetworkActivity` above, same reasoning for using equality lookups over correlated ones. `$documents` needed one non-obvious fix: it requires a database-level `{aggregate: 1}` command, which `Model.aggregate()` can't issue (always collection-scoped) — used the raw driver's `mongoose.connection.db.aggregate(...).toArray()` instead. `adders` and the ratings bulk-average aggregate were left as their own separate queries (unchanged) rather than folded in too — folding the ratings lookup into a per-document correlated `$lookup` was the exact mistake already caught and reverted in `getNetworkActivity` above, and folding `adders` in would have lost the original array-order-preserving "top 3" selection (a `$lookup` on an array-valued `localField` doesn't preserve the local array's order) for no real benefit at these volumes. Net: phase 2 went from 4 round trips to 3, plus removed `getPopularWithFriends`'s own redundant `User.findById(userId).select("following")` (same free win as `getNetworkActivity`'s, `req.user.following` already available).

Verified the same way: a standalone script with the old phase-2 logic next to the new one, run against 4 real cases (no-filter and movie-filter for `popular-this-week`, both test accounts for `popular-with-friends`) — byte-identical output on all 4, confirmed via the same deep-sorted-key comparison. Live-tested the real endpoints afterward with real data (`Pacific Rim: Uprising`, 3 real adders, correct avg rating) to confirm the actual controller — not just the standalone script — behaves the same. Re-ran the same 11-endpoint concurrent burst used throughout this investigation: **total wall time 3969ms → 2626ms** (~34% down), and `popular-with-friends` specifically dropped from the burst's worst straggler (~3.9s) to ~1.4s — no single endpoint in the latest burst exceeds ~2.6s, versus ~3.9s before. `getFeed` (`GET /api/feed`, a different endpoint) has the same redundant-`following`-fetch pattern but wasn't touched this round — not unused, though: it's not called by mobile, but **is** live in production for the web app (`frontend/src/pages/HomePage.jsx` via `frontend/src/api/feedService.js`), confirmed by grep before assuming otherwise. Left alone since it's out of scope for this mobile-focused pass.

### Follow-up round: same round-trip-reduction method applied to `getReviewsFeed`/`getPopularReviews`'s shared content hydration and `hydratePreviewItems` (backs `lists/popular` + `lists/discover`); real pill-smoothness bug fixed; real Shares-podium remount bug fixed
Three more asks in one message: (1) the drag-tracked pill from the previous round was smoother but still visibly froze right as the icon↔label content swapped mid-drag, then "caught up" after a pause; (2) the Shares page's own podium visibly loaded, then reset, then loaded again on first mount — a real bug, not just slowness; (3) one more Discover load-time pass if anything further was safely optimizable.

**Pill freeze, root-caused and fixed** (`CapsuleTabSwitcher.tsx`): the drag-tracked interpolation's two endpoints were `layouts[option.key]` — each slot's *live* measured geometry. But a slot's width depends on what it's currently rendering (label text vs. icon-only), and `activeKey` flips *during* the drag (at the same halfway-crossing point from the previous round), so both slots' content swaps instantly on that render — while their `onLayout` re-measurement (a real native layout pass + bridge round trip) only lands a frame or two later. In between, the interpolation was targeting stale (pre-swap) geometry, which is exactly the freeze-then-jump the user described. Fixed by caching each option's geometry specifically for its *label-showing* state only (`activeLayouts`, populated once per option key the first time it's ever rendered active, keyed by that render's own closed-over `activeKey` so a delayed callback can't mis-tag which state it belongs to) and interpolating toward those stable, already-known values instead of the live ones. With exactly 2 mutually-exclusive options, each one's own active-state geometry alone fully determines the capsule's layout at both drag endpoints, so this needs no extra cross-slot bookkeeping. One accepted limitation: option 2 ("Keşfet") starts icon-only, so its active geometry isn't cached until the user has switched to it at least once — the very first-ever switch still uses the old discrete tween, every switch after that (in either direction) is fully drag-tracked and smooth.

**Shares podium "loads, disappears, reloads" — a real remount bug, not slowness** (`SharesFeedSection.tsx`): the component branched `loading ? <View>…<PeoplePodium/>…</View> : <FlatList ListHeaderComponent={…<PeoplePodium/>…}>` — two structurally different trees, each containing its *own* `<PeoplePodium/>` element. React's reconciler doesn't diff across a ternary's two branches; the moment this section's own unrelated feed fetch finished and `loading` flipped, it unmounted the first `PeoplePodium` (destroying its already-fetched leaderboard data) and mounted a brand new one in the FlatList branch — which then had to fetch and load all over again from `loading: true`. That's the whole bug: the podium wasn't loading twice because it was slow, it was being torn down and rebuilt because a *different*, unrelated fetch happened to finish. Fixed by always rendering the same `FlatList` (never branching away from it), with `OnlineFriendsBar`/`PeoplePodium` permanently inside its `ListHeaderComponent` — `loading` now only swaps content *inside* that header (a spinner vs. the "Shares" title), never the tree position of `PeoplePodium` itself, so it mounts exactly once and keeps its own state regardless of how the surrounding feed's own load is going. Also fixed a latent related bug this exposed: `ListEmptyComponent` ("No shares yet.") was unconditionally set, which could have flashed while `feedRows` was still legitimately empty during the *first* load — now gated on `!loading` too.

**One more Discover round-trip pass** — applied the same `$documents`-based fold used for `getNetworkActivity`/`getPopularAdds` to two more shared hydration helpers that Discover's own rails depend on:
- `hydrateReviewResults` (`reviewController.js`, shared by `getReviewsFeed` — Discover's Reviews rail — and `getPopularReviews`): two separate `movies`/`series` `.find()`s folded into one `$documents`-seeded aggregation, deduped by distinct `contentType:contentId` first (multiple reviews can share the same content). Also removed `getReviewsFeed`'s own redundant `User.findById(userId).select("following")` (`req.user.following` already available). Net: this endpoint's round trips went from 5 (redundant fetch + reviews-aggregate/count pair + 2-query hydrate) down to 3.
- `hydratePreviewItems` (`customListRoute.js`, shared by `/lists/popular` — Discover's Lists rail — `/lists/discover`, `/lists/:id`, and `shareController.js`'s list-type `createShare`): same fold. `CustomList.items[].itemId` is already schema-typed ObjectId (unlike Review/Rating's String `contentId`), so this one needed no `$convert` step — a simpler case than the other two. Also removed `/lists/discover`'s own redundant `following` fetch; `User` import was then fully dead in that file (verified via grep — only the `import` line itself remained) and removed.

All three verified the same rigorous way as every round-trip change this session: a standalone script running the *old* implementation next to the *new* one against real data, deep-comparing every field after normalizing key order — byte-identical output in every case (`getPopularReviews`/`getReviewsFeed`'s shared hydration: 2 real accounts, byte-identical, old 1996ms→new 274ms on the first/coldest call; `hydratePreviewItems`: 20 real public lists, byte-identical, 840ms→299ms). Then live-tested the real endpoints afterward with real data to confirm the actual controllers behave the same, not just the standalone scripts. Re-ran the 11-endpoint burst 4 times after all three fixes: totals landed in the 2626-3017ms range (vs. the 3969ms baseline before this session's DB-latency work began) — a real, consistent improvement, but noisier run-to-run than earlier single readings suggested, since this environment's shared DB contention (this session's own repeated test traffic included) varies the total non-trivially between samples. The correctness verification is what should be trusted here, not any single burst-total reading in isolation.

### Follow-up: pill still stuttered after the previous fix — the window was smooth, but the slots underneath it weren't
User reported the stutter was still there. The previous round only made the *highlight window's* interpolation target stable — it didn't touch the fact that each `Pressable` slot's own width is naturally determined by its content (label text vs. icon-only), and that content still swaps *instantly* the moment `activeKey` flips mid-drag. So the window itself glided smoothly, but the slot content it was gliding toward was still popping to a new size underneath it at that exact instant — which is what kept reading as a freeze.

Fixed by explicitly driving each slot's own width the same way the window already is: `CapsuleTabSwitcher.tsx` now caches *both* states per option (`activeLayouts` from the previous round, plus a new `inactiveLayouts`) and interpolates each `Pressable`'s `width` between them continuously via `dragOffsetX`, instead of leaving it to natural content-driven sizing. Since a plain `Pressable` can't accept an `Animated.Value` in its style, wrapped it once at module scope via `Animated.createAnimatedComponent(Pressable)`. Added `overflow: "hidden"` + `numberOfLines={1}` on the label as a safety net for the moments mid-transition where the container is narrower than the label's natural width.

One real circular-dependency bug caught before shipping: once a slot's width is explicitly controlled by this interpolation, its own `onLayout` callback starts reporting back whatever the *animated* width currently is — not its true natural active/inactive size — so continuing to feed that into the `activeLayouts`/`inactiveLayouts` cache would slowly corrupt it with mid-transition values. Fixed by freezing the cache once `dragTracking` goes true (guard `if (dragTracking) return;` at the top of the layout handler) — by definition, once tracking is live, both states for both options are already known, so there's nothing left worth capturing anyway.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch (against the real running dev server, not a duplicate — confirmed via its own "Skipping dev server, already running" message) confirmed the new code compiled in.

### Reverted: the per-slot width animation caused a real regression (truncated labels), worse than the stutter it was chasing
User reported the pill still stuttered a little *and*, separately, that "Paylaşımlar"/"Keşfet" (Shares/Discover in English) were now rendering truncated — "Shar…"/"Discov…" — at rest, not just mid-drag. That's a real, more serious regression than residual jitter: a label that's permanently unreadable. Root cause of the truncation was never conclusively pinned down (suspected: the explicitly-set interpolated `width` and the natural `onLayout`-measured width disagreeing once one starts driving the other, though the exact mechanism wasn't confirmed since this couldn't be visually inspected, only reasoned about), but a broken label beats a marginally-smoother animation on any reasonable tradeoff — reverted the whole per-slot width/`AnimatedPressable`/`inactiveLayouts` addition from the previous round. `CapsuleTabSwitcher.tsx` is back to: window position/width drag-tracked continuously (the fix from 2 rounds ago, which is real and still in place), each slot's own size back to natural, content-driven sizing (a still-instant swap at the crossover, same as this component has always done, and same as the non-drag-tracked callers — Profile, Socials — still do). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle confirmed the revert compiled in (also confirmed a coincidental, unrelated `AnimatedPressable` string match elsewhere in the bundle — from a third-party package, not this file — wasn't a sign of stale code).

The residual "biraz tutukluk" (a little stutter) report predates this revert and hasn't been re-addressed — worth a fresh, more cautious look if the user raises it again, but not by re-attempting per-slot width animation blind; likely needs either a design compromise (accept the discrete content-swap as-is, focus purely on window smoothness) or a way to actually see the animation running before iterating further.

### Activity feed redesign: 2 new event types (`favorited`, `list_item_added`), sentence-style rows for 4 of the 6 types, real backend additions
A large, fully user-specified redesign of the network Activity feed (`ActivityRow.tsx`, Discover's own section, and the full paginated `/home/activity` page it links to).

**Section title**: `t("Activity")` → a new key, `t("Friends' Activity")`, used only by `ActivitySection.tsx`'s own header and `home/_layout.tsx`'s `activity` route title — the *shared* `"Activity"` key was deliberately left untouched since it's also used by Profile's own (self, not network) activity screen and a match-category label (`matchCategoryMeta.ts`), confirmed via grep before touching anything, to avoid renaming those by accident.

**Two brand-new event types, both real backend additions, not just UI:**
- **`favorited`** — powered by a new model, `backend/models/FavoriteEvent.js`: a small append-only log (`{user, contentId, contentType, createdAt}`), written only when `userController.js`'s `updateFavorites` (a whole-list-replace endpoint, not an add/remove toggle) detects an id in the new list that wasn't in the old one — diffed against `req.user[fieldToUpdate]` (already on hand from authMiddleware, no extra fetch). Deliberately does **not** touch `User.favoriteMovies`/`favoriteSeries` themselves (still plain, untimestamped ObjectId arrays) — those are read as raw id arrays by a dozen+ call sites across match-making, the leaderboard, and content-stats, and migrating that shape was exactly the "real, separate, carefully-scoped task" earlier rounds of this session deferred. The event log is purely additive, sitting beside those fields rather than replacing them. `logController.js`'s `resetData` now also clears a user's `FavoriteEvent` history, matching its existing favorites-wipe, so a reset account doesn't leave stale "favorited X" events showing in other people's feeds.
- **`list_item_added`** — an item added to an *existing* list, distinct from `list_created` (a brand-new list). No schema change needed: `CustomList.items[].addedAt` already existed, just wasn't surfaced as its own activity event before.

**`getNetworkActivity` (`activityController.js`)** grew from 4 to 6 parallel aggregations (still all in one `Promise.all`, same shape every round-trip fix this session established): `favorited` (equality-lookup content resolution, no `$convert` needed since `FavoriteEvent.contentId` was deliberately modeled as a real ObjectId, unlike Rating/Review's legacy String field) and `list_item_added` (`$unwind` on `items`, same `contentLookupStages` helper). Also added a bonus enrichment to the existing `watchlist_added` aggregation: if the same actor has also rated that exact content, its value now rides along as `rating`. Getting this right took real care — a naive per-document correlated `$lookup` on `{user, contentId}` would've repeated the exact `MaxTimeMSExpired` mistake this file's own comments already document; instead it's a plain equality `$lookup` on `user` alone (pulls in each actor's own ratings, still a hash join, not a nested loop) followed by a cheap in-memory `$filter` over that one already-fetched small array to find the matching `contentId` (with a `$toString` for the same String-vs-ObjectId mismatch as everywhere else in this file) — no second DB round trip, no correlated per-document query.

**Mobile (`ActivityRow.tsx`)**: `rated`/`list_created` keep their original icon/tag + inline-title treatment unchanged (not part of this ask). The other 4 types (`watchlist_added`, `reviewed`, `favorited`, `list_item_added`) now lead with a single icon (`bookmark-outline`, the pre-existing `chatbox-outline`, `star-outline`, `albums-outline` respectively) followed by a real translated sentence embedding the title (e.g. "Added {{title}} to their watchlist") — the standalone title `Text` next to the old tag/icon is gone for these 4 (redundant now that the title lives inside the sentence). `watchlist_added`'s bonus `rating` (when present) renders as a second, indented line below the sentence via the existing `StarRatingDisplay` — placement was an explicit design call the user left open; this was the recommendation.

**Translations**: added 5 new keys (the section title + 4 sentence templates) across all 12 locales in `mobile/src/locales/index.ts` — via a small one-off Python script (not 60 manual edits) that inserted each locale's translation right after its existing `"No activity yet."` anchor line, verified via diff before trusting it. Reused this app's already-established vocabulary per locale for "Watchlist"/"Favorites"/"Review"/"List" (grepped existing keys like `"Watchlist"`/`"Review"` per locale first, rather than inventing new terms) — same `{{var}}`-interpolated-key convention as the pre-existing `"Created list \"{{name}}\""`, not a hardcoded-English shortcut. Not mirrored into `frontend/src/locales/index.js` — confirmed via grep that frontend has no matching `"No activity yet."` key at all, meaning it doesn't have this feature to translate for; the two locale files have already diverged in content (only their structure is meant to mirror), so there was nothing to keep in sync here.

**Verified end-to-end with real data, not just code review**: live-tested the actual `/feed/activity` endpoint (via the JWT-minting convention) against Zachary's real network and confirmed all 6 event types now appear with correct real content — including seeding one genuinely new `favorited` event through the *real* `PUT /users/me/favorites` endpoint (not a bypassed DB write) for a real test account, confirming the whole diff→log→surface path end to end. Separately confirmed the `watchlist_added` rating enrichment against a real, independently-verified match (a direct DB query found 110 real watchlist-add+matching-rating pairs in Zachary's network; the API response for the one that landed on the first page matched that direct query's own numbers exactly). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch (against the real running dev server) confirmed the new code, icons, and translation keys all compiled in.

**Follow-up**: the 4 new sentences were truncating with `numberOfLines={1}` on longer titles — user asked to let them wrap instead of forcing a fit. Bumped to `numberOfLines={2}` on all 4, and switched `detailRow`'s `alignItems` from `center` to `flex-start` so the leading icon aligns with the sentence's first line rather than the vertical center of a now-possibly-2-line block (a no-op visually for the still-single-line `rated`/`list_created` rows, so safe for those too). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh bundle confirmed `numberOfLines: 2` compiled in (19 occurrences, matching the 4 new Text elements × several unrelated pre-existing 2-line usages elsewhere in the app).

### Follow-up: "Rated" prefix added back after all, and two real tappable-link features — list name → that list, "favorites" word → that person's Favorites tab
Three more asks. **"Rated" prefix**: user liked the previous round's reasoning but still wanted the word visible — `rated`'s row is now `⭐ Rated ★★★★☆ for {{title}}`. This time it safely reuses the app's existing bare `"Rated"` key (used elsewhere as a filter-chip label, `WatchlistGrid.tsx`) rather than needing a new 12-locale translation: checked every locale's existing value first and confirmed each is a plain past-participle/label form with no person or tense conjugation (`"Puanlanmış"`, `"Bewertet"`, `"Evaluato"`, etc.) — unlike the earlier `"Rated {{title}}"` mistake (a full conjugated sentence, "you rated X"), a bare label word doesn't carry that risk, so reuse was safe here. Needed a new non-`flex:1` style (`word`) for it, since giving it the same `flex:1` as the trailing sentence text would have let it greedily claim the row's width and push the stars out of place.

**Two tappable in-sentence links** — `list_item_added`'s list name now navigates to that list (`${basePath}/lists/${listId}`), and `favorited`'s "favorites" word now navigates to that actor's own profile, landing directly on their Favorites tab. Implementing "part of a translated sentence is interactive" without ever having used react-i18next's `Trans` component in this app (confirmed via grep — zero usages anywhere) needed a different technique: a new `renderLinkedSentence(fullText, linkText, onPress)` helper that splits the *already-resolved* sentence string (after `t()` has run) on a known substring and renders that substring as its own nested, independently-tappable `Text` — RN's `Text` supports `onPress` when nested inside another `Text`, and tapping it doesn't also fire the row's own outer `onPress`. This works for any locale's word order automatically, since i18next has already ordered the sentence correctly before the split ever runs — the helper only has to *find* the substring, not decide where it belongs (`Trans` would have needed per-locale re-authoring with embedded component tags at the exact right position instead).
- `list_item_added`: splits on `event.listName` itself — an exact match is guaranteed, since it's the literal value that was interpolated into the sentence.
- `favorited`: splits on `t("Favorites")` — the app's own existing nav-tab label, reused purely to know *where* the word landed in the resolved sentence, not re-translated for this. Verified programmatically (not just eyeballed) that the word is a real substring of the sentence in all 12 locales before trusting it — case-insensitive containment held in every one (Turkish's declined `"favorilerine"` containing the bare `"Favoriler"` as a prefix, etc.).

The "favorites" link needed one small new piece of navigation support: profile tabs (`PublicProfileCategoryTabs.tsx`) had no way to land on a specific tab — always defaulted to Sharings via a bare `useState<Category>("sharings")`. Added an optional `initialCategory` prop (falls back to `"sharings"` exactly as before when absent, so this is additive, not a behavior change for any existing caller) and had `app/user/[id]/index.tsx` read an optional `?tab=` query param to populate it, so `/user/:id?tab=favorites` now deep-links straight into that tab.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (real running server) confirmed `renderLinkedSentence`, `initialCategory`, and the `tab=favorites` navigation call all compiled in.

### Follow-up: the "favorites" link didn't actually navigate anywhere different — real bug, root-caused against this app's own history rather than guessed
User reported tapping "favorites" always landed on the content detail page (the outer row's own destination), not the person's profile. Real bug in the previous round's `renderLinkedSentence`: it nested a `<Text onPress={onLinkPress}>` inside the outer sentence `Text`, itself inside the row's outer `Pressable`. That shape looks like the standard "RN Text supports onPress on nested Text" pattern, but it doesn't reliably win the tap over an ancestor `Pressable` — confirmed by checking this codebase's own history rather than guessing from general RN knowledge: `ShareCard.tsx`'s `renderCaptionWithLinks` (lines ~572/621/647) uses the exact same Text-in-Text-in-Pressable shape, and README never actually verified *that* one routes taps correctly either — only that it compiled. Very likely has the identical live bug (tapping a username inside a share caption probably also just opens the underlying content instead), flagged to the user, not fixed in this round since it wasn't what was reported.

This app *does* have an already-proven, working mechanism for "one small tap target should win over a much larger enclosing Pressable": nested `Pressable`-in-`Pressable` (`ListRailCard.tsx`/`ReviewSwipeCard.tsx`'s `detailsButton` inside `detailsCatcher`, explicitly documented in this same README as the deliberate fix after two earlier z-index/`pointerEvents` attempts failed). Rebuilt `renderLinkedSentence` around that instead: a real nested `<Pressable onPress={onLinkPress}>` wrapping just the linked `Text`, not a `Text`-with-its-own-`onPress`. Trade-off: a `Pressable` can't nest inside `Text` for true inline reflow, so the sentence is now a `flexWrap: "wrap"` row of separate before/link/after pieces rather than one continuously-reflowing paragraph — accepted given these sentences are short and the user already said wrapping onto more lines (rather than truncating) is fine.

### Follow-up: `rated`'s wrapped 2nd line started at the wrong horizontal position
Separately, user reported that when `rated`'s row wraps to a 2nd line, that line starts aligned with wherever the star rating *ends*, not with where the sentence itself starts (the "Rated" word). Real cause: `rated` renders as 4 separate flex-row siblings (icon, "Rated", `StarRatingDisplay`, trailing text) — when the trailing text's *own* internal wrap (`numberOfLines`) kicks in, that 2nd line reflows relative to the trailing text's *own* box position (which starts well to the right, after the icon/word/stars), not the row's own left edge, which is what read as misaligned.

The more natural fix — embedding `StarRatingDisplay` directly inside the sentence `Text` so the whole thing reflows as one real paragraph — was considered and rejected: `StarRatingDisplay` is a `View` wrapping several of its own nested `Text` stars, and React Native's support for an arbitrary View-with-nested-children rendered *inline inside* another `Text` (as opposed to a single atomic inline image) has known, inconsistent behavior on Android specifically. Not worth the risk of trading a cosmetic alignment issue for a potential crash or garbled layout on one platform, especially unverifiable without a device. Used the same `flexWrap: "wrap"` technique as the fix above instead: `detailRow` itself now wraps, so when the trailing text doesn't fit next to the stars, it drops entirely to its own full-width line — starting flush with the row's own left edge — rather than continuing to hang off wherever the stars ended.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (real running server) confirmed the rebuilt `renderLinkedSentence`, `sentenceWrap`, and `detailRow`'s new `flexWrap` all compiled in.

### Follow-up: the `flexWrap` fix wrapped too *early* — same underlying flexbox limitation, needed real text reflow this time
User reported it still looked wrong: line 1 was leaving obvious empty space before jumping to line 2, rather than filling out as far as it could first. Real cause, and it's the same one flagged (but under-weighted) in the previous round's own writeup: flexbox treats each row child as an atomic block for wrap purposes. The moment the trailing "for {{title}}" `Text` (a separate flex sibling from "Rated"/the stars) doesn't fit in whatever space is left on line 1, the *whole* sibling drops to line 2 — it never gets the chance to fill the remaining space on line 1 first and only wrap what doesn't fit, the way one real paragraph would. `flexWrap: "wrap"` on the row didn't fix this; it just moved where the same atomic jump happens.

There's no flexbox-only fix for "fill to the end of the line, then wrap" — that's real text reflow, which only happens when everything lives inside one `Text`. Rebuilt `rated` that way: `"Rated"` and `"for {{title}}"` as plain text, with the star rating nested inline as its own styled `Text` containing a **plain star string** — not the `StarRatingDisplay` component, which is a `View` wrapping several of its own `Text` children and can't safely nest that way inside another `Text` on Android (the same concern already raised and rejected two rounds ago). A plain string of `"★"` characters (built by a small local `ratingStars()` helper replicating `StarRatingDisplay.tsx`'s own 1-10→0.5-5/full-stars/"1/2" scaling logic) nests inside `Text` with zero risk, since it's just characters, not a component. This gets true paragraph reflow: line 1 fills as far as it can, and only the overflow wraps to line 2, flush with the row's own left edge.

`favorited`/`list_item_added` (`renderLinkedSentence`) keep the exact same underlying limitation, deliberately left as-is this round — their linked segment has to be a real `Pressable` (for the tap-priority fix two rounds ago) and a `Pressable` can't nest inside `Text`, so there's no equivalent fix available without giving up either the reflow or the working tap target. Flagged as a known, accepted trade-off in the code's own comment rather than silently left unexplained.

Separately: mid-fix, discovered the entire dev environment (backend, Metro, ngrok) had gone down — not from anything done this session (every kill this session only ever matched throwaway verification instances on a different port; the real server used `--host localhost` with no port override). Restarted the full stack via `mobile/scripts/start-codespace.sh` and re-verified both the public backend URL and the ngrok tunnel were actually live (not just that the script printed success) before trusting it — same discipline as every dev-server restart earlier in this doc's history.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (against the freshly-restarted real server) confirmed `ratingStars`/`starsInline` compiled in.

### Follow-up: `favorited`/`list_item_added` had the identical "wraps too early" problem `rated` just had — fixed the same way, by actually checking this app's real RN version instead of assuming stale caution still applies
User reported `list_item_added`/`favorited` still wrapped early too, and specifically that a wrapped word could land on line 3 while line 2 had obvious room left — the exact same flexbox-atomic-child limitation as `rated`'s own earlier fix, just not yet applied to these two. The real fix (per that earlier round) is real text reflow — the link segment inside one continuous `Text` rather than a separate flex sibling. The blocker was that `renderLinkedSentence`'s link needs to be a genuine `Pressable` (for the tap-priority fix from 2 rounds ago), and an *earlier* round had avoided nesting `Pressable` inline inside `Text` specifically because older React Native has known, inconsistent Android support for that.

Before repeating that same avoidance a third time, actually checked whether it still applies to *this app*: `react-native` is 0.86.2, on Expo SDK 57, which defaults to the New Architecture (Fabric) with no old-architecture opt-out available at that SDK version. Inline non-Text content inside `Text` is substantially more mature on Fabric than the older-RN/Android behavior the earlier caution was based on — that caution was correct in general, just stale for this specific stack. Rebuilt `renderLinkedSentence` to embed the `Pressable` directly inside the sentence `Text` (before-text, then the inline `Pressable`-wrapped link, then after-text, all as children of one `Text`) instead of the flex-wrap-row version — same principle as `rated`'s own fix, now applied consistently everywhere a sentence needs both true reflow and an interactive segment. Removed the now-dead `sentenceWrap`/`sentencePart` styles the flex-row version needed.

One thing this round couldn't fully close out: whether nested Pressable-in-Pressable's proven "innermost wins" priority (`ListRailCard.tsx`/`ReviewSwipeCard.tsx`'s own confirmed mechanism) holds up specifically when the inner Pressable is laid out *inline inside Text* rather than as a plain block sibling — that combination hasn't been exercised anywhere else in this codebase yet. Flagged explicitly in the code's own comment as the one still-unverified part, worth a real tap-test on the actual "favorites"/list-name links now that the wrapping itself should be fixed.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (against the real running server, `metro`/tunnel/backend all re-verified live first) confirmed the rebuilt `renderLinkedSentence` compiled in.

### Follow-up: the wrapping fixed, taps confirmed working, but the linked word itself sat slightly off the surrounding text's baseline
Good news first: the user confirmed the tap-priority concern flagged in the previous round's writeup as unverified actually works correctly — nested Pressable-in-Pressable's "innermost wins" behavior does hold up even with the inner Pressable laid out inline inside Text, not just as a block sibling. One real bug found instead, much simpler than another layout-engine fight: `styles.link` (and `styles.starsInline`, the same oversight, not yet reported but caught proactively) only set `color`, nothing else — so the nested `Text` fell back to React Native's *default* font metrics instead of matching `sentence`'s own `fontFamily`/`fontSize`. Two Text nodes with different font metrics sitting on the same line don't share a baseline, which is exactly "sits a bit higher than the rest of the words." Fixed by giving both styles the same explicit `fontFamily`/`fontSize` as `sentence`, keeping only the differentiating `color`.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (real running server, endpoints re-verified live) confirmed both style fixes compiled in.

### Follow-up: font-matching wasn't the actual fix — the misalignment is the inline Pressable (a View, not Text) itself, and this one is genuinely unverified
User confirmed the font-matching fix (previous round) didn't resolve it — the linked word still sits above the rest of the line. That rules out font-metric mismatch as the cause and points at what's actually the harder, more fundamental issue: it's the `Pressable` itself — a `View`, not `Text` — that a text layout engine positions differently by default when embedded inline, independent of what font its own children use. Compounded here since this app's custom fonts (`theme/typography`) likely have non-standard ascent/descent metrics relative to whatever generic baseline the layout engine assumes for an inline View.

Tried React Native's own documented mechanism for this exact class of problem first: `verticalAlign` (built for aligning an inline image/view within surrounding text). It doesn't type-check on a `Pressable`/`View`'s style in this RN version — TypeScript only accepts it on `Text` — confirming it isn't the supported route for a View in this setup. Fell back to a small manual position nudge (`position: "relative", top: 2` on the Pressable wrapper) instead.

**This one is explicitly flagged, not claimed as fixed**: it's a pixel-value guess with no way to see the actual rendered result — genuinely different from every other fix in this activity-feed arc, which were all verified against real data or a real compiled bundle before being reported done. Told the user directly that `top` may need to move up or down from `2` once they can actually see it, rather than presenting an untested guess as a confirmed solution.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (real running server, endpoints re-verified live) confirmed `inlineLinkWrap` compiled in — compilation only, not visual correctness.

### Shares' list-post box: cascade replaced with a scrollable, gapless "film strip"
User asked for a real redesign of the list-post poster display in the Shares feed, not the overlapping/offset `PosterCascade` treatment it shared with Discover's Popular Lists rail (`ListRailCard.tsx`) — instead, posters flush edge-to-edge with zero gap between them, scrollable within the post's own frame ("film şeridi" — a film strip), and no rounded corners on the individual posters (a rounded corner at every poster boundary would read as a seam even with literally zero spacing between them, defeating the point of a continuous strip).

Scoped to `ShareCard.tsx`'s list-post box only, not `PosterCascade.tsx` itself — that component stays exactly as it was and Discover's Popular Lists rail (`ListRailCard.tsx`) keeps its own cascading look unchanged, since the ask was specifically about the Shares list post. Replaced the single `<PosterCascade items={...} direction="horizontal" posterWidth={56} fitToWidth />` call with an inline horizontal `ScrollView` mapping every `previewItem` to a flush, square-cornered poster `View` (image or, matching `PosterCascade`'s own fallback convention, a title-text placeholder when `poster_path` is missing) — no per-poster `borderRadius`, no `gap`/margin between them. `PosterCascade`'s import was then dead in this file and removed; confirmed via grep it's still independently used by `ListRailCard.tsx`, unaffected.

The new `ScrollView` is imported from `react-native-gesture-handler`, not `react-native` — `ShareCard.tsx` renders inside `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s vertical `FlatList`, itself nested inside `home/index.tsx`'s horizontal gesture-handler pager, so any new horizontal scroller in that ancestor chain needs to share the same gesture-handler resolution system this session already established for `PeoplePodium`/`ContentRail`/`LeaderboardPodium`, or the pager would just eat its drag.

Verified against real data: fetched the live share feed for a real account and found 6 real list-type shares in the first page, one with a real 11-item `previewItems` array (all carrying real `poster_path` values) — confirmed the film strip has genuinely enough real content to be worth scrolling through, not just a token few items. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (real running server, endpoints re-verified live) confirmed `filmStripPoster`/`filmStripFallback` compiled in.

### Follow-up: rounded-ends-only + a thin outline, real bug fixed (strip couldn't be scrolled at all), and the post's own text reordered
Three more asks in one message.

**Visual polish achieved with one technique, not two**: rather than conditionally rounding just the first/last poster's own outer corners (real per-index logic — different corner radii for the first item, the last item, and every item in between) and separately drawing a border around the whole thing, both came from the same simpler move: give the *container* (the `ScrollView` itself) a `borderRadius` (reusing `PosterCascade.tsx`'s own exported `CASCADE_POSTER_RADIUS` constant rather than a new magic number) plus `overflow: "hidden"` — the container's own rounded shape naturally clips the strip's outer silhouette, so only the first and last posters' outer edges end up visually curved, while every seam between posters stays a flush straight line, with zero per-poster conditional styling needed. The border itself uses `colors.border`, the same semantic token `PosterCascade.tsx` already uses for its own poster outlines — confirmed via this app's own palette file that it's lighter than `base200`/`base300` (checked against every one of this app's 9 dark-style themes; there is no light theme, so no separate check needed there) — not a new "make something lighter" color computed for this.

**Real bug, not cosmetic**: the strip couldn't be scrolled at all — dragging it scrolled the whole Shares page instead. The `ScrollView` was already the `react-native-gesture-handler` version, correctly matching the outer Media pager's own gesture system — the actual gap was the `listBox` `Pressable` directly wrapping it, which was still the *plain* `react-native` one. A plain `Pressable` sitting directly between a gesture-handler `ScrollView` and a gesture-handler outer pager doesn't participate in gesture-handler's own touch negotiation at all (it's a different system entirely), so the drag never had a chance to reach the strip — the outer pager's own gesture-handler resolution just claimed it first. Fixed by switching `listBox`'s `Pressable` to `react-native-gesture-handler`'s own `Pressable` (imported aliased as `GHPressable`, alongside the plain `react-native` one still used by every other Pressable in this file that doesn't wrap a nested scroller). **Worth remembering as a general pattern, extending the one already documented for this app's scroll chains**: it's not just *scrollers* that need to be gesture-handler's version throughout an ancestor chain — any plain-`react-native` `Pressable`/`Touchable` sitting directly between two gesture-handler components can itself break the chain, even though it isn't a scroller.

**Post text reordered**: the "{{user}} shared a list." info line now renders first (plain text, the linked-username version removed entirely — sidesteps the same unverified-tap-routing pattern flagged elsewhere in this file, `renderCaptionWithLinks`/`userLink`, rather than risk it here too), the list's own title follows it, and the list's own description (if present) now renders as an additional third line rather than replacing the info line the way it used to (previously mutually exclusive with it).

One thing this round couldn't verify hands-on: whether the `GHPressable` swap actually restores real scrolling — that's the whole point of the fix, but it's a touch-interaction question no amount of `tsc`/bundle-compile checking can confirm on its own. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle (real running server, endpoints re-verified live) confirmed `filmStripContainer`/`CASCADE_POSTER_RADIUS`/`GHPressable` all compiled in — flagged to the user as needing a real on-device check for the scroll fix specifically.

**Both translation keys — `"Add to Watchlist"` and `"Added to Watchlist"` — turned out to already exist in all 12 locales**, apparently added ahead of this feature but never wired to any actual UI before now (confirmed via grep: zero call sites for either key anywhere in the codebase prior to this change). ### Immediate correction, same day: the frame redone to actually hug the plus's own silhouette, not a generic circle around it

The circular CSS border from the round above missed the actual ask — the user clarified they wanted a frame that traces the plus shape's *own edges* ("kenarlarını takip ederek etrafını saran"), the same idea as the list-post film strip's own border, which clips to that content's real silhouette rather than sitting as an unrelated container shape around it ("alakasız şekilde bir çerçeve değil").

**Reworked as an SVG stroke-then-fill pass, not a CSS border on the wrapping `View`.** `watchlistStickerWrap`'s `borderRadius`/`borderWidth`/`borderColor` removed. The plus's two `Rect`s are now drawn **twice** at identical coordinates: first a stroke-only pass (`fill="none"`, `stroke={colors.primary}`, `strokeWidth={2}`) at the exact same `x/y/width/height/rx` as the real shape, then the gradient-filled pass on top. SVG centers a stroke on its own path by default (half inside the shape, half outside) — the fill pass on top covers the inner half, leaving only the outer half visible as a thin line sitting right along the shape's real boundary. Traced through the geometry by hand to confirm this holds at the cross's concave inner corners too (where the two bars meet, e.g. near `(8,8)`): each bar's stroke only remains visible where it isn't covered by *either* fill rect, which is exactly the region outside the real plus silhouette — not a coincidence, a property of drawing both rects' stroke-then-fill in the same pass order, so overlapping regions between the two bars always end up correctly covered by whichever bar's fill sits on top there.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle grepped for `strokeWidth` (56 hits across the whole bundle — confirmed the two new watchlist ones specifically by re-checking the source file directly, since a bundle-wide count isn't unique to this one component) present, and the source file confirmed to no longer contain the old `borderRadius:18`/`borderColor: colors.primary` CSS-border approach on `watchlistStickerWrap`.
