Still not visually screenshotted on-device.

### Eighth pass: chip width goes back to fitting each genre's own word length, and the coverflow gets a genuine leading empty rest position (nothing selected at rest, all ring colors lit, detail shows overall totals)

Two direct corrections to the previous round's fixed-width, always-something-selected model:

**Variable chip width.** `CHIP_WIDTH = 138` (one fixed slot for every genre, sized for the worst case) is gone — each chip is now sized to its own word length via `chipWidthFor(genre)`, a text-length estimate (`genre.length * 6.8 + padding`, clamped to a `MIN_CHIP_WIDTH` floor for very short names like "War") rather than a real `onLayout` measurement — the same fallback formula `CineGraphDonut.tsx`/`CineMatchGenreRing.tsx` already use before their own first real chip measurement lands, used here as the *only* method rather than just a pre-measurement fallback, specifically to avoid the "chip visibly resizes right after mount" jitter those two files have to freeze `chipSizes` after first commit to avoid.

**A real, reachable "nothing selected" rest position.** The previous round's coverflow always had *something* centered (genre index 0, at rest) because it copied `PosterCoverflow.tsx`'s fixed-pitch model exactly, where every slot is a real item. This round adds a genuine leading slot with nothing in it (`EMPTY_SLOT_WIDTH`, no chip rendered, not selectable by content) — at rest (before any scrolling), *this* is what's centered, not any genre, so `selectedGenre` starts (and returns, if scrolled back) as `null`: both rings show every slice in its own full, undimmed color (the ring's existing dimming logic — `isDimmed = selectedGenre !== null && ...` — already produced exactly this for a null selection, no ring-side change needed), and the You/username detail readout shows each person's overall total instead of any one genre's count (this fallback existed in round six, was dropped in round seven on the assumption a coverflow always has something centered, and is restored here now that that assumption no longer holds).

This forced a real mechanical change beyond just adding one more item: variable-width slots break `PosterCoverflow.tsx`'s own `pitch`/`snapToInterval`/`round(scrollX/pitch)` math, which only works when every slot is the same size. Replaced with: each slot's own centering scroll offset computed from the cumulative real width of everything before it (`offsets`, one entry per slot including the leading empty one), `snapToOffsets={offsets}` instead of a shared `snapToInterval`, and the scroll listener picking whichever precomputed offset the live position is currently closest to instead of a single `round()`. Verified this geometry with a standalone Node simulation (not by eyeballing it) before trusting it: for a realistic 9-genre mix including "Sci-Fi & Fantasy" and "War", `offsets[0]` came back exactly `0` (confirming the empty slot centers at rest with zero scroll), the full offsets array was strictly increasing (confirming no slot-ordering overlap), and the closest-offset matching correctly picked slot 0 at rest and slot 1 once scrolled to its own offset.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `chipWidthFor`/`EMPTY_SLOT_WIDTH`/`snapToOffsets` compiled in, the old fixed `CHIP_WIDTH = 138` constant is gone, and the round-six `totalMine`/`totalTheirs` fallback (removed in round seven, restored this round) is present again. Still not visually screenshotted on-device.

### Back to Shared Genres/Favorites: a real, previously-hidden backend data bug found while broadening the ratings criteria, plus four smaller direct fixes

Six distinct asks in one round, unrelated to the Variety card above — back on Shared Genres/Favorites (`matchController.js`, `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`, `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`, `useRevealAnimation.ts`).

**1. `getSharedGenreContent` broadened to include one-sided ratings.** Previously excluded a title entirely unless *both* sides had rated it (even after the earlier "closeness, not a high-rating floor" fix) — silently hiding anything only one of the two had actually rated. Now includes a title if either side rated it and, when both did, they're still within the existing deviation; only truly excludes "both rated it, but disagree by more than the deviation." The other side renders "Not rated yet" client-side rather than the title being hidden outright. (Titles rated by *neither* side can't come from this endpoint's own candidate pool at all — it's sourced entirely from `Rating` documents — so that specific case doesn't literally arise here; flagged as a possible follow-up if a different, non-ratings-sourced candidate pool for a genre is ever wanted.)

**A real, previously-hidden backend data bug found and fixed while live-verifying #1** — not from reading, from the numbers not adding up: right after deploying the broadened query, several titles came back with *both* `myRating` and `targetRating` null despite being present in the result at all, which shouldn't be possible if they only qualify by having at least one real rating. Traced it by adding temporary debug logging directly into the running endpoint (confirmed live: the title's real Mongo `_id` was genuinely absent from the computed candidate-id set, yet `Model.find({_id: {$in: candidateIds}})` still returned it) down to the actual root cause: `Rating.contentId` is schema-typed as `String`, but a chunk of this database's seeded rows actually store it as a raw `ObjectId` (bypassing Mongoose's own cast — likely a bulk-insert path that wrote real `ObjectId` values instead of going through `.create()`/`.save()`). `.lean()` returns whatever BSON type is really stored, so `r.contentId` was a `String` for some rows and an `ObjectId` object for others. Using it as-is as a `Map` key broke every `ObjectId`-typed row: `Map` keys compare objects by reference, so the later `myRatingById.get(d._id.toString())` lookup (always a real string) could never match a key that was itself an `ObjectId` object — the Mongo query still found the right document either way (the driver compares BSON values, not JS types, so `$in` matched correctly regardless), but the *rating* attached to it silently vanished, rendering as "Not rated yet" on both sides despite a real rating existing. Fixed by normalizing with `String(r.contentId)` when building the lookup maps — the same normalization every *other* `Rating.contentId` usage in this file already did via `.toString()` (confirmed by grep: `getContentRatings` and a couple of other functions were already careful about this; only this newly-written function had skipped it). Live-verified before and after on the real `Zachary`/`Peter` pair: 10 titles across 3 genres showing `null`/`null` before the fix, 0 after, with the correct number of genuinely one-sided ratings (21) now showing real values on the rated side.

**2–5, smaller direct fixes in the same area:**
- Shared Genres' own poster detail (`MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`) now shows "Not rated yet" (a new `ratingMuted` style, matching `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`'s own) instead of `formatFiveScale`'s bare `"-"` fallback when a rating is missing on one side — consistent with the broadened data now regularly including one-sided-only titles.
- The Shared Genres empty-state text was stale ("...you haven't both rated a {{genre}} title similarly") now that one-sided ratings count — reworded to "Neither of you has rated anything in {{genre}} yet.", the only condition that can actually produce an empty result now.
- The "show all genres" overview grid (tap the genre pill to open it) is tappable now — previously purely decorative ("no onPress at all" per its own prior comment). New `goToSpecificGenre(genre)` jumps the carousel directly to the tapped genre and closes the grid, landing on that genre's own poster carousel + detail info, the same destination the pill/arrows already reach a step at a time.
- Real bug fixed in the shared `useRevealAnimation.ts` hook (used across this whole match-analysis panel, not just here): its effect only ever handled `activeKey` becoming *truthy* (reset to 0, animate to 1) — becoming falsy was a silent no-op, leaving the animated value frozen at whatever it last reached instead of animating back down. Harmless wherever the revealed content is conditionally unmounted outright on hide, but reported live as info text visibly "stuck in the background" after rapid repeated taps on the genre pill (toggling `showAllGenres` faster than the animation could settle) — fixed by adding the missing symmetric branch (animate to 0 on hide), while still preserving the existing "replay from scratch on every new truthy key" behavior for the show side.

**6. `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`**: added a second divider between the poster-detail block and the badge legend below it (previously only had one, between the poster row and the detail block) — the detail block's own content was already vertically centered within its fixed-height reserve, so sandwiching it between two matching dividers puts it exactly in the middle of the two lines rather than just centered in an otherwise-unbounded area.

Verified: `node --check` clean on the backend controller; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on mobile; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `goToSpecificGenre`, the new "Not rated yet" branches, and the reworded empty-state text all compiled in, with the old stale empty-state string gone from the component source (a same-named but even-older string variant — "...highly" instead of "...similarly" — still exists in `mobile/src/locales/index.ts`'s static translation tables; this is a pre-existing dead/orphaned translation key from before this session even started, not a live bug — `t()` calls with no matching locale entry render the source-language key text directly, which is the correct new copy).

### New "Activity" card added (the last of the 5 breakdown categories to get one) — a real overlap made visible via a new endpoint, deliberately on its own 30-day window that doesn't touch the actual score

Design discussion first, same process as Variety's own card: of the 5 weighted breakdown categories, Taste/Favorites/Social/Variety already had dedicated cards; only Activity ("bonus" in the backend, "Recent activity overlap — what you've both been watching lately") didn't. Investigated `computeMatchBreakdown`'s three "bonus" sub-scores before proposing anything: `trendingAlignment` (50% of the sub-score) is a Jaccard ratio of each side's most-recent 10 rated `contentId`s — a real overlap SET exists in memory, just never exposed, only its ratio; `activityRecency` and `watchActivityScore` are pure counts/ratios with no title identity, nothing meaningful to visualize. Recommended and approved: surface the actual overlap set as a poster feed, the same visual language every other card in this panel already uses (poster row/coverflow + a two-column "You"/username detail readout), skipping the other two sub-scores entirely since there's no content behind them to show.

Direct follow-up on the time window: the score's own `RATING_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS` is 90 days, which read as too long for a card framed as "lately." Confirmed changing that shared constant would shift the real live match percentage for every user (it feeds `trendingAlignment`/`activityRecency` directly) before proposing anything, then built this card on its own separate, dedicated window instead — 30 days, chosen for the same reason recommended: short enough to genuinely mean "recent," long enough that a moderately active pair usually has *something* in it. `RATING_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS` itself is completely untouched; the actual match-percentage math for every user is unchanged.

**Backend**: new `getRecentSharedActivity` (`matchController.js`) + route `POST /:targetUserId/recent-activity` (`matchRoute.js`) — titles *both* sides rated within the new `RECENT_ACTIVITY_WINDOW_MS` (30 days), a deliberate intersection (not `getSharedGenreContent`'s own broadened one-sided-OK rule) since Activity is specifically about co-engagement, not "something either of you might like" — that's what Shared Genres/Favorites already cover. Sorted server-side by whichever side rated it more recently. Applied the same `String(r.contentId)` normalization `getSharedGenreContent` needed for the ObjectId/String `contentId` data bug found two rounds ago — this is a second, independent call site that would have hit the identical bug otherwise.

### Genre-filter awareness for Favorites/Variety, and a real `useCount` bug found while checking — both investigated before touching anything

Two questions about how the Sync search's own filters (`genres[]`, `useCount`, `useAvgRating`) reach the results deck's cards. Investigated the real code before proposing anything, rather than assuming either was broken:

**Favorites — already correct, nothing to change.** `matchInsights.favoritesOverlap` (what `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx` renders) is built server-side from the exact same `filterFavoritesByGenre`-scoped `favorites1`/`favorites2` arrays `computeMatchBreakdown` already uses for the *score* — confirmed by reading `buildMatchInsights`'s own call site, not assumed. So an active genre filter already narrows Favorites the same way it narrows Shared Genres; the user's own read that "Shared Genres already only looks at the selected genre, no problem there" turned out to already be true for Favorites too, just not yet checked.

**Variety — a real gap, fixed client-side, no backend change needed.** `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`'s data source (`getUserCineGraph` via `getCineGraph`) has no genre-scoping parameter at all — it always returns every genre's stats for the user's whole watchlist. Rather than adding backend filtering support, `MatchVarietyRings.tsx` now takes a new `activeGenres: string[]` prop (`MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` passes `filters.genres` straight through) and narrows the already-fetched `movieStats`/`seriesStats` down to just those genres client-side (`filterStats`, a plain object-entries filter) before anything derives from them — ring slices, the color map, the coverflow's own genre list, and the You/username totals all read from the filtered result. Empty `activeGenres` (no filter active) is a no-op, matching the same convention `computeMatchBreakdown` itself already uses server-side.

**A real, previously-unnoticed `useCount` bug found while verifying, not assumed**: traced exactly what `useCount`/`useAvgRating` touch in `computeMatchBreakdown`, expecting (per the user's own observation) that neither visibly affects any detail card — true for `useAvgRating` (score-only, as expected), but `useCount: false` turned out to leave `g1`/`g2` (the per-genre count maps) completely empty for every genre, and those exact objects were what `buildMatchInsights` read to build `sharedGenres` — meaning toggling off "use count" as a *scoring* preference was silently emptying the entire Shared Genres card too, a real bug rather than an intentional side effect. Fixed by decoupling the two: added always-populated `genreCounts1`/`genreCounts2` (same genre-filter scoping, but never gated by `useCount`) built in the same loop as `g1`/`g2`, and `buildMatchInsights` now reads from those instead — `g1`/`g2` themselves are untouched and still correctly gated by `useCount` for the score. Live-verified before/after on the real `Zachary`/`Peter` pair: `sharedGenres` came back with 19 genres with `useCount=false` (was 0 before the fix) — identical to the `useCount=true` count — while `breakdown.collaborative` still correctly differed (35 vs. 85), confirming the score-affecting behavior itself is unchanged, only the display-breaking side effect is gone.

Verified: `node --check` clean on the backend controller; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on mobile; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `activeGenres`/`filterStats`/`filteredMyStats`/`filteredTheirStats` compiled into `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`. Backend fix live-verified directly (`GET /match/swipe/queue?useCount=false` vs. default, real before/after counts); the Variety client-side filtering logic itself is a plain, pure array/object filter with no async/timing component, verified by direct code reading rather than a live device screenshot.

### Real bug found live: Social Overlap vanished outright for zero mutual connections, instead of showing an empty state like every other card

Direct report: unlike every other card in this deck, which shows an explanatory empty-state message when there's nothing to display (Shared Genres' "Neither of you has rated anything...", Activity's "Nothing you've both rated...", Shared Favorites returning `null` only when there are genuinely zero *candidate* IDs at all, not zero matches) — Social Overlap disappeared from the deck completely for a candidate with zero mutual connections, real inconsistency, not by design.

Root cause: two independent gates, both wrong for this. `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` only pushed the `"social"` card into the deck when `insights.socialOverlap.mutualFollowing > 0`; separately, `MutualConnectionsGrid.tsx` itself `return null`ed on an empty `items` array even if it *had* been rendered. Fixed both: the card now pushes whenever `socialOverlap` was computed at all (which is unconditional once `matchInsights` exists — no reason tied to *this specific candidate's* connection count to hide the card itself), and `MutualConnectionsGrid.tsx` now renders `t("No mutual connections yet.")` instead of `null` when `items.length === 0`, matching the same "the card stays, its body explains the empty result" convention already established everywhere else in this panel. The existing fetch-skip (`if (!insights?.socialOverlap || insights.socialOverlap.mutualFollowing <= 0) return;` inside the effect that loads `mutualConnections`) was correct already and untouched — no point fetching a connections page that's known to be empty; `items` staying `[]` is exactly what now triggers the new empty-state text.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed the new `"No mutual connections yet."` string compiled in, and confirmed by inspecting every remaining `mutualFollowing` reference in the compiled `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` chunk that the only real ones left are the (correct, untouched) fetch-skip effect — the old push-gating one is gone.

### Two real LLM-analysis display bugs found live: raw JSON occasionally leaking into the shown text, and long strengths/weaknesses/analysis/starter text bleeding across sections

Two direct reports in one round, both in the LLM-generated analysis path (`matchController.js` on the backend, `MatchSummarySwiper.tsx`/`AnimatedInsightList.tsx` on mobile).

**JSON leak (`{analyses:` and similar occasionally showing as the displayed text)**: traced the actual parsing chain — `callLLM` → `extractJsonFromLLMText` (three `JSON.parse` attempts against slightly different substring slices, strict-only, no repair) → if all three fail, the call site fell back to `{ analysis: rawText }`, i.e. the model's raw, still-JSON-shaped text became the "analysis" shown to the user verbatim whenever the LLM's own output had a minor formatting quirk (smart quotes, a trailing comma) that made strict `JSON.parse` fail. Fixed with two independent layers rather than one: (1) `extractJsonFromLLMText` now runs a `repairJsonText` pass (smart-quote normalization, trailing-comma removal) and retries parsing against the repaired text before giving up, so more real LLM output parses correctly instead of ever reaching the raw-text fallback; (2) as a hard safety net regardless of layer 1, `normalizeLLMAnalysis` now checks `/[{}]/.test(analysis)` (and the same check on `match_title`) and falls back to the existing `canonical` analysis (built from `buildCanonicalAnalysis`) whenever a curly brace survives into what would be shown — guaranteeing a raw JSON leak can no longer reach the user even if parsing itself somehow still fails in the future. Verified the repair/safety-net logic with a standalone Node simulation (the functions aren't independently exported/importable) against representative malformed inputs (smart quotes, trailing commas, fully-unparseable text) before considering this done.

**Text bleeding between sections when strengths/weaknesses/analysis/conversation-starters ran long**: `MatchSummarySwiper.tsx`'s three sections are fixed-height, `snapToInterval`-based siblings with no independent scroll — nothing before this stopped a genuinely long string from rendering past its own section's height into the next one. Fixed with the same "hard clip + graceful truncation" pairing used elsewhere in this deck: `overflow:"hidden"` added to `section` (the real containment guarantee — this is what makes sections physically unable to bleed into each other no matter how long the text is, not just look cramped), plus `numberOfLines`/`ellipsizeMode="tail"` on the actual `Text` components (`paragraph`: 7 lines, `starterButtonText`: 2 lines, and `AnimatedInsightList.tsx`'s own `listItem`: 2 lines) for a clean "…" truncation instead of an abrupt hard clip once that guarantee kicks in. Also fixed on the backend, same round: `normalizeLLMAnalysis` now truncates each `strengths`/`weaknesses`/`conversation_starters` item to `ITEM_MAX_CHARS` (110) — only when sourced from the LLM, not the canonical fallback — so the truncation happens once, predictably, rather than relying solely on the mobile-side `numberOfLines` clip for content that was never reasonable to show in full anyway.

### `match_title` redesigned from a full-width gradient heading into a small tilted corner badge, replacing the analysis section's sparkles icon

Direct design ask, discussed and agreed before building: the LLM's `match_title` (previously a full-width, centered `MatchGradientTitle` block at the top of the Sync Summary card's content) is now a small, tilted, gradient-filled sticker pinned to the **top-left corner** of the Sync Summary card itself — floating slightly outside the card's own bounds, same bare-shape/gradient-fill-on-glyph visual language as `ShareCard.tsx`'s heart/plus corner stickers (no pill/background, no border), just applied to text instead of an icon glyph. New `MatchTitleBadge.tsx`; the old inline `MatchGradientTitle` usage in the ai-summary card's `render()` is gone (that component is untouched and still used by the closing cover card's own static headline). The sparkles icon that used to sit at the top of `MatchSummarySwiper.tsx`'s analysis section is also gone — the badge now does the job both were doing (dynamic title + eye-catching accent) in one element.

Since `react-native-svg`'s `SvgText` doesn't auto-wrap, long titles (the backend already caps `match_title` at 60 chars) are pre-split into up to 3 lines of ~2-3 words each via a small greedy word-wrap helper before ever reaching SVG: a trailing comma or dash on a word is treated as a natural break point (ends the line early even under the word cap), so multi-clause titles read at their actual clause boundaries instead of breaking mid-phrase; a hyphen *inside* a word (e.g. "Slow-Burn") is correctly left alone since the break check only looks at the end of each word. Any theoretical overflow past 3 lines folds into the last line rather than dropping content. Verified with a standalone Node simulation across ten representative titles (short/one-line, comma-separated two-clause, internally-hyphenated, and a genuinely long 8-9 word case) — all wrapped sensibly, max 3 lines, breaks favoring punctuation as intended.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `MatchTitleBadge`/`matchTitleBadgeGradient` compiled into the live bundle.

### Immediate follow-up, same round: the badge was rendering clipped/behind the page, plus three direct polish asks

Direct report: the badge appeared to be "stuck behind the page" — visible in front of the card's own content, but not in front of everything else. Root cause: the badge's original negative `top`/`left` offset pushed it partly outside the per-card `<View>`'s bounds, but that View is a child of this deck's horizontally-paging `ScrollView` (`contentContainerStyle={{gap: CARD_GAP}}`) — that ScrollView clips its own viewport to each card's height, so the portion poking above `y:0` was silently cut off rather than rendered. Separately, the badge was the *first* child of the per-card View (rendered before its content `ScrollView`), and RN doesn't automatically paint `position:"absolute"` siblings above normal-flow ones the way CSS does — paint order follows JSX order unless `zIndex` says otherwise, and a sibling `ScrollView` (its own native composited view) isn't always guaranteed to respect a plain View's `zIndex` on Android.

Fixed both, no `elevation` used (it always brings an Android drop shadow with it, which would show as a stray rectangular shadow behind this transparent-background badge): (1) moved `MatchTitleBadge` to render as the *last* child of the per-card View in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`, after its content `ScrollView`, so JSX paint order alone puts it on top; (2) switched its offset from negative (`top:-12,left:-8`, poking outside the card) to positive (`top:14,left:10`, sitting inside the card's own bounds) — no longer a descendant of any clipping ScrollView at all, and this also directly satisfies the "move it down a bit" ask. Alongside that: font bumped from 14→19px and line height 19→26 (bigger/bolder, per direct ask — `fontWeight="bold"` was already set but read too small at the original size), badge width 150→180 to fit the larger text, and the gradient direction switched from diagonal (`x1,y1,x2,y2 = 0,0,1,1`) to horizontal (`0,0,1,0`) matching `MatchGradientTitle`'s own convention, per a direct reminder to make sure the fill actually reads as a gradient.

### Second follow-up, same round: page-level "Sync Summary" label moved into the swiper, an even bolder font weight added app-wide, line count driven by word count, clipped edges fixed, more tilt

Five more direct asks in one round, all on `MatchTitleBadge.tsx`/`MatchSummarySwiper.tsx`/`MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` (plus a new app-wide font weight):

- **"Remove the Sync Summary title, put it above the analysis text instead."** The ai-summary card's page-level header (`<Text style={styles.sectionTitle}>{card.title}</Text>`, shown at the top of every card in this deck for orientation) is now skipped specifically for `card.key === "ai-summary"` — every other card keeps it. In its place, `MatchSummarySwiper.tsx`'s analysis section gained its own `t("Sync Summary")` header (`analysisHeader` style — same shape as the swiper's existing `columnHeader`/`startersHeader`) directly above the analysis paragraph, the same "each section gets its own label" pattern Strengths/Weaknesses/Conversation Starters already use. Makes sense once the badge is doing the page-level "this is the Sync Summary card" job visually — the flat text label was redundant sitting right underneath it.
- **Bolder font, tried a heavier weight.** DM Sans only had Regular/Medium/Bold (400/500/700) loaded app-wide (`app/_layout.tsx`'s `useFonts`); `@expo-google-fonts/dm-sans` (already a dependency) ships 800/900 weights too, just not registered yet. Added `DMSans_800ExtraBold` to the app-wide font load and a new `fonts.extrabold` entry in `src/theme/typography.ts` (available for any future use, not badge-specific) — `MatchTitleBadge` now renders with `fontFamily: fonts.extrabold` / `fontWeight: "800"` instead of the `bold` weight every other gradient-text element in this feature uses, a deliberate one-off since this badge is meant to be the single most eye-catching element on the card.
- **Line count driven by word count** (1-2 words → 1 line, 3-4 → 2, 5+ → 3), replacing the previous flat "max 3 words per line" rule. `wrapMatchTitle` now computes `targetLineCount(wordCount)` first, then derives `wordsPerLine = Math.ceil(wordCount / targetLines)` so words spread evenly across exactly that many lines (comma/dash-triggered early breaks still apply on top). Verified via a standalone Node simulation across 12 titles spanning 1-8 words — every case produced exactly the specified line count.
- **Clipped edges fixed — nothing should crop the text.** Root cause: SVG viewports clip to their own declared width/height by default (spec behavior), and a wide line — a long word, or just the wider extrabold face — could render past the fixed `BADGE_WIDTH`, cropping the first/last characters even though the text was horizontally centered. Fixed with `style={{ overflow: "visible" }}` on the `<Svg>` (react-native-svg doesn't accept `overflow` as a direct prop, has to go through `style`) plus a wider canvas (150→200px) so the escape hatch is rarely even needed.
- **More tilt, right side higher.** Rotation increased from `-6deg` to `-10deg` — CSS/SVG rotation is clockwise-positive, so a more negative angle lifts the right edge further, exactly the "sağ tarafını daha üste al" ask.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (one real type error caught and fixed along the way — react-native-svg's `<Svg>` TS types reject a bare `overflow` prop, confirming it has to be routed through `style` instead of guessed); fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `DMSans_800ExtraBold`, `matchTitleBadgeGradient`, and `targetLineCount` all compiled into the live bundle, and the `-10deg` rotation value present.

### Third follow-up, same round: badge pulled tighter into the corner, a gold-frame-style shine added to its fill, the two-avatar/percentage row pushed down to clear it, and the cloud's "tap a profile" hint fixed on two fronts

- **Badge moved further toward the card's actual top-left corner** (`top:14,left:10` → `top:2,left:0`) — direct feedback it still read as "a bit inward and low." Deliberately not pushed negative even with `overflow:"visible"` already in place: negative would put the badge's own box origin closer to (or past) the *outer* deck ScrollView's own viewport edge, which still clips (unlike the inner per-card content ScrollView this sticker no longer lives inside, from the previous round's fix) — `top:2,left:0` is the closest-to-the-corner position that stays safely inside that boundary regardless of how wide a given title's text renders.
- **A shine added to the gradient fill** — direct reference to `ShareCard.tsx`'s gold premium-tier border, but explicitly *not* as an outer glow around the badge shape, only the inner text fill itself. That gold border's own "shiny" read turned out to just be a bright-highlight-to-saturated-color diagonal 2-stop gradient (`TIER_GOLD_HIGHLIGHT`→`TIER_GOLD`, `x1,y1,x2,y2=0,0,1,1`) — replicated the same technique on the badge's own `LinearGradient`, keeping both existing brand colors rather than swapping to gold: `#FFFFFF` at offset 0 → `colors.primary` at 0.35 → `colors.secondary` at 1, same diagonal direction. `#FFFFFF` (not a computed tint) mirrors `TIER_GOLD_HIGHLIGHT` itself being a fixed hex rather than derived — a literal highlight color reads correctly across all 9 palettes without per-palette tuning, the same reason ShareCard's own gold constants are hardcoded rather than theme-derived.
- **`MatchTierRow`'s two-avatar/percentage-ring row pushed down** (`marginTop:26` added) — it sits at the very top of the ai-summary card's own scrollable content now that the page-level "Sync Summary" header above it is gone (previous round), and the badge floating over that same top-left corner was overlapping its leading avatar.
- **`MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s "Tap a profile to see details" hint, two fixes**: it used to render unconditionally, staying visible even after a candidate was selected and the results deck was already open below it — now wrapped in `!selectedCandidate &&`, matching the "this hint is meaningless once you're look at at what it's pointing at" logic. Also moved down (`marginTop:4`→`36`) — it used to hug the bubble cloud directly; now sits closer to where `MatchAnalysisPanel` itself will open once a bubble is tapped (that panel's own outer wrap starts with `paddingTop:24`), reading as "here's where the results will appear" rather than a caption on the cloud above it.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed the new gradient stops and the conditional hint text compiled in.

### Fourth follow-up, same round: shine highlight moved to the midpoint, badge nudged further left

Two small direct corrections. The shine highlight was landing on each line's *first letters*, not reading as a sweep of light — because each line is its own `<SvgText>` with its own bounding box under `gradientUnits="objectBoundingBox"` (the default), an `offset:0` stop lands at that line's own leading edge, not some shared point across the whole badge. Reordered the stops so the white highlight sits at the midpoint instead: `colors.primary`@0 → `#FFFFFF`@0.5 → `colors.secondary`@1 (was white@0 → primary@0.35 → secondary@1). Badge offset nudged further left, `left:0`→`-8` — still well inside the 16px buffer `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s `HORIZONTAL_PADDING` reserves between the card and the outer deck ScrollView's own clipping viewport edge.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed the reordered gradient stops and `left:-8` compiled in.

### Fifth follow-up, same round: a real word-count bug in the wrap logic, plus the badge nudged further left again

Direct report with a concrete example: "Wide-Angle Explorers" — 3 real words by the user's own count, so per the existing 3-4-words-→-2-lines spec it should wrap to `["Wide-Angle", "Explorers"]`, but rendered as one line instead. Root cause: `wrapMatchTitle` counted words by splitting on whitespace only, so a hyphenated compound like "Wide-Angle" counted as a single token — 2 tokens total, which the 1-2-words-→-1-line rule then (correctly, by its own count, just the wrong count) kept on one line. Fixed with a new `conceptualWordCount()` helper that additionally splits each token on internal hyphens/dashes purely for the word-count used to pick the target line count (`"Wide-Angle"` → counts as 2) — deliberately *not* changing how tokens get grouped into lines, so a compound word still never gets split across two lines mid-word; only the counting that decides *how many* lines to target changed. Re-verified the full test suite (12 prior titles + 4 new hyphenated-compound cases) via the same standalone Node simulation — all correct, no regressions on the non-hyphenated cases. Badge nudged further left again, `left:-8`→`-14`, still short of the 16px `HORIZONTAL_PADDING` buffer.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `conceptualWordCount` and `left:-14` compiled in.

### Sixth follow-up, same round: corner placement dropped — badge now centers on the card's own top edge

Direct reversal of the corner placement: "vazgeçtim, rozetin merkezini tam kartın üst kenarının orta noktasında konumlandır" (changed my mind, center the badge exactly on the midpoint of the card's top edge). Reworked `MatchTitleBadge.tsx`'s positioning from a fixed corner offset (`top:2,left:-14`) to true centering, in both axes, on the card's own top edge:

- **Horizontal**: `left:"50%"` + `marginLeft: -BADGE_WIDTH/2` — the standard RN/CSS trick for centering an absolutely positioned element without needing to read the parent's actual width (the card's own width varies by device).
- **Vertical**: `top:0` + `marginTop: -svgHeight/2` — `svgHeight` is already line-count-dependent (1-3 lines), so the badge's own vertical center always lands exactly on `y:0` (the card's top edge) regardless of how many lines the current title wrapped to, rather than a fixed offset that only looked right for one line count.

Rotation (`-10deg`) stays a separate `transform`, deliberately not folded into the same style object as the centering math — RN rotates around an element's own center by default, so applying it after centering doesn't disturb the center point already established.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `left:"50%"` and `marginLeft: -BADGE_WIDTH / 2` compiled in.

### Seventh follow-up, same round: the layering bug was back — this time from the badge poking above the horizontal ScrollView's own clipped viewport

Direct report the badge was "behind the page" again, same symptom as an earlier round. Different root cause this time, exposed by the previous round's own change: centering the badge exactly on the card's top edge means roughly half its height now renders *above* `y:0` — and the badge was still a per-card child nested inside the deck's horizontal, paging `ScrollView`. That ScrollView's cross-axis (vertical) size is driven by its tallest child (`cardHeight`), so its own viewport clips anything outside `[0, cardHeight]` regardless of which card it belongs to or where in the JSX tree it's rendered — the earlier "render it last so paint order wins" fix solved a *different* problem (z-stacking against a sibling within the same card) and never addressed this clipping boundary at all.

Real fix: moved `MatchTitleBadge` out of the per-card `View` entirely — it's no longer rendered inside `cards.map(...)`. It now renders once, as a sibling of the `ScrollView` and the dots row (inside the same unstyled wrapper `View` that already holds both), gated on `cards[activeIndex]?.key === "ai-summary"` instead of a per-card conditional. That wrapper View isn't a ScrollView, so it doesn't clip; its own width equals `cardWidth` (the same `HORIZONTAL_PADDING` math `wrap` already uses) and its `y:0` lines up with every card's own `y:0`, and since a paging ScrollView always presents its active card flush with the viewport's own left edge, positioning the badge there tracks whichever card is active — including switching to render only while ai-summary specifically is the active card — without needing to read live scroll offset.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed the badge is no longer inside the `cards.map` per-card block and the new `cards[activeIndex]?.key === "ai-summary"` gate compiled in.

### Eighth follow-up, same round: nudged down a touch, vertical only

Direct, minimal correction: dead-center-on-the-card's-top-edge read a touch too high; horizontal position was confirmed good, explicitly not to be touched. Added a `VERTICAL_NUDGE = 12` constant — the badge's vertical center now sits 12px below the card's top edge (`top: VERTICAL_NUDGE` alongside the existing `marginTop: -svgHeight/2`) instead of exactly on it. The horizontal centering (`left:"50%"`/`marginLeft` in the separate `sticker` style) is untouched.

### A game-style "stamp" entrance animation, discussed first then built

Direct exploratory question: would a CS:GO-style rank-up "slap"/stamp-into-place entrance suit this badge? Recommended yes with one caveat (keep it a self-contained scale/rotate spring, not a full-screen shake/flash — disproportionate for an element this size), user agreed, then built.

`MatchTitleBadge.tsx` gained an `entrance` `Animated.Value` (0→1, `useRef`), driving three interpolated outputs: `stampScale` (`STAMP_START_SCALE=2.6`→`1`), `stampRotate` (`STAMP_START_ROTATE_DEG=-34deg`→`FINAL_ROTATE_DEG=-10deg`, the same resting tilt as before — the rotation entrance and the resting value are now one animated property instead of a fixed `transform`), and `stampOpacity` (fades in over the first 30% of the spring, `extrapolate:"clamp"`, so the badge doesn't jump-cut in at full opacity/oversized before the motion is visible). Driven by a single `Animated.spring(entrance, {toValue:1, friction:4, tension:45, useNativeDriver:true})` — friction 4 is loose enough to produce a visible bounce/overshoot past the resting scale and rotation before settling, matching the "slam into place" read. The outer `View` became an `Animated.View` to carry these.

Replays on every real candidate switch, not just first mount — `entrance` resets to 0 and the spring restarts in a `useEffect` keyed on `text` (the LLM's own `match_title`, which changes per candidate), matching the same "keyed on changing content, not mount timing" pattern this feature's other reset-on-switch effects already use, since `MatchAnalysisPanel` isn't remounted per candidate (no `key` on it) — this component's props just update in place.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `STAMP_START_SCALE`/`stampRotate`/the gradient id all compiled in.

### One more polish pass: the badge now fades out the instant a swipe away from it begins, not once the next card has already settled in

Direct report: swiping to another card, the badge stayed fully visible through the whole drag and only disappeared late — because it was gated purely on `activeIndex`, which only updates in `onScrollEnd` (bound to `onMomentumScrollEnd`), well after the drag gesture itself has started and the next card is already snapping into place.

Added a second, independent fade driven by live scroll position rather than the settled index: `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` now tracks the deck's horizontal scroll offset in a `scrollX` `Animated.Value` (`useRef`), fed by `Animated.event([...], {useNativeDriver:true})` on the outer ScrollView's `onScroll` (new `scrollEventThrottle={16}` alongside it — this ScrollView previously had no `onScroll` handler at all, only the momentum-end one), and passes `scrollX` down to `MatchTitleBadge` as a new required prop. Since the ai-summary card is always index 0, any positive `scrollX` means the user has started dragging away from it — the badge interpolates that into a `dragOpacity` (`1→0` over `DRAG_FADE_DISTANCE=40` px, `extrapolate:"clamp"`) and combines it with its existing entrance-animation opacity via `Animated.multiply(stampOpacity, dragOpacity)`, so the stamp-in animation and the drag-out fade compose correctly regardless of which one is currently driving visibility. Both opacity sources stay fully native-driven — no JS-thread round trip on either the scroll tracking or the resulting fade.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `DRAG_FADE_DISTANCE`/`dragOpacity` compiled in.

### Real crash found live: swiping the deck threw "Object is not a function" from inside ScrollView's own `_handleScroll` — the new `onScroll` needed `Animated.ScrollView`, not the plain one

Direct report with a full stack trace, five repeats per swipe (once per scroll frame that reached the listener before it crashed): `Uncaught Error: Object is not a function`, thrown from `ScrollView.js`'s `_handleScroll`, which does `this.props.onScroll && this.props.onScroll(e)`.

Root cause, confirmed by reading the actual RN source rather than guessing: `Animated.event(...)` doesn't return a plain callable function — it returns an instance of the `AnimatedEvent` class (`Libraries/Animated/AnimatedEvent.js`), an *object*. Only a component wrapped via `Animated.createAnimatedComponent` (which `Animated.View`, `Animated.ScrollView`, etc. are) knows to detect `instanceof AnimatedEvent` in its own props (`AnimatedProps.js`, several call sites) and specially attach it — either as a real native event listener (`useNativeDriver:true`) or a JS-callable wrapper. The previous round's fix passed `onScroll={Animated.event(...)}` to the deck's `ScrollView`, imported as the *plain* `ScrollView` from `"react-native"` (matching every other scroller already in this file) — that component has none of that unwrapping machinery, so the raw `AnimatedEvent` object was forwarded straight through as the literal `onScroll` prop, and `_handleScroll`'s `this.props.onScroll(e)` crashed on every scroll frame trying to call an object.

Fixed by switching just this one ScrollView (the outer, horizontal card-paging one) to `Animated.ScrollView` — the inner per-card ScrollViews and the "social" card's own scroll handler are untouched, they never needed this. `scrollRef`'s existing type (`useRef<ScrollView>(null)`) and its two `.scrollTo(...)` call sites (`goToCard`, the reset-on-candidate-switch effect) needed no changes — `tsc` confirmed Animated.ScrollView's ref still exposes the same `.scrollTo` surface.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `Animated.ScrollView` compiled in place of the plain one for this element.

### Real bug found live: the badge inconsistently failed to reappear after swiping back, and its stamp-in entrance was replaying on every return instead of just the first load

Direct report: returning to the ai-summary card, the badge was inconsistent — "sometimes it comes back, sometimes it doesn't." Also, a direct scope correction: the stamp entrance should only play once, when the analysis first loads in — not on every swipe back to this card.

Root cause of both: `MatchTitleBadge` was conditionally *mounted/unmounted* on `cards[activeIndex]?.key === "ai-summary"`, and `activeIndex` only updates inside `onMomentumScrollEnd` — an event iOS/Android don't reliably fire for every gesture (a slow drag released exactly on a snap point, with no residual momentum, can end via `onScrollEndDrag` alone, with no momentum event ever following). When that event didn't fire, `activeIndex` never flipped back to 0, so the badge stayed unmounted indefinitely — the actual inconsistency. And on the gestures where it *did* remount, a fresh mount meant a fresh `MatchTitleBadge` instance, whose own `entrance` `Animated.Value` starts at 0 again — replaying the full stamp-in animation on every single return, not just the first load.

Fixed by decoupling mounting from `activeIndex` entirely: the badge now renders whenever `parsed.match_title` exists at all (i.e. for as long as the ai-summary card's analysis has loaded for the current candidate), with no `activeIndex` gate. Visibility while scrolled to a different card is handled entirely by the existing `scrollX`-driven `dragOpacity` from the previous round — a live, continuous signal tied directly to actual scroll position, not the flaky momentum-end event, so it fades correctly regardless of which gesture path ended the scroll. And since the component itself no longer remounts on a same-candidate return, its `entrance` effect (keyed on `text`) has nothing to re-trigger unless `match_title` itself actually changes — meaning the stamp now genuinely only plays once per real candidate switch, exactly as intended.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed the badge's render condition no longer references `activeIndex`.

### New: a one-time Sync intro/pitch card, shown before the actual filter UI on a viewer's very first visit only

Exploratory design question first: the Sync tab dropped a first-time viewer straight into the filter/CineGraph UI with zero context for what the feature even does. Discussed the right amount of motion for an intro like this — recommended a single static card (headline + short pitch + 3 highlight chips + a CTA), not a multi-step carousel, with just a one-shot reveal on mount rather than continuous animation, since a carousel or looping motion reads as a tour to sit through more than once, and this should only ever be seen once. Confirmed, then scoped to "first showing only."

New `SyncIntroCard.tsx` — headline + subtext pitch + three staggered-in highlight chips (Match Score / Shared Favorites / Conversation Starters, each its own icon+color, same tinted-circle language `AnimatedInsightList` already uses elsewhere in this feature) + a "Get Started" CTA reusing `MatchFilterStrip`'s own gradient-fill button technique (SVG `Rect` with a `primary`→`secondary` `LinearGradient`) for visual consistency. Entrance is the same one-shot `useRevealAnimation` fade+slide this whole feature already uses everywhere else — deliberately not a new, heavier motion language just for this card. The three highlight chips stagger in via a small inline `Animated.timing` loop (`AnimatedInsightList`'s own stagger technique, not reused directly — that component is built around one shared icon/color for every row, not worth generalizing for three items with three different icons each).

`match/index.tsx` (page 0, the filter/CineGraph page): new `showIntro` state, defaulting to `false` (not a tri-state "still checking" — `expo-secure-store` has no synchronous read on native, and blocking the whole page behind an async check would cost every return visit just to avoid a one-time, one-frame flash on someone's actual first-ever visit) and flipped to `true` only if a `useEffect` confirms `STORAGE_KEYS.SYNC_INTRO_SEEN` was never set. While `showIntro`, `SyncIntroCard` renders *instead of* `MatchFilterStrip` (not stacked above it) — the whole point was that the actual Sync UI shouldn't appear immediately. Its `onStart` sets `showIntro` false and persists the seen-flag via `SecureStore.setItemAsync`, the same storage mechanism `ThemeContext`/`AuthContext` already use for their own persisted values (this app has no `AsyncStorage` usage anywhere — confirmed via grep before picking a persistence approach). New `STORAGE_KEYS.SYNC_INTRO_SEEN` constant alongside the existing keys in `apiRoutes.ts`.

New English-source strings (headline/pitch/highlight labels/CTA) added via plain `t("...")` calls with no matching `locales/index.ts` entries — confirmed this matches how every other string added earlier this session was left (i18next's `fallbackLng` renders the key text itself when no translation exists yet), not a new gap specific to this card.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; Metro had stopped running between rounds (no process on :8081) — restarted via the established `scripts/start-codespace.sh` (see the memory file's own "Mobile Codespace dev startup" note), waited for it to come back up through its own ngrok-proxy restart cycle, then fetched a fresh bundle confirming `SyncIntroCard`, `SYNC_INTRO_SEEN`, and the new strings all compiled in.

### Same known bug ported over from Profile's CineGraph, still unfixed in Sync's own copy — same fix applied

Direct report: some genre chip buttons in the Sync page's own ring jitter under certain conditions — the same bug already fixed once in Profile's `CineGraphDonut.tsx` (by someone else, on a different branch), pointed out explicitly as a lead. `CineMatchGenreRing.tsx` is a deliberate, documented copy of `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s positioning math (see this file's own header comment) made *before* that fix landed there — so the copy never inherited it, and the same root cause was still present here.

Root cause (already diagnosed and documented in `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s own `handleChipLayout` comment, confirmed still applicable here): a chip's onscreen position depends on its own measured width/height (`chipSizes`, populated via each chip's `onLayout`), and this component re-renders frequently — its rotation/collapse animations (`rotateAnim`/`collapseAnim`) plus any parent state change (a filter edit, a `loading` prop flip) — which re-fires `onLayout` on every already-placed chip. RN's text layout can report a ±1px oscillating width for the exact same string across otherwise-identical renders (sub-pixel font-hinting noise), and the previous `handleChipLayout` here committed every new value it saw (only guarded by "did the rounded value change"), feeding that noise straight back into the chip position math — a chip nowhere near whatever triggered the re-render could start visibly nudging on its own.

Fixed by porting `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s exact fix: `handleChipLayout` is now write-once (`if (prev[genre]) return prev;`) — a genre's size is committed on its first successful measurement and every later `onLayout` for that same genre is ignored, making the feedback loop structurally impossible instead of just less likely. Also confirmed (reading both files side by side) that the *other* jitter source `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s comments mention — an earlier ring-1 placement pass that pushed a chip's radius out on detecting overlap with an already-placed neighbor, creating a cross-chip position dependency — was never present in `CineMatchGenreRing.tsx` to begin with; its own ring-1 loop already computes each chip's radius from only its own width/height, so only the `chipSizes` freeze was actually needed here.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed the write-once guard compiled into the live bundle.

### Backend: Social's weight in the displayed match score/breakdown lowered from 20% to 15%, redistributed to Collaborative

Direct question first, not a bug report: on a *content* matching app, does Social really deserve 20% of the score — as much as Favorites, and only 5 points under the single biggest signal? Checked the actual code rather than guessing: `computeMatchBreakdown` (`matchController.js` — powers the displayed `matchPercentage` and the Sync Breakdown radar chart) weighs `collaborativeScore` 0.35, `contentScore` (Favorites) 0.25, `socialScore` 0.2, `diversityScore` 0.15, `bonusScore` (Activity) 0.05 — meaning taste-driven signals (collaborative+content+diversity+bonus) summed to 0.8, capping two perfectly taste-aligned users with zero mutual follows at 80%. Also surfaced along the way: `scoreHybridCandidate` (`matchController.js`) already weighs social at 0.15, not 0.2 — the two functions silently disagreed on this exact number, on top of the already-documented broader disagreement between `findMatches`/`getMatchWithUser` (see `CINEMATCH_ANALYZE_AND_SWIPE_REPORTS.md`). **Correction, from the full algorithm audit below**: `getSwipeQueue` does *not* actually call `scoreHybridCandidate` — a subsequent, undocumented change had already switched it to call `computeMatchBreakdown` directly (the same function `getMatchWithUser`/`analyzeMatchWithUser` use), specifically so genre filtering would actually affect the ranked order, not just the displayed detail score. `scoreHybridCandidate` is `findMatches`'s own function — reachable only from the web app's Cinematch page, not this mobile client at all. The weight fix below was still correct (and, it turns out, affected the actual live mobile ranking directly, not indirectly) — only the "which function does what" claim in the paragraph above was wrong.

Recommended lowering Social to 15% (matching `scoreHybridCandidate`'s existing number, rather than picking a third arbitrary value) with the freed 0.05 going to `collaborativeScore` (0.35→0.4) — the purest taste signal (real cross-user rating correlation), not `contentScore` (title-overlap is a narrower, more brittle signal — two people can have compatible taste without literally favoriting the same titles). Confirmed, then applied: `computeMatchBreakdown`'s `finalScore` is now `0.4*collaborative + 0.25*content + 0.15*social + 0.15*diversity + 0.05*bonus`. Deliberately scoped to just this one function/number — `scoreHybridCandidate`'s own social weight was already 0.15 (no change needed there), and its broader structure (dynamic collaborative/genre redistribution based on the `useCount`/`useAvgRating` toggles, no separate bonus term) differs enough from `computeMatchBreakdown` that attempting full parity between the two would be a much larger, separate refactor, not this fix.

Live-verified against the real `Zachary`/`Peter` test pair rather than trusting the arithmetic blind: their real breakdown sub-scores (`collaborative:85, contentBased:62, social:58, diversity:50, bonus:59`) computed by hand give 67% under the *old* weights and 69% under the *new* ones — the live endpoint (`POST /api/match/:targetUserId`) returned exactly **69**, confirming the new weights are actually live, not just edited. `node --check` clean on the controller.

### Full end-to-end algorithm audit, then six fixes applied in order

Asked for a genuinely thorough pass over the whole matching algorithm — consistency, correctness, gaps, performance, everything — not just the one weight already fixed above. Read all 1600+ lines of `matchController.js`, `matchRoute.js`, `llmAdapter.js`, the four "hybrid approach" service files, `Rating.js`/`User.js`'s indexes, and the historical `mds/CINEMATCH_ANALYZE_AND_SWIPE_REPORTS.md` (a real but *stale* doc — it predates the swipe-to-decide → browse-and-follow pivot, `MatchDecision.js`/`SwipeCard*`/`RejectedMatchesModal` were since deleted; treated as background, not current truth, and verified everything against the live code instead).

**Biggest finding, deliberately not acted on**: `findMatches`/`scoreHybridCandidate` (only reachable from the web app's own Cinematch page, `frontend/src/pages/MatchPage.jsx`) is a structurally different, never-unified scoring formula from `computeMatchBreakdown` (what every mobile call — `getSyncCandidates`, `getMatchWithUser`, `analyzeMatchWithUser` — actually uses): cruder diversity metric, no bonus/activity term at all, and its dominant 35% collaborative term isn't genre-filtered even when a genre filter is applied. Web and mobile can show different percentages for the identical pair of users today. **Explicitly scoped out per direct instruction** — the web app will only ever be used for marketing, real users reach Cinephix through mobile, so this mismatch doesn't matter in practice and wasn't touched.

Six fixes applied, in order:

1. **Dead code removed.** `contentBasedService.js`, `socialScoreService.js`, `diversityScoreService.js`, `bonusMetricsService.js` (566 lines total) were imported nowhere in the actual app — only `backend/scripts/test_hybrid_matching.js` referenced them directly, and that script wasn't wired into any npm script either. Deleted all five files. `bonusMetricsService.js` in particular had a real, live bug (read `r.content`, a field that doesn't exist on `Rating.js` — only `contentId` does) that would have bitten anyone who ever wired it back in; better gone than sitting there as a trap. Updated the now-stale descriptive comment at the top of `matchController.js` accordingly.

2. **Cooldown added to `analyzeMatchWithUser`.** It had zero throttling — unlike Profile Analysis (`userController.js`, tier-gated `analysisCooldownHours` + a `ProfileAnalysis` history collection), CineMatch's own "Analyze" button could be tapped as fast as the client allowed, each tap a real LLM call (Groq/Gemini/etc. via `llmAdapter.js`) for what's usually an identical result — the underlying data (CineGraph, ratings, favorites, social graph) rarely changes minute to minute. New model `MatchAnalysisLog.js` (`{user, targetUser, createdAt}`, indexed `{user:1,targetUser:1,createdAt:-1}`) plus a new tier field `matchAnalysisCooldownMinutes` (free:60, pro:15, premium:5, dev:0) in `tiers.js` — deliberately a *separate* field from `analysisCooldownHours` and scoped per `(user, targetUser)` pair rather than one global timer per user: analyzing several different candidates in one session is the expected, legitimate flow, only rapid re-analysis of the *same* pair should be blocked. On cooldown, returns the same `429` + `{retryAfterMs, lastRunAt}` shape `getProfileAnalysis` already established. Live-verified: back-to-back calls against the real Zachary→Peter pair — first succeeded (`provider:"groq"`, a real LLM round-trip), second immediately returned `{success:false,message:"Analysis on cooldown",errors:{retryAfterMs:299396,...}}` (Zachary's account is premium tier, ~5 min cooldown, matches).

3. **Timeout added to every LLM provider call.** None of the four `fetch()` calls in `llmAdapter.js` (OpenAI/OpenRouter/Gemini/Groq) had any timeout — a hung (not erroring, just never responding) provider would leave the request waiting indefinitely, and `analyzeMatchWithUser`'s own sequential provider-fallback loop (`for...try/catch`) never even reaches the next candidate (or the guaranteed-to-succeed mock) on a hang, only on a thrown error. New `fetchWithTimeout()` helper (`AbortController`, `LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 15000ms, env-overridable) — all four provider functions now race their request against it instead of a bare `fetch()`.

4. **Bonus sub-signal "no data" behavior made consistent.** `calculateTrendingAlignmentInMemory`/`calculateActivityRecencyInMemory` both deliberately return `0` on zero data (a bonus category should reward positive evidence, not treat absence of data as a coin-flip neutral — already documented reasoning). `calculateWatchActivityScoreInMemory` was the odd one out, returning `0.5` on zero watches. Brought in line with the other two: now returns `0`.

5. **Candidate pool switched from a fixed slice to a random sample.** `getSyncCandidates`'s `User.find({_id:{$ne:meId}}).limit(1000)` always returned the same first ~1000 users in Mongo's natural/`_id` order, every request, for every user on the app — anyone past that fixed slice could never appear as a match candidate for *anyone*, no matter how well their taste aligned. Switched to an aggregation with `$sample: {size: CANDIDATE_POOL_SIZE}` — a fresh random draw per request, so over repeated searches every user eventually gets a chance to be scored. Scoped to `getSyncCandidates` only (the live mobile path) — `findMatches`/web left untouched per the same "web doesn't matter" instruction above. Live-verified: `GET /match/sync/candidates` still returns candidates correctly post-change (96 candidates, top match still Zachary→Peter at 69%, matching the pre-change result exactly since the test DB has well under 1000 users).

6. **"Swipe" naming replaced with "Sync" throughout** — cosmetic, flagged as low-priority but inconsistent with the feature's actual branding (the swipe-to-decide flirt-app model this naming came from was abandoned before this session). Renamed end to end, backend and mobile together since the route itself changed: `GET /match/swipe/queue` → `GET /match/sync/candidates`; `getSwipeQueue` → `getSyncCandidates` (`matchController.js`, `matchRoute.js`, `matchService.ts`); `SwipeCandidate` → `SyncCandidate` and `SwipeQueueResult` → `SyncCandidatesResult` (`types/index.ts`, and every component that imports them — `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`, `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`, `MatchTierRow.tsx`, `MatchCloudBubble.tsx`, `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`, `MatchActivityFeed.tsx`, `MatchCoverCard.tsx`, `MatchAvatarRing.tsx`, `match/index.tsx`); `SWIPE_QUEUE` → `SYNC_CANDIDATES` (`apiRoutes.ts`); the `/* ===== SWIPE ===== */` section header and surrounding prose in `matchController.js`/`matchRoute.js`/`tiers.js`/`server.js`/`Rating.js`. Deliberately left alone: genuine touch-gesture language ("Instagram-post-swipe feel", `MatchSummarySwiper`, "swipe fully settles") — unrelated to the feature's old name, still accurate English — and the historical contrast comments explaining CineMatch *used to be* swipe-to-decide and no longer is (accurate history, not a current name). The reference to `CINEMATCH_ANALYZE_AND_SWIPE_REPORTS.md` also stayed as-is — it's a real filename, not a naming choice.

Verified end to end: `node --check` clean on every touched backend file; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on mobile; live-hit the new `GET /api/match/sync/candidates` (200, correct data) and confirmed the old `GET /api/match/swipe/queue` now 404s; repo-wide grep for the old identifiers came back empty except this doc's own historical entries (left as-is) and a runtime log file (not source).

### Same depth of audit, the other side: the whole Sync *screen* (not just the backend algorithm) — every component, real interaction timing, then four fixes

Same ask as the backend audit above, mirrored onto the client: every component under `mobile/src/components/match/` (~24 files, ~5100 lines) plus `match/index.tsx` read end to end, live-timed the actual network calls a candidate selection triggers, and traced what really happens on the key user actions, not just the static code. Honest caveat going in and reflected in what follows: this environment has no way to actually drive the RN UI (no simulator/screenshot capability here) — verification is `tsc --noEmit`, real Metro bundle fetches + grep, and live `curl` timing against the real backend with the two seeded test accounts, the same discipline this whole session has used throughout; it is not a substitute for an on-device pass.

**Biggest finding, live-measured, not guessed**: selecting a candidate in the results cloud fired **up to 8 parallel network requests at once** — `analyzeMatchWithUser` (`prefetchMatchAnalysis`), `getSharedGenreContent`, `getMutualConnections`, `getMoviesBulk`/`getSeriesBulk` + `getContentRatings` (`MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`, 2 calls), `getRecentSharedActivity` (`MatchActivityFeed.tsx`), and `getCineGraph` ×2 — one for the viewer, one for the candidate (`MatchVarietyRings.tsx`) — regardless of which card (if any) the viewer ever actually scrolls to. Real timings against the live `Zachary`/`Peter` pair, fired in parallel the same way the app does: `content-ratings` 0.30s, `mutual-connections` 0.88s, `recent-activity` 0.90s, `shared-genre-content` 1.18s, and — the real dominant cost — `analyzeMatchWithUser` itself at **3.19s** (a genuine Groq round-trip). Every card mounts at once in this deck (an established, deliberate choice earlier this session for animation continuity across the horizontal card-paging ScrollView — not something this pass reopened), so nothing was ever being deferred based on visibility.

**A real regression, self-inflicted the same round as the backend audit**: the `analyzeMatchWithUser` cooldown added there had zero handling on the client. Live-confirmed the exact failure mode: `.catch(() => {})` in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s own analyze effect silently swallowed a `429`, so a cooldown-blocked re-analysis (a real, reachable case — the client's own `analysisCache`, keyed per `(targetUserId, filters, language)`, only survives for the life of the JS engine, so a fresh app cold-start re-analyzing an already-analyzed candidate within the cooldown window would hit this) showed the exact same generic **"No analysis available."** text as a genuine failure, with zero indication it was expected or when to retry.

Four fixes applied, in the order requested — **explicitly not touched**: `MatchFilterStrip`'s client-side `DEFAULT_FILTERS` (`useCount:false, useAvgRating:false`) not matching the server's actual Free-tier default (`useCount:true, useAvgRating:true`) — flagged in the audit, but per direct instruction this is expected noise ahead of the not-yet-built tier-differentiation pass, not a bug worth fixing on its own right now.

1. **Cooldown UX fix.** `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s analyze effect now distinguishes the cooldown case: a new `analysisCooldownRetryAt` state, set from `err.response.data.errors.retryAfterMs` on a `429`, and a third render branch (`analyzing` → `parsed` → **`analysisCooldownRetryAt`** → generic fallback) showing `"You've already analyzed this match recently. A new analysis will be available in {{time}}."` — same `formatCooldown` shape (`"Xh Ym"`/`"Xm"`) `ProfileAnalysesTab.tsx` already established for its own cooldown, duplicated locally rather than shared (four lines, not worth the cross-feature coupling).

2. **Eager fan-out replaced with a single shared gate.** New `shouldLoadExtras = activeIndex >= 1` in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` — deliberately one shared boolean rather than per-card scroll-proximity math keyed to each card's own position in the (conditionally-built) deck, which would need computing "which index would this card have" in two separate places (an inline gate and the `cards` useMemo) with a real risk of the two drifting apart. Index 1 is always "breakdown" (`MatchRadarChart`, no fetch of its own — reads straight off already-loaded `candidate.breakdown`), so gating on `activeIndex >= 1` means every other card's fetch waits for genuine browsing intent — one swipe or dot-tap past the summary — instead of firing on selection alone. Threaded into: `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s own two inline fetches (`getSharedGenreContent`, `getMutualConnections`), and a new `shouldLoad` prop on `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`, `MatchActivityFeed.tsx`, `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`. Each fetch effect now has two layers: an unconditional reset-to-empty on candidate switch (independent of `shouldLoad`, so a stale previous candidate's data can never survive a switch even if `shouldLoad` happened to stay true across it), and a `shouldLoad`-gated fetch guarded by a "have we already started/finished this exact request" ref (keyed on content identity — `contentType:allIds`, `candidateId:isMovie`, etc.) so `shouldLoad` flipping true→false→true again (scrolling near a card, away, back) can't refire a request that already succeeded, or double-fire one still in flight. `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`'s own viewer-side `getCineGraph` call has no per-candidate identity at all (it's always "the viewer's own" stats) — reset only on a content-type change, not on every candidate switch.

3. **Dead code removed**: `MatchFiltersModal.tsx` (281 lines) — a Pro/Premium filter bottom-sheet from an earlier design iteration, imported nowhere (`MatchFilterStrip.tsx`'s CineGraph-ring picker replaced it); the only other repo-wide match was a comment in an unrelated file (`CommunityFiltersModal.tsx`) citing it as a style precedent, left as-is.

4. **`MatchRadarChart`'s state-reset inconsistency fixed.** Every other card in this deck (Shared Genres' carousel position, Shared Favorites'/Activity's focused poster, Variety's selected genre) clears its own "currently open" state on a candidate switch via an effect keyed on the candidate's id; `MatchRadarChart`'s `activeCategory` was the one exception — tapping "Social" on one candidate, then switching, left "Social" open showing the *new* candidate's Social score without an explicit re-tap. New `candidateId` prop (purely to key the reset effect — the component only received `breakdown` before) + `useEffect(() => setActiveCategory(null), [candidateId])`.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after each of the four fixes; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `shouldLoadExtras`/`analysisCooldownRetryAt`/`candidateId` all compiled in and confirmed `MatchFiltersModal` is gone from the bundle entirely (0 matches, was present before deletion).

### Same audit, aimed specifically at the results screen that opens after Sync — MatchResultsCloud, the Share flow, error/empty states — six more fixes

Direct follow-up ask: same depth of pass, this time on "the screen that opens after Sync" specifically rather than the deck cards audited above. Read `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`, `MatchCoverCard.tsx`, `SyncShareMessageCard.tsx`, `MatchAvatarRing.tsx`, `matchCategoryMeta.ts`, `MutualConnectionsGrid.tsx`, and `match/index.tsx`'s own page-1 (results) branch end to end; traced two real send/share flows all the way to the backend (`Message.js`'s schema, `conversationController.js`'s handling) rather than assuming from the client side alone. All six fixes applied, in the order presented and confirmed:

1. **Real visual bug: SVG gradient id collision.** `MatchAvatarRing.tsx`'s medal badge used a hardcoded, shared `RadialGradient id="medalShine"` — but `MatchResultsCloud` mounts up to 5 of these at once (one per cloud bubble), and up to 3 (rank 0/1/2 — gold/silver/bronze) render this same gradient simultaneously. Exactly the class of bug this feature has already guarded against explicitly elsewhere (`MatchGradientTitle.tsx`/`MatchTitleBadge.tsx` both require an explicit `gradientId` prop specifically because "every card in this deck stays mounted at once") — this one component had been missed. Fixed: `medalGradientId = \`medalShine-${candidate.user._id}\`` (unique per candidate, not per rank, in case this component is ever reused somewhere ranks alone wouldn't disambiguate).

2. **`MutualConnectionsGrid` given a real loading state.** It only ever had `loadingMore` (pagination) — the *first* page's own in-flight window had no signal at all, so an empty `items` array read identically whether the fetch had genuinely returned zero connections or just hadn't resolved yet. Harmless before this session's own `shouldLoadExtras` change (the window was sub-second), but that same change widened it — a fast multi-card fling straight to the Social Overlap card can now show the fetch in flight for its full real duration once the card is actually visible. New `mutualInitialLoading` state in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` (true only while the first page is in flight, not on the known-zero-synchronously case where `mutualFollowing <= 0` already skips fetching entirely) threaded through as a new `initialLoading` prop, checked before the empty-state text.

3. **Share button was sending the entire raw LLM provider response.** `MatchCoverCard.tsx`'s `handleShare` sent the whole `analysis` object (`MatchAnalysis`) as `analysisData` — including `raw: unknown`, `analyzeMatchWithUser`'s own full unfiltered provider API response. Traced both consumers (`SyncShareMessageCard.tsx`'s preview card, `AnalyzeModal.tsx`'s full view) to confirm `raw` is read nowhere — pure dead weight. The backend does nothing to catch this either: `Message.js`'s `analysisData: Schema.Types.Mixed` has no validation, `conversationController.js` stores whatever the client sends verbatim. Fixed by destructuring only the four fields actually used (`provider, matchPercentage, breakdown, parsed`) before sending. **Related, explicitly left alone**: `AnalyzeModal.tsx`'s own share handler (the public-profile compatibility card's entry point, a different screen from Sync) has the identical pattern — flagged for awareness, not fixed here, since it's outside this pass's actual scope.

4. **Stale-filters object identity caused a wasted, now-cooldown-relevant prefetch.** `match/index.tsx`'s filters page and results page both stay mounted (an established, deliberate slide-transition choice, untouched by this fix) — going back to the filters page via the results page's own back-arrow, toggling a switch, and returning *without* re-searching hands both `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s auto-prefetch effect and `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s own analyze effect a brand-new `filters` object reference with identical values. Both were keyed on `filters` itself (object identity), so this refired a real `prefetchMatchAnalysis` call for a candidate list that never actually changed — and since the very same round of work added `analyzeMatchWithUser`'s per-pair cooldown, this could now silently eat into that budget for zero benefit. Fixed in both files: a `filtersKey` string (`` `${type}:${genres.join(",")}:${useCount}:${useAvgRating}` ``) replaces `filters` in each effect's own dependency array (the real `filters` object is still what's passed into the actual call).

5. **No action on the "no matches found" empty state.** Unlike the `error` branch right above it (which has a "Retry" button), zero results left the user with only the small, easy-to-miss back-arrow (bottom-left) to go adjust filters. New "Adjust Filters" button in that branch, same `goToPage(0)` the back-arrow already uses.

6. **Unbounded animation-ref growth.** `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s `bobAnimsRef`/`lineBobAnimsRef` (one `Animated.ValueXY` pair per candidate, for the idle-drift bob + its JS-mirrored copy the connecting lines read) only ever grew — this component isn't remounted between searches, so re-searching repeatedly accumulated an entry for every candidate ever seen in the session, never pruned. New effect prunes both dictionaries down to just the current candidate set whenever it changes (keyed on the existing `layoutKey`).

Honest limitation, same as the previous audit: no way to actually drive the RN UI in this environment. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean after all six), a fresh Metro bundle fetch (confirmed `medalGradientId`/`mutualInitialLoading`/`filtersKey`/the new "Adjust Filters" string all compiled in, and the old hardcoded `"medalShine"` id string is gone from the bundle entirely), and a live re-hit of `GET /api/match/sync/candidates` confirming the backend side is completely unaffected (96 candidates, unchanged).

### Real live-testing bug report, same feature: Favorites/Variety going permanently blank, plus Shared Genres/Favorites/Variety coverflow polish

Direct report from actually using the app (not just reading code): some cards render blank and never load — reproduced in Favorites and Variety specifically. Plus a cluster of related coverflow polish asks: Shared Genres/Shared Favorites should rest on an empty slot at first (matching Variety's own genre coverflow) with a hint explaining the viewer needs to swipe; some Variety genre chips were truncating with "…"; and none of the three coverflows let a viewer tap a visible-but-not-centered item to jump to it — only an actual drag gesture moved the row.

**The blank-forever bug, root-caused precisely, not guessed at.** Both `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx` and `MatchVarietyRings.tsx` (added in the earlier "eager fan-out replaced with a single shared gate" fix above) used a ref to mark "this fetch has already started (or finished) for this key" — set as soon as the request fired, before it resolved. Real, reachable race: switching to a *different* candidate while `activeIndex` was still ≥1 from browsing a *previous* one starts `shouldLoad` already `true` (inherited stale state, one render ahead of `MatchAnalysisPanel`'s own `setActiveIndex(0)` reset-on-switch effect) — the fetch fires and marks the ref, then that same reset effect flips `activeIndex` back to 0 a moment later, `shouldLoad` follows it back to `false`, and the effect's own cleanup cancels the now-orphaned in-flight request. With the ref already marked "handled," every later `shouldLoad:true` (swiping past the summary again for that candidate) saw "already attempted" and silently skipped fetching — forever, for that candidate, with the underlying state (`itemsById`/`ratingsById`, `myStats`/`theirStats`) never actually populated and no way to recover short of leaving and reselecting. Fixed in both files the same way: the "handled" ref is now set only inside the success callback (`.then()`), never before the request starts — a cancelled attempt leaves it untouched, so the next `shouldLoad:true` genuinely retries instead of believing a request that never actually completed.

**Coverflow polish, four related changes, all landing in `PosterCoverflow.tsx` (shared by Shared Genres/Shared Favorites/Activity) and `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`'s own `GenreCoverflow`:**

- **Leading empty rest slot, extended from Variety to Shared Genres/Shared Favorites.** `PosterCoverflow.tsx` gained an opt-in `leadingEmptySlot` prop (off by default — `MatchActivityFeed.tsx`'s own usage untouched, out of this round's stated scope) that renders a real blank slot before item 0 and rests there at mount, reporting `onFocusChange(null)` instead of auto-focusing item 0 — the exact same "nothing selected at rest" convention `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`'s `GenreCoverflow` already established for its own leading slot. `onFocusChange`'s type widened to `(id: string | null) => void` to carry this (already source-compatible with every real caller, all of which already hold `string | null` state). Wired into `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx` and the Shared Genres card (`MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`) — both also had their own "pre-select item 0 for the coverflow branch" reset logic simplified to unconditionally reset to `null`, since the coverflow itself now starts there too; the Shared Genres one in particular used to carry a whole paragraph of comment explaining a mount-order race between itself and the coverflow's own effect — moot now that both branches agree on the same starting value, simplified accordingly.
- **The hint text now shows for the coverflow's own empty rest state, not just the <3-item tap fallback.** `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`'s hint visibility changed from `!useCoverflow` to `!focusedId` (the Shared Genres card's own hint was already keyed on `selectedPosterId`, no change needed there).
