Wording on both updated from "Tap a poster..." to "Swipe or tap a poster..." — matching the actual two ways to move the coverflow now (see below).
- **Genre chips no longer truncate.** `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`'s `GenreCoverflow` sized each chip from `chipWidthFor()` — a flat per-character estimate that occasionally undershot real rendered width for wider genre names, cutting them off with "…". Replaced with the exact write-once-then-freeze real-measurement pattern `CineGraphDonut.tsx`/`CineMatchGenreRing.tsx` already use for their own chips elsewhere in this app: a new `chipWidths` state, populated via `onLayout` on each chip (only ever written once per genre, never overwritten again), used in place of the estimate the moment it's available — the estimate stays only as the very first paint's placeholder before that measurement lands. Removed `numberOfLines={1}` from the chip text now that its own slot is guaranteed to eventually fit it exactly. **Correction, from real live testing the very next round (below): this fix was itself wrong** — measuring the visible chip directly doesn't work in this component the way it does in `CineGraphDonut.tsx`, see below for why and the actual fix.
- **Tap-to-scroll, all three coverflows.** Previously only an actual drag gesture moved any of them — the visible-but-not-centered neighbor peeking in from the side wasn't tappable at all. Both `PosterCoverflow.tsx` and `GenreCoverflow` (`MatchVarietyRings.tsx`) gained a scroll ref and a `goToIndex(i)` helper (`scrollRef.current?.scrollTo({x: <that item's own offset>, animated: true})`), with each item now wrapped in a `Pressable` calling it — the existing scroll-position listener still reports whichever item ends up centered the same way regardless of whether it got there by a drag or a tap, so nothing else needed to change.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after each of the two bug-fix files and each of the four coverflow-polish changes; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `leadingEmptySlot`, `chipWidths`, `goToIndex`, and the new "Swipe or tap a poster..." string all compiled in. The measurement/layout behavior itself (real chip widths, actual tap targets) can't be verified without a real device in this environment — same honest limitation as both audits above — but the underlying technique is a direct reuse of an already-proven, already-shipped pattern in this exact codebase (`CineGraphDonut.tsx`), not a new approach.

### More real live-testing bugs on the same cards: the previous round's own chip-width fix was still wrong, plus polish requests

Direct report from continued real use: genre chips ("Music", "Romance", "War", "Western", "Crime", "Comedy", "Drama" among the ones actually seen, explicitly flagged as maybe not the full list) were still wrapping to a second line — a letter or two dropping below the pill, breaking its shape. Plus: add the same divider `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx` uses between its poster row and detail block to Variety's own coverflow/detail transition; the detail area's count + unit ("425 movies") read too large/prominent; and poster-scrolling sections with too few items to actually need scrolling were falling back to tap-only instead of the same scroll mechanism.

**Root-caused precisely why the previous round's own "fix" didn't work, not just patched the symptom again.** That fix measured the *visible* chip's own `onLayout` — but unlike `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s chips (genuinely unconstrained: `position:"absolute"`, entirely outside flex flow), `GenreCoverflow`'s chip sits inside `item`, a **normal-flow** flex child with an **explicit** `width: slot.width`. `alignItems:"center"` only controls cross-axis alignment — it doesn't let a child render wider than that explicit ancestor width. So whenever the fallback estimate undershot a genre's true width, the text genuinely *wrapped* inside the too-narrow slot, and the "measurement" captured was the *already-wrapped* box — frozen forever, permanently locking in the exact broken 2-line chip being reported, for that genre specifically (explaining why only some chips were affected — whichever ones the flat per-character estimate happened to undershoot).

Real fix: decoupled measurement from the visible, constrained layout entirely. `GenreCoverflow` now renders an invisible probe — one `Text` per genre, `position:"absolute"`, `opacity:0`, wrapped in a container with `alignItems:"flex-start"` (not the flex default `"stretch"`, which would otherwise force every probe to the width of the widest genre name) — genuinely unconstrained the same way `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s real chips are, so `onLayout` on *this* reports the string's true single-line width regardless of whatever the visible slot's current width happens to be. `handleChipLayout` adds back the same `CHIP_H_PADDING*2` the old estimate already accounted for (the probe measures bare text, not the padded pill) and keeps the same `MIN_CHIP_WIDTH` floor. By the time the *visible* chip renders, its slot is already the correct width — it's never placed in a too-narrow box to begin with, so there's nothing left to wrap.

Three more direct fixes, same round:

- **Divider added to Variety.** New `divider` style in `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`, identical to `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`'s own (`height: hairlineWidth, backgroundColor: colors.border, marginTop:12, marginBottom:10`), placed between `GenreCoverflow` and the You/them detail row.
- **Detail count/unit text shrunk and muted.** `detailText` (the "425 movies" line under each bold "YOU"/username header) went from `fontSize:15, color: colors.baseContent` to `fontSize:12.5, color: colors.placeholder` — per direct feedback it was reading as too large/prominent next to `detailName` above it, which is meant to be the one bold attention-getting line in the pair.
- **Poster-scrolling sections now always use the coverflow, regardless of item count.** `PosterCoverflow.tsx`'s own `COVERFLOW_MIN_ITEMS` threshold (previously 3 — below that, every caller fell back to a plain tap-based `PosterRow`) removed entirely, per direct ask: "even with just 1 [poster], the scroll system should work exactly the same" — the fallback isn't a graceful degradation from the viewer's own perspective, it's a different, inconsistent interaction model kicking in unpredictably based on how much overlap happened to exist. Applied to all three real callers (`MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`, the Shared Genres card in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`, `MatchActivityFeed.tsx`) — each now renders `PosterCoverflow` unconditionally, with the now-dead `PosterRow`-branch code, `useCoverflow` variables, and `COVERFLOW_MIN_ITEMS` imports removed at all three. `MatchActivityFeed.tsx`'s own hint text/styles were removed here as apparently-dead (no `leadingEmptySlot`, item 0 auto-focusing immediately) — **corrected the very next round below**, where the user asked for exactly that empty-rest behavior on this card too, restoring what had just been deleted. `PosterRow.tsx` itself is untouched and not deleted — its `PosterBadge` type is still imported by `PosterCoverflow.tsx`, and it's not otherwise confirmed dead app-wide.

**Deliberately not implemented without confirming first**: a direct request for my own opinion on whether the detail readout should show more than just a raw count — a percentage share of that person's total, an average rating, or several of these stacked — genuinely open, not a bug or a clear directive, held for a follow-up answer rather than guessed at.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after each change; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `measureLayer`/`goToIndex` compiled in and confirmed `COVERFLOW_MIN_ITEMS` is gone from the bundle entirely.

### Fourth round on these same cards: the chip-width fix was *still* wrong, a real "stuck" animation bug root-caused and fixed, Activity's empty-rest state restored, percentage added

Direct report, continued real use: genre buttons (Music/Romance/War/Western/Crime/Comedy/Drama, again flagged as maybe not the complete list) were *still* wrapping to a broken second line despite the previous round's dedicated fix. Plus: double-tapping the *selected* genre pill in Shared Genres left the hint text visibly "stuck in the background" — a real bug, not a request; the hint should only ever show while genuinely displaying the empty state; Activity's poster row should rest on an empty slot at first like the others now do; and the agreed-on percentage should actually get added.

**Root-caused precisely why the previous round's "genuinely unconstrained invisible probe" fix still didn't work, rather than patching the symptom a third time.** That fix should have worked in principle (matching `CineGraphDonut.tsx`'s own proven position:absolute measurement technique) but evidently didn't hold up in practice. Rather than debug an RN layout/timing edge case blind with no device to test against, replaced the whole approach with the simplest fix that has zero dependency on any runtime measurement working correctly at all — the user's own suggestion: make the estimate itself generously wide. `CHAR_WIDTH_ESTIMATE` (a flat px-per-character constant) went `6.8`→`9.5` and `CHIP_H_PADDING` `14`→`16` — sized to comfortably clear real DM Sans Medium 11.5px text for every realistic genre name (checked by hand against the actually-reported words plus longer ones like "Science Fiction"/"Action & Adventure": all land with 40-70px of real text budget past what they need), not just tuned to the shortest ones. The entire invisible-probe machinery (`chipWidths` state, `handleChipLayout`, the measurement layer) was removed along with it — a little extra empty space inside a pill is a far smaller visual cost than the wrap it was trying (twice) to prevent.

**Real "stuck" animation bug, root-caused, not just re-triggered by removing the guard.** Shared Genres' hint text used a hand-rolled `Animated.Value` (`hintAnim`) whose *consuming JSX* lived inside a `showAllGenres ? grid : hintWrap` ternary — double-tapping the genre pill (open the grid, close it again) unmounted and remounted that `Animated.View`, but the hand-rolled effect only re-fired on the `selectedPosterId===null` boundary, never on this remount, so the freshly-remounted element could pick up a stale mid-animation value instead of a clean one. Compared against `MatchRadarChart.tsx`'s own equivalent hint, which has never had this bug: its hint is *always mounted* (opacity-only, no ternary that ever unmounts it) — structurally immune, since there's no remount for its animation to race against. Rebuilt Shared Genres' hint to match: it's now always mounted (only the grid is the one conditionally-mounted branch), and the hand-rolled `hintAnim` was replaced with the shared `useRevealAnimation` hook (already hardened earlier this session against exactly this class of bug) keyed on the *actual* full condition, `!showAllGenres && !selectedPosterId` — directly satisfying the explicit ask that the hint "should only appear when displaying the empty state," not a separate, narrower condition than what actually controls its visibility. Checked `MatchSharedFavorites.tsx`/`MatchActivityFeed.tsx`'s own hints for the same risk per the "check if this bug exists elsewhere too" ask — both already used `useRevealAnimation` from the start (never hand-rolled), and their hint elements were already always-mounted, not living inside an unmounting ternary — confirmed not affected.

**Activity's empty-rest state restored** (undoing the previous round's own "apparently dead" cleanup) — `leadingEmptySlot` added to its `PosterCoverflow` usage, matching Shared Genres/Shared Favorites, with the same hint text/styles brought back and its own reset-on-switch effect changed from auto-focusing item 0 to resting on `null`, per direct ask that this card behave the same way as the other two now that the user actually wants that everywhere, not just where it was first requested.

**Percentage added to Variety's detail readout**, per the agreed-on recommendation from the previous round. New `myPct`/`theirPct` — each person's selected genre count as a percentage of *their own* total (not a shared denominator, so "this genre is a bigger slice of my taste than of theirs" is visible), only computed once a specific genre is actually selected (against the resting "overall total" state, where a percentage of itself is always a meaningless 100%). Rendered as `"425 movies · 18%"`, appended to the existing count line rather than a new row.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after each of the four fixes; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed the new `CHAR_WIDTH_ESTIMATE`, `hintOpacity` (Shared Genres' replacement for the removed `hintAnim`), and `myPct` all compiled in, and confirmed `measureLayer`/`chipWidths` (the removed probe machinery) are gone from the bundle entirely.

### Fifth round: a real uneven-chip-spacing bug root-caused (not just re-measured), a scroll-lag fix applied to all three coverflows, the results-screen back button moved, and the "Your Top 5 Syncs" header resized

Direct report, continued real use: Variety's chip spacing looked uneven (explicitly "don't change or break anything else" otherwise); Shared Genres' detail info visibly lagged behind a fast scroll once a match had 100+ shared titles ("how do we solve this"); the results-screen back button should move from bottom-left to top-left; the "Your Top 5 Syncs" header should sit lower and read bigger/bolder.

**Uneven chip spacing, root-caused as a side effect of the previous round's own fix, not a `CHIP_GAP` bug.** `CHIP_GAP` (12px) was already applied identically in both the layout math (`centers`) and the rendered `gap` style — the *slot* spacing was already exactly uniform. The actual cause: each chip's `Pressable`/pill was sized to its own intrinsic content (text + padding) and centered within its slot via `alignItems:"center"`, not stretched to fill it. Once the previous round's fix made `chipWidthFor`'s estimate deliberately generous (to stop truncation), the gap between a slot's *reserved* width and its pill's *actual* (smaller, content-sized) width varied per genre name — leftover slack that read as visibly uneven gaps between pills, even though the underlying slot pitch never moved. Fixed by making the pill itself stretch to fill its slot (`alignSelf:"stretch"` on the `Pressable` and the chip's `Animated.View`) instead of floating centered inside it — the generous estimate now shows up as consistent breathing room *inside* each pill rather than inconsistent gaps *between* them. Nothing about `CHIP_GAP`, `chipWidthFor`, or the offset/centering math itself changed.

**Shared Genres/Variety/Activity scroll-lag, root-caused as committing to React state (and the parent detail-panel re-render that follows) on every intermediate scroll frame.** All three coverflows (`PosterCoverflow.tsx`'s shared component, plus `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`'s own `GenreCoverflow`) used a continuous `scrollX.addListener` firing on every scroll frame (~60fps), calling `onFocusChange` on each index change — fine at a handful of items, but with 100+ shared titles a fast fling produces many index changes per second, each triggering a parent re-render the JS thread visibly can't keep up with (the reported "detail info geriden geliyor"). The centered item's own grow/shrink `scale` was never the problem — that's a native-driven `scrollX.interpolate`, with no JS/state involved either way. Fixed by removing the per-frame listener entirely and committing focus (and therefore `onFocusChange`) only once the scroll genuinely settles, via `onMomentumScrollEnd` + `onScrollEndDrag` (both bound, since a slow drag with no residual velocity doesn't reliably fire momentum end on every platform) — a fast flick through a long list now commits once, right when it stops, instead of continuously while still moving. Applied identically to both coverflow implementations for consistency, even though `GenreCoverflow`'s own item count (bounded by the genre taxonomy) makes this less likely to bite in practice.

**Back button moved top-left.** This screen renders with `headerShown:false` (no native header, no built-in safe-area handling) — added `useSafeAreaInsets()` (matching `search/index.tsx`'s own established convention for this exact situation) and repositioned `pageBackButton` from `bottom:16` to `top: insets.top + 12`, so it clears the status bar/notch on every device instead of assuming a fixed offset.

**"Your Top 5 Syncs" header resized.** `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s `SvgText`: `fontSize` 13→19, `fontFamily`/`fontWeight` switched from `fonts.bold`/`"bold"` to `fonts.extrabold`/`"800"` (the DM Sans 800 weight added earlier this session for `MatchTitleBadge.tsx`), and `marginTop:14` added to push it down from the top of the cloud card.

**Open design question answered, not implemented**: whether to prefer top-5 candidates with more percentage spread over the literal top 5 by score, for a "more professional" read. Recommendation given: lean against it, or apply it only as a narrow tiebreaker — the Top-5/medal framing implies "these are your actual best matches," and silently swapping in a lower-scored candidate to manufacture visual spread undermines that meaning; a genuinely clustered top 5 is itself honest signal (this candidate pool doesn't have much variance), not a defect to paper over. Not implemented pending explicit confirmation.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after all edits; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `handleScrollSettle`/`onMomentumScrollEnd` present in both coverflow implementations, the chip `alignSelf:"stretch"` styling present, `useSafeAreaInsets`/`insets.top` present in `match/index.tsx`, and the resized header's `fonts.extrabold` (`DMSans_800ExtraBold`) present in the bundle.

### Sixth round: the ai-summary card's ring-badge-between-avatars replaced with a percentage bar, and a one-time reveal-streak animation added

Direct ask: replace `MatchTierRow.tsx`'s small circular percentage ring (sitting between the viewer's and candidate's avatars) with a horizontal bar instead — the bar's two ends aligned vertically under each avatar's own center, sitting below the avatar row, filled left-to-right by percentage, tier-colored (reusing the existing score-tier system), with the app's own bottom-tab Sync glyph (`sparkles`) marking exactly where the fill ends. Explicit constraint: removing the ring must not move the avatars. Also asked for a recommendation on card presentation — a colored border, or a one-time "shooting star" streak around the card on first open — and to implement whichever I recommended.

**`MatchTierRow.tsx` rebuilt.** The two avatars stay in the exact same row, at the exact same positions — the old ring badge's `48px` footprint (`BADGE_SIZE`) is preserved as an invisible spacer between them rather than removed, so nothing about their layout changes. Below the row, a new `barWrap` (same known width as the row, so its geometry is computable in absolute terms rather than guessed) holds a rounded track (`colors.border` background) with an `Animated.View` fill (tier-colored via the now-`export`ed `tierColorFor`, animated 0→target width over 700ms on candidate switch, same pacing the old ring used) — the track's own left offset (`AVATAR_SIZE/2`) and width (`rowWidth - AVATAR_SIZE`) are fixed constants derived once from the row's own known dimensions, so the bar's ends land exactly under each avatar's center by construction, not by any runtime measurement. A small circular marker (tier-colored background, white `sparkles` Ionicon, matching the bottom-tab Sync icon) rides the fill's leading edge via `transform:[{translateX: fillAnim}]` — starting centered on the bar's own start point at 0% and translating to the fill's end point as it animates — with the percentage number floating just above it the same way.

**Card-reveal question answered and implemented: a one-time tier-colored streak, not a permanent border.** New `MatchCardShine.tsx` — an SVG rounded-rect trace (two overlapping strokes sharing one animated dash: a soft wide translucent glow underneath a narrower solid line, standing in for a real gradient-along-the-path effect that a spatially-fixed SVG stroke gradient couldn't actually produce, since the gradient wouldn't "lead" a moving dash) sweeps a short comet (~22% of the card's own perimeter) once around the ai-summary card's border, then fades out. Reasoning given for choosing this over a permanent colored border: a static border reads as this app's own status/alert color language and adds permanent visual weight, where a one-time reveal captures "special moment" without lingering — the same family of idea as `MatchTitleBadge`'s existing stamp-in entrance. Mounted only once `parsed` (the loaded analysis) is actually available, keyed on the candidate's id — swiping away and back to the same candidate's card never remounts it (condition and key both stay the same), so it plays exactly once per candidate, matching `MatchTitleBadge`'s own "once per candidate, not once per scroll-back" precedent, not once per card view.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `MatchCardShine`, `COMET_FRACTION`/`GLOW_STROKE_WIDTH`, and the exported `tierColorFor` all present, and the old ring's `AnimatedCircle` usage gone from `MatchTierRow.tsx` (one remaining bundle hit was a comment, unrelated to this component).

### Seventh round: the new percentage bar shortened, sped up, and moved off the JS thread; two real flash/flicker bugs found and fixed

Direct ask, after actually seeing the bar built: make it shorter and faster, and fix a "tutukluk" (stutter/jank) in it. Two more real bugs reported from live use, unrelated to the bar itself: right before the results screen opens after tapping Sync, an "Adjust Filters"-style button flashes and disappears; and switching between candidates in the analysis deck briefly flashes a loading card before the new candidate's real content appears.

**Bar: shorter, faster, and moved onto the native driver.** `MatchTierRow.tsx`'s `BAR_WIDTH` fixed at 100px (was the full 152px avatar-center-to-avatar-center span), centered within that same span (`AVATAR_SPAN`) rather than touching each avatar's exact center, so it still reads as "between the two profiles" without stretching edge to edge. `FILL_MS` 700→380. The jank's real cause: the fill was an animated `width` (a layout property, `useNativeDriver:false`, JS-thread-driven) running at the same moment as the ai-summary card's own new `MatchCardShine` reveal streak (necessarily JS-driven too — SVG stroke props aren't native-drivable) — two concurrent JS-thread animations on the same reveal moment. Rebuilt the fill as a fixed-width `View` scaled in via `transform:[{scaleX}]` with `transformOrigin:"left"` (RN 0.86 supports this directly, no manual translate-compensation needed) driven by a plain 0→1 `Animated.timing` with `useNativeDriver:true` — the marker/percentage-text `translateX` were already transform properties, so the whole bar now rides the native driver end to end, only the shine remains JS-driven.

**Real bug found, "Adjust Filters" flashing before the results screen opens.** Root cause: `match/index.tsx`'s `loadQueue` calls `setCandidates(...)` from inside a promise continuation, and `tryFinishMatch`'s `goToPage(1)` (native-driven, `useNativeDriver:true`) starts sliding page 1 into view independent of whether React has actually committed/painted that state update yet — page 1's own "no results yet" empty state (with the "Adjust Filters" button added several rounds ago) could still be what's on screen for the first frame or two of the slide, before React catches up and swaps in the real `MatchResultsCloud`. Fixed by wrapping the actual transition (`setMatchAnimating(false); goToPage(1)`) in a `requestAnimationFrame`, giving React's scheduler a chance to flush the pending `setCandidates`/`setError` update first — covers both the success and error paths uniformly since both go through the same `finally()` → `tryFinishMatch` path.

**Real bug found, a loading card flashing when switching candidates.** Root cause: `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s candidate-switch effect sets `analyzing(true)` unconditionally on every switch, and the ai-summary card's render is gated directly on it — when the tapped candidate's analysis was already prefetched/cached (`MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s own ahead-of-tap prefetch, or simply revisited this session), `prefetchMatchAnalysis` resolves in a handful of milliseconds, so the "Generating your compatibility analysis..." spinner card rendered and vanished almost immediately — read as a card flashing on screen. Fixed with a debounced `showAnalyzingSpinner` (new `ANALYZING_SPINNER_DELAY_MS = 150`): only becomes true if `analyzing` has stayed true past that grace window, so a fast/cached resolution never renders the spinner at all; a genuinely slow fetch still shows it, just slightly later than before. The render chain's middle state (loading, but under the grace window, no data yet) renders nothing rather than falling through to the "No analysis available." text, which would otherwise have been its own brief false-negative flash.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `showAnalyzingSpinner`/`ANALYZING_SPINNER_DELAY_MS`, the `requestAnimationFrame` deferral, `transformOrigin`, and the new `AVATAR_SPAN`-based shorter bar constant all present.

### Eighth round: the card-reveal streak turned into a traveling dot, and a real check on whether "Adjust Filters" is still used

Direct ask: the border-tracing effect (`MatchCardShine.tsx`) reads as a bar/streak, not the "glowing point" originally described — make it an actual dot. Also: the "Adjust Filters" button (added several rounds ago, then implicated in the previous round's flash-race bug) — delete it if it's not actually used anymore.

**Streak turned into a dot.** Recalibrated the same underlying SVG technique rather than replacing it: `strokeDasharray` now uses a near-zero dash length (`DASH_LENGTH=1`, kept just above literal 0 since some renderers skip a truly zero-length dash's caps entirely) with `strokeLinecap="round"` — the two round caps on either end of an effectively invisible dash merge into a single solid circle. `DOT_SIZE=10` (solid) / `GLOW_SIZE=22` (soft, `strokeOpacity:0.35`) replace the old `STROKE_WIDTH=3`/`GLOW_STROKE_WIDTH=7` streak widths and `COMET_FRACTION` (a fraction of the perimeter) is gone entirely — the dot's size is now a fixed pixel value, not perimeter-relative. Same animated `strokeDashoffset` sweep, same one-time-per-candidate mount/fade lifecycle, unchanged.

**"Adjust Filters" checked, kept — genuinely still used, not dead code.** Grepped for every reference: it's used in exactly one place, `match/index.tsx`'s `candidates.length === 0` branch, and that branch is a real reachable state — a search whose filters happen to match zero users (a small/filtered candidate pool, not just theoretical). The previous round's flash bug was a *timing race* that could show this same branch transiently during a normal, non-empty search — fixed at the race, not by removing the branch — so the button still serves its original purpose (a direct way back to filters from a genuine "no matches" result) and wasn't removed.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `DASH_LENGTH`/`DOT_SIZE`/`GLOW_SIZE` present and the old `COMET_FRACTION` fully gone.

### Ninth round: the dot rebuilt as a tiny soft white "star" glint — not disliked for shape this time, disliked for scale and hard edges

Direct feedback: the dot was still wrong — needs to be much smaller and thinner, softer at the edges (no crisp boundary), read as a glinting star, and be plain white rather than tier-colored.

**Four concentric layers replace the previous two.** `MatchCardShine.tsx`'s single solid-plus-glow pair (`DOT_SIZE=10`/`GLOW_SIZE=22`) is now four stacked circles sharing the same dash trick and the same animated position — `HALO_SIZE=15` (opacity 0.1) → `OUTER_SIZE=9` (0.22) → `MID_SIZE=5` (0.5) → `CORE_SIZE=2.5` (0.95, near-solid). react-native-svg has no reliably testable blur/filter support in this environment, so this stack of barely-visible-on-their-own rings stands in for a real gaussian glow the same way a layered CSS `box-shadow` would — each ring softens the falloff a bit more, so there's no single hard edge anywhere, just a bright pinprick fading out. Color hardcoded to plain white (`#FFFFFF`) rather than the tier color it briefly used — reads as a glint of light, not a status indicator — so the `color` prop was dropped from the component entirely (and the now-unused `tierColorFor` import removed from `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s call site along with it).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `HALO_SIZE`/`CORE_SIZE`/the literal `#FFFFFF` present and the previous round's `DOT_SIZE`/`GLOW_SIZE` fully gone.

### Tenth round: the card-reveal effect abandoned entirely (three redesigns in, still not right), a real backend latency fix, and a fresh optimization pass over everything changed since the last one

Direct call after three failed redesign attempts (streak → hard-edged dot → soft white glint): drop the card-reveal effect altogether, nothing around the card border. Also asked for a fresh optimization/dynamics audit of the Sync and results screens given everything added since the last one (§3's seventh audit), and reported CineGraph loading a bit late on the Sync page's first paint, specifically the ring around the profile — asked whether that can be sped up.

**`MatchCardShine.tsx` deleted outright**, not just unmounted — its JSX call site and import removed from `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`, the file itself deleted, and the explanatory comment in `MatchTierRow.tsx` that referenced it (about why the bar's own fill moved to the native driver) reworded to describe the fix without pointing at a component that no longer exists. Confirmed nothing else references it via a full grep.

**Real backend fix: `getUserCineGraph` (backend/controllers/userController.js) was doing three sequential DB round trips where they could run concurrently.** `Movie.find`/`Series.find`/`Rating.find` (independent of each other, each only depending on the watchlist IDs from the *first* query, `User.findById`) were three separate sequential `await`s — rewritten as one `Promise.all`. Live-tested against this environment's own MongoDB Atlas cluster (JWT-minted for the Zachary test account): a *single* simple query (a plain profile fetch) already takes ~850ms end-to-end here — this specific Codespace's network path to Atlas, not something an application-code change can fix — so the real, honest win from parallelizing isn't eliminating that per-round-trip floor, it's cutting the *number* of sequential floors paid: 4 sequential round trips (User, Movie, Series, Rating) before, 2 now (User, then the parallel batch) — roughly half the total latency, whatever the per-round-trip time turns out to be in a real deployment closer to the Atlas region.

**Fresh optimization pass over everything touched since the last audit** (the bar/shine additions and removal, the coverflow settle-only commit changes, the debounced analyzing spinner, the safe-area-inset back button): re-read `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`, `PosterCoverflow.tsx`, `MatchVarietyRings.tsx`, `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`, and `match/index.tsx` in full against this round's changes. One real finding beyond the shine removal itself: `MatchTierRow.tsx` still imported `Text` from `react-native` after its bar redesign switched to `Animated.Text` — dead import, removed. Everything else checked out: `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`'s prefetch-key stabilization, bob-anim pruning, and `React.memo`-friendly `handleSelectCandidate` are all still doing their job; the coverflows' settle-only commit (previous round) has no new interaction with the debounced spinner or the now-removed shine; the `requestAnimationFrame` page-transition deferral has no unmount guard, but neither did the code before it, and the exposure window is one frame (~16ms) — noted, not treated as urgent. With the shine gone, there's no longer a second JS-thread animation competing with the bar's own (already native-driven) fill on this card at all, so that specific stutter risk is now moot rather than just mitigated.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `MatchCardShine`/`HALO_SIZE` are both fully gone from the bundle; `node --check` on the backend controller, plus a live re-hit of `GET /api/users/cinegraph-data/:id` confirming correct data still returns after the parallelization.

### Eleventh round: Free/Plus/Premium tier leveling built for Sync — the first real subscription-tier work in the app, scoped to this one feature

The app's account tiers (`free`/`pro`/`premium`/`dev`) had existed since early in this session (gating Sync filter access, match-analysis cooldowns, Profile Analysis richness) but nothing had ever been *designed* around them — no naming decision, no page explaining them, no per-feature leveling beyond a few numeric knobs. This round: renamed the middle paid tier `pro`→`plus` (a naming discussion, not this round's own call — free/plus/premium read as the more natural escalation for a lifestyle/social app than free/pro/premium, avoiding two "prestige" words — Pro and Premium — sitting adjacent with no obvious ordering), then built a full Sync-specific leveling scheme on top: a daily sync-search quota, a filter-access split (type/genre vs the useCount/useAvgRating weighting toggles), tier-locked bubbles in the results cloud, and partial/locked content across the analysis card deck. Payment itself stays out of scope for now — the existing dev-only `setOwnAccountTier` endpoint (already in the codebase, unrelated to this round, originally built for manual test-account tier assignment) doubles as this round's "simulate a purchase" mechanism.

**`pro`→`plus` rename, done everywhere it appeared.** Backend: `config/tiers.js`'s `TIER_LIMITS` key, `models/User.js`'s `accountTier` enum (the live, mutable field — old `'pro'` values migrated in the DB, one real user found and updated), `models/ProfileAnalysis.js`'s `tier` enum (an append-only historical log — `'pro'` kept *alongside* `'plus'` here rather than migrated, since old rows are never re-saved and rewriting "what tier the user actually was at analysis time" would be revisionist), `scripts/setUserTier.js`, and `controllers/userController.js`'s `setOwnAccountTier` validation list. Mobile: `types/index.ts`'s `AccountTier` union, `theme/tierFrames.ts`'s frame-style key (blue "platinum" gradient, unchanged — this tier already had that identity from an earlier round, back when it was still called Pro), and every literal tier-name comparison (`PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`, `ShareCard.tsx`, `ProfileAnalysesTab.tsx`, `settings.tsx`'s dev-tools `TIER_OPTIONS`, `match/index.tsx`'s `canUseMatchFilters`). No UI label mapping existed to update separately — tier names render as the raw string value directly, so the rename alone fixed display text too.

**New backend config (`config/tiers.js`)**: `syncSearchesPerDay` (free:1, plus:3, premium:15, dev:999) and `canUseAdvancedMatchFilters` (free:false, plus:false, premium:true, dev:true) — distinct from the existing `canUseMatchFilters` (type/genre access). New `models/SyncSearchLog.js` (mirrors the existing `MatchAnalysisLog.js` pattern — an append-only per-user timestamp log) backs the quota: `getSyncCandidates` counts today's rows before doing any real work and returns 429 (`{retryAfterMs, limit}`) over quota, logs a new row only after a search actually succeeds (a request that errors before that point doesn't silently burn quota). The advanced-filter gate is enforced the same "server decides regardless of what the client sends" way `canUseMatchFilters` already worked: `useCount`/`useAvgRating` are forced to `DEFAULT_MATCH_FILTERS`' values unless `canUseAdvancedMatchFilters` is true, live-verified by requesting `useCount=false&useAvgRating=false` as Plus (forced back to true/true, `breakdown.collaborative` stayed non-zero) versus as Premium (honored, `breakdown.collaborative` dropped to 0).

**Search page (`MatchFilterStrip.tsx`)**: the existing `locked` prop (whole-card dim + lock notice, built several rounds ago) already matched the "blur and a lock symbol" idea directly — reused as-is for Free, just re-labeled Plus. New `advancedLocked` prop dims/locks only the Watched Count / Average Rating switches (and the "Apply All Filters" shortcut, which toggles the same two) for Plus, showing a lock icon in place of each `Switch` plus a tappable "Upgrade to Premium…" hint. The whole-card lock notice was restructured into a real full-card tap target routing to the new subscription page — it used to sit *inside* the `pointerEvents:"none"` wrapper, which would have silently swallowed its own taps; pulled out to a sibling `Pressable` overlaying the same area instead of relying on any child-overrides-parent pointerEvents behavior that isn't reliably verifiable without a device. `match/index.tsx`'s `loadQueue` also gained 429-specific handling — a distinct `quotaExceeded` state drives an "Upgrade" button (routing to the subscription page) instead of the usual pointless "Retry" on the results page's error branch.

**Results cloud (`MatchResultsCloud.tsx`/`MatchCloudBubble.tsx`/`MatchAvatarRing.tsx`)**: `lockedRanksFor(tier)` returns which cloud ranks are gated — Free locks only rank 0 (the #1 match: already the cloud's largest, most-central bubble by construction, so this leverages the *existing* visual hierarchy for the strongest "what am I missing" pull, the same reasoning dating apps use for blurring a "someone likes you" reveal — recommended over locking the *lower* four, which would show only worse matches and undersell the app's own results), Plus locks ranks 3-4 (#4-5, keeping its own top 3 fully open). A locked bubble dims (`MatchAvatarRing`'s new `dimmed` prop, opacity only — the percentage stays legible as the actual tease) and gets a small lock badge (`MatchCloudBubble`'s new `locked` prop); tapping one routes to the subscription page instead of opening the analysis deck, via a `lockedIdsRef` read inside the existing stable `handleSelectCandidate` callback (kept dependency-free so `MatchCloudBubble`'s own `React.memo` still holds).

**Analysis card deck (`MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` + four card components)**: Free replaces every card between the summary and the closing Share card with one locked-teaser card (`{ ai-summary, locked, cover }` — 3 cards total) rather than building the full 8-card deck just to hide most of it; the two inline data-fetch effects that used to fire regardless (`getSharedGenreContent`, `getMutualConnections`) are now also gated on `!isFreeDeck`, so a Free viewer swiping past the summary card no longer fires two real network calls for content that was never going to render. Plus keeps the full deck but truncates four of them via a new shared `LockedUnlockNote.tsx` (a small tappable "Showing N of M — Get Premium to unlock all" row, routing to the subscription page — one consistent mechanic reused everywhere instead of a different trick per card): Shared Genres to the first 5 (narrows `total`/the carousel/the "show all" grid all at once, so nothing downstream needed separate slicing), Variety's chips to the first 6 (already sorted by combined count, so this is "top 6"), Activity's posters to half rounded up (minimum 1 stays visible), Social Overlap's mutuals to the first 10 (`MatchAnalysisPanel`'s own `loadMoreMutualConnections` also stops paginating past that point for Plus, so it doesn't keep fetching pages the grid would just slice away again). Shared Favorites deliberately left untouched — explicit ask not to gate it.

**New subscription page** (`app/(app)/match/subscription.tsx`, registered in `match/_layout.tsx`): a Sync-scoped plan comparison (daily searches / filter access / weighting access per tier), explicitly informational — no billing UI, a demo notice says so outright. "Upgrade"/"Switch" reuses the pre-existing dev-only `setOwnAccountTier` endpoint to actually apply the tier change immediately (this repo has no payment/IAP infrastructure at all yet — confirmed via a dependency check before assuming otherwise), then `updateUser({accountTier})` so the change reflects everywhere in the app without a reload. Every lock point built this round (`MatchFilterStrip`, the results-cloud bubbles, `LockedUnlockNote`, the quota-exceeded error state) routes here.

Verified extensively given the scope: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean after every stage; `node --check` on every touched backend file; live JWT-minted requests against the Zachary test account (temporarily flipped through free/plus/premium via `setOwnAccountTier` and restored to its original `premium` afterward) confirming the daily quota actually blocks at the limit (429 with the right `retryAfterMs`/`limit`), the advanced-filter gate is enforced (not just hidden) for Plus and genuinely usable for Premium, and one real stale-tier DB row (a leftover `'pro'` value) found and migrated; a full Metro bundle fetch for both `match/index` and the new `match/subscription` route confirming every new identifier compiled in and the old `"pro"` literal is gone from actual code (one remaining bundle hit was a comment, not a live comparison). Both the backend (nodemon) and Metro had been killed by an unrelated environment restart partway through this round — restarted via the established `mobile/scripts/start-codespace.sh`, then every live check above was re-run against the fresh processes before trusting any of it.

**Immediate follow-up, same round: a real bug that made Plus unable to Sync at all.** Reported live: with the two weighting switches now locked for Plus, "Apply All Filters" never showed as selected — because it genuinely wasn't. `DEFAULT_FILTERS` starts `useCount`/`useAvgRating` both `false` (a deliberate "nothing selected until Sync is pressed" choice, but only ever meant for the *interactive*, Premium-only case) — with the toggles now locked and non-interactive for Plus, there was no way to ever flip them to `true`, so `hasAnyCriterion` (genre AND signal both required) could never be satisfied and the Sync button stayed permanently disabled, on top of the filter card itself already being unusable. Fixed with a `useEffect` in `match/index.tsx`: whenever `canUseAdvancedMatchFilters` is false, `filters.useCount`/`useAvgRating` are forced to `true` in client state too — matching what the server was already going to force them to regardless, and making "Apply All Filters" correctly show as checked rather than looking unset. Free was never actually blocked by this specific path (its Sync button's own disabled check already skips `hasAnyCriterion` entirely while `locked`), but gets the same forced state for consistency with what the server actually uses.

### Twelfth round: locked-filter UX rework — no more dimmed CineGraph, no more jarring direct-navigation-on-tap, type selection opened up to every tier, and a real Upgrade badge

Four direct issues reported from live use of the round-eleven tier work: the CineGraph ring on the Free-locked filter card looked dim/muted (an unwanted side effect of the whole-card `opacity:0.5` treatment) and should look exactly like it did before any locking existed; tapping a locked control (Apply All Genres, Apply All Filters, and by the same logic Watched Count/Average Rating) jumping straight to the subscription page felt jarring — should show a temporary popup message instead; the Movies/Series type choice had been locked for Free along with everything else, but should be open to every tier; and the screen needed an actual, deliberate "Upgrade" entry point now that locked controls no longer navigate on tap.

**Backend: `type` is no longer gated by `canUseMatchFilters`.** `getSyncCandidates` (matchController.js) previously treated type/genres as one all-or-nothing unit — rewritten so `type` is read from the request and honored for every tier, while `genres` stays gated by `canUseMatchFilters` and `useCount`/`useAvgRating` stay gated by `canUseAdvancedMatchFilters`, each forced back to `DEFAULT_MATCH_FILTERS`' own value independently when its own gate is closed. Live-verified: a Free-tier request with `type=series` now genuinely returns series candidates (`contentType:"series"` in the response), while a `genres` param on the same request is still silently ignored. Hit a real environment snag mid-verification — an orphaned `node server.js` from an earlier manual restart this session was still holding port 5000, so nodemon's own restart after this edit was silently crash-looping (`EADDRINUSE`) behind it, meaning the *old* code kept answering requests for a few test calls before the mismatch was caught; killed the orphan, confirmed a clean single-process restart, then re-ran every check against it.

**`MatchFilterStrip.tsx` rebuilt around toasts instead of whole-card dimming/navigation.** The blanket `opacity:0.5` on the locked card is gone entirely — the CineGraph ring and everything else render at full, normal opacity regardless of tier, matching how the card looked before any tier gating existed. The type switcher (`CineGraphSubTabSwitcher`) is now *always* interactive, for every tier, and lives outside the "rest of the card" grouping entirely — matches the backend's own type-is-ungated change. Everything else that's actually locked (the genre ring, Apply All Genres, Apply All Filters, and — for Plus specifically — the two weighting switches) now shows a toast (the app's existing `ToastContext`/`useToast`, a 2.5s auto-dismissing popup already used elsewhere, reused rather than building a new one) reading an "Upgrade to ___ to ___" message on tap, instead of either doing nothing or jumping straight to the subscription page. Implemented via one absolutely-positioned tap-catching `Pressable` over the ring/apply-row region for Free (`restWrap`, sitting after those elements in paint order so it's on top), and per-control `onPress` swaps for Plus's narrower advanced-lock scope (genre ring and Apply All Genres stay fully real for Plus, only the weighting-related controls show the toast).

**New "Upgrade" badge** (`match/index.tsx`, top-right of the filters page, mirroring the existing top-left back-arrow's positioning convention) — a small pill with a star icon, visible for Free/Plus only (hidden once Premium/dev, and while the first-visit intro card is showing), routing directly to `/match/subscription`. This is now the *only* direct-navigation entry point on this screen — every other locked control shows a toast instead.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `node --check` on the backend controller; fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `showToast`, `upgradeBadge`, `upgradeFiltersMessage`, and `restWrap` all present.

**Immediate follow-up, same round: "Apply All Genres" wasn't showing checked either, same root cause as the earlier useCount/useAvgRating fix.** `DEFAULT_FILTERS.genres` starts `[]` — for Free (genre selection locked/non-functional), there was no way to ever fill it, so "Apply All Genres" looked unset even though the server-side effect of an empty genres array (no restriction) is practically equivalent to "every genre." Added a second `useEffect` in `match/index.tsx` mirroring the useCount/useAvgRating one: whenever `canUseMatchFilters` is false, `filters.genres` is forced to the full `MATCH_GENRE_KEYS[filters.type]` list — re-applies on a type switch too (Movies<->Series now being open to every tier per this same round's other fix), so switching type while locked refills with that type's own genres rather than leaving the previous type's stale list.

### Thirteenth round (2026-09-07): official Cinephix account — auto-posted trivia/tips/highlights/on-this-day/stats/announcements + a real poll mechanic

An Instagram-style official Cinephix account that auto-posts content to Media at intervals, requested after the podium-teaser/popup arc (§3's prior rounds) settled. Designed in two explicit phases per the user's own request: the full 7-category content pool was agreed first (no comment-inviting content — this app has no comment-writing feature — and the "fun question" category became a real closed-option poll with Instagram-style live percentage results instead), then the technical design.

**Backend — new `isOfficial` flag on `User`** (`models/User.js`), separate from `accountTier` (billing tier) so tier-gating logic elsewhere is untouched. One reserved account (`username: "cinephix"`, `accountTier: "premium"` for the existing gold-border post styling) created via `scripts/seedOfficialAccount.js`, idempotent.

**`Share.js` schema extension**: `type` enum gained `"official"` and `"poll"`; new `isOfficialPost` boolean **denormalized at creation time** (the poster is known to be official when the doc is created) so `getShareFeed`'s score `$addFields` can boost it (`FEED_OFFICIAL_BOOST = 6`, live-verified via a direct aggregation dump — official posts score ≈6 exactly as designed) with no extra `$lookup`. `type:"official"` carries `officialCategory` (trivia/tip/highlight/on_this_day/stats/announcement) + `officialText`, reusing the already-generic `contentId`/`contentType`/`contentData` for posts tied to a specific title. `type:"poll"` carries `pollData.options[].votes` (raw voter refs, never sent to the client — both `getShareFeed`'s aggregation and `getUserShares`'s mapping collapse it to `{text, voteCount}` + a separate `userVoteIndex` for the caller's own choice).

**New content-pool models** (`OfficialContent.js` + `OfficialContentLapState.js`, one lap-state doc per pool-backed category) implement the exact rotation dynamic agreed on: shuffle the active pool into a "lap" order, post through with no repeats, and on lap completion — trivia_rich only — soft-retire (never hard-delete) the oldest ~30 `active` items and activate up to that many `pending` ones before reshuffling (fewer swapped in if fewer are ready, never forcing low-quality filler). `services/officialContentService.js`'s `pickFromPool()` implements this; `postOfficialContent(category)` is the single orchestrator every category routes through. Live-authored content pool (`scripts/seedOfficialContent.js`, idempotent by exact text match): **150** hand-written trivia facts (Oscar records, franchise/director/actor/animation/practical-effects/box-office/TV/music/industry facts — all purely informative, no "what do you think?"-style questions), 25 app tips, 20 poll question sets (5 options each, e.g. "which is the goated sitcom"), 10 starter announcements.

**Two DB-native trivia templates** (the only 2 approved after a live schema check ruled out TMDB-rich-field assumptions — this DB's Movie/Series docs only carry `title`/`name`, `poster_path`, `release_date`/`first_air_date`, `genre_ids`, `original_language`/`origin_country`, nothing richer): same-day-release coincidence (`$group` by `release_date`, `$match` count≥2, `$sample`) and origin-country fact (`original_language`/`origin_country` mapped through a small Turkish name table). Trivia posts roll a 25% chance of one of these before falling back to the pool.

**Fully dynamic categories** (no pool — computed fresh from live data every post): `highlight` reuses `getLeaderboard`'s ranking logic — extracted into an exported plain `computeLeaderboard(type)` (`feedController.js`, the route handler now just calls it) so this doesn't fork a second copy — and `getPeopleThreePodiums`, picking a random current leader to feature; `on_this_day` aggregates `$convert`-to-date + `$month`/`$dayOfMonth` matching today's date; `stats` is plain `countDocuments` across User/Rating/Review/Share.

**Cron**: two new daily jobs alongside the existing 03:00 TMDB sync in `server.js` (same fire-and-forget `.catch(logger.error)` pattern) — 10:00 always posts trivia (≈7/week → the 150-item pool laps in ~5 months), 19:00 cycles through `["tip","highlight","on_this_day","poll","stats","announcement"]` by day-of-week (each posts ~weekly).

**Poll voting**: new `POST /shares/:id/vote` (`voteOnPoll`, `shareController.js`) — one vote per user, revoting a different option swaps it (pulls the caller from every option's `votes` first, then pushes to the chosen one) rather than double-counting; live-verified end to end (initial vote, a revote that correctly moved the count, a second independent user's own vote, and a rejected out-of-range `optionIndex`).

**Mobile**: `types/index.ts` gained `"official"|"poll"` on `ShareType`, `OfficialContentCategory`, `PollOption`, and the new `Share` fields; `FeedUserRef.isOfficial` drives a new checkmark-circle badge in `ShareCard.tsx`'s `usernameRow` (same slot pattern as the existing tier diamond). `typeMeta()` gained an `official` case (icon/label keyed off `officialCategory` via a new `OFFICIAL_CATEGORY_META` table) and a `poll` case. Two new render blocks in `ShareCard.tsx`'s shared return: a text(+optional poster) box for `official` posts reusing the `analysisBox`/`shareBox` inner-box convention, and a genuinely new interactive block for `poll` — pre-vote tappable option buttons, post-vote animated (`Animated.Value` per option, `Easing.out(Easing.quad)`, 400ms) percentage-fill bars with the caller's own choice checkmarked, local optimistic state (mirrors the `share` prop, rolled back on a failed `voteOnPoll` call) rather than lifting into `SharesFeedSection`'s own list state. New `voteOnPoll()` in `shareService.ts` / `SHARES.VOTE` route constant. New locale keys (Trivia/Tip/Highlight/On This Day/Stats/Announcement/Poll labels + `vote_count`/`vote_count_plural`) added across all 12 locales via the same anchor-based insertion script convention used all session.

Verified: `node --check` on every new/edited backend file; a full live run of `postOfficialContent()` against the real dev DB for all 7 categories (each produced a real `Share` doc with the expected shape); `getShareFeed`/`getUserShares` both confirmed to surface `officialCategory`/`officialText`/`pollData`/`userVoteIndex`/`user.isOfficial` correctly, per-user, with no raw voter list ever leaked; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle (via `expo-router/entry.bundle`, not the bare `index.bundle` path — this project's `main` is `"expo-router/entry"`, and the wrong path silently returns a tiny error-JSON "bundle" instead of failing loudly) confirmed `officialBox`/`pollBox`/`checkmark-circle`/`voteOnPoll`/`officialCategory`/`pollData`/`userVoteIndex` all present in the compiled output.

**Same-day follow-up: the score-boost approach didn't actually make official posts visible in practice, reported by the user testing on-device.** `FEED_OFFICIAL_BOOST=6` was a flat addition to the same score every organic post competes on, but a brand-new official post starts at 0 likes/0 follows like anyone else's — it only ever scored ≈6 (live-confirmed via a direct aggregation dump), which plenty of already-liked seeded posts comfortably beat. "Boost the score" and "always show up regardless of popularity" are actually two different asks, and this session initially built the former when the user meant the latter. Fixed by pulling official posts (`isOfficialPost:true`) **out of the ranked competition entirely**: `getShareFeed`'s organic query now explicitly excludes them (`$match: { isOfficialPost: { $ne: true } }`), and the response reserves one guaranteed slot per page (`OFFICIAL_SLOT_INDEX = 2`, i.e. always the 3rd item) for a rotating pick — `(page-1) % officialCount` through all official posts in `createdAt desc` order, so scrolling further surfaces a *different* official post each page rather than repeating the same one. Only applied for `scope:"all"`; `scope:"following"` stays exactly what it says — nobody's own official-account follow relationship, so no official posts there. `organicLimit`/`organicTotal`/`hasMore` are all computed against the official-excluded query so a requested `limit` still returns exactly that many total items. The shared per-item hydration (author/viewer lookups, `liked`, poll vote-count/`userVoteIndex` shaping, the final `$project`) was extracted into `shareHydrationStages(userId)` so the organic query and the one official-post query can never drift on shape — no mobile changes needed, since the client just renders whatever order the backend returns. Live-verified: page 1 now always contains a `cinephix`-authored item at index 2, page 2 contains a *different* official post at the same index, and `scope=following` contains none.

**Same-day, second follow-up: 4 more issues reported from continued on-device testing.**

1. **Still too rare.** The one-guaranteed-slot-per-page version above was itself replaced after the user reported it as "still very rare" in practice — the actual ask was the *first post of the whole feed* always being official, then another one every 3-4 organic posts after that (much denser than 1-per-20). Rewrote `getShareFeed` around `officialSlotPositions(beforeIndex)` — a pure, stateless function computing every official-slot ABSOLUTE index across the whole (infinite-scroll) feed: position 0 is always a slot, then each next slot sits `1 + gap` positions later, `gap` alternating 3/4 via a small deterministic hash (`stableHash`, Knuth multiplicative) rather than true per-request randomness — real randomness would make the same page's arrangement shift on every refetch, which reads as a bug, not variety. Per page: compute which absolute positions in `[pageStart, pageEnd)` are slots, fetch exactly `limit - slotCount` organic items (skip/limit adjusted for however many slots preceded this page), fetch the pool's official post ids once and pick each slot's content via a *second*, differently-mixed hash of the slot's own global sequence number (so slot timing and slot content choice don't correlate), then weave both back together at their exact reserved positions. Live-verified across two pages: index 0 is always official, then official posts land every 3-5 organic posts continuously across the page boundary, `hasMore`/pagination stay consistent, and `scope=following` still shows none.
2. **Official posts looked like a Premium user's (gold border, tier diamond) — explicitly unwanted for now** ("çerçeve elmas vs olmasın... başka bişey düşünücez ona"). The seed account had been given `accountTier:"premium"` purely to reuse the existing gold-border post styling — the user rejected that outright: the official account isn't a paid tier and shouldn't visually read as one. Fixed by changing it to `accountTier:"free"` (both the live DB doc and `scripts/seedOfficialAccount.js`'s own default for future reseeds) — `ShareCard.tsx` needed no changes at all, since `isPremium`/`tierMark` already key off `accountTier` alone; the checkmark-circle `isOfficial` badge (a separate, intentionally-kept signal) still shows. A dedicated official-account visual treatment is left for a future round, by explicit agreement — "şimidlik bişey olmasın."
3. **All official content was hard-coded Turkish, bypassing i18n entirely** ("dili neden türkçe. dil çevirisine sok bunu ve default dili ingilizce olsun"). The app's own `fallbackLng` (`src/i18n/index.ts`) was already `"en"` — the Turkish text was purely the *content itself* (the 150-item trivia pool, tips, polls, announcements, and the dynamically-generated highlight/on-this-day/stats/DB-native-trivia template strings in `officialContentService.js`), authored in Turkish earlier in this session and never routed through the translation system. Rewrote the entire pool and every dynamic template string in English (the app's own default/source-of-truth language) — old Turkish `OfficialContent`/`OfficialContentLapState` docs and the earlier Turkish test `Share` posts were deleted from the dev DB and re-seeded fresh via `scripts/seedOfficialContent.js`. Caught and fixed a real grammar bug along the way ("X is a American production") by adding a small `articleFor(word)` helper (vowel-letter check) instead of a hardcoded "a". **Scope note, by design, not an oversight**: this makes English the one source-of-truth language for this specific auto-generated content pool — it does NOT translate these 205+ items across all 12 locales (matching the same "kept English-only by agreement" precedent already set for the static legal pages, §3) — a non-English viewer would see this content in English regardless of their own app language setting. Flagged here explicitly in case full localization of this pool is wanted later; not requested this round.
4. **The poll's post-vote results view — reported as "seems to close instead of showing results, not like Insta."** Deep investigation (backend curl-verified working correctly both on localhost and through the real ngrok tunnel URL the app itself uses; client source AND the actual compiled Metro bundle both re-read and confirmed logically correct) found no definitive reproducible bug in the vote/render logic itself — the most likely real-world explanation is a transient failure during a backend nodemon restart mid-test (an in-flight vote request landing exactly during a ~1-2s server restart window would fail, triggering the existing rollback-to-pre-vote path, which *would* look exactly like "results didn't come, options closed back up"). Regardless of root cause, hardened the implementation as a genuine simplification: removed the per-option `Animated.Value` ref-array + `interpolate()` pattern entirely (a real category of subtle RN bugs when an array of refs has to stay in sync with changing state) in favor of `LayoutAnimation.configureNext(...)` (called before each of the three state transitions: optimistic vote, server-confirmed vote, and rollback) plus a plain `View` with a directly-computed `width: \`${percent}%\`` — RN's own native layout-animation system handles the smooth grow/shrink transition instead of hand-rolled per-value animation bookkeeping. Fewer moving parts, same visual effect, and if the original symptom really was restart-timing-related, this also happens to no longer be in the blast radius at all.

**Resolution, confirmed by the user after retesting: the poll "closing" symptom was a theme/contrast issue, not a code bug** — "tema değiştirmem gerekiyomuş artık görüyorum." The post-vote track's `colors.base300` background and the low-opacity (`0.28`) `colors.primary` fill likely read as near-invisible against whatever theme was active, which — combined with the *text* still being technically present but easy to miss at a glance — plausibly explained the original "nothing shows" report all along. No further poll-rendering-logic changes needed beyond the LayoutAnimation simplification above, which stays as a genuine simplification regardless.

**Same-day, third follow-up: poster-backed poll idea explored, then descoped — thinner result bars and a "who voted" avatar preview shipped instead.** The user first asked about showing 5 movie/show posters side by side per poll option; after this session flagged the real dependency (today's pool options are plain strings, not linked to actual Movie/Series documents — showing real posters would need title-matching each option against the DB, a nontrivial follow-up), the user opted to keep options as plain text for now. Two concrete asks landed instead: **(1) thinner bars** — `pollOptionButton`/`pollResultTrack` padding reduced (`paddingVertical` 10→7, `borderRadius` 10→8), `pollOptionsCol`'s own gap tightened (8→6), for a visibly slimmer stack; **(2) a "who voted" avatar preview at the end of each result bar**, same `StackedAvatars` component and visual language `viewRow`'s own "viewed by" indicator already uses elsewhere in this same file. Backend: `shareHydrationStages` (shared by `getShareFeed`'s organic AND official-slot queries) now flattens the first 5 voter ids across every option into one array (`_pollTopVoterIds`), resolves them via a single **pipeline-form** `$lookup` restricted to `{_id, username, profile_pic_url}` only (a plain localField/foreignField `$lookup` would have joined full user documents — password hash included — a real data-leak risk for what's ultimately a public vote-preview, not an authenticated profile fetch), then re-maps each option's own `topVoters` by matching ids back out of that small hydrated set. `voteOnPoll`'s direct POST response and `getUserShares`'s own independent poll-shaping path both got the equivalent treatment (plain `User.find` batched across the whole vote/page respectively, not a full aggregation, since both already hold a hydrated document/lean array to work from) — three separate code paths that must never drift on this shape, same reasoning `shareHydrationStages`' own extraction already documents. Live-verified: two different users voting on the same poll produced correct, distinct `topVoters` arrays under their respective options across all three endpoints (`GET /shares/feed`, the vote response itself, and implicitly `getUserShares`'s shared logic).

**Same-day, fourth follow-up: real scroll-corruption bug — "sayfa saçmalamaya başlıyor, yukarı aşağı zıplıyor."** Root-caused by writing a small script to fetch 10 consecutive feed pages and diff every returned `_id` against every other — found genuine duplicates: the official-post rotation's own content-selection logic (`getShareFeed`, previous round) picked which official post filled a given slot via `hash(globalSlotNumber) % officialCount`, which with a SMALL official pool (single digits during this session's own testing) can genuinely map two *different* slot numbers to the SAME underlying post well within one scroll session — first fix attempt (switching to a straight `globalSlotNumber % officialCount` sequential rotation, guaranteeing no repeat *within* one lap) reduced but didn't eliminate this, since a lap through a 9-item pool completes almost immediately at "one official post every 3-4 items." The real, complete fix: the SAME official `Share._id` legitimately recurring across a long scroll session isn't actually a bug to prevent (it's inherent once you've scrolled past a full lap of however large the pool currently is — the pool will hold hundreds of items in production, but nothing should assume that), it's a **duplicate React key** waiting to happen, since `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s `FlatList` accumulates every fetched page into one array keyed by `share._id` alone. Fixed at the actual point of failure: `keyExtractor` now suffixes with the row's own array `index` (`` `${row.share._id}-${index}` ``) — safe here specifically because `items` only ever grows via `loadMore`'s append or gets wholesale-replaced by `load`/`onRefresh`, never reordered or spliced in place, so a row's index is exactly as stable as its `_id`. Live-verified: fetched 10 consecutive pages post-fix and confirmed the SAME underlying content can still legitimately repeat (expected, pool-size-dependent) but no longer produces a duplicate FlatList key, which is what was actually causing the reported jumping.

**Same-day, fifth follow-up: trivia pool doubled to 300, and both DB-native templates gained real poster support.** Confirmed via `collStats` that the entire 205-item pool only occupied ~92KB on disk — storage was never actually a constraint, so growing it was free. Authored 150 more trivia facts across 10 new subcategories (awards beyond the Oscars, sequels/remakes, streaming-era records, voice acting/dubbing, stunt work, soundtracks, international/anime cinema, famous troubled productions, child actors, film preservation) — 300 total, all verified unique, no duplicates against the original 150. At ~1 trivia post/day this roughly doubles the lap length past a year, comfortably outrunning any practical "seen this before" concern; the existing oldest-30-retirement mechanism (still dormant — no "pending" replacement docs exist yet) is untouched.

**Poster support for the 2 DB-native templates**: origin-country trivia already had it for free (it was always single-title, reusing the generic `contentId`/`contentType`/`contentData` fields `official`-type posts already support). Same-day-release trivia references TWO titles at once, so it needed a new `Share.officialContentItems` field — an array of `{contentId, contentType, contentData}` (vs. the existing fields' single-item shape) — populated only for this one template, and rendered in `ShareCard.tsx`'s `officialBox` as two posters side by side (each its own nested `Pressable`, same "inner tap wins over the box's own double-tap handler" pattern the single-poster row already used) above the fact text.

**Two real bugs caught while wiring this up, neither hypothetical:** (1) Switching the same-day-release aggregation from `$addToSet` on plain title strings to `$push`-ing `{id, title, poster_path}` objects turned a query that grups the ENTIRE 578k-movie collection by `release_date` into one that exceeded MongoDB's `$group` memory limit — confirmed live, and confirmed that even `.allowDiskUse(true)` didn't help (grouping every document in a collection this size is simply too much regardless). Fixed by `$sample`-ing a bounded 8000-document random subset *before* grouping, capping memory completely independent of collection size — the trade-off (a same-day coincidence might not always be found in a bounded sample) is fine since this template is already only rolled 25% of the time with a graceful pool fallback on `null`. (2) The very first test hit revealed a real data-quality trap: `2000-01-01` alone matched 36 movies in one 8000-doc sample — real release dates never cluster that hard, a dead giveaway of an "unknown date" fallback value in the underlying TMDB-sourced data, not a genuine coincidence. Excluded a short list of known placeholder dates (`1970-01-01`, `1900-01-01`, `1901-01-01`, `2000-01-01`) and additionally capped matched-group size at 6 as a defensive catch-all against any other undiscovered placeholder values, so this template can never present a data artifact as a real fact. Live-verified across 8 consecutive runs post-fix: every match was a small (2-3 title), plausible, real coincidence with genuine posters on both sides.

**Same-day, immediate reversal: poster support removed again.** Not a data-load concern (this session had already confirmed the whole pool costs ~92KB) — the user simply preferred every trivia post staying visually consistent as plain text, same as the rest. Reverted `officialContentService.js`'s `generateSameDayReleaseTrivia` back to `$addToSet`-ing plain title strings (no `poster_path`, no per-item ids), removed `Share.officialContentItems` entirely from the schema and `shareHydrationStages`' own `$project`, and removed the dual-poster render branch + `officialDualPosterRow` style from `ShareCard.tsx`. The two real fixes discovered while building the poster version — bounding the aggregation to a random 8000-doc sample before grouping, and excluding known placeholder release dates — were kept, since both are genuine correctness/performance issues independent of whether a poster is ever shown.

**Also from this point on**: the user gave standing approval to proceed without asking for confirmation on this feature's ongoing implementation work ("her seferinde yes'e basmak yorucu, hepsine izin veriyorum") — subsequent rounds on this feature skip the usual pause-for-confirmation step for routine code changes.

**Same-day, seventh follow-up: tip posts can now link one word to a real in-app screen.** Same idea/helper the recommendation type's own "Watchlist" word already used (`renderRecommendMessage`), generalized to the official-tip type. `OfficialContent` (pool) and `Share` (posted docs) both gained optional `linkWord`/`linkHref` (`officialLinkWord`/`officialLinkHref` on `Share`, to disambiguate from the pool's own field names) — populated only when the pooled tip doc has them, most don't. Mapped all 25 existing tips against the app's REAL current routes (verified via a dedicated Explore pass reading actual screen files, not assumed) — 18 of 25 got a real link, 7 stayed deliberately plain where no single good destination exists (visibility toggle has no UI at all yet; a few tips are inherently generic — "someone's profile," "a title's detail page" — with no single concrete target a broadcast post could point to).

Four small, precedented navigation additions were needed to make several of these links land accurately instead of approximately, none of which existed before: (1) `app/(app)/profile/index.tsx` + `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx` gained `?tab=` support (`favorites`/`cinegraph`/`analyses`/`sharings`) — mirrors `app/user/[id]/index.tsx`'s own `initialCategory` pattern for the public-profile equivalent exactly, previously never wired to the *own*-profile screen; (2) `home/index.tsx` gained `?outerTab=discover` to force-land on Keşfet (previously only `?podiumCategory=` existed, which forces the *other* tab); (3) `home/index.tsx` → `SharesFeedSection.tsx` gained `?scope=following` → `initialScope` prop (mirrors `jumpToPodiumCategory`'s own one-shot-seed threading); (4) `socials/index.tsx` gained `?tab=communities` to land on Community instead of always defaulting to Messages. `seedOfficialContent.js`'s tip-seeding loop was rewritten from `insertIfMissing` (skip-if-present) to a real `updateOne(...,{upsert:true})` specifically so re-running it also backfills `linkWord`/`linkHref` onto the 25 tip docs that already existed in the dev DB from earlier rounds, without a separate one-off migration script.

**One more real bug caught live, unrelated to links directly:** a `limit=1` feed request (used while spot-checking the link fields) crashed with `"the limit must be positive"` — MongoDB's `$limit` stage hard-rejects `0`, and the official-slot math (previous round) can legitimately compute `organicCountThisPage = 0` for a small enough `limit` (every position in a 1-item page is a reserved official slot). Fixed by skipping the organic aggregate entirely (same `Promise.resolve([])` short-circuit pattern the official query itself already used) whenever there's nothing organic to fetch, rather than trying to `$limit: 0` it away. Live-verified: `limit=1` and `limit=20` both succeed now, `officialLinkWord`/`officialLinkHref` confirmed flowing correctly through `GET /shares/feed` end to end.

**Same-day, eighth follow-up: link mechanism generalized to multiple links per post, plus a CineMatch→Sync rename.** Two direct asks: (1) the app renamed CineMatch to "Sync" a while back (`app/(app)/match/_layout.tsx`'s own title) — the tip #6 text/link and one announcement still said "CineMatch," both fixed (old-worded pool docs deleted, new ones re-seeded, since they're matched by exact text and a text change doesn't update-in-place). (2) Since poster support was dropped from trivia's DB-native templates last round, the user asked for the lighter-weight substitute instead: link the movie/series **name itself** to its content detail page — "database'i zorlamıyorsa" (if it doesn't strain the database), which it doesn't (same id already resolved during generation, no extra query).

This needed generalizing beyond a single link: same-day-release trivia names TWO titles, each needing its own link. `Share.officialLinkWord`/`officialLinkHref` (singular, previous round) were replaced with `officialLinks: [{word, href, contentId, contentType}]` — tips still carry one item with `href` (an absolute route); trivia's title-referencing templates carry one or two items with `contentId`/`contentType` instead, resolved client-side against whichever stack (`basePath`) the card is rendered in (same pattern the existing single-item contentId/contentType fields' own `goToContent` already uses) rather than a hardcoded absolute path. `ShareCard.tsx` gained `renderTextWithLinks(text, links, style)` — a general N-link version of the existing single-link `renderRecommendMessage` (left untouched; its own call site, the recommendation type's "Watchlist" word, works fine as-is) — matching each word case-insensitively, first occurrence, skipping any accidental overlap. `generateSameDayReleaseTrivia` went back to fetching each title's real `_id` (dropped when posters were removed, needed again for the link) — cheap enough this time (just an id alongside the title, not a poster_path string) that the earlier $sample-bounding fix alone keeps it safe, no new memory concern. `generateOriginCountryTrivia` (which already had a poster via the pre-existing generic contentData mechanism — never part of the poster back-and-forth) now ALSO explicitly links the title word in the body text, on top of the poster/box already being tappable — a visible affordance being more discoverable than an invisible whole-box tap, same reasoning tip links exist for at all.

**Same-day, ninth follow-up: a real "posts invisible on the official account's own profile" bug found and fixed, plus a batch of polish and two real safety gaps closed.**

**Root cause of the "can't see them on cinephix's profile" report**: `src/components/profile/ShareGridTile.tsx` — the square grid used by Profile's own "Your Sharings" tab (a DIFFERENT, lighter component than `ShareCard.tsx` used in the main feed) — had a hardcoded 3-way if-chain (`recommendation` → `analysis` → an implicit `review` catch-all reading `share.reviewText`) that predates this whole feature. `"official"` and `"poll"` posts fell into that catch-all, found `reviewText` undefined, and rendered as a blank tile with only the corner type-badge visible — not missing, just invisible. Converted to a proper `switch` with explicit `official` (shows `officialText`), `poll` (shows the question), and `list` (shows the list name — same bug, fixed as a freebie) cases. Also found, while in there: the checkmark `isOfficial` badge was only ever wired into the recommendation-branch's header, never the shared header every other type (including every official post) actually renders through — fixed by adding it there too.

**Tip links reverted (again) — trivia keeps them, tips don't.** The user reconsidered after seeing both in practice: tip links stay removed (back to `TIPS` as plain strings in `seedOfficialContent.js`, `OfficialContent`'s stray `linkWord`/`linkHref` `$unset` from existing tip docs), trivia's two DB-native templates keep theirs.

**Cosmetic follow-ups on the official account's own presentation**: the type-chip badge (Trivia/Tip/Poll/...) moved back below the username (an inline-next-to-username version was tried immediately before this round and reverted just as fast); the "CINEPHIX" display name is now italic (`fonts.boldItalic`, a new `DMSans_700Bold_Italic` variant added to `app/_layout.tsx`'s `useFonts` call and `theme/typography.ts`'s `fonts` map — didn't exist before, the app had never needed a bold-italic weight); the checkmark badge recolored from `colors.info` to `colors.primary` so it stays "on-brand" and coordinates with the avatar gradient across every theme instead of a fixed info-blue that could clash with some palettes; Trivia and Tip post bodies specifically (not Highlight/On This Day/Stats/Announcement) now render in that same bold-italic weight, direct ask, to read as more distinct/editorial.

**Two real safety gaps closed, both explicitly requested checks**: (1) **podium exclusion** — `getPeopleThreePodiums` (`feedController.js`) now explicitly excludes `isOfficial:true` from all 5 people-podium rankings (Most Followed/Watched excluded directly via a `$match` on `User`'s own `isOfficial` field; Most Reviewed/Liked/Top Recommenders resolve the official account's `_id` once and exclude by author id, since `Review`/`Share` don't carry an `isOfficial` field of their own) — live-verified the official account appears in none of them.
