(2) **reserved username** — `registerUser` and the username-change path inside `updateUserBio` (both `userController.js`) now reject the exact name "cinephix" under any case/diacritic/punctuation disguise via a new `isReservedUsername()` helper: NFKD-normalizes, strips combining marks (so a Turkish dotted "İ", which naively lowercases to "i" plus a stray combining dot rather than a clean "i", is still caught), lowercases, strips non-alphanumerics, then compares for an EXACT match — deliberately not a substring block, so real pre-existing accounts like "cinephix_6gnn" and "cinephix_online_test" aren't affected by the rule, only the bare reserved word itself is off-limits. Live-verified: "CİNEPHİX" and "cine-phix" both rejected, a normal username still registers fine. Leetspeak substitutions (e.g. "c1nephix") are explicitly out of scope — not what was asked, no precedent for that elsewhere in this app's validation.

**Same-day, tenth follow-up: category-1 (trivia) consistency pass — no poster on the origin-country template either, plus a rotating opener.** Discussed as an explicit design tradeoff first (exploratory question, held for confirmation before touching code, per this session's own established rhythm): origin-country trivia already had a poster (via the pre-existing generic `contentData`) while every other trivia post — the 300-item pool, same-day-release — was plain text; the two options were drop the poster (keep the link) or keep the poster (drop the link). **Same-day, fifteenth follow-up: real poll first-vote render-freeze bug fixed by removing `LayoutAnimation`.** Reported consistently reproducible: on a poll's first-ever vote, the tapped option button visually froze in its dark/pressed state instead of switching to the result-bar view — the vote was correctly recorded server-side the whole time (a full Expo reload always revealed the right result), so this was a pure client repaint failure, not a data/network bug, and distinct from the earlier-diagnosed theme/contrast issue (§ twelfth-round entry above) despite superficially similar "results don't show" phrasing. Root cause: `LayoutAnimation.configureNext(...)` (added several rounds back, § fourth-follow-up-adjacent entry, as a simplification replacing a per-option `Animated.Value`/`interpolate` array) combined with a subsequently percentage-width-changing view is a known React Native bug class — the JS state updates correctly but the native view doesn't repaint until an unrelated later layout pass forces it, which is exactly what a reload does. Fixed by removing `LayoutAnimation` (and the now-unused `Platform`/`UIManager` imports plus the module-level Android opt-in block) from `ShareCard.tsx` entirely — `handleVote`'s three state-setting paths (optimistic vote, server-confirmed vote, rollback) now apply as an instant snap instead of an eased transition, trading a small amount of animation smoothness for reliability. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) and a fresh Metro bundle: extracted `handleVote`'s own compiled body and confirmed no `LayoutAnimation` call sites remain in it (the raw `grep -c "LayoutAnimation"` count of 216 across the full bundle is expected — React Native's own bundled internals reference the module throughout a 13MB+ app bundle regardless of any one screen's usage).

No content-pool or generator changes — `generateStats()` was already fully dynamic (live `countDocuments` across User/Rating/Review/Share, no pool). Since `insertIfMissing`/pool matching is by exact text, the 3 old dash-bearing pool docs (and the lap state, to force a clean rebuild) were explicitly deleted before re-running `seedOfficialContent.js`, rather than left as stale duplicates alongside the rewritten versions. Live-verified with 2 fresh posts, both dash-free.

**Same-day, eighteenth follow-up: poll first-vote freeze bug — real second cause found and fixed (LayoutAnimation removal alone wasn't sufficient).** The user retested after the sixteenth-round `LayoutAnimation` removal (a genuinely correct fix in its own right, kept) and reported the exact same freeze still happening. Re-diagnosed from scratch: `pollOptions.map()`'s button-mode and result-mode `Pressable` elements shared the same `key={i}` across the vote transition, so React reused the SAME underlying native `Pressable` instance and just swapped its style/children in place rather than mounting a new one — and that instance is the one that was *just pressed*, i.e. still mid-touch on Android's native responder chain at the exact moment its style flips from `pollOptionButton` to `pollResultTrack`. That's a known category of Android Pressable bug: the native ripple/pressed-state drawable can get stuck rendering its dark pressed look on a reused view whose props changed while a touch was still resolving, and only a full remount (which a reload forces for the whole tree) clears it. Fixed by splitting the key by mode (`` `${i}-btn` `` vs `` `${i}-result` ``) so the button->result switch always mounts a brand-new `Pressable` with no stale native touch state to inherit, instead of mutating the pressed one. (A revote, result-mode to a different result-mode option, keeps the same `-result` keys for both — not the risky transition, since that path was never the one reported broken.) Verified via `tsc --noEmit` clean and a fresh Metro bundle grep confirming the new key strings compiled in.

**H. Real, separately-diagnosed bug: the star-rating input's half-star fill would leave stale, half-updated visuals mid-drag** (`StarRatingInput.tsx`) — reported with an exact repro: rating 2.5→3.5 by tapping star 4's first half left star 3's own second half wrongly unfilled while only star 4's first half updated, instead of the whole row recomputing cleanly. Same underlying bug class as the poll-vote freeze fixed earlier this session: each star's `fill` (full/half/empty) is correctly recomputed fresh every render from `displayValue`, but the `<View key={i}>` wrapping each `<Star>` shared one key across every fill state, so React reused (restyled in place) the same native SVG view rather than mounting a fresh one — and `react-native-svg`'s `<ClipPath>`/`<Rect>` can leave a stale clip painted when only the Rect's own `width` prop changes on a reused view. Fixed the same way: `key={`${i}-${fill}`}` instead of `key={i}` forces a genuinely new native view on every fill-state change, guaranteeing no stale paint carries over.

New `GET /content/:type/:id/similar` (`contentStatsRoute.js`) ranks by genre overlap against a popularity-sorted, vote-count-floored, bounded (500-doc) candidate pool — the strongest signal actually available for free, same bounding discipline this app's other large-collection queries already use. 8 new route wrapper files (one per stack) + `Stack.Screen` entries, same established thin-wrapper pattern every other content sub-page in this app uses.

**Favorites "Favorites" stat page — a real inconsistency fixed.** It was the only one of Content Detail's 4 stat pages (Watched/Reviews/Favorites/Lists) not built as a sentence-style `ActivityRow` card — a plain avatar+username row instead, because `favoriteMovies`/`favoriteSeries` genuinely have no per-item timestamp. Real fix: `GET .../favorited-by` now enriches each item with `createdAt` from `FavoriteEvent` (the network Activity feed's own append-only favorite log) wherever a matching entry exists — accurate for anyone who favorited after that log started, `null` (rendered as simply no time-ago label, not a fake one) for anyone who favorited before it existed. `ActivityEvent`'s `favorited.createdAt` is optional app-wide now for this reason; `ContentFavoritedSection.tsx` rebuilt to construct real events and reuse `ActivityRow`.

**Real bug found and fixed while building "Similar"/"What to Watch": `getRecommendations` (feedController.js) had never actually worked.** CineGraph entries are keyed by genre *name* (`ratingController.js`'s own `updateCineGraph` stores them that way), but this endpoint treated the raw key as if it already were the numeric TMDB id Movie/Series documents store — `Number("Drama")` is `NaN`, so `genre_ids: { $in: topGenreIds } }` could never match a single real document, and the endpoint silently always returned an empty list. Fixed with real per-type reverse maps (`MOVIE_GENRE_NAME_TO_ID`/`SERIES_GENRE_NAME_TO_ID`, built from the existing `MOVIE_GENRE_MAP`/`SERIES_GENRE_MAP`) — movie and series genre ids are also now kept separate (the same name can map to a different numeric id per type, e.g. movie "Action"=28 vs series "Action & Adventure"=10759, so a single shared list was wrong for whichever type didn't originate a given id). Live-verified: real, correctly genre-matched, already-excludes-watched recommendations now come back with `hasPersonalization:true`.

**Cinephix's own feed distribution — a real fixed category sequence, not a flat rotation.** The first post on the page is always official and specifically a poll (was: whichever official post happened to be next in a flat chronological rotation). `getShareFeed`'s official-slot gap widened to 3-5 (was 3-4, `OFFICIAL_GAP_SPREAD` 2→3). New `OFFICIAL_CATEGORY_SEQUENCE` (`shareController.js`) — an 8-step repeating cycle (poll → trivia from the 300-pool → trivia from the same-release-date live template → a binary "this or that" poll → on-this-day → highlight → tip → stats) — each official Share doc is classified into one of these buckets from its own already-persisted shape (`classifyOfficialDoc`: poll option count for binary vs. not, `officialLinks` count for same-release-date trivia vs. everything-else trivia, `officialCategory` for the rest — no new field needed), bucketed, and each slot picks from its own category's bucket via a per-category occurrence counter (not the slot's own global number) — that's what makes the very first poll slot land on the single most recent poll while a later poll slot rotates to the next one instead of repeating it. Live-verified end to end: fetched a real page and confirmed positions 0/4/10/14 were exactly poll→trivia_pool→trivia_same_release→poll_binary, in that order.

**Plus/Premium consistency, actually fixed this time — two real bugs, not one.** (1) `ShareCard.tsx`'s own SECOND username render site (the shared header every non-recommendation post type — review/list/analysis/official/poll — actually renders through) was still the old plain `<Text>`, never updated to `usernameEl` (the gradient-fill version) when that was first built — only the recommendation-type branch's copy ever got it, because the original `replace_all` edit's `old_string` didn't exactly match both call sites' whitespace. Fixed by flipping which element is absolute: the measuring Text now sits in normal flow (reserving the correct width immediately, same font/size/text as what's being measured) and the SVG is the one absolutely positioned on top of it. `SuggestedUsersBox.tsx` (Shares' own suggested-users cells) gained the same tier frame (`UserAvatar`'s own `tier` prop, was a plain custom avatar) + diamond-before-username treatment everyone else already had.

**New feature, first badge category: genre achievement badges, real backend + a new Profile tab.** First slice of a larger planned badge system (8 categories scoped/discussed, this one built end to end as the trial round) — 8 genres (Action/Comedy/Drama/Horror/Romance/Thriller/Sci-Fi/Documentary), each with a Devotee (15+ rated titles) and Master (40+) tier, art supplied by the user (IconScout 3D badge packs, 512×512 PNG, now in `mobile/assets/badges/genres/`).

**Backend — new `badgeController.js`/`badgeRoute.js`, mounted at `/api/badges`.** `GET /api/badges/genres` computes real per-genre RATED-title counts fresh from `Rating` + `Movie/Series.genre_ids` at read time — reusing `tallyGenres` (`utils/analysisMath.js`), the exact same shared helper `getProfileAnalysis`'s own `genreBreakdown` card already uses, so a badge's count and the Genre Breakdown chart's own count for the same genre can never quietly disagree. Deliberately NOT read from `User.movieCineGraph`/`seriesCineGraph` — `getUserGenreDetail`'s own comment already flags those fields as having known drift bugs from the TV Time/Letterboxd import and log-revert paths, which would have shown a wrong badge count/tier with no way for the user to tell. `GENRE_BADGES` maps each unified badge to a movie-genre-name list and a series-genre-name list (e.g. `action` = movie `"Action"` + series `"Action & Adventure"`, same movie/series genre-name drift `feedController.js`'s own `getRecommendations` fix had to account for) — Horror/Romance/Thriller are movie-only badges by nature of the data, TMDB's own series genre taxonomy has no equivalent genre for any of those three. Live-verified against both named test accounts: Zachary's real Drama count (37) matches exactly what Profile Analysis's own genreBreakdown already reported for him earlier this session — direct cross-check that the new endpoint and the existing analysis feature agree on the same ground truth.

**Mobile — new "Rozetler" tab on Profile, 5th alongside Sharings/Favorites/CineGraph/Analyses.** `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx`'s `Category` union gained `"badges"` (also added to `profile/index.tsx`'s own `VALID_CATEGORIES` deep-link array); new `ProfileBadgesTab.tsx` self-fetches via a new `badgeService.ts`, same "owns its own fetch, nothing else in Profile needs this data" pattern `ProfileAnalysesTab.tsx` already uses. Two tiles per genre (Devotee + Master), not one "best tier" tile — same reasoning real trophy systems (Xbox/PlayStation) use: a higher tier earned doesn't retire the lower one from view. **Locked-tile visual, direct ask**: a real flat gray silhouette of the SAME artwork that keeps its exact shape/edges, not a placeholder or a second grayscale asset — done with RN's own built-in `Image` `tintColor` style (recolors every non-transparent pixel to one flat color, leaves the alpha channel/silhouette exactly as the PNG drew it), zero new image-processing dependency. A small lock badge + a live `{{count}} / {{threshold}}` progress caption sit under each locked tile — the "what could this be" curiosity the user was going for, paired with a concrete, actionable path to unlock it rather than a totally opaque mystery. New `GenreBadge`/`GenreBadgesResponse` types, new `mobile/src/data/genreBadgeDefinitions.ts` (static label + `require()` asset table, genre names deliberately left untranslated — same convention every other genre label in this app already follows). New `"Devotee"`/`"Master"`/`"Unlocked"`/the intro sentence translated across all 12 locales.

**Known simplification, not yet built**: badge state is fully live-computed on every fetch, nothing is persisted as "earned" — if a user's rated count in a genre ever dropped back under a threshold (removing ratings), that badge would show locked again rather than staying permanently unlocked. Acceptable for this trial; a real "earned" ledger (with an award timestamp, a notification moment, etc.) is a deliberate next step once more categories are built out, not an oversight here. Streak/volume/social/sync/loyalty/seasonal badges from the original 8-category plan are not built yet — this round was genre only, per direct ask ("deneme olarak sadece tür badgelerini yapalım").

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; full backend `node --check` sweep clean; fresh Metro bundle fetched and grepped for `ProfileBadgesTab`/`getGenreBadges`/`GENRE_BADGE_DEFINITIONS` and the actual bundled asset references (`badge_genre_action_devotee`, `badge_genre_horror_master`) — all present, confirming Metro resolved every `require()` path correctly, not just that the source compiled.

**Same-day follow-up: badges tab compacted into a flat 4-across grid — no more per-genre grouping, full name per tile.** Direct ask: smaller tiles, drop the genre-heading + two-tile-row structure, lay all 16 devotee/master tiles out flat (4 per row, same `(screenWidth - padding*2 - gap*(columns-1))/columns` sizing math `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx`'s own `FAVORITES_COLUMNS` calc already uses), and label each tile with its full name ("Action Devotee") instead of a genre heading + a short "Devotee"/"Master" tier label underneath. `tiles` is now one flat array (`GENRE_BADGE_DEFINITIONS.flatMap`, 2 entries per genre) instead of one array rendered as 8 two-tile rows. Image shrunk 72→44px, tile padding/lock-badge/type scale all scaled down to match; the earned state's own caption is now a small checkmark icon instead of an "Unlocked" text label — kept the locked state's `{{count}}/{{threshold}}` text as-is, dropping the separate "15+"/"40+" threshold line since the label now already says the tier by name. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetched and grepped for `checkIcon`/`COLUMNS`/`GRID_GAP` (present) and `genreSection`/`tierRow`/`tierThreshold` (fully gone).

**Same-day follow-up: tap-to-open badge detail popup, the checkmark/progress-caption both removed from the grid tile, and a Credits screen for IconScout's own attribution requirement.**

- **Grid tile simplified further**: the earned-state checkmark icon and the locked-state `{{count}}/{{threshold}}` caption are both gone — direct ask, "obtained olan zaten renkli görünüyor" (full color already reads as earned; the count moved elsewhere rather than being deleted outright).
- **New `BadgeDetailModal.tsx`**: tapping any tile opens a small popup, badge art on the left (still tinted gray if locked — tapping a locked badge is how you find out what it's *for*, not a shortcut to seeing its real colors before actually earning it), title + a real sentence on the right: `"You earned this badge by watching {{count}} {{genre}} titles!"` when earned, `"You've watched {{count}} {{genre}} titles. Watch {{remaining}} more to earn this badge."` when not — both new keys translated across all 12 locales. `ProfileBadgesTab.tsx`'s `tiles` array now carries `genreLabel`/`tierWord` separately (not just the combined grid caption) so the modal can build that sentence.
- **A real entrance animation on the badge itself when the popup opens** (direct ask) — a spring `scale`+`opacity` reveal on the image (RN's own `Animated` API), not Lottie. Asked directly whether Lottie was worth doing (IconScout's own "animated" export is a Lottie JSON per icon): recommended against it for this — `lottie-react-native` would be a new native dependency, and every one of the 16 badges would need a *second* download in Lottie format on top of the PNGs already in hand, for a one-time reveal a spring scale already delivers well. Left as a real option to revisit if a specific future badge needs bespoke motion (a shine sweep, particles) a scale genuinely can't do.
- **New Credits screen** (`app/(app)/profile/credits.tsx`, linked from Settings, `Stack.Screen` added to `profile/_layout.tsx`) — IconScout's license requires each icon's attribution link shown wherever it's used; a small badge tile can't legibly carry "IconName by Author on IconScout," so (same pattern most apps use for Flaticon/Freepik-style requirements) this is one central page listing all of them instead. New `mobile/src/data/iconAttributions.ts` holds the 16 credits the user pasted verbatim (name + icon URL + author + author URL, wording/URLs kept exactly as IconScout's own required snippet — not reworded). Built on the existing `LegalPage.tsx` primitives (`LegalTitle`/`LegalSection`/`LegalParagraph`/`LegalLink`, the last already wrapping `Linking.openURL`) rather than new components, and left hardcoded English like `about.tsx`/`privacy.tsx`/`terms.tsx` already are (this app's own established convention for legal-adjacent static content, not run through `t()`) — only the Settings row label and stack title are translated.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; fresh Metro bundle fetched and grepped for `BadgeDetailModal`/`ICON_ATTRIBUTIONS`/`CreditsScreen` (present), the old `checkIcon`/`progressDone` (fully gone), and two of the pasted attribution URLs (`.../jester-hat`, `.../volcano`) landing in the bundle correctly.

**New feature: a real-time "you earned a badge!" popup (same visual shape as `PodiumNewsModal.tsx`'s own "you made the podium!" card, direct ask), with a Share-to-Media button that posts the badge as a real feed post.**

**Backend — badge-crossing detection lives in the rating flow itself, not a separate poll.** `addOrUpdateRating` (`ratingController.js`) already has everything needed at the exact moment a NEW rating lands (the just-rated content's own genre names, and whether this is a first-time rating vs. a score edit) — since a rating only ever moves a genre's real rated-count up by exactly 1, "did this specific rating just earn a badge" reduces to "does the genre's new total land EXACTLY on a threshold," a new `crossedThresholdTier(count)` export from `badgeController.js` (distinct from the existing `tierFor`, which answers "at or above," the wrong question here — it would refire on every later rating in an already-earned genre). `computeGenreBadgeCounts(userId)` was factored out of `getGenreBadges`'s own handler so this reuses the identical, already-verified-correct computation instead of a second implementation that could drift from it. Scoped to just the badge keys the rated content's own genres actually touch (usually 1-2 of the 8), not a recompute-and-check-all-8 on every single rating. Response shape stays backward compatible — `newlyEarnedBadges` is spread alongside the rating's own fields (`{ ...newRating, newlyEarnedBadges }`), not a differently-shaped envelope; `rateContent()`'s only real caller in the app (`ContentDetailScreen.tsx`, all 3 of its call sites) keeps reading `.value`/`._id` etc. exactly as before, with one new optional array alongside.

**Mobile — a global notifier + one mounted display component, same architecture `ToastContext`/`useToast` already uses app-wide.** New `BadgeEarnedContext.tsx` (`reportEarnedBadges`, a real FIFO queue — one rating can cross more than one genre's threshold at once, e.g. a movie tagged both Horror and Thriller, and each deserves its own full moment rather than being dropped or crammed together) + `BadgeEarnedModal.tsx` (mounted once in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` alongside `PodiumNewsModal`, reads `queue[0]`). `ContentDetailScreen.tsx`'s 3 `rateContent()` call sites (`handleRate`, `toggleWatchlist`'s add branch, `handleOpenFavorites`) all report `result.newlyEarnedBadges` — between them these cover every path a rating can actually get persisted through, including the exact "rated locally, then added to Watched List" deferred-save flow the direct ask described ("15.yi watchedliste eklediğimde... gelsin"). Popup card: spring-animated badge art (same technique `BadgeDetailModal.tsx` already uses), "Congratulations!", "You unlocked the {{genre}} {{tier}} badge!", "Tap to see your badge" (`router.navigate` to `/profile?tab=badges` — not `push`, same reasoning `PodiumNewsModal.tsx`'s own `goToPodium` already documents: reuses the already-mounted Profile screen instead of stacking a fresh, refetching-from-scratch one on top of it), and a nested "Share to Media" Pressable.

**New Share type: `"badge"`.** `Share.js` gained the type plus a `badgeData: {key, tier, count, threshold}` sub-schema; `createShare`'s new branch **re-verifies the badge is actually earned server-side** via `computeGenreBadgeCounts` before allowing the share to be created — unlike `"analysis"` (the user's own already-generated content, nothing persisted to check it against), a genre badge is a checkable fact, so a stale or tampered client claiming a tier it doesn't have gets rejected rather than trusted. `shareHydrationStages`'s own `$project` needed `badgeData: 1` added explicitly (a real, easy-to-miss step confirmed by checking — `getUserShares`'s plain `.lean()` needed no equivalent change, only the aggregation pipeline's own field allowlist did). Mobile: `ShareCard.tsx` gained a `typeMeta` case (`ribbon` icon, `colors.warning`) and a new centered `badgeBox` render block — badge art + `"{{genre}} {{tier}}"` + `"Earned by watching {{count}} {{genre}} titles"`, resolving the actual image/label via the same `GENRE_BADGE_DEFINITIONS` table `ProfileBadgesTab.tsx` already uses, so there's exactly one place that ever maps a badge `key` to art.

**Live-tested the whole detection path with 22 real rating calls (`Loren_Pacocha50540`'s account), not just code review.** Direct ask: bring her Horror count from 22 to one below the Master threshold (40) so the user could trigger the real popup themselves in-app with the final rating. First batch (17 movies) undershot — landed at 34, not 39 — because the throwaway seeding script's own "is this already rated" check used a hand-rolled `mongoose.model(..., {strict:false})` Rating model with no schema type for `user`, so Mongoose never cast the query's string id to ObjectId and the check silently matched nothing; 5 of the 17 "unrated" picks turned out to already be rated, so those 5 calls were harmless updates, not new ratings. Caught by directly re-verifying the real count against `Rating`+`Movie.genre_ids` with proper `ObjectId` casting instead of trusting the first script's own count. Fixed the query, found 5 more genuinely-unrated Horror titles, rated those — confirmed the account now sits at exactly 39/40, one real rating away from Master. Every one of the 22 calls returned the correct (empty) `newlyEarnedBadges`, live-confirming the "no false positive below a threshold" path across real data; the "true positive at the threshold" path itself was left for the user's own final rating to trigger live, by design — that's the actual test being set up.

**Same-day follow-up round: real requirements change (badges count Watched-List membership, not just rated titles), plus several concrete UI fixes from actually using the feature.**

**Counting basis switched from Rating documents to `User.watchlist` — direct ask, "sadece ratelenmiş olanları saymasın, watchedliste eklenenleri de saysın."** `countGenreBadgesFromWatchlist` (badgeController.js, replacing the old Rating-based tally) walks `User.watchlist` — the real "Watched List" membership array, same source `getCineGraph`'s own watchlist-based counting already reads, just recomputed fresh rather than trusted from a persisted counter — cross-referenced with `Movie`/`Series.genre_ids`, exactly the same `tallyGenres` shared helper as before. `computeGenreBadgeCounts(userId)` now fetches the user fresh; a new lower-level `countGenreBadgesFromWatchlist(watchlist)` takes an already-in-hand array directly, since `userWatchlistRoute.js`'s own add handler already has the user document (with the new item already pushed) loaded in memory and shouldn't re-fetch it a second time just to check badges.

**Badge-crossing detection MOVED from `addOrUpdateRating` to the actual watchlist-add endpoint (`POST /api/users/me/watchlist`, `userWatchlistRoute.js`) — the counting-basis switch made the old hook point wrong, not just suboptimal.** Since a genre badge now counts Watched-List membership rather than ratings, and this app's own existing invariant requires an item to already be on the watched list before it can be rated (`handleRate`'s own gate in `ContentDetailScreen.tsx`), the count can never actually change at rating time anymore — whatever change was going to happen already happened when the item was added to the watchlist. `addOrUpdateRating` (`ratingController.js`) reverted cleanly back to its original form; the exact same `crossedThresholdTier`/`GENRE_BADGES` detection logic now lives in the watchlist-add handler instead, reading `user.watchlist` (already updated in memory) via `countGenreBadgesFromWatchlist`. Mobile: `addToWatchlist()` (`watchlistService.ts`) now returns `{watchlist, newlyEarnedBadges}` instead of just the array (this endpoint's own response shape was never the standard `{success,data}` envelope to begin with, so this was always going to need an explicit shape update, not a "spread it in" trick); `ContentDetailScreen.tsx`'s 2 real watchlist-add call sites (`toggleWatchlist`'s add branch, `handleOpenFavorites`) report `newlyEarnedBadges`, its 3 `rateContent()` call sites no longer do. **Live-verified the corrected "true positive" path for real, not just re-verified the "no false positive" path a second time**: re-seeding Loren's account for the new watchlist-based basis (11 real watchlist-adds, `POST /api/users/me/watchlist`), one of the 11 titles (also tagged Action) organically pushed her real Action count to exactly 15 and the API correctly returned `newlyEarnedBadges: [{key:"action", count:15, tier:"devotee", threshold:15}]` on that exact call — a real threshold crossing caught live, not staged. Final state: Horror sits at exactly 39/40 again under the new counting basis, ready for the user's own next watchlist-add to trigger Master live.

**Real bug fix: the Badges tab never refreshed after being visited once, so a freshly-earned badge tapped through from `BadgeEarnedModal` still showed gray.** Reported live right after building the popup. Root cause: `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx` keeps every visited category mounted (so switching tabs is instant) but never re-fetches an already-visited one — the exact same problem `ProfileSharingsTab.tsx` already had and already fixed once, with an `active` prop + a `lastFetchedRef` timestamp + a "revalidate silently if stale" effect (`REVALIDATE_TTL_MS`). Gave `ProfileBadgesTab.tsx` the identical fix (`active={category === "badges"}` now passed down, 5s TTL) instead of inventing a different mechanism for the same shaped problem.

**`BadgeEarnedModal.tsx` refinements, all direct asks after seeing the popup in the app**: "Share to Media" moved above "Tap to see your badge" (was below); shrunk from a full-width stretched bar to a small, self-sizing pill (secondary action, not a second primary CTA); a real spam-prevention bug fixed — repeated taps were posting a new Share every time — now the button flips to a disabled "Shared" state (grayed, both re-styled) the instant a share actually succeeds, reset only when a different badge takes over the popup. Post caption reworded (`ShareCard.tsx`'s `badgeBox`): `"I earned a new badge by watching {{count}} {{genre}} titles!"` (was the flatter "Earned by watching..."), same key text updated across all 12 locales rather than adding a parallel key. New low-opacity `ribbon-outline` watermark, top-right — same `analysisCover`'s own decorative-icon technique (large, `opacity:0.07`, bled slightly past the box edge and clipped by its own `overflow:"hidden"`), just mirrored to the opposite corner and a different glyph, direct ask to bring the same touch to this box too.

**Answered: are genre badges movie-only or movie+series?** Both, for 5 of the 8 — Action/Comedy/Drama/Sci-Fi/Documentary combine a movie genre count and a series genre count under one badge (`GENRE_BADGES`'s own `movieGenres`/`seriesGenres` pair per key). Horror/Romance/Thriller are movie-only, not by omission — TMDB's own series genre taxonomy (`SERIES_GENRE_MAP`) has no equivalent category for any of those three at all, confirmed against the real map rather than assumed.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; full backend `node --check` sweep clean; fresh Metro bundle fetched and grepped for the new identifiers (`shareButtonDone`, `REVALIDATE_TTL_MS`, `badgeBoxWatermark`, the new caption text) present, `RateContentResult` (the now-removed type) fully gone.

**Same-day follow-up: the Badges tab's own revalidate-on-refocus fix from the round above wasn't actually catching the real reported path — a second, deeper fix.** `active` (`category === "badges"`) only flips when the CATEGORY changes — but "Tap to see your badge" very often lands back on a tab that was ALREADY "badges" (the user had just been checking it, e.g. right before the Loren test), so no category change ever happens and an effect keyed on `active` alone never re-fires, even though the screen was genuinely left and come back to. Fix: `screenFocused` — already threaded down from `profile/index.tsx`'s own `useFocusEffect` through `ProfileCategoryTabs.tsx`, previously only reaching `AddFavoriteModal`/`ProfileAnalysisModal` — now also reaches `ProfileBadgesTab.tsx`, and the revalidate effect is keyed on the COMBINED `active && screenFocused` transitioning to true instead of `active` alone. `screenFocused` genuinely does toggle false→true across leaving Profile and coming back, regardless of which category tab was already selected, which is the signal this actually needed.

**Found and fixed a second, closely-related real bug while tracing this one through:** `profile/index.tsx`'s own deep-link tab seeding (`initialCategory`, derived from the `?tab=` param) only ever ran once, at this screen's own first mount — a real gap for a bottom-tab screen that normally stays mounted for the rest of the session. `BadgeEarnedModal`'s `router.navigate("/profile?tab=badges")` on an *already-mounted* Profile would have silently done nothing if some OTHER category was selected at the time (the screen just keeps showing whatever was already there, never actually switches to Badges) — hadn't surfaced yet only because the reported case happened to already have Badges selected. New effect syncs `category` to `initialCategory` whenever the param actually changes to a different valid category, deliberately comparing against the current selection first so a manual tap on a different tab doesn't get fought by a now-stale `tab` param still sitting in the URL.

**Backend — 3 new independent single-metric ladders, each shaped exactly like volume's own movies/series (one key, `{badges:[{key,count,tier}], tiers}}`), so `shareController.js`'s badge-share verification could become one small dispatch table instead of growing a per-family if/else.** `badgeController.js`: `tierForVolume`/`crossedVolumeTier` generalized into `tierForCount(count, tiers)`/`crossedCountTier(count, tiers)` (tiers passed as a parameter, `crossedVolumeTier` kept as a thin wrapper so no existing caller needed touching); `RATING_COUNT_TIERS`/`REVIEW_COUNT_TIERS`/`LIST_COUNT_TIERS` (thresholds picked from a real DB distribution check — median rating count ~38 across the app's 98 seeded users, most reviewers have 1, most listers have 1 — rather than guessed blind) with tiers `"tier1".."tierN"`, deliberately neutral (not invented words) matching the badge art's OWN file-naming convention (`badge_rating_count_tier1.png`) — real display names are a mobile-only concern (see below), same split volume's own Amateur→Cinephile ladder established. **Detection lives in each metric's own real creation endpoint — a genuinely different (and correct) hook point than genre/volume's shared watchlist-add hook, not an inconsistency.** Genre/volume count Watched-List membership, so their crossing can only ever happen at the watchlist-add step (already established earlier this project). Rating/review/list counts are literal document counts, so THEIR crossing can only happen where those documents are actually created: `ratingController.js`'s `addOrUpdateRating` (only on a genuinely NEW rating, `!existingRating` — an edit can never move the count), `reviewController.js`'s `addOrUpdateReview` (same `!existingReview` guard), and `customListRoute.js`'s `POST /` (no guard needed — every call there is a brand new list, no upsert exists on this endpoint). Response shape for all 3 mirrors the pre-revert genre pattern exactly: `newlyEarnedBadges` spread alongside the rating's own fields (`{...newRating, newlyEarnedBadges}`) — chosen deliberately, not accidentally re-adding the thing that got reverted earlier, since THIS time the hook point is actually correct for what's being counted.

**A genuinely different shape from every badge before it: these 3 cross their threshold from someone ELSE's action or a ranking shift, not the viewer's own — so none of them gets a live "you just earned a badge!" popup, by design, not by oversight.** Documented explicitly in `badgeController.js`'s own `FOLLOWERS_TIERS`/`INFLUENCER_TIERS` comment and `feedController.js`'s `computePodiumBadge` comment: followers crosses when someone ELSE follows you, influencer when someone ELSE likes your post, podium when ANYONE's stats shift the rankings — none of these has a single request on the affected user's own side to hang a live notification off of (unlike every prior badge, always triggered by the user's own direct action). A real-time cross-user notification would need its own delivery mechanism (push/socket to the target's own active session) this feature doesn't need to justify building. All 3 are still fully real, correctly computed, and visible/shareable from the Badges tab — only the instant-popup moment is the deliberate gap. Thresholds again picked from a real DB check (followers: median 3, max 12 across 96 users; summed likeCount: median 6, max 63), scaled into round aspirational numbers.

**`computePodiumBadge` deliberately lives in `feedController.js`, not `badgeController.js` — the one badge family that doesn't.** It's built entirely out of that file's own `getPeopleThreePodiums` (the exact ranking the podium itself shows, reusing it rather than a second copy — same reasoning `getMyPodiumPlacements`/`activityController.js`'s own `getFollowedPodiumEvents` already establish); `feedController.js` already imports `computeAllUsersBadgeCounts` FROM `badgeController.js`, so importing the reverse direction for podium would be a genuine circular import, not just an awkward one. `badgeRoute.js` and `shareController.js` both import it from `feedController.js` directly (a route/dispatch layer depending on two controllers is fine; the cycle would only exist between the two controllers themselves). Confirmed live, not just by reasoning about it: the server loaded and served requests correctly after the change.

**Podium badge is the one family deliberately excluded from the "Most Badges" total** (`totalBadgeCount`'s own doc comment) — Most Badges is itself one of the podium's 6 categories, so counting the podium badge toward that same total would be self-referential (being podium-decorated would inflate the very total that decides whether you're podium-decorated). **Real investigation before building anything**: confirmed via direct research that no Match/SyncResult model exists anywhere — the compatibility score (`matchPercentage`, 0-100) is computed fresh on every request and, at most, cached 60 seconds in-process memory; the only persisted trace of the feature at all is `MatchAnalysisLog` (`user`, `targetUser`, `createdAt` — an append-only, undeduped, directional log written only by the "Analyze" LLM button, purely for its own per-pair cooldown, never by browsing candidates or viewing a cached score). This meant **First Sync** (≥1 analysis run) and **Sync Explorer** (≥5 distinct people analyzed, via `MatchAnalysisLog.distinct("targetUser")`) were directly computable from what already existed, but **High Match** (≥80% reached with anyone, ever) was not — nothing captured the score itself. **Fourth new badge category shipped: "Loyalty" (founding cinephile, membership anniversary, streak) — 4th of 6 planned categories, and the round that required a genuinely new piece of infrastructure (a real streak counter), not just new read-side computation over existing data.**

**Founding Cinephile — a fixed absolute registration-rank cutoff (first 100 users ever, official account excluded), checked directly against this app's real data before picking it.** A percentage-of-timeline rule (e.g. "earliest 10%") was considered and rejected: this app's real registrations are heavily front-loaded (most accounts were bulk-seeded near launch), so a percentage rule would tag the large majority of the whole user base as "founders." A fixed round number stays meaningful regardless of how bursty registration is, and still means something once the user base grows past it. One-off badge; its own compute function does a direct rank comparison rather than reusing `tierForCount` (that helper answers "is this COUNT large enough," the exact inverse of "is this RANK small enough").

**Membership anniversary scaled in weeks/months, not years — also checked directly first.** The oldest real account is ~265 days old, so a 1-year tier would be unreachable by anyone today; tiers are 30/90/180 days instead. Standard 3-tier ladder, its own invented rank words (Member→Loyalist→Veteran).

**Streak is the one genuinely new subsystem this round**: no login/session/daily-activity tracking existed anywhere in the app before this (confirmed directly — no `lastLogin`/`lastActive` field, no streak-shaped model; the closest thing, `ActivityLog`, only logs a narrow subset of actions and real usage in this dev DB shows a max 3-day consecutive-active-day run even among the most active users). Rather than build a streak off that thin signal, added a proper Duolingo-style counter to `User` — two fields, `currentStreak` and `lastStreakDate` (always truncated to a UTC calendar day) — updated by a new shared `bumpStreak(userId)` in `badgeController.js`, called unconditionally (unlike every count-based badge's own "only a genuinely new document" guard — even editing an existing rating is real evidence of showing up today) from all 4 of the app's real engagement endpoints (`ratingController.js`, `reviewController.js`, `customListRoute.js`, `userWatchlistRoute.js`'s watchlist-add). Idempotent within a single UTC day (a 2nd qualifying action the same day is a no-op, so hitting multiple endpoints in one sitting never double-advances it) and lazily self-correcting: nothing runs on a schedule to reset a streak that's gone stale, so every READ (`computeStreakBadge`, and the same check duplicated inline in `computeAllUsersBadgeCounts` for the Most Badges total) first checks whether `lastStreakDate` is today-or-yesterday and reports 0 otherwise — the stored `currentStreak` number itself only gets corrected for real on the user's own next action.

**Streak tier VALUES are real day-counts** (`"7day"|"30day"|"100day"`, thresholds 7/30/100 — the user's own exact ask) rather than generic `tier1..tierN`, the one other exception to that convention besides genre's own devotee/master, matching the badge art's own file names (`badge_streak_7day/30day/100day.png`, already agreed in the very first asset-naming round). `Share.js`'s tier enum extended with these 3 literal strings alongside the existing `tier1`-`tier5` set.

Also added a `displayLabel` override (defaults to `label`) so a ladder's GRID tile caption can differ from the noun its own progress sentences use — needed here because streak and membership both share the sentence-noun "Days," which would otherwise put two adjacent tiles in the grid captioned identically; each now shows its own distinct word (`Membership`/`Streak`) on the tile while still saying "Days" inside the count sentences. 2 new no-`{{label}}` sentence variants added for the same reason ("You've earned the {{tier}} badge!" / the matching maxed-tier version), reusable by any future ladder whose tier words are similarly self-descriptive. New `loyaltyBadgeDefinitions.ts` holds all 3 definitions (founding as a single one-off image, membership as a real 3-tier `tierImages`/`tierLabelKeys` ladder, streak as a 3-tier ladder with no `tierLabelKeys` map at all). **Two definitions had to be redesigned once checked against real data, not assumed from the brainstorm alone.** Hidden Gem Hunter was originally meant to use TMDB's `vote_average`/`vote_count` (low popularity + high score) — checked directly first and found that only 169 of this catalog's 578,000+ movies even HAVE those fields at all (the bulk TMDB import never populated them for the vast majority). Redesigned to use a signal that reliably exists instead: a title the user rated ≥8 that ≤3 total users (across the whole app) have on their own Watched List — derived entirely from this app's own data, never TMDB metadata. Scoped to just the current user's own high ratings (never a full-catalog scan) so the watcher-count aggregation stays cheap regardless of catalog size (578k+ movies, but a small combined watchlist footprint). Eclectic Taste was designed around the SAME unified 8-genre system `GENRE_BADGES` already establishes (not raw TMDB `genre_ids`, which would double-count e.g. movie "Action" and series "Action & Adventure" as two separate genres) — reuses `computeGenreBadgeCounts` directly, so it can never quietly disagree with what the Genre badges tab itself shows; earned at ≥6 of the 8 keys touched at all (breadth, not depth — deliberately not requiring Devotee-level counts in each).

Poll Participant reuses the ALREADY-BUILT, ALREADY-ACTIVE poll-voting feature (`shareController.js`'s `voteOnPoll`, confirmed live with 22 real poll Shares and 20 real votes already in this dev DB from the official-account content feature) — zero new poll infrastructure needed, just checking `pollData.options[].votes` for the current user's id.

**2026-09-13: four direct asks in one round — public-profile badges, a per-target recommend cooldown, a Sync/profile-analysis chat card redesign, and Discover poster-border consistency.**

**1. Public-profile Badges tab.** All 19 badges (8 categories) were viewer-only until now (`badgeRoute.js`'s own doc comment explicitly flagged this as "a deliberate later step, not an oversight"). Rather than widen all 20 own-profile endpoints with an optional `:id`, added one new bulk route, `GET /api/badges/user/:id` (`badgeRoute.js`), composing all 20 `compute*` functions already exported from `badgeController.js` (plus `computePodiumBadge` from `feedController.js`, imported here rather than into `badgeController.js` itself specifically to avoid the exact circular-import `getPodiumBadge`'s own comment already flags) into one response — gated by the same `isAuthorizedToView` (`userController.js`) every other public-profile surface (favorites, CineGraph) already uses, returning `{authorized:false}` for a private profile the viewer doesn't follow. `ProfileBadgesTab.tsx` (the existing own-profile component) gained an optional `userId` prop: when set, `load()` calls the new bulk endpoint instead of firing its own-profile's 20 separate requests — same tile-building logic either way, zero own-profile behavior change. `PublicProfileCategoryTabs.tsx` gained a 5th "badges" tab reusing this same component. Live-verified: Zachary viewing Peter's badges via the bulk endpoint returns Peter's real counts (distinct from Zachary's own), confirmed via a side-by-side call.

**2. Recommend cooldown — independent per target (Media/person/group), not a single shared timer.** Direct ask: repeatedly tapping Recommend on the same title spammed the same target; recommending to Media, a person, AND a group in one sitting must all still work (they're independent), only re-recommending the exact same title to the exact same target within the window should be blocked, with a clear "you just recommended this" reason. Added 3 independent 1-hour cooldowns (same value/shape as the existing `REVIEW_SHARE_COOLDOWN_MS` precedent in `shareController.js`), one per file/target: `shareController.js`'s `createShare` (`type:"recommendation"`, keyed on `user+contentId+contentType`, scoped to Media only), `conversationController.js`'s `sendMessage` (keyed additionally on `roomId`, one DM's own history), `groupController.js`'s `sendGroupMessage` (keyed on the group's own `roomId`) — each returns 429 with a specific message ("You just recommended this to Media/this person/this group. Try again later.") and `retryAfterMs`, same shape `createShare`'s existing review-cooldown rejection already uses. Mobile's `handleSendRecommendation`/`handleConfirmRecipients` (`ContentDetailScreen.tsx`, `socials/messages/recommend.tsx`, `ProfileAnalysisModal.tsx`) switched from `Promise.all` to `Promise.allSettled` so one recipient's cooldown rejection can't sink the send to everyone else picked in the same batch; surfaces the backend's own specific message via `e?.response?.data?.message` (same convention `ReviewWriteScreen.tsx`'s Save-and-Share error handling already established) only when EVERY target in the batch failed. Live-verified all 3 cooldowns independently: recommended the same title to Media (succeeded), then immediately to a person via DM (succeeded — proving Media's active cooldown doesn't block it), then a 2nd identical DM recommend correctly 429'd; same independent-success-then-blocked-repeat pattern verified for a group. All test shares/messages deleted afterward.

**3. Sync + profile-analysis chat cards redesigned together, plus a follow-up caption message for both.** Direct complaints: the stacked "deck" illusion behind the front Sync card (`SyncShareMessageCard.tsx`) was barely visible (`colors.base300` at 0.45/0.75 opacity read as near-invisible against some palettes' own similar base300), and the front card itself (flat color + bare percentage + "SYNC") wasn't "cezbedici" (compelling); separately, profile-analysis shares had never gotten any card treatment at all — still the very first plain-text bubble ("📊 Shared their profile analysis") from before Sync's own card existed.

**Backend.** New `User.currentlyWatching` field — a single embedded `{itemId, itemType, startedAt}`, not an array (one active status per person, keeps the feed one row per viewer). `POST`/`DELETE /api/users/me/currently-watching` (`userController.js`) set/clear it directly. Auto-cleared for real (not just lazily) the moment the SAME item lands on the Watched List — hooked into `userWatchlistRoute.js`'s existing watchlist-add handler, right before its own `user.save()`, mirroring the exact spot `bumpStreak`/badge-crossing logic already hooks into that same handler. `GET /api/feed/currently-watching?scope=all|friends` (`feedController.js`) — one query filtered by a 1-day-old cutoff (`CURRENTLY_WATCHING_TTL_MS`) for `scope=all`, additionally scoped to the viewer's own `following` array for `scope=friends` (same `_id: {$in: ...}` pattern `getPopularWithFriends` already established), hydrating each watcher's active item against Movie/Series in one batched pair of queries rather than N+1.

**A real Mongoose quirk found and fixed along the way**: a single-nested-object schema path (like `currentlyWatching`, a plain object shape rather than a proper sub-`Schema`) auto-vivifies into `{}` the instant it's accessed on a live (non-`.lean()`) document instance — even for a user who's never touched the feature at all — so a naive `user.currentlyWatching ?? null` in the watchlist-add response shipped a misleading `{}` instead of `null` for that (very common) case. Fixed with an explicit `user.currentlyWatching?.itemId ? user.currentlyWatching : null` check instead. `GET /feed/currently-watching` itself was never at risk of the same bug — it queries via `.lean()`, which returns raw MongoDB documents with no such auto-vivification.

**A real live-testing detour, documented for next time**: mid-implementation, several rounds of curl tests against the watchlist-add response kept coming back without the newly-added `currentlyWatching` field, despite the file on disk clearly having the code and `node --check` passing clean every time. Root-caused via a hardcoded literal marker in the response body plus a `console.log` right before it — both confirmed the exact edited code WAS executing, which mostly ruled out a stale process, but the response still lacked the field on several consecutive tries immediately after edits, before finally appearing after one more explicit restart. Read together with the file's own mtime lagging noticeably behind several edits earlier in the same round, the likely cause is nodemon's chokidar watcher occasionally missing or coalescing a rapid-fire edit into an already-in-progress restart cycle rather than queuing a fresh one — not a new bug in this specific feature, but a reminder that "the file has the code and syntax-checks clean" doesn't guarantee the *running* process has actually picked it up; when a live test result doesn't match what a just-edited file clearly says, checking the dev server's own restart log (`mobile/.dev-logs/backend.log`, `grep "restarting due to changes"`) before assuming a logic bug would have saved real time here.

State (`isWatchingThis`) is derived entirely client-side from `AuthContext`'s cached `user.currentlyWatching` plus a local 1-day TTL check (mirroring the backend's own `CURRENTLY_WATCHING_TTL_MS`) — no extra request needed just to paint the button's own active/inactive state. `AuthContext.updateUser` (already existed, used elsewhere for bio/avatar edits) is reused to keep that cache in sync after every set/stop/auto-clear, including threading the watchlist-add response's own `currentlyWatching` field through `toggleWatchlist`/`handleOpenFavorites` so an auto-clear reflects in the button immediately without a refetch.

**2026-09-15: two real UI bugs fixed, reported live.** (1) `StarRatingDisplay.tsx`'s half-star sat visibly out of alignment with the full stars next to it — root cause: full stars rendered as a plain "★" text glyph (`fontSize`/`lineHeight` styling), the half-star as an SVG clipped path; a font glyph's own ink isn't reliably centered in its layout box the way an SVG viewBox is, so the two never lined up. Fixed by rendering every star (full and half) as the same SVG path at the same size — one rendering technique, not a font-metrics tweak — which fixed every call site of this widely-reused component at once (review cards, watched-by rows, feed rows, ShareCard, etc.), not just the one screen it was reported on. (2) Content Detail's "Watched by Friends" avatars were reported as too small with overlapping star rows — root cause wasn't really the gap value, it was `friendCard`'s own fixed `width:40` being narrower than a full 5-star row at the display's own star size (~59px at size 11, with gap), so a high rating's star row genuinely overflowed into the next card. The "memory efficient" pagination itself needed a real design call: this tab (like every other category body) renders inside the profile screen's own single outer `ScrollView` — nesting a `FlatList` in there trips RN's VirtualizedList warning and doesn't meaningfully virtualize anyway once it's inside an already-fully-rendering ScrollView. Rather than restructure the whole profile screen's scroll container (a much bigger, riskier change touching every other tab), pagination is driven by a plain ref (`nearBottomRef`) the *parent* screen's own `ScrollView` (`profile/index.tsx` for the own profile, `app/user/[id]/index.tsx` for a public one) writes a near-bottom signal into on scroll — populated only while this tab's own feed mode is the one currently active, `null` otherwise, so a scroll-near-bottom on Favorites/CineGraph/grid-mode-Sharings never accidentally triggers a fetch meant for a different view. This keeps memory bounded the way the user actually asked (pages fetched/appended incrementally, never loaded all up front) even though rows already scrolled past stay mounted rather than being recycled by true virtualization — an explicit, documented tradeoff (in the component's own comment) rather than a silent gap, given the alternative was a much larger restructure out of this ask's own scope.

New `ProfileFaqTab.tsx` — a plain accordion (tap a question to expand its answer; several can be open at once, nothing here is mutually exclusive) grouped under section headings, matching this app's own card+row visual language rather than introducing a new one.

`PublicProfileCategoryTabs.tsx` now picks one of two whole tab sets based on `profile.isOfficial` (already a real field, `GET /users/profile/:id` already spreads it in — no backend change needed at all): the official account gets `["sharings", "faq"]` instead of every real user's `["sharings", "favorites", "cinegraph", "badges"]` — Favorites/CineGraph/Badges are all meaningless for a bot account that never watches or rates anything, the user's own direct read. A stale `initialCategory` deep-link (e.g. `?tab=favorites` landing on the official account somehow) now falls back to `sharings` instead of trying to render a tab that isn't in the active set.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Live-confirmed `GET /users/profile/:id` for the real seeded official account (`isOfficial:true`) actually resolves that flag end to end. A fresh Metro bundle confirmed `ProfileFaqTab`, `FAQ_SECTIONS`, and real FAQ answer text all present in the compiled output.

## 4. API layer conventions

`src/api/client.ts` is a single axios instance: request interceptor attaches the JWT from `expo-secure-store`, response interceptor unwraps the backend's `{success, message, data, pagination?}` envelope so callers just get `res.data` (and `res.pagination` when paginated).

**Global 401 handling, added after a real reported "infinite loop" of 401s.** `authMiddleware.js`'s 401 always means one thing — the request's own token is missing/invalid/expired — but nothing client-side ever acted on that; anything polling on a fixed interval while logged in (`NotificationContext`'s 10s unread-count poll is the obvious one) just kept silently retrying and failing forever once whatever session was active stopped being valid, with no logout and no prompt to sign back in. `client.ts` now exposes `setUnauthorizedHandler(handler)` — a plain module-level slot, since it has no hook access of its own — and calls it from the response interceptor on a 401 *from a request that actually carried an `Authorization` header* (deliberately excluding login's own "Invalid email or password", which is also a 401, `userController.js`, but never sends that header in the first place). `AuthContext.tsx` registers its own `logout` there once, on mount — a 401 now actually logs the user out (clearing the stored token, `user` going back to `null`), which in turn stops `NotificationContext`'s poll on its own (already keyed on `user?._id`), rather than that poll — or anything else authenticated — spinning on a dead token indefinitely. The specific token that triggered the report was never directly inspected (no device access in this environment); this fixes the *symptom* (an unbounded retry loop with no recovery path) regardless of what actually invalidated that particular session — logging back in gets a fresh, valid one either way.

**Real environment bug found right after, same day: an undetected orphaned backend process, not a code/Mongo/LLM issue.** Reported live: logging in crashed with `Cannot find module '../encodings'` (`raw-body`→`iconv-lite`, deep inside `body-parser`/`express`). Root-caused precisely, not just restarted-and-hoped: `mobile/scripts/start-codespace.sh`'s own cleanup step (`pkill -f "nodemon server.js"`) only ever matches nodemon's *wrapper* process — nodemon's actual spawned child runs as a bare `node server.js`, with no "nodemon" anywhere in its own command line, so it doesn't match that pattern at all. A child that outlives its wrapper (from an earlier session's restart, or a manual run) becomes a silent orphan still holding port 5000 — every *later* attempt to start a fresh backend then crash-loops behind it with `EADDRINUSE` (logged, but easy to miss), while the orphan itself — running whatever on-disk `node_modules` state existed at the moment *it* started — keeps answering every request as if nothing were wrong. This is exactly what happened here: an `npm install` earlier the same day (fixing an unrelated missing-`safe-buffer` crash, §"General app-wide fix" above) deduplicated/removed some nested per-package copies (`backend/node_modules/raw-body/node_modules/iconv-lite`) that were only ever hoisted to the root `node_modules` — completely fine for a *fresh* process (Node's own resolution walks up and finds the intact root copy), but the *orphan* had `iconv-lite`'s outer module already loaded in its own `require` cache from before the cleanup, and `iconv-lite` lazily requires its `../encodings` folder only when actually asked to transcode something — so the crash only surfaced later, on the first real request that needed it (a JSON login body), not immediately. Fixed two ways: (1) immediately, by finding the true orphan via `lsof -i :5000` (its start time predated the current nodemon instance) and killing it directly; (2) at the source, `start-codespace.sh`'s cleanup step now kills whatever's actually bound to port 5000 (`fuser -k 5000/tcp`, falling back to `lsof -ti :5000 | xargs kill -9`) *in addition to* the existing pattern-based kills, so this class of orphan can't survive a restart regardless of how it was spawned. Verified: a real `POST /api/users/login` with a JSON body returns the correct `401 Invalid email or password` instead of crashing; `ps`/`lsof` confirm exactly one process on port 5000 after a full script run.

**Immediate follow-up, same day: locked cloud bubbles get a real blur, not a dimmed copy — two attempts, the first one wrong.** Reported live: the tier-locked bubbles in the results cloud (`MatchCloudBubble.tsx`) used a reduced-opacity render of the actual profile (`MatchAvatarRing`'s `dimmed` prop) instead of an actual blur — the profile itself was being altered (faded), not covered.

First attempt: added `expo-blur` and layered a circular `BlurView` on top of the ring — technically "a blur," but not what was actually meant. Corrected once an example image was shared: what was wanted is the *photo itself* rendered like a real blurred photograph (a strong, uniform Gaussian-style blur baked into the image), not a translucent frosted-glass pane laid over sharp content — visually a very different look. `expo-blur` removed again (uninstalled, confirmed unused elsewhere via grep) — a `BlurView` overlay is fundamentally the wrong tool for "blur the photo," not just a tuning issue.

**Actual fix**: React Native's `Image` component has a built-in `blurRadius` prop — a real blur baked into the rendered image itself, native on both iOS and Android, no library needed. `UserAvatar.tsx` gained an opt-in `blurRadius?: number` passthrough (every other call site omits it, unaffected); `MatchAvatarRing.tsx`'s `locked` prop (renamed back from the removed `dimmed`) sets it to a value scaled off `avatarSize` (`Math.max(8, avatarSize * 0.18)`, not a flat px number — a fixed blur radius reads far stronger on a small rank-4/5 bubble than a large rank-1 one, so scaling keeps the effect visually consistent across the cloud's different bubble sizes) — only the photo blurs, the ring/medal badge stay sharp. `MatchCloudBubble.tsx` reverted to a plain small lock-icon badge on top (its original, pre-`BlurView` design) — the blur itself now lives entirely in the image, not in an overlay.

### Search algorithm + filters: full end-to-end audit, then seven fixes applied in order

Same depth of pass as the earlier Cinematch algorithm audit, this time aimed at Search: `GET /movies`, `GET /series` (and their `/search` siblings), `searchUsers`, `getPopularLists`, `getPopularReviews`, the Atlas Search stages backing all of them, and the mobile filter UI driving them — correctness, gaps, performance, all checked against live data on the real dataset (578,539 movies / 166,532 series), not just read from the code.

**Critical finding, live-confirmed against real numbers**: `GET /movies` and `GET /series` both ran a `$limit: 2000` *before* `$facet`'s own `$count` stage, silently capping `pagination.total`/`pages` at 2000 no matter how many documents actually matched. Direct DB count for genre 35 (Comedy): **113,938** real matches; the API reported exactly `total: 2000` — over 98% of matching content was permanently unreachable through any amount of pagination. Removed the cap entirely (the pipeline's own `.allowDiskUse(true)` was already the real safeguard this was trying, wrongly, to provide by hand).

Seven fixes applied, in order:

1. **The `$limit: 2000`-before-`$facet` bug (above), removed in both `movieRoute.js` and `seriesRoute.js`.**
2. **New compound indexes on `genre_ids`**, live-created on both collections (`{genre_ids:1, popularity:-1, vote_count:-1, release_date:-1}` on `movies`, same shape with `first_air_date` on `series`) — genre filtering on a 578k/166k-document collection had no supporting index at all before this.
3. **Atlas Search's post-`$search` `$limit: 200` reordered to run *after* the genre/year/hasPoster `$match` stages**, not before — the old order meant a title search combined with a filter could silently drop valid genre/year matches that ranked outside the top 200 by text relevance alone. The same class of bug existed on the reviews side: `getPopularReviews`'s content-title prefilter (`reviewController.js`) used to `.limit(200)` the *movies/series* it resolved a title query against before ever filtering reviews by them — removed that cap too, since resolving content ids is cheap (`_id`-only, `.lean()`) and has no real reason to be capped.
   - **Found during verification of this exact fix, not by the user**: removing that `.limit(200)` turned the review prefilter's `getMovie().find({title:regex})`/`getSeries().find({name:regex})` into a full, unindexed, case-insensitive regex scan across the whole 745k-document movies+series catalog — no index can serve an unanchored `$regex`. A generic query like `q=the` took **45 seconds**. Fixed properly rather than just re-capping it: switched this prefilter to the same Atlas-Search-backed `buildFuzzyTitleSearchStage` the movie/series search bars already use, `$limit`ed to 500 — index-backed, so it stays fast regardless of catalog size, and safe to cap because Atlas Search ranks by relevance (the cap only ever drops the least-relevant matches, not an arbitrary slice, unlike the plain-regex version this replaced). Re-verified: `q=the` now resolves in ~2s; realistic queries (`q=dragon`, `q=boys`) still return the correct reviewed titles. `escapeRegex` in `reviewController.js` became dead code once the regex path was gone — removed.
4. **`searchUsers` regex-injection fixed.** `userController.js` built `{$regex: query, $options:'i'}` directly from unescaped user input — live-confirmed real: searching `"Zach.ry"` matched `"Zachary"` via the unescaped `.` acting as a wildcard. Added a local `escapeRegex` helper (same one-liner already used in `customListRoute.js`/`movieRoute.js`/`seriesRoute.js`). Re-verified: `"Zach.ry"` now correctly returns zero results, literal `"Zachary"` still matches.
5. **`hasPoster` handling made consistent.** `movieRoute.js` treated *any* value other than exactly `"yes"` as "posterless only" (a ternary bug) — `seriesRoute.js` already had the correct explicit `"yes"`/`"no"`-only check. Movies brought in line with series. Currently unreachable from the mobile client (the `hasPoster` UI control was removed in an earlier round) but the server-side inconsistency was real regardless.
6. **Atlas Search `should`-array logic de-duplicated.** The autocomplete + fuzzy-text + optional queryString `should` array was copy-pasted near-verbatim 4 times (movies' 2 routes, series' 2 routes). Extracted into new `backend/utils/atlasSearch.js` (`buildFuzzyTitleSearchStage(query, path)`, `combinedScoreSortStages()`), used by all 4 original call sites plus, after fix #3 above, `reviewController.js`'s prefilter too.
7. **`years` filter regex escaped** (same `escapeRegex` helper as #4) — was building a regex directly from unescaped user input, same class of bug as #4 just lower severity (years are usually numeric, but the field accepts arbitrary query-string text). Also removed a pointless no-op `{$match:{}}` stage in `movieRoute.js`'s `GET /` that fired whenever no filters were active — dead weight, cleaned up as part of the same rewrite.

**Noted, not a bug**: `GET /movies/search`/`GET /series/search` are unreached by the mobile app (mobile's own search hits the list endpoints' filter params instead — see §8) but are actively used by `frontend/src/api/contentService.js` for web — correctly left in place.

Verified end to end: `node --check` clean on every touched backend file; live JWT-minted requests confirmed genre=35 now reports the real `total: 113938`; timed queries (1.127s genre-filtered, 0.864s deep-paginated) show acceptable performance under the new index; title+genre combo returns sensible, correctly-filtered results; `/movies/search`/`/series/search` still work through the refactored shared helpers; `searchUsers`'s escape fix and `hasPoster` consistency fix both re-verified live; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on mobile (no mobile files touched this round, checked anyway per convention).

**Known envelope inconsistencies in the backend** — several endpoints don't follow that envelope, and the corresponding service functions read fields directly instead of relying on the interceptor:
- Watchlist (`GET/POST/DELETE /users/me/watchlist`) returns raw `{message, watchlist}`.
- `GET /users/profile/:id` returns raw JSON on both branches (authorized and masked/private).
- Custom Lists (`GET /lists/me`, etc.) return `{lists}` / `{list}` — works fine either way since the interceptor only unwraps when it recognizes the envelope shape, otherwise passes the object through untouched, and these services read `.lists`/`.list` off whatever comes out.
- Follow endpoints are the worst offender for this — `POST /users/remove-follower` and the accept/reject follow-request endpoints return raw `{success,message}` with no `data` key at all (not unwrapped); `GET /users/me/follow-requests` and `.../sent-requests` return bare arrays with no envelope whatsoever. See `src/api/userService.ts`'s per-function comments before adding more follow-related calls.

Each `src/api/*.ts` file has a comment noting when this applies. **If a new endpoint's response looks wrong (extra nesting, or fields missing), check whether it's actually one of these unwrapped-envelope cases before assuming a bug.**

### Search *page* audit (not the algorithm this time): item loading, the filter bar, first-page load — five fixes

Same audit depth as the search-algorithm pass above, this time aimed at the Search screen itself rather than the backend query logic — `app/(app)/search/index.tsx` and every one of its 5 tabs' own data-fetching, not what each fetch actually queries.

**Biggest finding, present in all 5 tabs**: no guard anywhere against an out-of-order response. `SearchBar.tsx`'s 400ms debounce narrows the window but doesn't close it — network timing isn't request-order-guaranteed, so a slower response for an older query/filter combination could resolve *after* a faster one for a newer combination and silently overwrite already-correct state with stale data. Sharpest concrete case: Films/Series' own `loadMore` (page 2) resolving after a fresh criteria change had already reset back to page 1 used to get appended onto the *new* list, visibly mixing results from two different searches.

**Second finding**: Lists and Reviews were both hard-capped at a fixed 30 results with zero way to reach anything past that — `getPopularLists`/`getPopularReviews` were both originally "top N" endpoints built for Home's own rails (no `page`/`skip` at all), reused wholesale for Search without ever getting real pagination. Same class of gap as the movies/series list endpoints' own pagination bug from the algorithm audit above, just by omission here rather than a misplaced stage. Both also rendered via a plain `ScrollView` (no virtualization) rather than `FlatList`.

**Third finding**: Users already had full `page`/`limit` pagination support server-side (`searchUsers`, `$facet`-based, already used elsewhere) — this tab just never called it with anything past page 1, a pure mobile-side gap with zero backend work needed.

**Fourth finding**: `query`/filters live above the tab bar and reach every already-*visited* tab at once (by design, so tab-switching doesn't refetch) — but this meant every visited-but-not-currently-showing tab also re-searched in the background on every debounced query change, not just the active one.

**Fifth, minor**: the year filter's decade chips stopped at 1900 — a hard, arbitrary floor with no way to filter anything older (TMDB does carry a handful of titles predating it).

Five fixes applied, in order:

1. **Request-generation guard added to all 4 fetch-driven components** (`SearchContentRows.tsx`, `SearchListsSection.tsx`, `SearchReviewsSection.tsx`, `SearchUsersSection.tsx`) — each call now stamps the request it started with in a `requestIdRef`, and a response is only applied if that ref still matches by the time it resolves; a superseded response is silently dropped instead of corrupting state. Also incidentally fixes a `loadMore`-vs-fresh-search page-counter corruption case (a stale `loadMore` could otherwise bump `page` past what a since-reset search had already set it back to).
2. **Real pagination added to Lists and Reviews, backend and mobile together.** `backend/routes/customListRoute.js`'s `/lists/popular` and `backend/controllers/reviewController.js`'s `getPopularReviews` both switched from a flat `$sort`+`$limit` to `$facet` (metadata count + skipped/limited data), gaining an optional `page` param — additive for Lists (`getPopularLists`'s 3 existing Home callers, `KesfetSection.tsx`×2/`ListsSection.tsx`, still get the same bare-array/fixed-count shape; a new `getPopularListsPaginated` sits alongside it for Search specifically), a real shape change for Reviews (`getPopularReviews` had exactly one caller — Search — so it was safe to change directly to `{items,page,hasMore}`, reusing the existing `ReviewsFeedResult` type rather than inventing a new one). `SearchListsSection.tsx`/`SearchReviewsSection.tsx` rewritten from a fixed 30-item `ScrollView` to `FlatList` + `onEndReached`, matching Films/Series' own pattern (fixes the missing-virtualization issue in the same pass).
3. **Real pagination wired up for Users** — `SearchUsersSection.tsx` switched to `FlatList` + `onEndReached` against the backend's already-existing `page`/`limit` support on `searchUsers`; no backend change needed.
4. **Background-tab fetching stopped.** Every fetch-driven section gained an `isActive` prop (`mainTab === <tab>` from `index.tsx`) and now skips its fetch effect entirely while inactive — `isActive` is itself one of the effect's dependencies, so the moment a tab becomes active again the same effect re-runs against whatever criteria the viewer already changed while away, and catches up then.
5. **Year filter's decade floor moved from 1900 back to 1870** (`ContentFilterSheetContent.tsx`) — comfortably covers the earliest surviving films (1880s-90s) with one extra decade chip, rather than picking a different arbitrary cutoff that just moves the same gap further back.

Verified: `node --check` clean on both touched backend files; live JWT-minted pagination checks confirmed distinct, non-overlapping pages for lists (`_id` sets compared directly — zero overlap between page 1 and page 2), reviews, and users; a combined sort+rating-filter+pagination request (`sort=rating&minRating=8&page=1`) returned correctly filtered and ordered results; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh full Metro bundle (`node_modules/expo-router/entry.bundle` — this Metro instance's actual working entry path, plain `index.bundle` 404s under this Expo Router setup) grepped for `getPopularListsPaginated`, `requestIdRef`, `PAGE_LIMIT`, and `1870`, all present, with the old fixed `getPopularReviews(30` call site confirmed gone.

**Immediate follow-up, same day: fix #4 above superseded by a stronger, simpler fix — tabs reset instead of persisting, and the wrong loading UI on Films/Series got swapped out.** Reported live: typing on one tab (e.g. Films) then switching to another (e.g. Series) left that tab looking stuck on loading, and separately, Films/Series' own full-first-load state showed a jarring 2-column grid of large skeleton squares instead of the plain circular spinner Lists/Reviews/Users already used.

Root cause of the "stuck" read: `query` lived above the tab bar and reached every already-*visited* tab at once, by original design (§ earlier "One shared search box feeds whichever sub-tab is active" note) — switching tabs never cleared it, so arriving at a tab could silently carry over a query/filter combo from wherever the viewer just was, with no visible reason why results looked the way they did. Fixed by reversing that original design decision on direct request: **`app/(app)/search/index.tsx` now only ever mounts the single currently-active tab** — `switchTab` resets the shared query, closes any open filter sheet, and clears the filter-badge state, and switching between tabs unmounts the old section and mounts a brand-new instance of the new one, which is what actually resets that tab's own internal filter state for free (no lifted per-tab filter state to separately clear). `SearchBar` gets a `key={mainTab}` for the same reason — it owns its typed text internally, so it needs a real remount, not just a prop change, to clear on switch. This also fully supersedes fix #4's `isActive`-gating approach from the entry above (removed from all 4 fetch components along with the `visitedTabs`/`activeFilterByTab`-per-tab bookkeeping it depended on) — there's no more persistently-mounted hidden tab left to gate background fetches on, since inactive tabs no longer exist as mounted components at all.

Separately, `SearchContentRows.tsx`'s first-load state (`SkeletonGrid`+`SkeletonPosterCard`, a 2-column grid of large poster-shaped placeholders — left over from when this tab was still a poster grid, before the row-layout redesign) replaced with the same plain `ActivityIndicator` Lists/Reviews/Users already show while loading, for visual consistency across all 5 tabs.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `visitedTabs`/`activeFilterByTab`/`makeFilterActiveHandler` fully gone from `search/index.tsx`'s own compiled module (extracted and checked module-by-module, not just bundle-wide grep — a `visitedTabs` bundle-wide hit turned out to be Home's own unrelated, identically-named tab-persistence variable, a plain sample dataset feature elsewhere), `setQuery("")`/`hasActiveFilter`/the `key`+`mainTab` remount present in its place; `SearchContentRows.tsx`'s own compiled module confirmed to contain `ActivityIndicator` with `SkeletonGrid` fully absent from it specifically (the few remaining bundle-wide `SkeletonPosterCard` hits traced to `Skeleton.tsx`'s own export list plus two unrelated call sites, `home/lists/[id].tsx` and `ToWatchListView.tsx`).

### Media/Shares: Free/Plus/Premium tier privileges — Plus recolored to silver, Shares' own podium gated

First round of tier-leveling work scoped to the Media/Shares tab specifically (Sync got its own pass earlier, §"Eleventh round" above). Investigated before touching anything: `ShareCard.tsx` already had every post-level piece of this fully built from that earlier work — `UserAvatar`'s `TierAvatarFrame` ring on every post's author avatar (tier-colored, sourced from `theme/tierFrames.ts`), an inline `tierMark` diamond next to the username in that same color, and a gold `premiumBorder` SVG frame wrapping only Premium posts' content box (`isPremium`-gated, every other tier including Plus gets a plain gray `contentBoxFrame` instead) — so nothing there needed changing, it already matched today's ask exactly ("sadece Premiumların postları altın çerçeve ile kaplı").

What was actually missing/wrong, found by reading `tierFrames.ts` (the single color source of truth every one of the above pulls from) and `PeoplePodium.tsx`/`PeoplePodiumCard.tsx` (Media's own Most Followed/Watched/Reviewed podium):
