1. **Plus was steel-blue ("Platinum blue"), not silver** — changed `TIER_FRAME_STYLES.plus` in `theme/tierFrames.ts` to a silver gradient/glow (`["#F2F3F5", "#C7CBD1"]` / `"#C7CBD1"`), reusing `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`'s own existing rank-2 medal silver rather than picking a fresh one, so "silver" reads as the same color everywhere it already appeared (medals) and everywhere it now also appears (tier rings/marks). This is the single shared source every Plus ring/diamond in the app pulls from (ShareCard's post avatar ring+diamond, Profile's own avatar frame, this podium's diamond, etc.) — one edit, propagates everywhere automatically. `app/(app)/match/subscription.tsx`'s own separately-duplicated `ACCENT.plus` constant (kept in lockstep with `tierFrames.ts` by its own doc comment) updated to match; no other hardcoded copy of the old blue hex found anywhere else in the codebase (confirmed via a repo-wide grep for the exact old hex values).
2. **`PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`'s own tier diamond was hardcoded gold for both Plus and Premium** — a Plus podium user wore a Premium-colored mark. Fixed to read `TIER_FRAME_STYLES[tierLabel]?.glowColor` per-tier, same pattern `ShareCard.tsx`'s own `tierMark` already used correctly.
3. **Media's own podium had no Free-tier gate at all** — new `locked` prop on `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`, computed once in `PeoplePodium.tsx` from the *viewer's* own `accountTier` (`useAuth()`, same plus/premium/dev-unlocked scope as Sync's own `canUseMatchFilters`) and threaded into every card on all 3 podium pages. When locked: `UserAvatar`'s existing `blurRadius` prop bakes a real blur into the profile photo itself (same technique as Sync's `MatchAvatarRing`/`MatchCloudBubble`, scaled the same way — `Math.max(8, avatarSize * 0.18)`), plus a small lock badge centered on top (`Ionicons` `lock-closed`, same look as `MatchCloudBubble.tsx`'s own) — rank badge, username, tier diamond, and metric count all stay fully visible either way, same "still the actual tease" reasoning as Sync's own locked bubbles. Tapping a locked card routes to `/match/subscription` (the app's one existing subscription page — Sync-specific copy today, reused as-is rather than redesigned, since generalizing its content wasn't asked) instead of that person's profile. Paging between the 3 podium categories and the Most Watched movie/series toggle stay fully usable regardless of tier — only the profile reveal itself is gated.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; repo-wide grep confirmed zero remaining references to the old blue hex values; a fresh Metro bundle's `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx` module confirmed to contain `lockBadge`, `blurRadius`, and the `/match/subscription` route string, with the old hardcoded `TIER_GOLD` constant fully gone from it. No backend changes — `accountTier` was already present on every user object these components already receive.

**Immediate follow-up, same day: two real bugs reported live on `ShareCard.tsx`'s double-tap-to-like, unrelated to the tier work above.**

**Bug 1 — a genuine double-tap sometimes navigated away instead of liking.** `DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_MS` was 250ms — reported live as too tight: a real second tap landing just past that window reads as a *second, isolated* single tap rather than part of one double-tap gesture, and since nothing had canceled the *first* tap's own deferred navigation timer, it still fires on schedule and the viewer gets sent to Content Detail instead of registering the like. Widened to 350ms, closer to how this gesture actually lands. Also fixed a related latent gap while in this code: starting a new pending-navigation timer now clears any old dangling one first — previously, two isolated taps spaced just over the window apart (but too close together to feel unrelated to a viewer) could each schedule their own navigation, firing twice in a row and double-pushing the same route.

**Bug 2 — the center double-tap burst and the corner heart's own color change didn't read as simultaneous.** Root cause: the corner heart's fill used to snap instantly between gray and the red gradient the moment `share.liked` flipped, while the burst is a proper multi-hundred-ms spring pop-in — an instant cut sitting next to a gradual reveal never reads as "at the same time" even when both technically start on the same frame. Restructured the corner heart into two stacked layers — an always-present gray base heart, and the red gradient version on top inside an `Animated.View` whose `opacity` now crossfades in (`likeColorAnim`, 260ms, `Easing.out(Easing.quad)`) instead of the fill snapping. Driven directly off `share.liked` via its own `useEffect` (not wired into the double-tap handler specifically), so it animates the same way regardless of which path triggered the like — a direct tap on the sticker itself, or a double-tap on the content box.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle's `ShareCard.tsx` module confirmed `likeColorAnim` present and `DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_MS` compiled as `350` (the two remaining bundle-wide `250` hits in this module traced to the unrelated burst fade-out duration and this doc's own explanatory comment, not the double-tap window). No device access to confirm the felt timing directly — verification here is code-level (the crossfade and widened window are real, correctly-wired changes) rather than an on-device side-by-side comparison.

**Same-day, third round on `ShareCard.tsx`'s recommendation posts: the "Add to Watchlist" button made optimistic, its confirmation toast made more prominent, and the whole post's tap surface narrowed to just the poster + linked word.**

**Speed**: `addRecommendedToWatchlist` used to `await addToToWatchList(...)` before showing *any* feedback at all — reported live as feeling slow. Live-measured the actual endpoint at ~0.6s round trip in this dev environment (`POST /api/users/me/to-watch`) — not pathological, but a real, noticeable wait with zero visual feedback during it (the plus sticker just sat there unchanged). Made optimistic: `setAddedToWatchlist(true)` and the success toast now fire immediately on tap, the request itself fires in the background, and both roll back (state, toast, the fade-out timer, `watchlistOpacity`/`watchlistBounce` reset to visible) if it actually fails — same optimistic-then-reconcile shape `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s own like toggle already uses. The now-redundant `addingToWatchlist` loading-state boolean (its only job was gating this same button while awaiting the request `setAddedToWatchlist` now covers directly) removed as dead code.

**Toast prominence**: rather than restyling the app's one shared `Toast.tsx` component globally — used by 38 other call sites across the app that were never asked to change — added an opt-in `type?: "default" | "success"` to `ToastContext`'s `showToast(message, type?)`, defaulting every existing call site's look untouched. A `"success"` toast (used here for "Added to Watchlist") gets a light tint of `colors.success` as its background, a solid `colors.success` border, and a checkmark icon, instead of the plain neutral `colors.base300` — text stays `colors.baseContent` regardless. Deliberately not a solid `colors.success` fill: that token's actual luminance varies a lot across this app's 9 themes (a dark saturated green in some, a light mint in others), so guessing one fixed contrasting text color against it risked poor contrast in at least a few of them — a light tint keeps the always-safe `baseContent` text legible everywhere while still reading as distinctly more prominent than a default toast.

**Narrowed tap surface**: recommendation posts' content box used to be one large `Pressable` — tapping the title, the message background, or any empty padding all navigated to Content Detail, alongside the poster and the inline "Watchlist" word. Per direct ask, only the poster and that linked word should do anything now; everywhere else in the box is inert on a single tap. The poster became its own nested `Pressable` (`onPress={goToContent}`, resolving before the outer box's own handler — same "inner tap wins" pattern this file's review-excerpt Pressable already relies on), and the outer box's `onPress` changed from `handleContentPress(goToContent)` to `handleContentPress()` (no `originalOnPress`, same call shape the analysis box already uses) — a single tap on the rest of the box is now a genuine no-op, while double-tap-to-like (not asked to change) still works across the whole box exactly as before.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed the optimistic ordering (`addedToWatchlist`/the `"success"` toast call both compiled before the `await`), `addingToWatchlist` fully gone, `ToastContext.tsx`'s new `msgType` param present, `Toast.tsx`'s `isSuccess`/checkmark-icon branch present, and the recommendation box's poster now a separate nested `Pressable` around `goToContent`. Live-measured the real `POST /api/users/me/to-watch` latency (~0.6s) to confirm the perceived-slowness report was real and not imagined before making it optimistic.

**Same-day, fourth round: the Media header's own Paylaşımlar/Keşfet pill slide started stuttering — real root cause, not the pill itself.** Reported live: tapping the header filter used to slide smoothly, now visibly stutters/freezes. `CapsuleTabSwitcher.tsx` (the pill) and `home/index.tsx` (its pager) were both untouched this whole session — so the pill's own code wasn't the cause. The actual mechanism: `home/index.tsx`'s `switchTab` calls `setOuterTab`, which re-renders the whole `HomeScreen`; `SharesFeedSection` and `PeoplePodium` both take zero props and weren't `React.memo`'d, so that re-render was *already* cascading into a full re-render of the entire mounted Shares subtree — the live FlatList of `ShareCard`s and the podium — on every single tap, even before today. The pill's own slide position is JS-thread-driven, not native (`home/index.tsx`'s `handleScroll` uses `useNativeDriver: false`, needed since `CapsuleTabSwitcher`'s window also animates `width`, which the native driver can't touch) — so JS-thread work competing for the same frames as that tap-triggered cascade directly shows up as the pill stuttering. This cascade was always there; it only became *visible* once today's earlier rounds made every card in it heavier to re-render (the tier-lock logic in every `PeoplePodiumCard`, the new like-color crossfade `Animated.View`+`Svg` in every `ShareCard`).

Fixed at the actual source rather than trying to lighten the new features back down: wrapped `SharesFeedSection` and `PeoplePodium` in `React.memo` (both take zero props, so this makes them immune to a parent's re-render entirely — they now only ever re-render from their own internal state). `ShareCard` itself also wrapped in `React.memo`, which needed its `onToggleLike` prop reshaped from a fixed `() => void` to `(shareId: string) => void` — the previous shape only worked pre-bound per row (`onToggleLike={() => handleToggleLike(row.share._id)}`), a fresh closure on every render that would have defeated `React.memo` for every single card regardless of the fix above. `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s own `handleToggleLike` (and `ProfileSharingsTab.tsx`'s, the other of `ShareCard`'s two callers) rewritten to a dependency-free `useCallback([])` — the rollback-on-failure used to read `items` from its own closure (forcing a new function, and a new prop for every mounted card, on every fetch/page-load/like anywhere in the feed); now captures just the one row's own pre-toggle snapshot inside the functional `setItems` updater instead, so it never needs `items` in its dependency array at all. This also happens to make liking one post no longer re-render every *other* already-rendered post either (a second, related win — `.map()` already returns the same object reference for every non-toggled item, `React.memo` just wasn't there to take advantage of it before).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed all three components' `React.memo` wrapping compiled in, and the old per-row inline `onToggleLike` closures fully gone from both `SharesFeedSection.tsx` and `ProfileSharingsTab.tsx`'s own compiled modules. No device access to directly feel the tap-to-slide smoothness — verification here is structural (the actual re-render cascade this traced to is now provably cut off) rather than an on-device frame-rate comparison; worth a real on-device check next.

### Media/Shares algorithm + page audit: full end-to-end pass, same depth as Search's own — six fixes applied in order

Same audit style as the earlier Search algorithm/page passes — this time aimed at the whole Media/Shares tab: `SharesFeedSection.tsx`, `PeoplePodium.tsx`, `ShareCard.tsx`, `OnlineFriendsBar.tsx`, `SuggestedUsersBox.tsx`, and their backend counterparts (`shareController.js`'s `getShareFeed`, `feedController.js`'s `getPeopleLeaderboard`). Six fixes, in order:

1. **Real out-of-order-response race condition in `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s `load()`/`loadMore()`** — the exact same bug class already found and fixed twice on the Search page, missed here. Unlike this, `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own fetch already correctly guarded itself with a plain `cancelled` flag — this was the one fetch on the page that didn't. Fixed with the same `requestIdRef` generation-guard pattern already established for Search's components: a response is only applied if it's still the most recent request by the time it resolves. Toggling All/Friends rapidly, or toggling it mid-`loadMore`, could otherwise let a slower/stale response overwrite or get appended onto a newer, already-correct list.
2. **Poster images fetched at ~7-8x more resolution than ever displayed.** `ShareCard.tsx`'s `POSTER_BASE` was `w500` (500px wide) for every actual use in the file — all three (`sharePoster` 64×96, `filmStripPoster` 56×84, `modalPoster` 48×72) are small thumbnails. Every visible post in the feed was downloading/decoding far more pixel data than it ever renders. Changed to `w185`, matching the precedent Search's own `SearchContentRow` already set (`w154` for a similarly-sized 52px poster) — a direct, real "faster loading" win, not a guess.
3. **`OnlineFriendsBar`/`SuggestedUsersBox` were the two components on this page missed by the previous round's `React.memo` pass** — both now wrapped, for the same reasoning as `SharesFeedSection`/`PeoplePodium`/`ShareCard` there.
4. **`SuggestedUsersBox` could never actually benefit from that memoization as originally structured** — its `users` prop used to be a fresh, already-sliced array computed inline inside `renderItem` (`suggestedSlice(suggestions, row.occurrence)`) on every call, a brand-new reference every time regardless of whether the inputs actually changed — `renderItem` is a plain callback, not a component, so the slicing couldn't be `useMemo`'d at that call site at all. Moved `suggestedSlice` itself into `SuggestedUsersBox.tsx`, which now takes the stable `pool` array + primitive `occurrence` as props and slices internally via its own `useMemo` — memoization can actually take effect now.
5. **Backend: `getShareFeed`'s `$sort` (a blended recency+engagement+network score) and `getPeopleLeaderboard`'s three rankings (followerCount/watchedCount/reviewCount) all sort on fields computed per-request — no index can back any of them, so each is a full-collection scan + in-memory sort.** Live-checked real current scale (72 shares, 97 users) and confirmed this isn't an active slowdown today — a raw-driver baseline test showed a trivial `findOne({})` taking ~281ms, essentially identical to the "expensive" aggregation's ~283ms, meaning the measured ~0.6-1.2s HTTP round trips are dominated by this dev environment's Atlas connection latency, not the query plans. Still the same class of "silently breaks past a size threshold" risk as the earlier `$limit:2000` bug (Mongo's default in-memory sort has a hard 100MB cap with no fallback) — added `.allowDiskUse(true)` to both defensively, free to add now before it's ever actually needed. A real fix for the underlying full-scan-by-nature design (denormalized counter fields, updated incrementally on follow/watch/review rather than computed fresh every request) would be a bigger schema change, flagged but not undertaken this round.
6. **Two minor UX gaps, both in `SharesFeedSection.tsx`**: switching the All/Friends scope used to leave the list at whatever scroll offset the viewer happened to be at, which could land in the middle of (or past the end of) the new, differently-sized list — now scrolls to the top on every scope change. Separately, the Suggested Users pool (`getSuggestions(10)`) was fetched exactly once per app session (this section stays mounted for the whole session, `React.memo`'d, never remounts on tab switches) and never refreshed even as the viewer's own mutual-connection graph changed over a long session — now also re-fetched on manual pull-to-refresh (reusing that existing trigger rather than adding a new polling interval).

Verified: `node --check` clean on both touched backend files; live-hit `GET /api/shares/feed` and `GET /api/feed/people-leaderboard` post-`allowDiskUse` change, both still returning correct data; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `requestIdRef`/`scrollToOffset`/`loadSuggestions` present in `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s own compiled module (its old inline `suggestedSlice` definition gone), `suggestedSlice` now present in `SuggestedUsersBox.tsx`'s module instead, both `OnlineFriendsBar.tsx` and `SuggestedUsersBox.tsx` confirmed `React.memo`-wrapped, and `ShareCard.tsx`'s `POSTER_BASE` confirmed compiled as `w185` (the one remaining bundle-wide `w500` hit traced to this file's own explanatory comment, not a live URL).

**Same-day follow-up: a real cross-post watchlist-state bug found live, plus reverting one part of the earlier toast-prominence change.**

**Bug**: adding a recommendation post's content to the Watchlist correctly hid that post's own "+" sticker, but scrolling to a *different* post recommending the exact same title still showed its own live "+" — tapping it there hit the backend's own duplicate-add rejection (`409 "Already in watchlist"`), which the client's generic catch surfaced as a misleading "Something went wrong." Root cause: `ShareCard.tsx`'s `addedToWatchlist` was a purely local "did *this* card's own button get tapped" flag, with no idea whether the content was already in the viewer's real Watchlist via some other post.

Fixed with the same shared-membership-set pattern `FollowGraphContext.tsx` already established for follow status: new `WatchlistGraphContext.tsx` (`itemIds: Set<string>` of `"type:id"` keys, `ensureLoaded`/`applyAdd`/`applyRemove`/`replaceAll`), registered in `app/_layout.tsx` alongside `FollowGraphProvider`. `ShareCard.tsx` now derives its own `isInWatchlist` live from this shared set (calling `ensureLoaded()` on mount) and syncs `addedToWatchlist` to it — a card whose content is already in the watchlist hides its sticker immediately (no animation, since there's no "just did it" moment to communicate for a card the viewer never actually tapped), and a successful add/remove anywhere writes through to the shared set (`applyAdd`/`applyRemove`) so every other already-mounted card for that same title updates too. Wired into every other place that mutates the real Watchlist for full consistency: `ToWatchListView.tsx`'s own `handleRemove` (`applyRemove`) and its focus-triggered `load()` (`replaceAll` off the same `getToWatchList()` result it already fetches — the single most authoritative read of the list anywhere in the app, reused rather than double-fetched), and `ContentDetailScreen.tsx`'s `toggleToWatch` (`applyAdd`/`applyRemove`). Also fixed the error message itself while in this code: a real (if now much rarer) failure surfaces the backend's actual message now (`e?.response?.data?.message`, same fallback shape `useFollowState.ts` already uses) instead of a hardcoded generic string.

One real bug found and fixed while wiring this: `ToWatchListView.tsx`'s `load()` initially depended on the whole `watchlistGraph` object, which is a fresh literal every time the provider re-renders — including every time `load()` itself calls `replaceAll`. That would have made `load`'s own identity change on every successful load, and since it's the dependency of a `useFocusEffect` callback, risked a repeated-refetch loop on every screen focus. Fixed by depending on `watchlistGraph.replaceAll` specifically (a genuinely stable `useCallback([])` reference in the provider) instead of the whole object.

**Toast style reverted for this one call site**: the "Added to Watchlist" toast's `"success"` (tinted green + border + checkmark) styling from the earlier round was reported as not fitting here, even though the style itself was liked in general — reverted this specific `showToast()` call back to the plain default look. The `type: "success"` capability itself stays in `ToastContext`/`Toast.tsx` for wherever it does fit; this wasn't a request to remove it entirely.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `WatchlistGraphContext.tsx` compiled with `replaceAll` present, `ShareCard.tsx` using `isInWatchlistGraph`/`applyAdd`/`applyRemove` with the `"success"` toast argument gone (the one remaining bundle-wide `"success"` hit traced to this file's own explanatory comment), and `replaceWatchlistGraph`/`watchlistGraph` present in `ToWatchListView.tsx`/`ContentDetailScreen.tsx` respectively. No device access to click through the actual repro (add via one post, scroll to a duplicate-title post, confirm its own "+" is already gone) — verification here is structural (the shared-graph wiring and its write-through call sites are all in place and type-correct) rather than an on-device walkthrough.

### Discover: tier badges on Reviews/Activity, its own podium gated, and a real mode-switch data-mixing bug fixed

Three-part round on Discover (`home/KesfetSection.tsx`), started by the user pointing at Media's already-shipped tier work and asking for the same treatment here.

**1. Tier ring + diamond on Reviews and Activity avatars.** `ReviewFeedCard.tsx` (Discover's Reviews tab) and `ActivityRow.tsx` (Discover's Activity feed) both showed a plain `UserAvatar` with no tier signal at all — unlike `ShareCard.tsx`'s posts, which already got this in an earlier round. Root cause for Activity specifically: `activityController.js`'s `actorLookupStages()` already does an unrestricted `$lookup` (the full user doc, `accountTier` included, was already sitting in `$_actor`) — the only thing missing was `actorProjection` (the shape actually sent to the client) not including it, a one-line fix that covers all four event types (`rated`/`reviewed`/`favorited`/`list_item_added`) since they all share that same projection object. For Reviews: `reviewController.js`'s `getPopularReviews`/`getReviewsFeed` both `$lookup` the review's `user` through their own field-restricting `pipeline: [{ $project: {...} }]` — added `accountTier: 1` to both. Mobile-side: `ReviewAuthor` (was missing `accountTier` entirely — `PopularReview.user`'s type) and `FeedUserRef` (already had the field for `Share.user`, its own comment updated now that `ActivityEvent.actor` populates it too) both extended; `ReviewFeedCard.tsx`/`ActivityRow.tsx` each gained the same `UserAvatar tier={...}` + inline diamond mark pattern `ShareCard.tsx` already established, colored from the same shared `tierFrames.ts`.

**2. Discover's own podium (`LeaderboardPodium.tsx`/`LeaderboardCard.tsx`) gated the same way Media's `PeoplePodium` already is** — Free sees every card's poster blurred+locked (a real `blurRadius` bake, not an overlay, same technique as everywhere else this session), tapping one routes to the subscription page instead of Content Detail; Plus/Premium/dev see it unlocked. This podium ranks *content* (Most Favorited/Highest Rated/Most Recommended), not people, so the same lock mechanics from `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx` were re-applied to `LeaderboardCard.tsx`'s poster instead of an avatar — title/rank/metric stay visible regardless of tier, same "still the actual tease" scope as everywhere else.

**3. Real bug found and fixed while in this file, matching a live report: switching the movie/series mode mid-podium mixed up the category title and the data actually shown.** Root cause: `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`'s `loading` state used to swap the *entire* horizontal `ScrollView` out for a spinner on every mode toggle, not just the very first load — the ScrollView unmounting loses its scroll offset, so the freshly-remounted one always lands back at page 0, but the separate `page` state (driven by `onScroll`, used to pick which title to show — `titles[page]`) was never itself reset. A viewer who toggled Movies/Series while scrolled to, say, "Most Recommended" (`page === 2`) would see that page's own *title* still showing while the actually-displayed content silently reset to "Most Favorited"'s. This is the exact same bug class Media's own `PeoplePodium.tsx` already hit and fixed in an earlier round (its own doc comment describes the identical symptom, "podyum yüklenip gidiyor, sonra tekrar yükleniyor") — that fix was never ported over to this, Discover's older sibling component. Applied the same fix here: a new `refetching` state (true only on a mode-change refetch, once the podium has already loaded once) keeps the `ScrollView` permanently mounted — current page/scroll position never moves — with only a small overlay spinner during the refetch, instead of tearing the whole thing down.

**Exploratory question answered, not acted on**: asked what the optimal max count for Trending should be. Current: mobile requests `getPopularThisWeek(20, ...)` for both Movies and Series rails; backend caps at 40 but nothing currently requests past 20; `ContentRail.tsx` has no `onEndReached`/load-more, so whatever comes back is the hard ceiling for that session. 20 already lines up with what similar "Trending" rails elsewhere (TMDB, Letterboxd) typically use — recommended keeping it as-is rather than changing it speculatively; no code change made pending an actual decision.

Verified: `node --check` clean on both touched backend files; live JWT-minted requests against real seeded tiered accounts (Peter/dev, Sheridan+Zachary/plus, furkangg01/premium) confirmed `accountTier` now present and correct on both `GET /api/reviews/feed` and `GET /api/feed/activity` responses (a first single-page check on `getReviewsFeed` happened to return only `free`-tier authors, `None` for all — re-verified with a larger page size that found the tiered accounts, confirming the field really does flow through rather than accepting the first empty-looking result); `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `tierLabel`/diamond logic present in both `ReviewFeedCard.tsx` and `ActivityRow.tsx`'s own compiled modules, and `podiumLocked`/`refetching`/`lockBadge`/`blurRadius`/the subscription route all present in `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`/`LeaderboardCard.tsx`.

### Discover: Lists preview redesigned into a one-card-per-swipe pager, Premium gold frames extended to Reviews/Lists, and Activity gets real icon reuse + 4 brand-new event types (one tier-gated)

Two big, largely independent asks landed in the same round.

**Part 1 — Lists preview redesign + Premium gold frames.** Discover's Lists preview used to be `ListRailCard.tsx` inside a horizontal `ContentRail` — a poster-forward rail, several cards visible side by side. Replaced with new `ListsSwiper.tsx`, a real full-width one-card-per-swipe pager (same page-per-swipe + bobbing chevron-hint mechanism `ReviewsSwiper.tsx`/`LeaderboardPodium.tsx` already use) per direct ask to match Reviews' own "one at a time, swipe sideways" feel — each page renders `search/SearchListCard.tsx` (Search's own Lists tab card design — owner row, name, description, film strip, like/view footer), reused verbatim rather than rebuilt, per direct ask that this read as that exact design; its `basePath` prop widened from `"/search"`-only to `"/search" | "/home"` to allow this. `ListRailCard.tsx` itself deleted once nothing referenced it anymore (confirmed via grep — zero remaining imports/JSX usage anywhere).

Both `SearchListCard.tsx` and `ReviewSwipeCard.tsx` (Discover's Reviews preview card) gained the same Premium gold-frame treatment `ShareCard.tsx`'s posts already have — a hollow gradient-stroke SVG overlay (same `TIER_GOLD`/`TIER_GOLD_HIGHLIGHT` hex pair reused verbatim, not repicked) shown only when the list owner / reviewer's `accountTier === "premium"`, replacing the plain gray border those cards used unconditionally before. Backend: `accountTier` added to `customListRoute.js`'s owner projections in both `/discover` (its two `.populate()` calls) and `/popular` (its `$facet`-scoped `$lookup`) — `DiscoverListItem.owner` gained the field on the mobile side. Live-verified against a real premium-owned list ("Miraculous", owned by `furkangg01`) actually appearing in `/api/lists/popular`'s response with `accountTier: "premium"` intact.

**Part 2 — Activity's inline links fixed, icons redesigned, 4 new event types.** Reported live: `ActivityRow.tsx`'s tappable inline words (a list name, "favorites") sat visibly out of position, unlike `ShareCard.tsx`'s own inline "Watchlist" link in recommendation posts, which doesn't. Root cause: `ActivityRow.tsx`'s `renderLinkedSentence` embedded a `Pressable` inline inside `Text` with a hand-guessed `top: 2` nudge — this file's own prior-round doc comment had already flagged that exact approach as unverified, and `ShareCard.tsx` had *already* hit and fixed this identical problem in an earlier round by switching to a plain nested `Text` with its own `onPress` (no wrapper View sitting inside Text to fight its layout). Ported that same fix here instead of re-guessing another pixel value — the `inlineLinkWrap` fudge-factor style is gone entirely.

Icons: every existing type's bare "-outline" glyph replaced with a small circular badge (`iconWrap`, `colors.base200` background) holding a solid glyph in `colors.primary` — same treatment `PersonalActivityRow.tsx` (profile's own self-activity log) already uses, reused per direct ask ("kendi profilimizde açtığımız activitydeki simge tasarımları daha güzel"), scaled down (20px vs. Personal's 32px) to sit inline with the sentence text rather than as a row-leading element (this row already has `UserAvatar` for "who", the icon here only ever needs to say "what"). Icon choices for the 4 types shared with Personal (`rated`→star, `reviewed`→pencil, `watchlist_added`→checkmark-done) reuse its exact glyphs; the rest picked fresh in the same solid-glyph style.

Four new `ActivityEvent` types added, none of which `getNetworkActivity` tracked before:
1. **`towatch_added`** — the *real* Watchlist queue (`User.toWatchList`, distinct from the already-existing `watchlist_added`, which is this app's own inverted-naming "Watched List", `User.watchlist`). Same unwind-then-lookup aggregation shape `list_item_added` already used, just on a different array — no separate actor `$lookup` needed since the User document being unwound *is* the actor.
2. **`followed`** — no follow-timestamp field exists on `User.following`/`followers`, but one didn't need adding: `feedController.js`'s own (mobile-dead, kept for reference) `getFeed` already had a working "followed" event built off the `Notification` collection's own `type: "follow"` records, which every follow already creates with a real `createdAt`. Ported that exact query into `activityController.js` rather than adding a new schema field.
3. **`shared`** — Media posts (`Share` model), same `actorLookupStages` aggregation shape as `ratings`/`reviews`. Deliberately no content preview (a Share's real content shape varies too much by type — recommendation/review carry a poster, list/analysis don't) — just "shared a `{{type}}` to Media", the actual post is one tap away in Media's own feed.
4. **`podium`** — "so-and-so made the podium" news, **Plus/Premium-viewer-only** (`req.user.accountTier`, same plus/premium/dev-unlocked scope as every other tier gate in the app) — a Free viewer's response omits this event type server-side entirely, never a client-side hide. Live-verified both directions: Zachary (plus) received 7 podium events in one page; the exact same following-list content viewed as a known-Free account (`Camylle.Schuppe40266`) returned zero. **Deliberate design decision, flagged transparently**: this is a live status check, not a persisted event — a podium spot is a ranking that can change on the next request, not a one-time achievement with a natural "moment it happened" the way a rating/review/follow has. Implemented by reusing the *exact* ranking logic `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own Most Followed/Watched/Reviewed pages show (extracted from `feedController.js`'s `getPeopleLeaderboard` into a new shared `getPeopleThreePodiums()` export, called by both, so this can never silently drift from what the podium itself displays) rather than a second copy of that query — checks whether any of the caller's followed people are in the current top-3 of each category, synthesizes an activity item stamped `createdAt: now` for each hit. Surfaces near the top of the feed while genuinely true and simply stops appearing once that person drops out of the top 3 — no stale "made the podium" leftover from days ago, but also not a real historical timestamp; worth revisiting with a proper snapshot/diff system later if a persisted, one-time "achievement" framing turns out to matter more than staying live-accurate.

Also fixed while touching the union: two other consumers of `ActivityEvent` (`ActivityFeedSection.tsx`, `ActivitySection.tsx`) had their own `eventKey` helper unconditionally reading `.content.id` — a real compile break once content-less types existed, fixed with a per-type fallback distinguisher (`targetUser._id` for `followed`, `shareType` for `shared`, `` `${category}-${rank}` `` for `podium` — the last one specifically needed since multiple podium entries for the same actor in different categories otherwise share an identical "now" timestamp and would collide on a bare `type-actor-createdAt` key).

Translations: found and fixed a real **pre-existing** gap while adding these — `ActivityRow.tsx`'s existing sentence keys (`"for {{title}}"`, `"Added {{title}} to their watched list"`, `"Wrote a review for {{title}}"`, `"Added {{title}} to their favorites"`, `'Added {{title}} to their list "{{listName}}"'`) had never actually been added to `locales/index.ts` at all — every non-English viewer was silently seeing raw English text there this whole time (i18next's own fallback-to-key behavior masked it, since the keys are themselves written in English). Added those 5 alongside this round's own 7 new keys — 12 keys × all 12 locales (144 entries) — the podium sentence deliberately templated as one `"Made the {{category}} podium — #{{rank}}"` key with `{{category}}` interpolating `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own already-translated "Most Followed"/"Most Watched"/"Most Reviewed" titles rather than 3 separate hardcoded sentences, and the 4 "shared" sentences interpolating the already-translated "Media" nav-tab label the same way, rather than re-translating that brand word inside each new key.

Verified: `node --check` clean on all three touched backend files (`activityController.js`, `feedController.js`, `customListRoute.js`); live-hit `GET /api/feed/activity` confirmed all 4 new types appear with correct shapes for a plus-tier account (7 podium/4 followed/5 shared alongside the existing types) and confirmed `podium` is fully absent for a real free-tier account with an overlapping following list; `GET /api/feed/people-leaderboard` re-verified still working correctly after the `getPeopleThreePodiums` extraction; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `ListsSwiper.tsx` present, `isPremium`/the gold-gradient SVG id present in both `SearchListCard.tsx` and `ReviewSwipeCard.tsx`'s own compiled modules, `iconWrap`/`towatch_added`/`podium` present in `ActivityRow.tsx`'s, and the old `ListRailCard` import fully gone from `KesfetSection.tsx`'s (the only remaining bundle-wide hits traced to that file's own now-corrected historical comment). All 12 new/fixed translation keys spot-checked present across all 12 locale blocks.

**Immediate correction, same day: Discover's Lists preview was using the wrong reference design.** Reported live: "posta benziyo, see alldaki gibi olsun" — the swiper's card (`search/SearchListCard.tsx`, reused from Search per the *original* ask in this round) actually reads too much like a Media post; what was actually wanted is the exact same design the "See all" Lists page (`ListsSection.tsx`) already uses — `DiscoverListCard.tsx` — with only one addition: like/view counts in the box's own bottom-right, and per the same follow-up ask, that addition (plus the Premium gold frame from earlier in this round) should land on `DiscoverListCard.tsx` itself so the "See all" page picks it up too, not just this preview.

`ListsSwiper.tsx` switched from `search/SearchListCard.tsx` to `DiscoverListCard.tsx` (its `page` style gained its own `paddingHorizontal:16` in the process — `DiscoverListCard` has no side margin baked in, unlike `SearchListCard`, which relied on one since its usual home, a plain `FlatList`, doesn't supply it). `DiscoverListCard.tsx` itself gained: (1) a footer row with like (heart) + view (eye) counts next to the existing item count, same icons `SearchListCard.tsx`'s own footer already uses — previously just a bare item-count line; (2) the same Premium gold-frame SVG treatment (`isPremium` off `list.owner.accountTier`, same `TIER_GOLD` pair) `ShareCard.tsx`'s posts and `SearchListCard.tsx`/`ReviewSwipeCard.tsx` (added earlier this round) already carry — the existing plain gray border now only applies when the owner isn't Premium. Since `DiscoverListCard.tsx` is also reused by `ContentListsSection.tsx` (Content Detail's own "Lists" tab, across all 8 tabs it's duplicated into), both additions reach that surface too as a side effect, not just Discover/the "See all" page — not explicitly asked for there, but the same card design change naturally, harmlessly extends there too. `search/SearchListCard.tsx` itself (and its own Premium frame from earlier in this round) is untouched and still backs Search's own Lists tab — this correction was specifically about which *design* Discover's swiper uses, not a reason to undo Search's own already-correct one.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s own compiled module now contains `isPremium`/`engagementRow`/the gold-gradient SVG id, and `ListsSwiper.tsx`'s confirmed using `DiscoverListCard` with the old `SearchListCard` import fully gone (the one remaining bundle-wide hit traced to this file's own historical comment explaining the correction).

**Same-day follow-up correction: the previous round's own gold-frame addition to `DiscoverListCard.tsx` introduced two new regressions, both reported live.** (1) "şu an listlerin etrafında geri çerçeve var bu olmasın" — while adding the Premium gold-frame split, a plain gray `cardFrame` border (`borderWidth:1, borderColor: colors.placeholder`, shown whenever the owner isn't Premium) got copied in from `search/SearchListCard.tsx`'s own convention without checking that `DiscoverListCard.tsx` — like `ReviewSwipeCard.tsx` — never had any border at all for non-Premium cards. Fixed by removing the `cardFrame` style and its `!isPremium && styles.cardFrame` application entirely; non-Premium cards are now borderless again, in both the Popular Lists preview and the "See all" page (same shared component, one fix covers both). (2) "popular list kısmında liste kısmındaki posterleri kaydıramıyorum, list kartının kendisi kayıyor" — `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s film-strip poster row used a plain `react-native` `ScrollView`, which was fine as long as this card only ever sat inside `ListsSection.tsx`'s plain *vertical* ScrollView (orthogonal axis, no conflict). Once this same card got reused inside `ListsSwiper.tsx`'s gesture-handler-based horizontal one-card-per-swipe outer `ScrollView` (the very change from the entry above), the two horizontal scrollers shared an axis, and the outer pager — being gesture-handler-based — won the drag negotiation outright, making the inner poster strip fully unscrollable (dragging on it just swiped to the next list card instead). Fixed the same way this exact bug class has been fixed everywhere else in this app (see `ShareCard.tsx`'s own film strip, `home/index.tsx`'s doc comment): switched the film strip's `ScrollView` import to `react-native-gesture-handler`'s version, and — per the established rule that every `Pressable` directly ancestor to a gesture-handler scroller needs to itself be gesture-handler's version too, or it can claim the touch before the scroller ever gets a chance — also switched the card's own outer wrapping `Pressable` to gesture-handler's `Pressable` (aliased `GHPressable`). The individual poster thumbnails' own `Pressable`s inside the strip were left as plain `react-native` ones — they're children of the scroller being dragged, not ancestors of it, so they aren't part of this negotiation.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s own compiled module now imports `react-native-gesture-handler` (visible via its own `require(_dependencyMap[...], "react-native-gesture-handler")` line) and that the only remaining `cardFrame` string in the whole bundle traces to `search/SearchListCard.tsx`'s own unrelated, still-correct copy (Search's own Lists tab keeps its border by design, untouched by this fix).

**Same-day follow-up: list descriptions, description placement, and a real correction to how Premium/Plus is shown on Popular Lists/Popular Reviews.** Three separate asks: (1) every `CustomList` in the DB should have a real `description` — 18 of 25 lists had none (schema default `""`); backfilled via a new one-off `backend/scripts/backfillListDescriptions.js` (never overwrites a real, user-written description — only touches empty/missing ones, picks from a small/medium/large description-template pool based on the list's own item count so a 20-item list doesn't read like a 2-item one). (2) `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s description block moved to sit *above* the film strip (was below it) and gained `fontStyle: "italic"` — still only rendered when a description exists. (3) A real correction to the previous round's own Premium gold-frame addition on `DiscoverListCard.tsx`/`ReviewSwipeCard.tsx`: direct ask that the gold card-border SVG treatment (`TIER_GOLD`/`TIER_GOLD_HIGHLIGHT`, the hollow rounded-rect stroke) stay a `ShareCard.tsx` post-only signal — Popular Lists and Popular Reviews shouldn't have it at all. Both files' `premiumBorder`/`premiumBorderSvg`/`isPremium`/`TIER_GOLD*` were removed entirely. In its place: a new shared `TierAvatarFrame`-driven ring on the owner/reviewer avatar (via `UserAvatar`'s existing `tier` prop — both cards previously rendered a raw `<Image>`/fallback instead of `UserAvatar`, now switched over) plus a new `TierGradientText.tsx` component that paints the username itself with a metallic gradient fill, gold for Premium / silver for Plus, off the exact same `TIER_FRAME_STYLES` gradient pair the ring already uses (so "gold ring + gold name" reads as one consistent signal, not two different golds) — same underlying technique (`react-native-svg`'s `SvgText` with `fill="url(#...)"`) as `match/MatchGradientTitle.tsx`'s own Sync-results headline, just applied to a short inline label instead of a centered title. Since `react-native-svg`'s `<Text>` can't auto-size a canvas to arbitrary content the way RN's own `Text` can, `TierGradientText` estimates its own SVG canvas width from the label's character count (a hand-picked `CHAR_WIDTH_FACTOR`, same "generous canvas, not measured" spirit `MatchTitleBadge.tsx`/`MatchGradientTitle.tsx` already use) rather than doing a real text-measurement pass — acceptable here since usernames are short and bounded, unlike an LLM-generated title. Every gradient id is per-card-instance (`` `discoverListOwnerGradient-${list._id}` `` / `` `reviewSwipeUsernameGradient-${review._id}` ``), not a shared hardcoded id — necessary since, unlike the match feature's own small fixed card deck, these cards render in long scrollable lists with many simultaneously-mounted instances (same collision risk `MatchGradientTitle.tsx`'s own doc comment already flags). Falls back to a plain flat-colored `Text` when the user has no gradient-eligible tier (free/none/dev — `TIER_FRAME_STYLES` has no `dev`... actually it does, dev gets its own purple/magenta ring but `TierGradientText` only defines gold/plus visually meaningfully for plus/premium; dev's own ring color still applies via `TierAvatarFrame` regardless, `TierGradientText` just renders dev usernames as plain text since no gradient stop pair was asked for there).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `TierGradientText` present, the old `premiumDiscoverListGradient`/`premiumReviewCardGradient` SVG ids fully gone from the bundle, the new per-instance `discoverListOwnerGradient-`/`reviewSwipeUsernameGradient-` ids present, and both gold (`#FFC94A`) and silver (`#F2F3F5`) `TIER_FRAME_STYLES` colors reachable from the compiled bundle.

**Same-day, backend: Discover was thinning out ("discover sayfası boşalmaya başladı") — a broader re-run and real extension of `backend/scripts/seedMediaActivity.js`.** This dev-only, re-runnable seed script already existed from an earlier round; extended rather than forked, since its own doc comment already describes exactly this recurring need. Changes: (1) active user set widened from 15 extra accounts to 70 (96 of 97 real users touched this run, up from ~38); (2) a new follows step — ~60% of active users follow 1-4 new (public-visibility) accounts, updating both sides' `following`/`followers` arrays and creating the same `Notification{type:"follow"}` `followUser()` itself creates, so new follows surface in the Activity feed too, not just raw follower counts — 135 new relationships this run (`usersWithFollows` 23→70); (3) the `CONTENT_POOL` gained 10 fresh, well-known titles (The Dark Knight, Inception, Interstellar, Parasite, Everything Everywhere All at Once, Dune: Part Two, Breaking Bad, Chernobyl, The Last of Us, Stranger Things) with a concentrated extra boost pass (high ratings + favorites + recommend-shares from ~45 users) on 4 of them specifically so Discover's content podium (Most Favorited/Highest Rated/Most Recommended) visibly reshuffles instead of just reinforcing whatever already led — live-confirmed via `GET /feed/leaderboard`: Parasite and Breaking Bad now sit in `mostFavorited`'s top 3; (4) a favorites-churn step — some users remove one existing favorite and add a different one, direct ask ("favorilerine bişey çıkartıp eklesinler") rather than favorites only ever accumulating; the first version of this step gated removal on the favorite being one of `CONTENT_POOL`'s ~31 items, which barely ever matched a user's *real* pre-existing favorites and produced 0 churns on the live run — fixed to track `favoriteMovies`/`favoriteSeries` as separate real sets and remove directly from whichever the user actually has, no `CONTENT_POOL` intersection required (confirmed via a small standalone follow-up pass: 25 of 89 eligible users churned); (5) seeded lists now get a real paired name+description from `LIST_TEMPLATES` at creation (was `description: ""`) and 7-14 items each (was 3-6), matching this round's other ask that lists carry real, sizeable content. End-to-end DB movement this round: lists 25→47 (0 without a description, backfill + new lists combined), shares 72→199, reviews 76→121, ratings 4244→4507, users with any follow 23→70.

**Same-day, backend: balanced `accountTier` distribution — a new `backend/scripts/balanceAccountTiers.js`.** Direct ask ("3 tip kullanıcıyı da görmek istiyorum") — most of the user base (83 of 97) had no `accountTier` set at all (the schema's `'free'` default was never actually backfilled onto them at the DB level, only applied to brand-new documents going forward), so almost every tier-gated surface built this session (podium blur, avatar rings, `TierGradientText`, the Premium post gold-frame) had very few real Plus/Premium accounts to actually show. Script splits every non-`dev` user except `Zachary.Macejkovic73330` (left untouched — one of this project's two standing named test accounts, and other rounds of testing assume his current tier) into three shuffled, roughly-equal groups and sets `accountTier`/`tierUpdatedAt` accordingly. Result: 31 free / 31 plus / 32 premium (plus the 3 pre-existing `dev` accounts, also untouched). Re-running it re-shuffles the same 93 users again — it's a distribution tool, not a one-time migration, safe to run again whenever the tier mix needs refreshing.

**Same-day, mobile: a real bug in `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s owner row — noticeable gap between the Premium/Plus username and the avatar, reported live.** Root cause: `TierGradientText` (added earlier this same round) can't auto-size its SVG canvas to its own rendered glyph width the way RN's plain `Text` can (`react-native-svg`'s `Text` has no such intrinsic-sizing behavior — see that component's own doc comment), so it estimates a canvas width from the label's character count instead; that estimate runs a bit wide. `ReviewSwipeCard.tsx` never showed this because its row order is avatar-then-username — any overestimate trails off after the username with nothing next to it to visibly crowd. `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s `ownerRow` had the opposite order (username-then-avatar, preserved from this card's original pre-existing layout), so that same overestimate showed up as visible dead space *before* the avatar instead — only visible for Plus/Premium owners specifically, since a free owner's plain-`Text` fallback branch sizes to content correctly regardless of order. Fixed by reordering `ownerRow` to avatar-then-username, matching `ReviewSwipeCard.tsx`'s own working order exactly, per direct ask ("aynı popular reviewstaki gibi") — free-tier owners render identically either way (their branch doesn't use the estimated-width canvas at all), so this is a pure fix for Plus/Premium with no regression for Free.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle (confirmed via content hash, not just byte size, since both bundles happened to be the same total size) shows `UserAvatar`'s own `createElement` call now landing before `TierGradientText`'s within `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s compiled module, matching the new JSX order. Live-verified the tier distribution via `User.aggregate` grouped by `accountTier`.

**Same-day follow-up: the avatar-then-username reorder above turned out not to be what was actually wanted, plus two more real fixes in the same round.**

(1) **Order corrected back, gap fixed properly instead of just avoided.** Direct correction: the owner's avatar should sit immediately to the *right* of where the username ends (name-then-avatar, `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s original order), not avatar-then-name — the earlier reorder fixed the visible symptom by avoiding it structurally, not by fixing `TierGradientText`'s own imprecision. Replaced the character-count width *estimate* with a real measurement: an invisible plain RN `Text` (which *can* auto-size to its own content) reports its true rendered width via `onLayout`, and the SVG only mounts once that measurement lands — exact regardless of font metrics or string content, not a hand-picked `CHAR_WIDTH_FACTOR` anymore. `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s `ownerRow` swapped back to `TierGradientText` (name) then `UserAvatar` (avatar), which is now safe since there's no more excess canvas width to leave a gap. `ReviewSwipeCard.tsx` needed no change (its own order was never the actual problem, just the reason the bug wasn't visible there). The row's own top-right position within the card (`topRow`'s `justifyContent:"space-between"`) was already correct and untouched — confirmed, not modified.

(2) **Plus's "silver" ring/gradient-name didn't read as metallic, reported live** ("hiç gümüş hissi vermiyor... altın çerçevedeki o efekt çok iyi altın hissi veriyor"). Root cause: `TIER_FRAME_STYLES.plus`'s gradient (`#F2F3F5`→`#C7CBD1`) was a straight copy of `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`'s own rank-2 medal silver — two close, low-saturation grays with very little tonal contrast, unlike Premium's own gold pair (`#FFF3C4`→`#FFC94A`), which spans near-white to a properly saturated gold and reads as "shiny" from that contrast alone. Widened Plus's own range the same way — near-white highlight (`#FAFBFC`) to a clearly darker, cool-toned steel gray (`#6E7580`), `glowColor` bumped to `#9099A6` to match — same 2-stop formula as gold, just silver's own hue instead of adding new gradient stops or changing the underlying technique. `theme/tierFrames.ts` is the single source of truth for this (both `TierAvatarFrame`'s ring and `TierGradientText`'s username fill read from it), so both picked up the richer silver automatically. `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`'s own `MEDAL_COLORS[2]`/`MEDAL_HIGHLIGHT_COLORS[2]` (and `LeaderboardCard.tsx`'s matching copy) are separate, rank-based constants by this app's own established "don't share a small repeated pattern" convention — deliberately left untouched, since this ask was specifically about the Plus *tier* signal, not podium rank medals (a Free user can rank #2 on a podium and get that silver medal regardless of their own account tier).

(3) **Real bug, not a UI scroll bug: list-type Shares in Media only ever showed ~5 posters in the film strip no matter how many the underlying list had, reported live** ("fazlaca item olmasına rağmen rayda 5 tane falan gözüküyor kaydıramıyorum"). `ShareCard.tsx`'s own film strip already correctly uses a `react-native-gesture-handler` `ScrollView` (fixed and documented earlier this session) — there was nothing to scroll to because only 5 items were ever included in the post's own `listData.previewItems` snapshot in the first place. Root-caused to this session's own `seedMediaActivity.js`: its list-share creation step built `previewItems` with a hardcoded `.slice(0, 5)`, diverging from the real `POST /shares` list-share endpoint (`shareController.js`), which already deliberately calls `hydratePreviewItems(list, 20)` — "Bigger limit than the default 5... not a fixed small preview count," per that endpoint's own pre-existing comment. So this was never a real ShareCard.tsx bug, just a seed-script one. Fixed in two parts: `seedMediaActivity.js`'s own slice raised from 5 to 20 (matching the real endpoint) so future runs don't repeat this; and a new one-off `backend/scripts/fixListSharePreviewItems.js` re-hydrated all 36 existing list-shares' `listData.previewItems` using the exact same `hydratePreviewItems` helper the real endpoint uses, so already-seeded posts got fixed immediately rather than waiting for a future reseed. Live-verified via `GET /shares/feed`: list-shares now carry 8-15 preview items each (matching their real list's own item count), not capped at 5.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `TierGradientText`'s compiled module now uses `onLayout`/measured-width state instead of the old character-count estimate, `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s module shows `TierGradientText` created before `UserAvatar` again (name-then-avatar), and the new silver hex values (`#FAFBFC`/`#6E7580`/`#9099A6`) are present in the bundle (the old flat pair `#F2F3F5`/`#C7CBD1` still appears elsewhere, correctly — that's `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`/`LeaderboardCard.tsx`'s own separate rank-medal constants, untouched by design). `GET /shares/feed` live-checked post-fix: list-shares return 8-15 `previewItems` matching their real list size.

**Same-day: Free-tier podium locking rebuilt from a leaky blur into a real "frame-only" upgrade teaser.** Raised as an exploratory question first ("free kullanıcılar podyumdaki profilleri görüntüleyemiyor ama... kendisi çıktıysa yine de göstermeyelim mi", plus the blur-still-shows-the-name complaint from the round above) — recommended and approved: (a) a viewer's *own* podium entry should stay visible to them even on Free, since it's their own data, not something to gate; (b) replace the blur (which never actually hid anything meaningful — title/username/metric all rendered in plain text right below the blurred image) with an empty "skeleton" podium — rank-medal gradient frames with nothing inside, no name, no count — so there's no leak at all, paired with an upgrade banner, category icons, and a real CTA button; (c) for the movie/series content podium specifically, leave one of the 3 categories fully open (real posters, no lock) rather than gating all 3, a direct ask to make the paywall itself more enticing — **Highest Rated** was the one picked (an assistant judgment call, not specified by the user): it's the closest thing to an "objective quality signal" that can be found elsewhere anyway, while Most Favorited/Most Recommended (community-specific, exclusive-to-this-app signals) stay the actual upgrade bait.

Two new shared components: `PodiumSkeletonSlot.tsx` (an empty rank-medal-framed placeholder — same gradient-stroke-+-glow technique and `MEDAL_COLORS`/`MEDAL_HIGHLIGHT_COLORS` pair as `LeaderboardCard.tsx`/`PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`, duplicated per this app's own established "small repeated pattern, don't share it" convention, just filled with a blank `colors.base300` shape and no text) and `PodiumUpgradeTeaser.tsx` (the auto-cross-fading — not swiped, a passive tease — carousel between 2-3 categories: banner text via a new templated key, `Animated.timing` opacity crossfade on a plain `setInterval`, a row of category icons with the active one highlighted, and an "Upgrade Now" button routing to `/match/subscription`; a slot can carry a `selfNode` — already-built real `PeoplePodiumCard`/`LeaderboardCard` markup — instead of a blank frame, which is how the "show my own entry" exception actually renders inside an otherwise-empty category).

`PeoplePodium.tsx` (Media's Most Followed/Watched/Reviewed): Free viewers now get a completely separate render branch — no manual swipe/paging, no mode toggle (not meaningful when nothing but a possible self-entry is ever shown) — just the teaser, cycling through all 3 categories. Each category's 3 slots compare `item.user.id` against the viewer's own `user._id`; a match renders a real, fully-visible `PeoplePodiumCard` (`locked={false}`) in that one slot, everything else stays a blank `PodiumSkeletonSlot`. Plus/Premium/dev keep the exact swipeable UI from before, byte-for-byte unchanged (the branch is a hard `if (podiumLocked) return (...)` placed after all hooks, not a prop threaded deeper in).

`LeaderboardPodium.tsx` (Discover's Most Favorited/Highest Rated/Most Recommended): Free viewers get Highest Rated rendered as a real, always-open row (no lock, `locked={false}` unconditionally) above a hairline divider, with the movie/series mode toggle still functional above it; below the divider, `PodiumUpgradeTeaser` cycles between just Most Favorited and Most Recommended. Content has no "viewer's own entry" concept (a user can't rank on a movie/series podium), so every teaser slot here is always a blank frame — no `selfNode` branch needed, unlike `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own version. Same "hard early return, Plus/Premium/dev path untouched" structure.

Translations: 3 new keys × all 12 locales (36 entries) — `"Podium"` (the Free-tier section's own title, since `titles[page]` isn't meaningful without a page to be on), `"Upgrade to Plus or Premium to see {{category}}"` (one templated sentence with the active category's own already-translated label interpolated in, same pattern as the Activity feed's own `"Made the {{category}} podium — #{{rank}}"` key from earlier this session — deliberately not built from smaller fragment keys like "Upgrade to"/"Plus"/"or"/"Premium" stitched together, which risks broken word order in languages with different grammar), and `"Upgrade Now"` (the button label).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (including a real type-correctness fix along the way — `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s self-comparison originally read `user?.id`, but this app's own `User` type uses `_id`, not `id`); a fresh Metro bundle confirmed both new components present, both new translation keys reachable in the bundle (13 hits each — 12 locale definitions + this file's own `t(...)` call site), and the new silver-teaser's `podiumSkeletonGradient` id present. Not screenshot-verified in a running Expo Go session (this session's own established convention for RN changes — see repeated notes elsewhere in this doc — is tsc + a real compiled-bundle check + live backend data checks, not a browser, since there is no browser for a native app); the user drives visual confirmation from their own device.

**Same-day follow-up: the Discover (content) podium's Free-tier layout reworked again, same day — the stacked "open row + divider + teaser" version above wasn't actually what was wanted.** Direct correction: "açık olan kategori altında reklam var. ayrı ayrı olmasın. kaydırmalı yapıyı koru" — the two pieces (Highest Rated's real row, and the Favorited/Recommended teaser) had been stacked simultaneously in one static view; the ask was to go back to a genuinely swipeable structure instead, one page at a time, with the side arrow hints restored. `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`'s Free-tier branch is now a real 2-page `pagingEnabled` `ScrollView` (`FREE_PAGE_COUNT = 2`), reusing the exact same `scrollRef`/`page`/`handleScroll`/`goToPage`/`bobAnim` machinery the original 3-page Plus/Premium view already has (no new state duplicated) — page 1 is Highest Rated, completely unchanged from before; page 2 is a single "ad card" reached by swiping over.

Two more changes to that ad card, both direct asks: (1) **the banner text was two separate rotating sentences** ("to see Most Favorited" / "to see Most Recommended", swapping via the old `PodiumUpgradeTeaser`'s cross-fade) — merged into one static sentence naming both categories at once ("to see Most Recommended and Most Favorited," matching the user's own given phrasing/order), via a new templated key (`"Upgrade to Plus or Premium to see {{first}} and {{second}}"`, `first`/`second` interpolated with the already-translated category labels — same "one full sentence, not fragments" reasoning as the round above). (2) **The bottom-row "which category is active" icon dots were replaced entirely** — direct ask: "mevcut podyum yapısı gibi olsun, her çerçevenin altına mevcut sembolü koy, şu anki sembol yapısını kaldır" (make it read like the real podium's own convention — the real `LeaderboardCard`'s own metric row, an icon directly under *each* card/frame — not a separate category-selector strip at the bottom). `PodiumSkeletonSlot.tsx` gained two new optional props, `metricIcon`/`metricIconOpacity`, rendering that icon right below the platform line — the same position a real card's own metric icon sits — with the amount of animation intentionally narrowed: **only this one small icon cross-fades** (`Animated.timing` opacity, a plain `setInterval` alternating `"star"`⇄`"gift"` inside `LeaderboardPodium.tsx` itself, `TEASER_ICON_CYCLE_MS`/`TEASER_ICON_FADE_MS`), the frames underneath it stay completely static — direct ask ("smooth geçiş işlemi sadece bu iki tür semboller üzerinde olacak") that the earlier version's whole-row cross-fade was more motion than intended.

Since this content podium no longer uses `PodiumUpgradeTeaser.tsx` at all (dropped in favor of the real paging ScrollView + a directly-authored ad page), that component and its own category-icon-dots/whole-row-crossfade behavior are now used **only** by `PeoplePodium.tsx` — left completely untouched this round, since the correction was scoped explicitly to Discover's own podium ("discoverydeki podyumla başlayalım," a "let's start with" that leaves the door open for `PeoplePodium.tsx` to get an equivalent pass later, just not yet asked for).

**Same-day, third pass on the ad page — a real bug this time, not just a design preference.** Direct report: "metinde şu an sadece recomended and most favorited yazıyor" (the banner sentence's own lead-in, "Upgrade to Plus or Premium to see", was missing — only the tail end showed). Fixed properly, not just papered over, by combining it with two other direct asks from the same report: (1) the "Podium" placeholder title for page 2 was pointless (nothing meaningful to call this page) — "reklam kartındaki podium başlığına gerek yok, o hizadan direkt reklam metniyle başlat" — so the *banner sentence itself* now renders inside `titleRow` (a new `adBannerTitle` style, `flex:1`, multi-line, replacing `titles[page]` on page 2) instead of inside the height-constrained page content; `titleRow` has no fixed height of its own, so a longer wrapped sentence there just grows the row instead of ever risking the old clipping again. **Same-day: three more direct reports on the new podium ad pages — a real clipping bug, a spacing inconsistency, and a centering bug specific to `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`.**

(1) **"podyumdaki profillerin kenarlarında hafif kesilme var"** — `PodiumSkeletonSlot.tsx`'s own gradient-stroke ring is drawn on a `Rect` inset at 1-1.5% with `strokeWidth={3}`; since an SVG stroke straddles its own path (half the width extends outward, half inward), the outer half of that stroke mathematically sits slightly *past* the nominal Rect bounds — at this component's own smaller sizes (46-76px, vs. the real `LeaderboardCard`/`PeoplePodiumCard`'s own 68-108px, where the exact same math produces a much smaller and easy-to-miss overflow), that sliver was large enough as a fraction of the ring's own size to read as visible clipping. Same root cause (and same fix) as `TierGradientText.tsx`/`MatchTitleBadge.tsx`'s own `overflow: "visible"` Svg style elsewhere in this app — added to `PodiumSkeletonSlot.tsx`'s `frameSvg` style.

(2) **"reklam kartındaki profil çerçeveleri arası mesafe çok fazla"** — a real inconsistency between the two files this round's own porting missed: `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`'s ad page already used a tight `justifyContent:"center", gap:14` for its 3 skeleton frames, but `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own port used `justifyContent:"space-evenly", width:"100%"` instead (a leftover from that file's own *real* card row style, `styles.page`, copied without adjusting) — spreading its now-smaller (46-60px) avatars across the entire row width with far more gap than intended. (3) **"discover podyumundaki reklam metinini ortalamamışsın... aynı profildeki reklam metni gibi ortada olacak"** — `adBannerTitle` already had `textAlign:"center"` (added last round), so this wasn't a missing style, it was a real layout bug: `titleRow` also always renders the movie/series mode toggle `Pressable` (kept permanently mounted even when hidden, per this file's own established "never conditionally unmount — that caused a real vertical-jump bug once already" rule), and on the ad page that Pressable is invisible (`opacity:0`) but was still a *normal flex sibling*, still reserving its own width on the row's right side. `adBannerTitle`'s `flex:1` + `textAlign:"center"` was therefore centering the text within a narrower box (row width minus the toggle's reserved space), not the row's true full width — so the sentence visibly drifted left of center. `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own ad page never had this problem since it has no mode toggle at all on that branch (nothing competing for width), which is exactly why it looked correctly centered and became the reference the report compared against. Fixed with a new `modeToggleAbsolute` style (`position:"absolute", right:0`), applied alongside `modeToggleHidden` only on the ad page — the toggle stays mounted (preserving the original vertical-jump fix) but stops participating in the row's flex layout once hidden, so the banner text can truly center across the full row width without touching the toggle's own real page-0 layout at all.

**Same-day, two more direct reports: the edge-clipping fix from the round above didn't actually work, and a real "platform line shifts vertically while swiping" bug on both podiums.**

(1) **"profillerin etrafındaki o kesilmeyi giderememişsin... özellikle reklam kartında profil yuvarlağının etrafında belirgin kesilme var."** `overflow:"visible"` on the Svg alone (the previous round's fix) turned out not to be enough — the clipping was real and still visible, especially at the ad page's own smaller sizes. Root-caused more precisely and fixed geometrically instead of relying on the overflow style to do the work: an SVG stroke straddles its own path (half its width renders outside the path's nominal bounds), and the old percentage-based inset (`x="1.5"`/`"97%"` etc.) left less margin than `strokeWidth`'s own overflow needed, especially at this component's small sizes (46-76px) where that shortfall is a much bigger fraction of the ring's total size than on the real cards' own larger 68-108px avatars/posters. `PodiumSkeletonSlot.tsx` now gives its own `Svg` canvas a real `STROKE_MARGIN` (4px) of extra space past the visible shape on every side (negative `left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom` insets), and draws the `Rect` with fixed pixel coordinates (`x`/`y` = `STROKE_MARGIN`, `width`/`height` = the true `size`) instead of percentages — the stroke's own outer edge now always lands measurably inside the Svg's own larger canvas, not relying on `overflow:"visible"` to rescue an already-too-tight fit (kept as a defensive fallback regardless).

(2) **"açık podyumdan reklam metni olan kısma kaydırınca alt çizgide aşağı doğru hafif kayma oluyor... hem discoverydeki hem de sharesteki podyum için geçerli."** Root cause: page 1 (the open category)'s real cards are bottom-anchored within their fixed-height page (`alignItems:"flex-end"`), so their platform line always lands a fixed distance above the page's own bottom edge — specifically, however tall that card's own title-or-username row + metric row are (≈37px on both `LeaderboardCard.tsx`'s and `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`'s own layouts). The ad page, introduced two rounds ago, top-aligned its own content instead (`justifyContent:"flex-start"`, to fix an earlier clipping bug in the banner text that has since moved out entirely into `titleRow`) — meaning its own platform line sat at a completely different, much-higher Y position than page 1's, which read as a visible vertical jump precisely at the moment of swiping between the two. Fixed by abandoning flex-alignment tricks for this entirely and switching to pixel-precise absolute positioning: a new `CARD_BOTTOM_RESERVE` constant (37, matching the real cards' own trailing-content height on both files) positions `adFrameRow` via `position:"absolute", bottom: CARD_BOTTOM_RESERVE` — landing its own platform line at *exactly* the same distance from the page's bottom edge as page 1's real cards, by construction, not by coincidence — with the upgrade button in its own separately absolutely-positioned `adButtonWrap` (`bottom: 2`) underneath it, decoupled from the frame row's own exact height entirely.
