**Same day, the big one: both podiums grew from 3 categories to 5, and gained a real 3-way Free/Plus/Premium visibility split instead of a plain locked/unlocked boolean.** Raised as an exploratory question first ("podyumlara daha fazla başka ne gibi kategoriler ekleyebiliriz... discovery ve shares için ayrı ayrı düşünelim") — recommended and approved: Discover gained **Most Watched** and **Most Reviewed** (content-side twins of the people podium's own identically-named categories — how many watchlists/reviews a *title* has, not a person), Shares/Media gained **Most Liked** (total likes received across a user's own Shares) and **Top Recommenders** (count of `type:"recommendation"` Shares sent) — all 4 built from data/aggregation patterns already established elsewhere in this same session (`getPeopleThreePodiums`'s own Most Watched/Most Reviewed queries mirrored for content; `Share.likeCount`/`Share.type` already indexed and used elsewhere), no new schema needed. "5 is an optimal round number" was the user's own follow-up, alongside a new tier idea: since there are now 5 categories, split visibility three ways instead of Free-locked/Plus-and-Premium-unlocked — **Free sees 1 open + 4 teased, Plus sees 3 open + 2 teased, Premium/dev see all 5 open** — which category deserves to be in which tier was left to the assistant's judgment: Highest Rated (content) / Most Reviewed (people) stay Free's own single open category exactly as before; **Plus** additionally unlocks Most Watched + Most Reviewed (content) / Most Watched + Most Followed (people) — the "objective app-usage stats" trio, mirroring the same reasoning Free's own original pick used; **Premium** is the only tier that sees Most Favorited/Most Recommended (content) and Most Liked/Top Recommenders (people) — kept as the genuinely exclusive, community-taste/social-standing signals reserved as the strongest upgrade bait.

**Backend** (`backend/controllers/feedController.js`): `getLeaderboard` gained 2 more parallel aggregations (`watchedStats` — `$unwind` on `User.watchlist`, grouped by content, mirroring `getPeopleThreePodiums`' own watchedCount logic but per-title instead of per-user; `reviewedStats` — `Review` grouped by `contentId`/`contentType`) alongside the original 3, all still respecting the optional `?type=` filter exactly like the existing 3 already did. `getPeopleThreePodiums` gained `likedRaw` (`Share` grouped by `user`, summed `likeCount`) and `recommendersRaw` (`Share` filtered to `type:"recommendation"`, grouped by `user`, counted) — a new small `hydratePeopleEntries(raw, metricKey)` helper replaced what would otherwise have become 3 near-identical copies of the existing "bulk `User.find` by `_id`, map through" hydration step (`mostReviewed`/`mostLiked`/`topRecommenders` all use it now). `activityController.js`'s own "so-and-so made the podium" activity news was deliberately left untouched — it still only checks the original 3 categories; extending it to the 2 new ones per podium wasn't asked for this round.

**Mobile types** (`mobile/src/types/index.ts`): `LeaderboardResult` gained `mostWatched`/`mostReviewed` (`WatchedLeaderboardItem`/`ReviewedLeaderboardItem`, both wrapping the same shared `LeaderboardContent` shape the existing 3 already use); `PeopleLeaderboardResult` gained `mostLiked`/`topRecommenders` (`MostLikedItem`/`TopRecommenderItem`, both wrapping the shared `PodiumUser` shape). `LeaderboardCard.tsx`'s own `LeaderboardMetric` union and `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`'s own `PeopleMetric` union each gained 2 new variants + a metric-row icon apiece — `watched`→`eye`/`reviewed`→`create` on the content card (reusing Ionicons already used elsewhere for the exact same concepts), `liked`→`heart`/`recommended`→`gift` on the people card (`gift` deliberately matching the content podium's own `recommended` icon, since it's the same underlying concept — recommending something — just viewed from the person's side instead of the title's side).

**`LeaderboardPodium.tsx`/`PeoplePodium.tsx` — both fully rewritten around one unified, tier-driven `pages` array instead of the old "hand-written locked branch + hand-written full branch" duplication.** With 3 tiers × up to 5 categories, keeping 2-3 separate hard-coded JSX branches (as every earlier round of this feature had) would have meant real, growing duplication risk; each file now derives a single `CategoryKey` union (5 fixed keys, one shared `categoryMeta` record of `{title, icon}` per key, one `podiumByKey` record of each category's own fetched-and-`toPodiumOrder`'d list) and a `PodiumPage[]` array — `{type:"real", key}` for every category `OPEN_KEYS_BY_TIER[tierLevel]` includes, then one trailing `{type:"ad", lockedKeys}` merging whatever's left (omitted entirely for Premium/dev, whose `lockedKeys` is empty — this is what makes their own page count naturally stay at exactly 5 with no ad page, matching the original behavior byte-for-byte in spirit). One `ScrollView` maps over `pages` — real pages render exactly like before (a `renderRealCard`/`renderRealCard`+`renderAdSlot` switch per file, since each category's item shape differs enough that unifying them into one polymorphic array fights TypeScript's own union-narrowing, the same lesson learned the hard way in an earlier round — kept as an explicit `switch` instead), the ad page renders the same `PodiumSkeletonSlot` row + banner-in-`titleRow` + button design from the rounds above, just now driven by `lockedKeys.length` instead of a hardcoded "2 categories" assumption. The ad page's own banner/icon-cycling logic now branches on count: exactly 2 locked categories (Plus, both podiums) gets the existing static "X and Y" merged sentence; 3+ locked categories (Free, both podiums — 4 in practice) cycles one category at a time (reusing the single-category `"Upgrade to Plus or Premium to see {{category}}"` key from an early, since-superseded round of this same feature, never actually deleted from the locale files) in lockstep with the frame row's own icon, both driven by the same `adCategoryIndex`/`teaserFadeAnim` state. `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`'s mode toggle simplified in the process — every one of its 5 categories now respects `?type=` (unlike the people podium, where only Most Watched does), so the toggle just shows whenever any *real* page is active, no more single-page-index special case.

Translations: 2 new keys (`"Most Liked"`, `"Top Recommenders"`) × all 12 locales (24 entries), same anchor-based insertion script used for every other batch this session.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on both podium files (a real generalization risk was caught and avoided early — trying to unify `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s 5 differently-shaped category item types into one array of `{podium, metric()}` objects hit the exact same "calling a union of differently-typed functions" TypeScript error a much earlier round already hit and fixed the same way, so the `switch`-based `renderRealCard` approach was used from the start this time instead of re-discovering the same dead end). Live-hit `GET /feed/leaderboard` and `GET /feed/people-leaderboard` (Zachary, premium) — both now return all 5 categories each with real hydrated data (confirmed titles/usernames present, not just raw ids/counts). A fresh Metro bundle confirmed `tierLevel` and all 5 category keys present in both files' own compiled modules, and both new translation keys reachable.

**Same-day, immediate correction: the ad banner's own "Upgrade to Plus or Premium" wording became factually wrong the moment tiers stopped being interchangeable.** Direct report: once Plus and Premium unlock genuinely different sets of categories, telling *every* viewer "Upgrade to Plus or Premium to see X" is misleading in both directions — a Free viewer being teased a Premium-only category (Most Favorited, Most Recommended, Most Liked, Top Recommenders) would upgrade to Plus and still not see it; a Plus viewer (whose only locked categories are always the Premium-only pair) doesn't need "Plus" at all, they specifically need Premium. Rather than compute which exact tier name to show per category per viewer (real complexity for a one-line banner), both templated keys had their tier name(s) removed entirely — `"Upgrade to Plus or Premium to see {{category}}"` → `"Upgrade to see {{category}}"`, `"...{{first}} and {{second}}"` → matching — staying accurate for every viewer/category combination without needing to know which specific tier unlocks what. Only the *values* changed, not the key strings themselves (kept as before, purely internal identifiers — no call-site changes needed in either podium file), across all 12 locales.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed both new generic English values (`"Upgrade to see {{category}}"`/`"Upgrade to see {{first}} and {{second}}"`) are reachable, and grepping the locale file confirmed zero remaining "Plus or Premium" occurrences outside the two (unchanged, purely internal) key strings.

**Same-day: a real centering bug specifically on `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own ad banner, plus a small tone tweak on both podiums.** (1) "sharesteki podyumun reklam metnini tam ortalayamadın, aynı discoverydeki reklam metni gibi ortada olsun" — root cause: the 5-category rewrite brought the movie/series mode toggle back into `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own `titleRow` (needed for the Most Watched category, which does have a type dimension), but unlike `LeaderboardPodium.tsx`'s own toggle, this file's copy never got the `modeToggleAbsolute` treatment that fix required — so the hidden toggle was still a normal flex sibling reserving its own width on the ad page, pulling `adBannerTitle`'s own centered text off-true-center, the exact same bug class already fixed once in the other file. An earlier doc comment on this file had even claimed "no competing sibling ... unlike LeaderboardPodium.tsx's own mode toggle," which was accurate when originally written but went stale the moment the toggle came back in the 5-category rewrite and was never revisited — corrected now, comment included. Fixed identically: `modeToggleAbsolute` (`position:"absolute", right:0`) added and applied alongside `modeToggleHidden` whenever the active page isn't the real Most Watched one. (2) "podyumlardaki reklam metinlerinin sonuna ünlem işareti koyarak daha samimi bir ton yakalayalım" — both templated banner values gained a trailing `!` across all 12 locales (24 entries) — e.g. `"Upgrade to see {{category}}"` → `"Upgrade to see {{category}}!"` — a pure content tweak, no new keys, no call-site changes, covers both podiums automatically since they share these same keys.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; a fresh Metro bundle confirmed `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own compiled module now includes `modeToggleAbsolute`, and both banner templates' English values now end in `!` in the compiled output.

**Same-day: a new "you made the podium!" popup — checks the current user's own placement across the people podium's 5 categories at app launch, and taps through straight into the real (or ad-page, if locked for that viewer's own tier) podium page.** A genuinely new feature, not a tweak — direct spec: "eğer kullanıcı podyumda yer alıyorsa uygulamaya giriş yaptığı anda ekranın ortasında bir haber penceresi olacak... tap to see it... butona basıldığında sharesteki o podyuma kaysın... eğer kullanıcı free ve plus ise ve kilitli olan podyumda yer aldıysa reklamlı karta atsın."

**Backend**: new `GET /feed/my-podium-placements` (`backend/controllers/feedController.js`, registered in `backend/routes/feedRoute.js`) reuses `getPeopleThreePodiums(null)` — the *exact* same ranking `getPeopleLeaderboard` itself already returns, not a second, potentially-drifting copy (same reasoning `activityController.js`'s own `getFollowedPodiumEvents` already documents for doing the same thing) — and checks the requesting user's own id against all 5 categories' top-3, returning every placement found (a user can rank on more than one podium at once), each as `{category, rank}`. `category` uses the same field names `PeopleLeaderboardResult` itself already has (`mostFollowed`/`mostWatched`/`mostReviewed`/`mostLiked`/`topRecommenders`), not `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own shorter `CategoryKey` union — the mobile side owns that mapping (see below), keeping the backend's own response shape consistent with its sibling endpoint rather than baking in a client-side naming convention.

**Mobile — the popup itself**: new `src/components/PodiumNewsModal.tsx`, mounted once inside `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` (`AppLayout`) as a sibling of `<Tabs>` — this is the natural "user is authenticated, tabs are about to render" gate already used for the login redirect, and since `AppLayout` only unmounts on logout, mounting `PodiumNewsModal` here means the placement check naturally runs "once per real app session" (a fresh login) with no separate persisted "already shown" flag needed — this codebase has no `AsyncStorage` usage anywhere yet, so avoiding that dependency for a first version was a deliberate scope choice, not an oversight. On mount, it calls the new endpoint; if the user has 1+ placements, the single *best* (lowest) rank is featured (ties broken by the backend's own fixed category order, which is also the order the response array itself already reflects). Renders a plain, locally-owned `Modal` (`visible`/`onClose`-by-local-state, matching every other modal in this app — `AnalyzeModal.tsx`, `FavoritesModal.tsx`, etc. — there's no global modal context in this app to plug into, and building one for a single feature wasn't warranted) — a centered card with a trophy icon, `"We've got great news for you!"`, then `"You're #{{rank}} in the {{category}} podium! Tap to see it."` (rank shown as `#{{rank}}` rather than an ordinal word like "third" — deliberately reusing the exact same convention `activityController.js`'s own "Made the {{category}} podium — #{{rank}}" activity-feed key already established earlier this session, since generating correct ordinal words per rank per one of 12 languages is real, avoidable i18n complexity `#N` sidesteps entirely), a close (X) button, and a tap-outside-to-dismiss zone — tapping the card itself navigates and dismisses together.

**Mobile — the navigation chain** (three files threaded together, since neither `SharesFeedSection.tsx` nor `PeoplePodium.tsx` took any props before this): tapping the card calls `router.push(\`/home?podiumCategory=${key}\`)` (`key` being `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own shorter category key, e.g. `"liked"` — `PodiumNewsModal.tsx` owns the `mostLiked→"liked"` etc. mapping table). `app/(app)/home/index.tsx` now reads `useLocalSearchParams<{podiumCategory}>()`, force-switches to the Paylaşımlar tab (instant, not animated — `outerTab`'s own default was already `"shares"`, so this only actually matters if the viewer had already swiped to Keşfet before tapping the popup) and passes `podiumCategory` down as a new `jumpToPodiumCategory` prop on `SharesFeedSection`, which forwards it to `PeoplePodium` as `jumpToCategory`. `PeoplePodium.tsx` itself does the real work: once loaded, it looks up which of its own `pages` has that category as a *real* open page and jumps there — or, if the category is locked for the viewer's own tier, jumps to the shared ad page instead, which (per this file's own established design from earlier this round) already renders *that exact viewer's own entry* for real within its skeleton row regardless of lock state — so a Free/Plus viewer tapping through to a category they can't fully browse still lands somewhere that shows them their own actual placement, never a dead end. A `jumpedRef` prevents re-jumping on unrelated re-renders (a mode toggle, a refetch) once the one-time jump has already fired.

Translations: 2 new keys (`"We've got great news for you!"`, `"You're #{{rank}} in the {{category}} podium! Tap to see it."`) × all 12 locales (24 entries), same anchor-based insertion script used for every other batch this session.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean across all touched files. Live-hit `GET /feed/my-podium-placements` for two different real accounts — Zachary (premium): `[{mostLiked, rank:1}, {topRecommenders, rank:2}]`; Peter (dev): `[{mostFollowed, rank:2}, {mostReviewed, rank:2}, {mostLiked, rank:3}]` — confirming both the multi-placement case and the tie-break-by-canonical-order behavior work correctly on real data. A fresh Metro bundle confirmed `PodiumNewsModal.tsx`'s own compiled module is present, `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s module includes the new `jumpToCategory`/`jumpedRef` jump logic, and both new translation keys are reachable.

**Same-day, two real bugs reported after using the feature.** (1) **"kullanıcı podyumdaki yerini korurken... her girişte bu pop up çıkmasın"** — the popup was checking the placement fresh on every login and showing it every time it was still true, which for anyone holding a stable rank meant the exact same "great news" on every single app open. Fixed with the same SecureStore "seen once" pattern `match/index.tsx`'s own `SyncIntroCard` already established for its own one-time intro card (`STORAGE_KEYS.SYNC_INTRO_SEEN`) — a real, pre-existing precedent for exactly this need that the earlier round's own research pass (focused on grepping for `AsyncStorage`, which this app has never used) missed, having found no persistence precedent and explicitly scoping it out as a "first version" limitation. Rather than a plain boolean flag, the new `STORAGE_KEYS.LAST_SHOWN_PODIUM_PLACEMENT` stores the *signature* of whichever placement was last actually shown (`"<category>:<rank>"`) — compared against the current best placement's own signature on every check, so an unchanged placement stays silent, but a genuinely new one (a new category, or an improved/worsened rank on the same one) still shows, since that's real news rather than a repeat. (2) **"basınca ilgili podyuma kaydırırken sayfayı yeniden yükleyip kaydırıyor... arkada sayfa yüklenmişse... 2 yükleme gerçekleşiyor"** — root cause: `router.push()` always stacks a *new* screen instance regardless of whether the target route is already the current one, so tapping the popup (which appears at app launch, when Media/Home — and its own `SharesFeedSection`/`PeoplePodium`, already fetching or already loaded — is almost always already mounted underneath it) mounted a genuinely second `home/index.tsx` instance on top of the first, re-fetching everything from scratch instead of reusing what was already there. Fixed by switching to `router.navigate()` — Expo Router's own "go to this screen; if it's already the current one, update its params in place instead of stacking a duplicate" method, which is exactly this situation's actual need and requires no other change (`home/index.tsx`'s own `useLocalSearchParams()`-driven effect already reacts correctly to a param update either way, remount or not).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. A fresh Metro bundle confirmed `PodiumNewsModal.tsx`'s own compiled module now includes `LAST_SHOWN_PODIUM_PLACEMENT`/a `SecureStore` call, and that `goToPodium` now calls `.navigate(...)`, not `.push(...)`.

**Same-day, direct reversal: `PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own ad page no longer highlights the viewer's own entry, even if they placed in that locked category.** "free ve plusta reklam kartında eğer podyumda yeri varsa sadece kendisini gösteriyor. hayır onu da göstermemeli. reklam kartı görünüşü fixed olacak. hiçbir durumda bozma" — the "self-exception" feature (built at the very start of this whole podium-teaser feature, and referenced again when `PodiumNewsModal.tsx`'s own popup was designed around it) was a real, deliberate design call at the time, but got a direct, explicit reversal once actually seen in practice: the ad page's entire appeal is being a *fixed*, empty rank-medal silhouette — identical for every viewer regardless of who they are or where they placed — and a real photo+name breaking that consistency (even just for the viewer's own slot) undercut it more than the self-highlight was worth. `renderAdSlot` in `PeoplePodium.tsx` now unconditionally returns a blank `PodiumSkeletonSlot`, full stop — the `item.user.id === user?._id` check and the `renderRealCard` branch it used to take are both gone from that function (`renderRealCard` itself is untouched and still used for the actual open/real pages, unaffected). Every doc comment that referenced the old self-exception behavior (this file's own top-of-component comment, the `jumpToCategory` prop's own comment, and `PodiumNewsModal.tsx`'s own top-of-file comment) was corrected in the same pass rather than left stale — a lesson this session has hit more than once now (`PeoplePodium.tsx`'s own mode-toggle centering bug earlier this same round came from exactly this: a doc comment describing behavior that had since changed, never revisited).

One real consequence worth flagging, not hidden: `PodiumNewsModal.tsx`'s own "tap to see it" now lands a Free/Plus viewer on a locked category's ad page same as anyone else — no special reveal of their own placement there anymore. That's the direct, accepted trade-off of this reversal, not a bug — the popup itself already told them their placement and rank; the ad page's job is just being the fixed teaser it always was.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. A fresh Metro bundle confirmed `renderAdSlot`'s own compiled body now unconditionally renders `PodiumSkeletonSlot` with no self-id branch.

**Same-day (2026-09-15): profile-header tier diamond, Currently Watching test-seed data, and a real profile-load performance fix.** Three-part direct ask: "profillerde başta yazan kullanıcı isminin hemen sağına plus veya premium ise elmasını koy... profillerde post tabı çok yavaş yükleniyor... gerekli optimizasyonları yap... currently watching kısmına test amaçlı bi 7 8 kişi koyar mısın."

**(1) Diamond tier mark on profile headers.** `ProfileHeaderInstagram.tsx` — username now wrapped in a new `usernameRow` `<View>`, with the same `Ionicons name="diamond"` + `TIER_FRAME_STYLES[tier].glowColor` convention `PeoplePodiumCard.tsx`/`SuggestedUsersBox.tsx` already use, shown for `plus`/`premium` tiers right after the username. This is a deliberate divergence from `ReviewFeedCard.tsx`'s own opposite choice (tier gradient text instead of ring+diamond, to avoid redundancy with its own avatar ring) — here the direct ask was explicitly for both the ring (already present via `TierAvatarFrame`) *and* the diamond, not an oversight.

**(2) Currently Watching test data.** 8 real accounts seeded directly into `User.currentlyWatching` at staggered ages (8–200 minutes ago, all inside the 4h TTL — see this section's earlier Currently Watching entry) for the user's own manual device testing: Peter.Altenwerth29467, Antonette_Von24105, Sheridan.Greenholt2771, Mariela_Lemke101, Alexandria_Osinski48, Leanne_Von82364, Meaghan_Veum4815, Reynold_Prosacco94893. Live-confirmed via `GET /api/feed/currently-watching?scope=all` (all 8 present with correct titles). Left in place intentionally, unlike other test data this session that gets cleaned up after verification.

**(3) Profile load/tab-switch performance.** Root cause investigated via direct measurement rather than assumption: `time curl` showed `getUserShares` at ~2.0s cold; a raw `ping()`/`findOne()` timing script against the live Atlas cluster confirmed every single DB round trip from this Codespace costs a flat ~300ms regardless of query complexity — a cross-region network-latency fact, not a missing-index problem. This redirects the fix toward cutting the *count* of sequential round trips per request, not query tuning. Two targeted fixes: `authMiddleware.js` gained a short-TTL (3s) `userCache` Map layered on top of the pre-existing `pendingUserLookups` in-flight dedup — the dedup only coalesces truly-concurrent lookups, but a profile screen's tab switches fire 3-4 *sequential* auth'd requests a few hundred ms apart, each re-paying the same ~300ms user lookup; the new cache catches those too, deliberately scoped to a short window since nothing in this codebase reads `req.user` back after a same-request write (mutation endpoints return their own fresh value directly; the mobile client updates `AuthContext` from that response, never a later refetch). `shareController.js`'s `withViewerMeta` had its `voters` and `likedIds` queries parallelized via `Promise.all` instead of running sequentially. Net effect, measured live: `getUserShares` dropped from ~2.0s to ~0.89-0.9s (~55%) on warm requests. Since `ProfileSharingsTab.tsx` already fetches feed data once per session (not re-fetched on grid/feed mode toggle), the perceived slowness switching between grid and feed views was this same endpoint's first-load cost — this fix applies there too, not just initial profile load. `getUserCineGraph`/`getUserFavorites` were evaluated and deliberately left as-is (already reasonably optimized, or not safely improvable under the same round-trip-count strategy without an unfavorable tradeoff) — not part of this round's scope unless reported as still slow.

Verified: `node --check` clean on both backend files plus a full backend-wide sweep (no FAIL lines). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on the mobile diamond change. A fresh Metro bundle fetch confirmed `usernameRow`/`TIER_FRAME_STYLES` are reachable in the compiled `ProfileHeaderInstagram.tsx` module.

**Same-day, follow-up: the profile-page round-trip-parallelization pattern extended app-wide, plus real loading-state fixes across the pages that had none.** A colleague's note: "caching is currently only done on the profile page. This needs to be done on all pages [and] the loading states while pages load need to be resolved." Rather than assume this applied uniformly, two full audits were run first (backend sequential-round-trip patterns; mobile loading-state coverage per screen) to find the *actual* gaps before touching anything.

**Backend — 9 more places with the exact same class of bug** (2+ independent DB calls awaited sequentially instead of via `Promise.all`, each paying its own ~300ms cross-region round trip): `shareController.js`'s `getShareFeed` (currentUser + officialCount), `feedController.js`'s `getRecommendations`/`getNewReleases` (movies + series fetch) and `getPeopleThreePodiums` (officialUser + badgeUsersRaw), `conversationController.js`'s `sendMessage` (populated + Conversation update + notifyMessage, a 3-way parallelization — fires on every single DM sent), `groupController.js`'s `sendGroupMessage` (populated + Group update) and `getAllGroups` (groups + joined), `matchController.js`'s `findMatches`/`getSyncCandidates`/`getMatchWithUser`/`analyzeMatchWithUser` (several independent-pair patterns across CineMatch's whole surface), `userController.js`'s `getProfileAnalysis` (user + lastAnalysis) and its own separate `findMatches` (allUsers+currentUser, then contentDetails+allRatings), and `customListRoute.js`'s list-create (bumpStreak + listCount). All verified independent (neither side's query reads the other's result) before parallelizing — a couple of lower-priority write-path spots (`importController.js`'s already-multi-second import flow) were deliberately left alone since the audit judged the risk/reward not worth it there.

Every one of these was live-hit with a real JWT (both named test accounts) after the edit — `getShareFeed`, `getRecommendations`, `getNewReleases`, `getLeaderboard`, `getAllGroups`, `findMatches`, `getMatchWithUser`, `analyzeMatchWithUser` (hit its own real cooldown, unrelated to this change), a real DM send, a real group message send, and a real list create+delete — all returned correct data, and every test artifact this round created (a DM, a group message, a list) was cleaned up afterward (message/notification deleted, conversation/group preview+unread counts restored to their pre-test values) — the one exception being a harmless, real `currentStreak` bump from the list-create test, left as-is since it's an accurate reflection of genuinely-occurred activity, not test pollution. Full backend `node --check` sweep clean.

**Mobile — the actual loading-state gaps**, found via a screen-by-screen audit (most of Lists/Notifications/Chat/Socials already used the existing `Skeleton.tsx` library correctly, so this was scoped, not a rewrite): `SharesFeedSection.tsx` (Home's main feed) had a bare spinner where the feed's first page loads — replaced with a new `SkeletonShareCard` (mirrors ShareCard's own avatar+header / poster+text body / like-row shape), 3 stacked. `CurrentlyWatchingSection.tsx` returned `null` outright while loading (a silent gap, popping the whole rail in once done) — now shows the existing `SkeletonRail`, matching `KesfetSection.tsx`'s own already-correct use of it. The 4 Search tabs' first-load state was spinner-only despite matching primitives already existing in `Skeleton.tsx` — `SearchContentRows.tsx` (Films/Series) now shows a new `SkeletonSearchResultRow` (mirrors `SearchContentRow.tsx`'s 52×78-poster row shape) ×6; `SearchListsSection.tsx`/`SearchReviewsSection.tsx` now reuse the existing `SkeletonListRow` ×5; `SearchUsersSection.tsx` now reuses the existing `SkeletonRow` ×8. `ContentDetailScreen.tsx` had a full-screen spinner covering the whole page — replaced with a new `SkeletonContentDetail` mirroring its own top-of-page layout (38%-width 2:3 poster beside title/year/overview, then the 4-stat row). The import/sync screen (`profile/import.tsx`) had no placeholder at all on a cold cache (`getCachedImportSources()` returning empty before `fetchImportSources()` resolves) — a blank grid area until then; now shows a new `SkeletonImportSourceGrid` (mirrors `ImportSourceGrid.tsx`'s icon-plate card shape) whenever `sources.length === 0`. Pagination/"load more" footer spinners (Search tabs, list screens) were deliberately left as plain `ActivityIndicator`s — a small footer spinner while appending more rows is a standard, accepted pattern and wasn't what was reported as broken; only *page-load* states were in scope.

**CineMatch (`app/(app)/match/index.tsx`) was deliberately left alone** despite the audit flagging its own unused, already-built `SkeletonMatchResults` as "the cheapest fix in the whole audit" — read closely, wiring it in would have been the wrong call: this screen's own ring-spin transition (three rounds of prior animation tuning, per its own doc comments) already waits for the real results to be ready before sliding to page 2, so there's no moment where a skeleton would ever actually be visible — forcing one in would only risk breaking an already-correct, carefully-synced loading treatment for zero visible benefit. `SkeletonMatchResults` stays defined but unused; not a bug to fix, just dead code from an earlier design.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean across every touched mobile file. A fresh Metro bundle fetch + grep confirmed all 4 new skeleton components (`SkeletonSearchResultRow`, `SkeletonContentDetail`, `SkeletonShareCard`, `SkeletonImportSourceGrid`) are reachable in the compiled output (22 total occurrences across their definitions + call sites).

**Same-day, follow-up: `ListDetailScreen.tsx` rebuilt on the Watched List / Watchlist's own machinery** — direct ask: any list opened from anywhere (a Media "list" post, a Discover list card, My Lists, Search, a "list" ShareCard) loaded slowly, and specifically requested were the Watched List/Watchlist's own quick loading skeleton, its filter sheet (replacing the old right-side dropdown), and its quick in-grid Edit/remove-with-undo design, all brought over.

**Root cause of the slowness, found before touching anything**: `GET /api/lists/:id` returned bare `{itemId, itemType}` refs for every item, so `ListDetailScreen.tsx` used to hydrate posters itself with one `getMovieById`/`getSeriesById` call *per item* — a 15-item list meant 15 extra round trips just to render. This is the exact bug `collectionCache.ts`'s own doc comment already names as the reason it exists for the Watched List/Watchlist ("both screens used to fetch their list and then request every title individually... one round trip per movie or series") — the list detail page had simply never gotten the same fix.

**Backend fix**: `GET /api/lists/:id` (`backend/routes/customListRoute.js`) now calls the already-existing `hydratePreviewItems` (`backend/utils/listPreview.js`, shared with `/discover`/`/popular`/`/for-content`) with a limit covering the *whole* list instead of a 5-item preview slice — one bulk `$documents` aggregation instead of N per-item requests. `hydratePreviewItems` itself was extended to also project `release_date`/`first_air_date`/`popularity` (previously title/poster only) so the mobile client's sort/search engine has what it needs — additive fields, harmless to the other 3 callers that don't read them. Live-verified as Zachary against a real 15-item public list ("Fun"): all 15 hydrated correctly with poster/title/release_date/popularity, response time ~0.85s warm (down from what would have been 1 + 15 sequential-ish round trips before). Also live-verified DELETE+re-add on a real item.

**Mobile — reused the Watched List/Watchlist's own query engine and grid wholesale, rather than a scoped-down copy**: `ListDetailScreen.tsx` now maps the server's hydrated `previewItems` straight into `CollectionEntry` (the same shape `useCollectionQuery`/`CollectionGrid` already run on) — `rating` is always `null` (a curated list isn't a watch record, no personal rating concept), and `order` is assigned in *reverse* index (`total - 1 - index`) so the query engine's own default descending-by-order tie-break reproduces the owner's actual item order first-to-last, matching this screen's pre-existing behavior rather than reversing it.

- **Loading skeleton**: the old generic 2-column `SkeletonGrid`+`SkeletonPosterCard` replaced with the real `CollectionSkeleton` (5-column, exact tile geometry via `useGridMetrics`) — the same shimmer Watchlist/Watched List use.
- **Filter/sort**: the old right-side filter-icon dropdown (All/Movies/Series only) replaced with `CollectionSearchBar` + `CollectionToolbar` + `CollectionFilterSheet`, reusing `WATCHLIST_SORT_GROUPS` verbatim (Title A–Z/Z–A, Release date Newest/Oldest — no rating group, same reasoning `filterLabels.ts`'s own comment already gives for the Watchlist: "nothing here has been watched, so nothing here has a rating," equally true of a curated list).
- **Edit design**: `CollectionGrid`'s own edit-mode (Edit/Done toggle in the toolbar, animated remove overlay, `CollectionUndoBar`'s 4s undo window) replaces the old always-on remove icon with no undo. Owner-only (`onRemove`/`onToggleEdit` both `undefined` for a viewer browsing someone else's public list, same as before). The pre-existing "Edit" button that opens the full list editor (rename/description/visibility/reorder) is now labeled **"Edit List"** specifically to disambiguate it from the new toolbar's own "Edit"/"Done" — the two are genuinely different things (full metadata editing vs. a quick single-item remove) and both stay, matching how Watchlist's own quick-remove doesn't replace its list-management equivalent either.
- Removal itself is a local optimistic hide-then-commit-with-undo state machine (mirrors `CollectionScreen.tsx`'s own `pendingRef`/`commit`/`flushPending` shape) backed by a direct `removeItem()` call rather than porting the full cross-visit `CollectionCache` module — a deliberate scope call: that cache's whole reason to exist (bulk content hydration) is now solved server-side for lists, and a list detail page only ever manages the one list it's showing, so a shared cache keyed by list id would have been a bigger abstraction than this actually needed.
- One new translation key, `"Removed from list"` (the undo bar's message) and one more, `"Search this list"` (the search bar's placeholder) — both across all 12 locales; every other string reused verbatim from the Watchlist/Watched List (`"Edit"`, `"Done"`, `"Edit List"`, `"No titles match your search."`, `"Clear all"`, etc. all already existed).

**Deliberately not ported**: a persistent stale-while-revalidate cache across visits to the *same* list id — unlike Watchlist/Watched List (exactly one fixed list per user, visited constantly as an anchor screen), a list detail page is reached for an unbounded number of different list ids from many entry points, so "instant on revisit" for an arbitrary id is a materially different, bigger caching problem than this ask's actual complaint (which was the N+1 network bug, now fixed server-side). A revisit still re-fetches, but as ONE fast request instead of 1+N — judged to satisfy "hızlı yüklensin" without the added complexity of a multi-entry cache with its own invalidation story.

**Same-day, large follow-up round: `list-editor` reduced to creation-only, a real list-card double-navigation bug fixed, the Badges tab's own real slowness root-caused and fixed, the Favorites tab got drag-reorder + undo + 2 visual fixes, and CineGraph's Sync Score card gained a real Free/Plus/Premium gate plus 2 unrelated Sync-carousel bugs fixed.** Seven distinct asks in one round; each is its own item below.

**(1) `list-editor` (`ListEditorScreen.tsx`) reduced to creation-only** — direct ask, confirming the previous round's own flagged side effect: "yeniden sıralama özelliği olmasın zaten gerek yok" (no need for reordering). The entire `listId`/`isEditing` branch (loading an existing list via `getListById`, saving via `updateList`, the whole `status: loading|ready|error` state machine that branch needed) is gone — the screen only ever creates a new list now, exactly as `MyListsScreen.tsx`'s "New List" button (its only remaining caller) already used it. `getListById`/`updateList`/`ensureContent`/`entryFor` stay exported and used elsewhere (`ListDetailScreen.tsx`, `collectionCache.ts`) — only this screen's own now-dead usage of them was removed.

**(2) Real bug fixed: tapping a list card from anywhere would briefly show the list page, then a movie/series Content Detail page would stack on top of it.** Root cause, found by reading rather than guessing: `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s and `search/SearchListCard.tsx`'s own film-strip poster thumbnails were each wrapped in their own `Pressable` with `onPress` navigating straight to that title's Content Detail page — a second, competing tap target nested inside the card's own outer `Pressable`/`GHPressable` (which navigates to the list itself). `DiscoverListCard.tsx`'s outer wrapper is specifically `react-native-gesture-handler`'s own `Pressable` (needed for its film strip's horizontal scroll to negotiate against Discover's outer horizontal pager — see that file's own comment), while the inner poster `Pressable`s were plain React Native — two different touch-recognition systems nested inside each other, which don't reliably guarantee "innermost wins" the way two same-system Pressables nesting normally would. Fixed by making every film-strip poster a plain, non-interactive `View` in both files — matching `ShareCard.tsx`'s own list-post box, which already got this right (its own film-strip posters were always plain `View`s, never `Pressable`s) and was the actual template for the fix. Direct ask either way: "list kartında nereye bastığı hiç önemli değil, direkt o listin sayfası gelecek" — wherever on a list card you tap, it should always open the list, never a specific title inside it.

**(3) Real perf bug found and fixed: the Badges tab (own profile AND public profile) loaded noticeably slower than every other tab.** Root cause, found by direct measurement (timing all 20 individual badge endpoints, not guessing): `computePodiumBadge` (backend `feedController.js`, checked by the "Podium" tile) calls `getPeopleThreePodiums(null)` — the exact same function backing the whole People Leaderboard page — which recomputes the ENTIRE app's leaderboard (5 aggregations, one with `.allowDiskUse`, plus `computeAllUsersBadgeCounts` over every non-official user) from scratch, just to answer "is this one user in anyone's top 3." This ran on every single Badges tab open, for every user, own or public. Fixed with a short-TTL (60s) cache + in-flight dedup on `getPeopleThreePodiums` — same shape as `authMiddleware.js`'s own `userCache`, just a much longer TTL since a leaderboard has no correctness reason to be millisecond-fresh, keyed on `type` (the only input that changes the result). Separately, `computeHiddenGemBadge`'s own `$unwind: "$watchlist"` aggregation was unwinding EVERY user's entire watchlist array just to count how many people had watched a specific title or two — added a `$match` with `$elemMatch` before the `$unwind` so Mongo can skip unwinding users who have none of the target items at all, instead of materializing every user's full watchlist first. Also: `ProfileBadgesTab.tsx`'s own-profile path used to fire **20 separate HTTP requests** (one per badge family) instead of the public-profile path's already-existing single bulk `getAllBadgesForUser` endpoint — now both paths always use the one bulk endpoint (own profile defaults its target id to the signed-in user via `useAuth()`), cutting 19 of 20 round trips for the common case. Measured end-to-end: `GET /badges/user/:id` (podium already cached) dropped from a cold ~4.9s to a steady ~1.8-2.3s. That's a real, meaningful improvement but not fully at parity with this session's other ~0.9s-class fixes — the remaining time is spread thin across ~18 still-independent-but-genuinely-small queries running concurrently; consolidating those into fewer combined queries is a bigger, separate restructuring not attempted in this round (flagged, not silently left unfinished-feeling).

**(4) Favorites tab, four separate fixes in one pass**: the 5-star rating row under each favorite poster shrank from `size={13}` to `size={9}` — at the default size, 5 stars (`5*13+4 ≈ 69px`) were actually *wider* than the poster itself (~65px on a typical phone, 5-across grid), visibly overflowing; `size={9}` (`5*9+4 ≈ 49px`) comfortably fits. A thin `colors.border` hairline divider (this app's own established convention, e.g. `ProfileHeaderInstagram.tsx`'s `statsRowDivider`) now sits between the Favorite Movies and Favorite Series rails, which never had one. Edit mode now supports real drag-to-reorder — long-press a poster to pick it up, matching `react-native-draggable-flatlist` (already a dependency, previously unused in this app after the Lists-reorder feature it was originally added for got removed — see item 1) wired into `ContentRail.tsx` itself via 3 new optional props (`dragEnabled`, `onReorder`, `footer`) rather than a Favorites-only fork, so the shared rail component stays the one source of truth and any other rail could opt into the same behavior later. The empty "+" add-slots moved out of the rail's own `data` array into the new `footer` slot specifically because they're not reorderable — an add-slot has nothing to drag. And removing a favorite (the X in edit mode) now goes through the same optimistic-hide-then-commit-with-undo state machine (`CollectionUndoBar`, 4s window) `CollectionScreen.tsx`'s own Watched List/Watchlist removal already uses, replacing the old immediate-no-undo delete — direct ask, "watchedlistteki gibi undo özelliği de ekleyelim."

**(5) CineGraph's Sync Score card (a public profile's own ⓘ analysis, `SyncScoreCard.tsx`) gained a real tier gate it never had** — direct ask: Free blocked outright with an upgrade prompt, Plus capped at **5 per week**, Premium unlimited, all while leaving the Sync page's own Analyze button (the *same* backend endpoint, `analyzeMatchWithUser`) completely untouched for every tier. The two entry points share one function, so the new gate is scoped by a new `source: "sync" | "profile"` field sent only by the profile entry point (`matchService.ts`'s `analyzeMatchWithUser`/`prefetchMatchAnalysis` gained an optional third `source` argument) — omitted (defaulting to `"sync"`), every existing caller is a no-op against this change. Backend: `config/tiers.js` gained `profileSyncAnalysesPerWeek` (free: 0, plus: 5, premium/dev: 999 — same "generous enough not to be felt" convention `syncSearchesPerDay` already uses for Premium), `models/MatchAnalysisLog.js` gained a `source` field (defaulting to `"sync"`, so every pre-existing row is correctly never counted as a `"profile"` one), and `analyzeMatchWithUser` (`matchController.js`) gained a second, separate gate — checked only when `source === "profile"` — sitting right alongside the pre-existing per-pair cooldown gate, not replacing it: Free gets an immediate 403 (`requiresUpgrade`) before any real work; Plus counts `"profile"`-sourced `MatchAnalysisLog` rows since the most recent Monday 00:00 (a calendar week, same "resets at a fixed boundary" convention `getSyncCandidates`' own daily quota already uses) against the limit, 429 (`requiresUpgrade`, `retryAfterMs` to next Monday) once hit.

Mobile: `SyncScoreCard.tsx`'s own ⓘ tap checks the viewer's tier directly (`useAuth()`) — Free shows a toast (`"Upgrade to see your sync analyses"`) and never opens the modal at all, matching `MatchFilterStrip.tsx`'s own established "locked control shows a toast instead of navigating away" convention elsewhere in this exact feature. A real, non-obvious side effect this round had to account for: this card's own *speculative* prefetch (warms the LLM analysis right after the score loads, so opening ⓘ feels instant) used to fire unconditionally on every profile visited — once ⓘ started counting against a real capped quota, that would have silently burned a Plus user's whole weekly allowance just from passively browsing 5 profiles, without ever tapping ⓘ once. Fixed by scoping that eager warm-up to Premium/dev only; Free/Plus still get the correct analysis the moment they actually tap ⓘ (via `MatchAnalysisPanel`'s own on-demand fetch, unchanged), just without the instant-open optimization — a fine trade for not spending a capped resource on speculation. `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` gained a `source?: "profile"` prop (passed only by `SyncAnalysisModal.tsx`, the profile entry point's own wrapper — the Sync page's own direct use of this panel never passes it) and a new `analysisUpgradeRequired` state/message, kept genuinely separate from the pre-existing `analysisCooldownRetryAt` state since they mean different things ("come back in N minutes" vs. "upgrade, or wait for next week") — Free never reaches this state at all (blocked one level up), so in practice it only ever fires for a Plus user who's used all 5.

**(6) Real bug fixed: the Sync analysis deck's own closing "Share" card (`MatchCoverCard.tsx`, rendered inside `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`) visually sat low/half-cut-off on some devices.** Root cause: each card renders inside a fixed-height `ScrollView`, and `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` already had a `cardScrollCentered` style (`flexGrow:1, justifyContent:"center"`) specifically for vertically centering a card whose own content is shorter than that fixed height — but it was only ever applied to the `"breakdown"` card's key, never the `"cover"` (Share) card's, despite `MatchCoverCard` being reliably one of the shortest cards in the deck (no chart, no rail). Fixed by adding `"cover"` to that same condition — one-line fix, once the actual mechanism was found.

**(7) Real bug fixed: after switching to a different candidate in the Sync results screen (2nd+ switch, not the first), that new candidate's own first card (the LLM-generated match-title badge) rendered invisible until you swiped through the deck and back.** Root cause: `MatchTitleBadge`'s own fade-in/out is driven directly by `scrollX` (an `Animated.Value` mirroring the deck's horizontal scroll offset via `Animated.event`), read independently of `activeIndex` (a deliberate choice, per that code's own comment, for a live drag-following fade). Switching candidates already reset the *visual* scroll position (`scrollRef.current.scrollTo({x:0, animated:false})`) but never reset `scrollX` itself — and a non-animated programmatic `scrollTo` doesn't reliably re-fire the `onScroll` event that would otherwise update it, on every platform, in every case. So after scrolling partway through candidate A's deck and then switching to candidate B, `scrollX` could stay stuck at candidate A's old non-zero position even though the deck had visibly snapped back to card 0 — `MatchTitleBadge` then computed itself as still-faded-out based on that stale value. A genuine swipe gesture always "fixed" it because a real drag reliably does fire `onScroll`, which is exactly why the bug only ever reproduced through the programmatic reset path, never a manual one. Fixed with one line, `scrollX.setValue(0)`, added directly alongside the existing `scrollRef.current.scrollTo(...)` reset — no longer dependent on the native event firing at all.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, backend `node --check` clean (full sweep). Live-verified against real accounts: the list-card fix confirmed by inspecting both files' film-strip rendering directly (a visual double-navigation isn't independently curl-testable, so this one leans on the root-cause fix matching `ShareCard.tsx`'s own already-correct precedent exactly); the Badges perf fix measured via repeated timed `curl` calls (podium: 4.9s cold → ~0.001s cached; combined endpoint: ~4.9s cold → ~1.8-2.3s steady); the Sync Score tier gate fully live-tested as both Zachary (Plus) and Peter (Free) — Free correctly 403'd on `source:"profile"` but still gets a real 200 LLM analysis via the Sync page's own unmodified flow; Plus correctly succeeded 5 times across 5 distinct targets then correctly 429'd on a 6th, while the Sync page's own flow kept working normally throughout — all 5 test `MatchAnalysisLog` rows deleted afterward so Zachary's own quota starts fresh for the user's own manual testing. A fresh Metro bundle fetch + grep confirmed the new mobile logic (`requiresUpgrade`, `analysisLocked`, `analysisUpgradeRequired`, `cardScrollCentered` on `"cover"`, `scrollX.setValue`) reachable in the compiled output.

**Same-day, immediate follow-up: 2 more real bugs in that same Sync Score card, reported right after the round above shipped.** Both traced back to the SAME root cause — `SyncScoreCard.tsx`'s own `getMatchWithUser` call (backing a public profile's ⓘ analysis) was never given the full picture the Sync page's own `getSyncCandidates` call already had.

**(8) "Sync sonucu movies/series moduna göre değişmiyordu"** — the CineGraph tab's own Movies/Series sub-tab switcher (`CineGraphSubTabSwitcher`) never actually changed the Sync Score shown alongside it; it silently always computed (and cached) the movie-based score. Root cause: `SYNC_SCORE_FILTERS` (`api/syncScoreCache.ts`) is a module-level constant hardcoded to `type: "movie"`, and the score cache/in-flight map was keyed by `userId` alone — even if `SyncScoreCard.tsx` had passed a different type through, the SAME cache entry would've served whichever type was fetched first, forever. Fixed properly, not papered over: `SyncScoreCard` gained a required `type: ContentType` prop (`PublicProfileCategoryTabs.tsx` now passes `cinegraphSubTab` straight through — that state already existed, driving the switcher and `ProfileCinegraphsTab`, just was never threaded to this card too), builds its own `filters = {...SYNC_SCORE_FILTERS, type}`, and `syncScoreCache.ts`'s `getCachedSyncScore`/`prefetchSyncScore` both now key by `` `${userId}:${type}` ``, not `userId` alone — so movie and series genuinely cache (and recompute) independently, and switching the sub-tab now triggers a real refetch for whichever type is newly selected. Live-verified: the exact same pair's movie score (59%) and series score (57%) now come back as genuinely different numbers from `getMatchWithUser`, confirming the type actually reaches the computation.

**(9) "Analiz kartları eksik"** — opening the ⓘ breakdown from a profile showed only 5 of the 8 possible cards (Sync Summary, Sync Breakdown, Variety, Activity, Share) — Shared Genres, Shared Favorites, and Social Overlap, all real cards the Sync page's own deck shows, were silently always absent from this entry point specifically. Root cause: those 3 cards in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx` are each gated on a piece of `candidate.matchInsights` (shared genres / favorites overlap / social overlap) — data the Sync page's own `getSyncCandidates` endpoint already returns per candidate, but `getMatchWithUser` (backing `SyncScoreCard`) never did, even though the shared `computeMatchBreakdown` function backing BOTH endpoints already computes `matchInsights` internally at zero extra query cost — `getMatchWithUser`'s own response payload just never captured or returned it (the same destructuring that intentionally dropped the unrelated, genuinely-expensive `llmInput` field also silently dropped this free one). Fixed: `getMatchWithUser` now includes `matchInsights` in its response; mobile's `MatchWithUserResult` type gained the matching optional field; `SyncScoreCard.tsx`'s own synthesized `SyncCandidate` now carries it through. All 3 previously-missing cards now render correctly from a profile's own ⓘ, matching the Sync page's own full deck exactly. Live-verified: the same `getMatchWithUser` call now returns `matchInsights` with real data (10 shared genres for movies, 6 for series on the same test pair).

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, backend `node --check` clean (full sweep). **Same-day, follow-up: the Subscription page (`app/(app)/match/subscription.tsx`) rebuilt from a Sync-only feature comparison into the one place that lists every tier-gated thing in the whole app, and stacked vertically instead of Free/Plus sharing a row.** Direct ask: "free ile plus yan yana olmasın, abonelikler alt alta dizilsin... cinephixe dair tüm levellandırmaları bu abonelik kutucuklarında belirtelim."

**Layout**: the old `planRow` (Free + Plus at 50% width each, Premium full-width below) is gone — `PLAN_ORDER.map(renderCard)` now stacks all three, full width, in order (Free, Plus, Premium), in one `planStack` column. Each card's own feature list grew from one flat 4-line list into 5 grouped sections (Sync, Sync Results, Sync Analysis, Profile Analysis, Leaderboards) — a real reason the vertical stack isn't just a preference call: at half-width, that much content per card would have meant scrolling inside a card, which a full-width stacked column avoids outright.

**Content — every real tier gate in the app, copied by hand from `backend/config/tiers.js` and the mobile-side `OPEN_KEYS_BY_TIER` tables (`LeaderboardPodium.tsx`/`PeoplePodium.tsx`), since there's no shared import between the two codebases** (same reason the page's own pre-existing numbers were already hardcoded, e.g. the old "15 sync searches per day" line):
- **Sync**: searches/day (1 / 3 / 15), type & genre filters (Plus+), weighting by watch count/avg rating (Premium only).
- **Sync Results**: how many of the 5 sync-cloud matches are actually open — Free's own #1 (the most enticing one) stays locked with the other 4 visible, Plus opens its own top 3, Premium opens all 5. A real, slightly counter-intuitive detail (`lockedRanksFor` in `MatchResultsCloud.tsx`) worth surfacing since a user would otherwise have no way to know Free's *best* match is the one behind the paywall.
- **Sync Analysis**: the per-pair cooldown on the Sync page's own Analyze button (60 / 15 / 5 minutes — same underlying `matchAnalysisCooldownMinutes`), plus the brand-new profile-entry-point gate from 2 rounds ago (0 / 5-per-week / unlimited, `profileSyncAnalysesPerWeek`).
- **Profile Analysis**: schema richness + history + advanced cards + cooldown (`analysisSchema`/`analysisHistory`/`analysisAdvancedCards`/`analysisCooldownHours`).
- **Leaderboards**: how many of Discover's 5 content categories and Media's 6 people categories are open per tier (1/5 + 1/6 for Free, 3/5 + 3/6 for Plus, all for Premium) — one shared templated line (`"{{count}} of {{total}} leaderboard categories unlocked"`) reused 4 times with different numbers rather than naming every category, to keep each card scannable.

**A real, separate gap found and fixed along the way**: this whole page — every string on it, including "Free"/"Plus"/"Current"/"Upgrade"/"Switch"/the header/subtitle/demo-notice/error text — had **zero locale coverage** in any of the other 11 languages (`t()` was silently falling back to the raw English key every time). Not something this round's own new copy introduced; a pre-existing gap on a page that had apparently never gotten the same translation pass as the rest of the app. Since this round was already rewriting the page's entire content, fixed it properly rather than perpetuating it: every string the page uses now, old and new alike, is translated across all 12 locales (31 keys × 12 locales added in one pass). `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`'s own `t("Upgrade")` (added 2 rounds ago for the weekly-quota upsell link) and every other pre-existing `t("Upgrade")` call site across the app inherits this same fix for free, since they all share the one key.

### Same-day follow-up: the + button's 6th category, a real like-mirroring inconsistency found (not fixed — flagged), Shared Genres' "See All" built, and a new Sync-only "Watch Together" card

Direct follow-through on the previous round's own open questions, after the user weighed in on each.

**+ button gained its missing 6th category: List.** `SharesFeedSection.tsx`'s `composeCategories` — `router.navigate("/lists")` (MyListsScreen, the same route `ProfileDrawerContent.tsx`'s own "Lists" row already uses) + `t("Go to the list you want to share")`. Same "navigate + one-line hint, nothing else" rule as the other 5; `List` itself reused an already-translated label.

**The post-like vs. list/review-like question — checked, and it's genuinely inconsistent, not left alone.** The user's ask was "if they're already separate, don't touch it" — turned out they AREN'T uniformly separate. `toggleShareLike` (`shareController.js`) explicitly mirrors a `type:"list"` share's like (and, in `registerShareView`, its view) into the underlying `CustomList.likes`/`views` — by design, with its own doc comment explaining why (`/lists/popular` ranks by `list.likes`, so a like via the feed should count there too). But **no equivalent mirroring exists for `type:"review"` shares at all** — `Review.likes` is completely untouched by liking a review-post, despite `getPopularReviews` ranking by `review.likes.length` the exact same way `/lists/popular` does. This is a real asymmetry, not a deliberate split design: lists get the fix, reviews have the identical architectural reason to need it and don't have it. **Not changed** — this needs the user's own call on which direction (mirror reviews too, for consistency and to close the Popular Reviews blind spot; or strip the list-mirroring back out for a genuinely uniform separation) rather than picking one silently.

**Shared Genres "See All" — built, per the user's acceptance of the earlier recommendation.** `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`: a genre whose `genreItems.length` (from `getSharedGenreContent`, uncapped server-side) exceeds `SEE_ALL_POSTER_THRESHOLD` (20) gets a small underlined "See all {{count}}" link right under the coverflow. Opens a full-screen `Modal` (slide-up), a plain 3-column `FlatList` grid of every title in that genre (poster + a small rating badge when the viewer rated it), tapping one sets `selectedPosterId` and closes back to the card's own existing detail view — additive only, the coverflow itself is completely untouched and stays the default browse experience below the threshold. Reset alongside `showAllGenres`/`selectedPosterId` on both a genre-arrow tap and a candidate switch.

**New "Watch Together" card — titles on BOTH sides' own to-watch queue, not the "shared recommendations" idea originally floated.** Direct refinement from the user: show a real overlap of `toWatchList` (the genuine to-watch queue — see this doc's own note elsewhere on the `watchlist`/`toWatchList` field-naming mismatch, `watchlist` is actually the WATCHED list), not a guessed recommendation. New backend `GET /match/:targetUserId/mutual-to-watch` (`getMutualToWatch`, `matchController.js`) — same shape as the existing `getMutualConnections`: builds a `Set` of the target's `${itemType}:${itemId}` keys, filters the caller's own queue against it, batch-hydrates whichever Movie/Series docs matched. New mobile `getMutualToWatch` (`matchService.ts`) and a new card in `MatchAnalysisPanel.tsx`, reusing the existing `PosterRow.tsx` component (already shared with `MatchSharedFavorites`) rather than building a new poster-row renderer. Fetched once per candidate on the same `shouldLoadExtras`/`isFreeDeck` gate every other extra card uses; **the card is omitted entirely when the intersection is empty** — same "only push a card when there's real data" rule already established for `fav`/`variety`/etc., no "nothing in common yet" empty state needed. Live-verified against real data: Zachary and Peter's real queues share exactly one title ("The Odyssey"), returned correctly.

Verified: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, backend `node --check` sweep clean, live JWT-minted `GET /match/:id/mutual-to-watch` confirmed the real one-title overlap between the two named test accounts, fresh Metro bundle fetch + grep confirmed `getMutualToWatch`, `seeAllPostersVisible`, `SEE_ALL_POSTER_THRESHOLD`, and the new locale keys all present in the compiled output.

### Same-day, real bug caught by the user testing "Watch Together": Shared Genres was showing a UNION of both sides' ratings, not an intersection

Reported live: syncing from a real account ("Nurelski") against Peter, the Shared Genres card showed ~370 titles for Comedy/Drama even though Peter had only rated 7-10 titles in those genres total. Asked to find the real cause and check whether any other card has the same problem.

**Root cause, confirmed by reading `getSharedGenreContent` (`matchController.js`) line by line**: `candidateIds` was built as the UNION of both sides' rated content ids (`[...myRatingById.keys(), ...targetRatingById.keys()]`), only ever EXCLUDING an id when BOTH sides had rated it and disagreed by more than `SHARED_GENRE_CONTENT_MAX_RATING_DEVIATION` (2 points) — a title only ONE side had rated was always kept in, per an explicit (deliberate, not accidental) comment: `// Only one side has rated it — no disagreement to check, always include.` Whichever account has more total ratings in a genre completely dominates that union — exactly what happened here.

**Checked every other "shared X" card for the same union-vs-intersection mistake — only this one had it**:
- `getRecentSharedActivity` (Activity card) — already a true intersection (`[...myRatingById.keys()].filter(id => targetRatingById.has(id))`). Fine.
- `buildMatchInsights`'s `favoritesOverlap` (Shared Favorites card) — already a true intersection (`favIntersection`), with one-sided-but-same-genre favorites kept in an explicitly SEPARATE, separately-labeled `genreOnly` bucket rather than silently merged into the "shared" count. Fine, and actually the right template for how to surface "not exactly shared but related" data without it looking like real overlap.
- `getMutualConnections` (Social Overlap) and the same round's own new `getMutualToWatch` (Watch Together) — both already true intersections by construction (`Set` membership checks both ways). Fine.

**Fix**: rewrote `getSharedGenreContent`'s candidate selection to a genuine intersection — a title is only ever a candidate if BOTH sides rated it, still narrowed further by the same ±2-point agreement filter as before (now a real "you both rated this and largely agreed" set, not "everyone's individual ratings unioned together"). This also matches what the card's own name and its own hint text ("Swipe or tap a poster to compare ratings") already promised, which the union version could never fully deliver (most of its 370 "shared" items had no comparison to show at all, just "Not rated yet" on one side).

Live-verified against real data post-fix: Nurelski vs. Peter's Comedy dropped from ~370 to **2**, Drama to **3** — numbers that actually match Peter's own small rated set. Re-checked Zachary vs. Peter across 6 genres too: 1–16 each, all realistic. `node --check` clean, mobile `tsc --noEmit` clean (no mobile changes needed — the bug was entirely server-side).

### Same-day, immediate follow-up: "both rated it" was still too narrow — the real bar is "both watched it"

Direct correction right after the fix above: two people who both genuinely watched something but never rated it (the user's own example — both watched *The Shining*, neither rated it) should still count as shared, not be excluded just because there's no rating to compare.

**Rewrote `getSharedGenreContent` again** — candidate membership now comes from `User.watchlist` (this app's own confusingly-named WATCHED list, not `toWatchList`) intersected between both sides for the requested content type, instead of from either side's `Rating` documents at all. Ratings still matter, but only to further NARROW an already-watched-by-both title (excluding a real scored disagreement beyond `SHARED_GENRE_CONTENT_MAX_RATING_DEVIATION`) — never to widen the set by pulling in something the other side never watched, and never to exclude a mutually-watched-but-unrated title. This is the same "both watched it" bar `getMutualToWatch` (the Watch Together card, same day) already uses for the to-watch queue — this card uses the equivalent field for the WATCHED list.

**Live-verified two ways.** (1) Existing real overlap: Nurelski/Peter have 5 movies in both watched lists; genre-filtered across all 19 movie genres it correctly narrowed to exactly the 3 distinct titles among those 5 that actually carry a matching genre tag (`The Odyssey`, `The Devil Wears Prada 2`, `Disclosure Day`) — smaller than the ratings-intersection version's own numbers for this particular pair, because (confirmed by direct DB inspection) rating and watching are genuinely independent actions in this app — a title can be rated without ever being marked watched, and vice versa, not just a seeding artifact. (2) The exact "watched by both, rated by neither" case itself: added *Coyote vs. Acme* to both Zachary's and Peter's real watched lists via the actual `POST /users/me/watchlist` endpoint (not a direct DB write), confirmed neither had rated it, called `getSharedGenreContent` for Comedy, and got back both `Deadpool 2` (rated by both, ratings shown) AND `Coyote vs. Acme` (no `myRating`/`targetRating` fields at all, exactly the Shining scenario) in the same response — then removed it from both watched lists again via the real `DELETE` endpoint to leave no test residue. `node --check` clean.

### 2026-10-02: Groq removed as an LLM provider entirely

Direct ask, after a long gap in this doc's own timeline (the previous entry's own "4/5 live success rate via real Groq calls" milestone was from before this) — the user said they'd never liked Groq's actual output quality and asked to just remove it rather than keep tuning it further.

**Backend**: `llmAdapter.js` lost `DEFAULT_GROQ_MODEL`, `callGroq()`, and the `if (provider === 'groq')` branch inside `callLLM` entirely (along with the model-pin/`reasoning_effort` tuning history documented in this file's own earlier entries — that tuning is now moot, not revived). `matchController.js`'s `providerCandidates` fallback chain is now Gemini → OpenRouter → OpenAI → mock (`GROQ_API_KEY` dropped from the candidate list and from `LLM_MODE`'s allowed values); the `promptTemplate.instruction` conciseness constraints stayed (still real, still useful regardless of which provider ends up serving a request) but their own comment no longer cites Groq-specific truncation behavior as the reason. `GROQ_API_KEY`/`GROQ_DEFAULT_MODEL` removed from `.env`/`.env.example`. Mobile: `MatchAnalysis.provider`'s union type dropped `"groq"` (no UI branched on it directly — confirmed via grep before removing).

**Live-verified no regression**: `node --check` clean on all 3 touched backend files, `tsc --noEmit` clean, a real `analyzeMatchWithUser` call against Zachary/Peter still returns a valid 200 with usable analysis content post-removal (no crash from the missing `callGroq` reference). **Separate finding surfaced while verifying, not fixed (out of scope for this ask)**: that same live call, and a second one against a different pair with `?provider=gemini` forced explicitly, both came back `provider:"mock"` rather than a real Gemini response, despite `GEMINI_API_KEY` being set in this (post-migration, see `project_clone_migration` memory) `.env` — Gemini itself appears to be failing right now, independent of anything touched in this round. Worth a dedicated look if Profile Analysis or CineMatch Analyze seem to only ever return mock-flavored text going forward.

## 5. What's NOT built (remaining scope)

Chat, Cinematch, Community/Groups, Notifications, i18n, Home tab, Follow/Network + Public Profile, Reviews, Favorites, Activity Log/Undo, TV Time/Letterboxd Import, Forgot/Reset Password, Setup Profile onboarding, Theme/Appearance selection, Offline handling — Tier 1, Recommendation + Analysis-Share sending, the To-Watch queue + Watched List rename, Home's Activity Feed + Top Picks, Analyze Profile, Cinematch-with-a-specific-user, Movies/Series search filters, and the static legal/info pages (§3) are now built — this section previously listed several of those as not-started; that's stale, kept only as a marker of what changed.

**Correction (2026-08-11)**: an earlier version of this section claimed every functional gap was closed. That was wrong — it was based on the incremental roadmap of milestones explicitly planned so far, not a systematic re-check against web's actual current feature set. A fresh audit (prompted by the user catching a real miss) found 7 more gaps. **All 7 are now closed (§3), as of 2026-08-12** — audit item #1 (recommendation/analysis-share sending), #2 (To-Watch queue), #3 (Home Activity Feed + Top Picks), #4 (Analyze Profile), #5 (Cinematch-with-a-user), #6 (search filters), and #7 (static legal/info pages). Nothing remains open from this audit.

The lesson for future audits: don't trust the roadmap list alone — cross-reference every backend endpoint web's frontend actually calls against mobile's `src/api/*.ts` exports; an endpoint web calls that mobile never calls anywhere is a mechanical signal of a missed feature.

- **Offline handling, Tier 2/3** — cached-data fallback (show last-known GET results while offline instead of an error) and queued-write retry (mutations made offline get queued and auto-synced on reconnect) were explicitly scoped out of the Tier-1 pass (§3) as a much bigger architectural undertaking (a real cache layer, conflict handling). Not currently planned, but flagged as the natural next step if offline support needs to go further. Also flagged in that section: `ChatRoom.tsx`'s message-send REST fallback silently never indicates a failed send — a good candidate for whenever this area gets revisited.
- **Google OAuth on a physical device over plain Wi-Fi (no ADB connection)**: the current Google Sign-In fix for the emulator relies on `adb reverse tcp:5000 tcp:5000` — see §7. This does *not* apply to a phone connected only via Expo Go over Wi-Fi with no USB/wireless-debugging ADB connection. That case needs a different solution (most likely: register the LAN-IP or a tunnel URL as an additional authorized redirect URI in Google Cloud Console, or switch to native Google Sign-In with server-side token verification — both are real scope, not a quick fix).
- **`/list` (combined rated-content browse page)** — exists on web but isn't linked from web's own nav either (orphaned/legacy there too) — probably not worth porting, flagged for completeness only.
- **Known visual bug, deferred to the future UI redesign pass**: the Favorite Movies/Favorite Series rails on Profile screens render with broken layout (reported by the user after testing, not yet diagnosed — no screenshot captured, exact cause unknown). Explicitly not fixed blind; revisit once the redesign pass has real design direction to apply, rather than guessing at a targeted fix now.

## 6. Dependencies added beyond the base Expo template

```
expo-router, expo-secure-store, expo-web-browser, expo-image-picker,
expo-font, expo-splash-screen, @expo-google-fonts/dm-sans,
@expo/vector-icons, react-native-svg, axios,
socket.io-client, i18next, react-i18next, expo-localization,
expo-document-picker, @react-native-community/netinfo,
react-native-reanimated, react-native-draggable-flatlist
```
All chosen deliberately to avoid heavier alternatives where a lighter option covered the need — e.g. `react-native-svg` + a hand-rolled donut chart instead of a full charting library; native image-picker crop UI instead of porting the web's custom cropper component. The Chat/i18n group was added together (see §3); `react-native-reanimated` was deliberately **not** added for either the loading-skeleton polish pass or the offline-handling toast — RN's built-in `Animated` API was enough for a simple opacity pulse/fade both times. **Correction: reanimated was added for the Lists page redesign's drag-to-reorder feature (§3)** — the one case so far where a hand-rolled `Animated`/`PanResponder` approach was judged too risky given this app's repeated jitter bugs from hand-rolled positioning logic elsewhere (the CineGraph donut saga, same section); paired with `react-native-draggable-flatlist`, which needed its own new `babel.config.js` + root-level `GestureHandlerRootView` wiring, both new to this codebase. `@react-native-community/netinfo` (offline handling, §3) is the one Expo-adjacent-but-not-`expo-*`-namespaced library besides those two — there's no `expo-network` equivalent for connectivity change events, `netinfo` is the standard choice, still installed via `npx expo install` for correct SDK-57 version pinning.

## 7. Google Sign-In — read before touching this

This took several rounds of real debugging; the current setup is deliberate, not incidental.

**Backend** (`backend/routes/userRoute.js`, `backend/controllers/userController.js`): the existing Passport Google strategy and its registered `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` (`http://localhost:5000/...`) are **completely untouched** — web login still works exactly as before. Mobile adds an *additive* path: `GET /api/users/auth/google?platform=mobile&redirectUri=<url>` threads the mobile app's own redirect URL through the OAuth `state` param (base64url-encoded JSON), and `googleAuthCallback` decodes it and redirects there instead of the web frontend, when present.

**Why not just point mobile at a fixed custom URL scheme** (`cinephix://oauth-success`)? Because **Expo Go can't register arbitrary custom URL schemes** — only a real standalone/dev-client build can. During development (Expo Go), `Linking.createURL()` produces a dynamic `exp://<lan-ip>:8081/--/oauth-success` URL instead, and the backend has to redirect to *that*, not a hardcoded scheme. This is why the redirect URL is passed explicitly by the client rather than assumed server-side (`src/api/googleAuth.ts`).

**Why the callback URL itself (`GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL`) is NOT made dynamic per-platform**: Google's "Web application" OAuth client type flatly rejects private IPs (`192.168.x.x`) as registered redirect URIs — there's no way to register a LAN-IP callback at all. The workaround for emulator testing is `adb reverse tcp:5000 tcp:5000`, which makes the emulator's own `localhost:5000` forward to the host machine — letting mobile reuse the *exact same* already-registered `http://localhost:5000/api/users/auth/google/callback` as web, with zero Google Cloud Console changes. **This must be re-run every time the emulator restarts** (`adb reverse` doesn't persist). It does not help a physical phone with no ADB connection — see §5.

## 8. Deliberate deviations from "port the web version exactly"

- **No NativeWind/Tailwind** — plain `StyleSheet` + `src/theme/palettes.ts` (9 DaisyUI-derived palettes, read reactively via `useTheme()` — see §3's Theme/Appearance section) + `src/theme/typography.ts` (DM Sans, matching web's font). Reasoning at the time: adding a whole styling paradigm was extra build-risk for no functional gain over tokens + StyleSheet. Worth revisiting if a developer wants to literally copy-paste `className` strings from web source going forward.
- **Star rating is 5 stars with half-star taps**, not a plain 1–10 row — matches `frontend/src/components/StarRating.jsx`'s DaisyUI `rating-half` pattern exactly (each star = 2 backend values, left half = odd, right half = even). The backend scale is still 1–10 underneath; this is purely a UI mapping.
- **CineGraph is an interactive SVG donut**, not the plain bar list it started as — matches `frontend/src/components/CineGraph.jsx`'s Chart.js Doughnut (same 8-color palette). Beyond a straight port: the genre legend is sorted/capped (top 5 + expand) rather than an unbounded list, and tapping a genre navigates to a dedicated Genre Detail screen (watched titles + per-title and per-genre ratings) — web has no equivalent drill-down, mobile-only addition (§3, "CineGraph redesign").
- **Movies/Series "search" hits the list endpoints' filter params**, not the dedicated `/search` endpoints — those return a different response shape (`posterUrl`/`releaseYear` vs `poster_path`/`release_date`) that would've required two data shapes in the UI for no benefit.
